title: 萬曆十年廣東鄉試錄
text:
廣東鄉試錄序
今玆歷在壬午蓋
聖天子十紀元四設科云廣東爲
南海隩區士喁喁北面以待
舉巡按監察御史羅應鶴先
期至申約束而綱紀之矻矻
乎其愼重□□至也於言
===
時藩臬□□□□□□□□
則左布政使李江左參政周
之屏監試則按察使徐時可
副使朱東光諸文學以聘至
考試則道淳曁敎諭胡仕朝
同考試則敎諭姜天麒鄒絢
高應恮姚一理訓導鄭人和
punctuated:
廣東鄉試錄序

今玆歷在壬午，蓋聖天子十紀元、四設科云。廣東爲南海隩區，士喁喁北面以待舉。巡按監察御史羅應鶴先期至，申約束而綱紀之，矻矻乎其愼重□□至也。於言時，藩臬□□□□□□，□□則左布政使李江、左參政周之屏，監試則按察使徐時可、副使朱東光。諸文學以聘至：考試則道淳曁敎諭胡仕朝，同考試則敎諭姜天麒、鄒絢、高應恮、姚一理，訓導鄭人和、
translation_en:
Preface to the Record of the Guangdong Provincial Examination

Now the calendar stands at the renwu year (1582), which is the tenth year of the Sacred Son of Heaven's reign era and the fourth time the civil service examinations have been held. Guangdong is a secluded region by the Southern Sea, where scholars eagerly face north waiting to be recommended. Regional Inspector and Investigating Censor Luo Yinghe 羅應鶴 arrived ahead of schedule, reiterating the regulations and putting the administration in order; how tirelessly conscientious and […][?] to the utmost he was! At this time [?], the provincial administration and surveillance commissions […]; serving as [Proctors] were Left Administration Commissioner Li Jiang 李江 and Left Administration Vice Commissioner Zhou Zhiping 周之屏, while serving as Examination Overseers were Surveillance Commissioner Xu Shike 徐時可 and Surveillance Vice Commissioner Zhu Dongguang 朱東光. The various Confucian teachers arrived by invitation: serving as Examiners were I, Daochun 道淳, together with Instructor Hu Shichao 胡仕朝; serving as Associate Examiners were Instructors Jiang Tianqi 姜天麒, Zou Xuan 鄒絢, Gao Yingquan 高應恮, and Yao Yili 姚一理, and Assistant Instructors Zheng Renhe 鄭人和,…

title: 萬曆十年廣東鄉試錄
text:
楊成性楊敦敘羣有司以檄
至程能授事唯其人旣就列
御史奉
詔令而令之三旣授成帥百執事
告司盟而申之五比日至合
提學副使支可大海南提學
副使唐□□至如約言
===
百有奇□□□□□□
五人策名程藝上之
天府故事多士始進主司宜必有
乂要之言籍旣成御史揖道
淳而授簡竊聞天地盛德之
氣始於西北而盛於東南疇
昔聖帝明王率由北產帝臣
punctuated: 楊成性、楊敦敘。羣有司以檄至，程能授事，唯其人。旣就列，御史奉詔令而令之三；旣授成，帥百執事告司盟而申之五。比日至，合提學副使支可大、海南提學副使唐□□至，如約言百有奇，□□□□□□五人策名，程藝上之天府。故事，多士始進，主司宜必有乂要之言。籍旣成，御史揖道淳而授簡。竊聞天地盛德之氣，始於西北而盛於東南。疇昔聖帝明王，率由北產，帝臣…
translation_en:
…Yang Chengxing 楊成性, and Yang Dunxu 楊敦敘. The various local officials arrived upon receipt of the summons, and their abilities were assessed to assign duties solely according to their suitability. Once they had taken their places in the ranks, the Censor reverently upheld the imperial edicts and ordinances and instructed them three times; once the completed instructions had been imparted, he led the hundred functionaries to report to the deities of the covenant and reiterated the injunctions five times. When the appointed day arrived, the scholars selected by Education-intendant Surveillance Vice Commissioner Zhi Keda 支可大 and Hainan Education-intendant Surveillance Vice Commissioner Tang □□ 唐□□ arrived, numbering over… [?] hundred as stipulated. [After the three sessions were completed, seventy-]five men had their names inscribed on the roster, and their model essays were presented to the imperial court. According to precedent, when the many scholars first advance, the chief examiners ought certainly to offer words on the essentials of governance. Once the register was completed, the Censor bowed to me, Daochun 道淳, and handed me the writing tablets.

I have humbly heard that the vital force of Supreme Virtue between Heaven and Earth begins in the northwest and flourishes in the southeast. In ages past, the sage emperors and enlightened kings were generally born in the north, and the ministers of emperors…

title: 萬曆十年廣東鄉試錄
text:
王佐亦以類從薄海而南曁
聲敎而已迄我
太祖中天而興
挺生南國
嚮明而治此其嚮方由是閎儒莊
士奮起海濱或參
密勿或職論思至以直言
===
我
世祖重明麗正南紀
應符
文命覃敷
光被海寓二三大夫握珠懷寶蔚
爲
國華其言骨鯁其行瑰琦美哉
punctuated: 王佐，亦以類從；薄海而南，曁聲敎而已。迄我太祖中天而興，挺生南國，嚮明而治，此其嚮方。由是閎儒莊士，奮起海濱，或參密勿，或職論思，至以直言。我世祖重明麗正，南紀應符，文命覃敷，光被海寓。二三大夫，握珠懷寶，蔚爲國華；其言骨鯁，其行瑰琦，美哉
translation_en: … and aides to kings likewise followed after their own kind; south to the edges of the seas, they merely received the reach of civilizing prestige and instruction. When our Grand Progenitor (Taizu) arose at the zenith of Heaven, he was born forth in the southern realm and governed facing the brightness of the south—this was the direction toward which he faced. From this time onward, erudite scholars and dignified gentlemen rose up vigorously along the seashore: some participated in confidential state counsels, some held office to deliberate and advise, and some even became known for their forthright remonstrance [?]. When our Epochal Progenitor (Shizu, the Jiajing Emperor) doubled the radiance and cleaved to rectitude, the southern region responded to the auspicious portent; his civilizing mandate spread far and wide, its glory covering the maritime realm. Two or three great officers, clasping pearls and cherishing treasures within, flourished as the splendor of the state; their words were outspoken and unyielding, their conduct extraordinary and admirable. How splendid, …

title: 萬曆十年廣東鄉試錄
text:
煌煌乎蓋鶉火之次也及我
穆考坐銷熒惑海不揚波
皇上在宥萬方
文德四洽多士摶扶搖而上殆將
乗海運而天飛有如垂天之
雲何論朱鳥敦牂之歲盛德
在南天澤□□之至斯葢言
===
壬午乃今鄉國□□□
多士寔應
昌期夫律天時協地紀本之以
帝德類應之以人文多士其皆得
之殆千古一覯也顧士之自
獻必重先資主司爲之推轂
而戒塗必重先發君子慎始
punctuated: 煌煌乎，蓋鶉火之次也。及我穆考，坐銷熒惑，海不揚波。皇上在宥萬方，文德四洽，多士摶扶搖而上，殆將乗海運而天飛，有如垂天之雲，何論朱鳥？敦牂之歲，盛德在南，天澤□□之至，斯葢言壬午。乃今鄉國□□□，多士寔應昌期。夫律天時，協地紀，本之以帝德，類應之以人文，多士其皆得之，殆千古一覯也。顧士之自獻，必重先資；主司爲之推轂而戒塗，必重先發。君子慎始，
translation_en: …and resplendent, truly answering to the astral lodge of the Quail-Fire! Coming down to our late Father Emperor [Muzong], he dispelled the baleful glare of Mars from his throne, and the seas raised no waves. Now His Majesty governs the myriad regions with indulgent grace, and his civilizing virtue permeates all four directions. The multitude of scholars beat the whirlwind to soar aloft; they are well-nigh ready to ride the moving seas and fly through the heavens, like clouds that hang from the sky—what need is there even to speak of the Vermilion Bird? In the Dunzang year, flourishing virtue resides in the south, and heavenly favor […][?] reaches its utmost—this refers to the renwu year [1582]. Now in the provincial examination […][?], the multitude of scholars truly answer to this prosperous era. To conform to the seasons of Heaven, harmonize with the terrestrial order, ground this in imperial virtue, and respond to it in kind through cultural refinement—for the multitude of scholars to attain all of these is an encounter seen perhaps once in a thousand ages! Yet when a scholar presents himself for service, he must place great weight upon his initial pledge; and when the examiners push the wheel-hubs to send him forth and prepare him for the road, they must place great weight upon the outset of the journey. In a gentleman's care for beginnings…

title: 萬曆十年廣東鄉試錄
text:
何莫不然子之成人父命之
冠焉之有室父命之婚入學
親師師命之學夫何命命其
始也故三加同祝醮同誓鼓
篋同呻卽父師無異辭子弟
信而從之無改慮要以天親
則父道尊則師之至也□□
===
可知已主司以□□□□□
多士於千百什一之中非有
父之親師之尊也藉第令有
口不越乎質文言行以爲言
上士聞而服膺儼若
功令此何以故主司之所昭事
則奉
punctuated: 何莫不然？子之成人，父命之冠；焉之有室，父命之婚；入學親師，師命之學。夫何命？命其始也。故三加同祝，醮同誓，鼓篋同呻，卽父師無異辭，子弟信而從之無改慮，要以天親則父、道尊則師之至也，□□可知已。主司以□□□□□多士於千百什一之中，非有父之親、師之尊也。藉第令有口，不越乎質文言行以爲言，上士聞而服膺，儼若功令。此何以故？主司之所昭事，則奉
translation_en: …how could it be otherwise? When a son reaches manhood, his father charges him at the capping ceremony; when he goes to take a wife [?], his father charges him at the wedding ceremony; when he enters school and attaches himself to a teacher, his teacher charges him in his studies. Now why do they charge him? They charge him at his beginning. Thus, the three bestowal of caps share the same invocations, the ceremonial toasts share the same vows, and the beating of the drum on opening the book-boxes shares the same chanting. Even though fathers and teachers have no different words, sons and younger brothers trust and follow them without a change of heart. In sum, because in heavenly kinship the father is supreme, and in the veneration of the Way the teacher is supreme, […] can be known. When the chief examiners […] the many scholars as one out of ten or a hundred or a thousand, they do not possess the kinship of a father or the veneration of a teacher. Even supposing they have words to offer [?], their words do not go beyond speaking of substance and refinement, words and deeds; yet when superior scholars hear them, they take them to heart as solemnly as if they were official statutes of merit. Why is this so? Because what the chief examiners brightly serve is to uphold…

title: 萬曆十年廣東鄉試錄
text:
君事也其所颺言則代
天言也臨之以勿貳律之以在三
加于父師一等矣道淳幸爲
役疇敢以不佞而廢言今夫
士寧質有其文無寧言過其
行比年主司之所忠告率術
此爲繩墨之言道至此以言
===
揚則其文以也□□□日所
習非所用朝藉手而夕屏之
靜言之謂何違何亟也仲尼
四敎首事以文其言兩端小
大殊矣小言之則莫吾猶人
是也大言之則文在兹是也
爾多士擅經術飫道腴該古
punctuated: 君事也；其所颺言，則代天言也。臨之以勿貳，律之以在三，加于父師一等矣。道淳幸爲役，疇敢以不佞而廢言？今夫士，寧質有其文，無寧言過其行。比年主司之所忠告，率術此爲繩墨之言，道至此以言揚，則其文以也。□□□日：「所習非所用，朝藉手而夕屏之。」靜言之謂何，違何亟也！仲尼四敎，首事以文，其言兩端，小大殊矣：小言之，則「莫吾猶人」是也；大言之，則「文在兹」是也。爾多士擅經術，飫道腴，該古
translation_en:
… is the ruler's business; and the words he proclaims aloud are spoken on behalf of Heaven. Approaching them with undivided devotion and governing them according to the threefold obligation—this stands a degree above even father and teacher. Since I, Daochun, have the good fortune to serve in this role, how could I dare, on account of my own inadequacy, refrain from speaking?

Now as for a scholar, it is better that his substance be graced with refinement than that his words exceed his deeds. In recent years, the earnest counsel offered by the examiners has generally followed this as a standard rule. That the Way has come to be promoted through words is because of their literary refinement [?]. [Someone] [?] said: "What one practices is not what one puts to use; in the morning one relies on it as a stepping-stone, and by evening one casts it aside." What then becomes of "pondering it in quietude," and how swiftly one betrays it!

In the four subjects taught by Confucius (Zhongni 仲尼), he began with culture and letters (wen 文). When he spoke of it in two ways, the lesser and the greater differed: spoken of in the lesser sense, it is "In letters, I am perhaps equal to others"; spoken of in the greater sense, it is "Is not this culture (wen) lodged here in me?" All you scholars excel in classical learning, are steeped in the richness of the Way, and encompass ancient…

title: 萬曆十年廣東鄉試錄
text:
今盡倫物挟策具在其誰曰
不文由是而見之行則得時
而駕矣上之經緯天地黼黻
治功下之廣厲四方斌斌君
子之士也之文也在坤爲五
在乾爲二美中四暢天下文
明以是爲文文之至也猶未
===
也士之得與于斯文也本之
吾心文滅其質極于不慙其
心亡矣夫坤陰德也本諸二
之敬義乾陽德也本諸三之
乾乾天命不已地主有常天
地無心此其心也二曜五辰
四時百物山澤通氣草木蕃
punctuated: 今，盡倫物，挟策具在，其誰曰不文？由是而見之行，則得時而駕矣。上之經緯天地，黼黻治功；下之廣厲四方，斌斌君子。之士也，之文也，在坤爲五，在乾爲二，美中四暢，天下文明。以是爲文，文之至也。猶未也，士之得與于斯文也，本之吾心。文滅其質，極于不慙，其心亡矣。夫坤，陰德也，本諸二之敬義；乾，陽德也，本諸三之乾乾。天命不已，地主有常。天地無心，此其心也。二曜、五辰、四時、百物，山澤通氣，草木蕃
translation_en: … and the present, and thoroughly fathom human relations and the principles of things. With the scripts you carry all present here, who could say you lack literary culture (wen)? When from this it is manifested in action, you will seize the timely moment and mount the carriage of service. At the highest level, you will give warp and woof to Heaven and Earth, and add ornamental splendor to the achievements of governance; below, you will broadly encourage the four quarters as refined gentlemen in whom substance and culture are evenly balanced. Such scholars and such culture correspond in the hexagram Kun to the fifth line, and in the hexagram Qian to the second line: beauty within radiates through the four limbs, and all under Heaven is civilized and bright. To take this as literary culture is the utmost perfection of culture. Yet even this is not the whole of it. That a scholar is able to partake in this culture (siwen) is rooted in his own mind. When outward ornament extinguishes inner substance, going so far as to feel no shame, his mind is lost. Now Kun, the yin virtue, is rooted in the reverence and righteousness of its second line; Qian, the yang virtue, is rooted in the unceasing diligence of its third line. The Mandate of Heaven is unceasing; the way of Earth holds to constancy. Heaven and Earth have no deliberate mind of their own, yet this very constancy is their mind. The sun and moon, the five planets, the four seasons, the hundred things—mountains and marshes mingle their vital breaths, and grasses and trees flourish in…

title: 萬曆十年廣東鄉試錄
text:
燕雖天地未始廢文文有本
也多士仰觀俯察宜莫盛于
乾坤乾乾敬義以純其心彌
綸之本在是矣幸哉得士若
此寧非盛德之旺于南也與
哉夫然則南極列星不爲熒
羅浮之山牂牁之水不爲麗
===
明珠翠羽珊瑚木難不爲珍
以是而觀人文日幾幾望其
熾而昌也何可廢耶
上屢
詔詔臣工一以正人心端士習爲
務心純則正習吉則端誠得
若而人相帥而潤色[]
punctuated: 燕，雖天地未始廢文，文有本也。多士仰觀俯察，宜莫盛于乾坤；乾乾敬義，以純其心，彌綸之本在是矣。幸哉！得士若此，寧非盛德之旺于南也與哉！夫然，則南極列星不爲熒，羅浮之山、牂牁之水不爲麗，明珠、翠羽、珊瑚、木難不爲珍。以是而觀人文，日幾幾望其熾而昌也，何可廢耶？上屢詔詔臣工，一以正人心、端士習爲務。心純則正，習吉則端。誠得若而人相帥而潤色[]
translation_en: …luxuriantly [transcription error: 燕 for 蕪]. Even Heaven and Earth have never dispensed with patterned culture, yet patterned culture has its root. When the many scholars look up to observe and look down to examine, surely nothing is more flourishing than the hexagrams Qian and Kun. Being unceasingly diligent and upholding reverence and righteousness so as to purify their minds—herein lies the root of encompassing and ordering the world. How fortunate! To obtain scholars such as these—is it not the flourishing of great virtue in the South? This being so, the arrayed stars of the Southern Pole do not count as dazzling; the mountains of Luofu and the waters of Zangke do not count as splendid; bright pearls, kingfisher feathers, coral, and munan gems do not count as precious. Observing human culture in this light, day by day we earnestly hope for it to blaze forth and prosper—how could it be dispensed with? His Majesty has repeatedly issued edicts instructing his officials to make rectifying people's minds and correcting scholars' habits their sole task. When the mind is pure, it is rectified; when habits are auspicious, they are correct. If we truly obtain such men to lead one another in adorning…

title: 萬曆十年廣東鄉試錄
text:
帝業
當宁方注目而視拊髀而思逐逐
耽耽猶懼不𦾔非惡文也惡
其文之敝也然則主司所爲
口實非述陳言良以廣
詔旨云爾多士受
命而虔其始視父師有加由是而
===
爲天瑞爲地靈爲髦髦爲連
茹爲四暢爲文明
令出惟行主司之言信矣毋將
曰闈以內余爲政闈以外余
無預焉是猶旣弁之髦旣奠
之鴈旣贄之束脩無所用之
矣假令法言可距謂
punctuated: 帝業，當宁方注目而視，拊髀而思，逐逐耽耽，猶懼不𦾔。非惡文也，惡其文之敝也。然則主司所爲口實，非述陳言，良以廣詔旨云爾。多士受命而虔其始，視父師有加，由是而爲天瑞，爲地靈，爲髦髦，爲連茹，爲四暢，爲文明，令出惟行，主司之言信矣。毋將曰：「闈以內，余爲政；闈以外，余無預焉。」是猶旣弁之髦、旣奠之鴈、旣贄之束脩，無所用之矣。假令法言可距，謂
translation_en:
… the Imperial enterprise, the Sovereign on the throne is at this very moment fixing His gaze upon them, slapping His thigh in longing thought, pursuing them eagerly and eyeing them intently, still fearing they may not be reached. It is not that He dislikes literary refinement, but that He dislikes the corruptions of literary refinement. Thus, what the Examiners have taken as their theme is not a repetition of worn-out sayings, but truly a means to broaden and propagate the Imperial edicts.

You many scholars receive the charge and are reverent at the outset, regarding us with even greater respect than your fathers and teachers. From this, if you go on to become auspicious signs of Heaven, spiritual prodigies of Earth, preeminent talents, worthies advancing together like intertwined roots, flourishing limbs of the state, and ornaments of civilization, so that when the Sovereign's commands go forth they are strictly carried out, then the words of the Examiners will be proven trustworthy. Do not let it be said: "Within the examination compound, I am governed by it; outside the examination compound, I have nothing to do with it." That would be like hair-tufts cast off after the capping ceremony, the wild goose after it has been presented at a wedding, or the bundle of dried meat after it has been offered as a gift to a teacher—things for which there is no longer any use! Even supposing that model words of admonition could be rejected, what of …

title: 萬曆十年廣東鄉試錄
text:
明詔何彼鵬以鯤化起羊角而下
鴻毛何所貴之貴嚮往也浸
假而浮沉呴沫直將與鰋鮪
同科去鯤千里去鵬萬里矣
多士生斯世也長斯土也其
將爲鯤鵬耶鰋鮪耶愼所擇
矣是舉也總督兩廣軍務先
===
兵部左侍郎兼都察
院右都御史劉堯誨夙著勳
猷士風丕變今兵部尚書兼
都察院左副都御史陳瑞文
武爲憲譽髦斯士提督南贛
軍務先都察院右僉都御史
張煥今都察院右副都御史
punctuated:
明詔何？彼鵬以鯤化，起羊角而下鴻毛，何所貴之？貴嚮往也。浸假而浮沉呴沫，直將與鰋鮪同科，去鯤千里，去鵬萬里矣。多士生斯世也，長斯土也，其將爲鯤鵬耶？鰋鮪耶？愼所擇矣。
是舉也，總督兩廣軍務、先兵部左侍郎兼都察院右都御史劉堯誨，夙著勳猷，士風丕變；今兵部尚書兼都察院左副都御史陳瑞，文武爲憲，譽髦斯士；提督南贛軍務、先都察院右僉都御史張煥，今都察院右副都御史
translation_en:
… the enlightened imperial decree? When that great Peng bird transforms from the Kun fish, rising on a whirlwind and looking down upon wild geese as mere feathers, what is so valued in it? What is valued is its lofty aspiration. Suppose instead that it merely bobbed up and down, blowing foam to moisten itself—then it would simply be in the same class as mudfish and sturgeon, a thousand li removed from the Kun and ten thousand li removed from the Peng! Born in this age and raised in this land, will you many scholars become the Kun and the Peng, or mudfish and sturgeon? Be careful in what you choose!

In this undertaking, Supreme Commander of Military Affairs of Guangdong and Guangxi, formerly Left Vice Minister of War and Right Censor-in-Chief of the Censorate Liu Yaohui 劉堯誨, has long demonstrated meritorious counsel, greatly transforming the ethos of the scholars; currently Minister of War and Left Vice Censor-in-Chief of the Censorate Chen Rui 陳瑞 serves as a model in both civil and military affairs, bringing renown and distinction to these scholars; Grand Coordinator of Military Affairs of Nan'gan, formerly Right Assistant Censor-in-Chief of the Censorate Zhang Huan 張煥, and currently Right Vice Censor-in-Chief of the Censorate …

title: 萬曆十年廣東鄉試錄
text:
王緝陳常申畫訓典旁宣刑
部郎中王橋平亭疑法嘉樂
章逢右布政使王元敬右叅
政張明正左叅議胡時化副
使鄭岳僉事侯應爵沈植張
友舜薛夢雷總兵官署都督
僉事黃應甲副總兵陳璘于
===
嵩叅將成大儒葉歡濮朝宗
張應科遊擊李棟署都指揮
僉事秦經國胡九經咸綜理
防範協襄
盛典而副使劉倬右叅議陸萬鍾
署都指揮僉事陳居仁以入
賀行按察使今陞廣西右布政
punctuated: 王緝，陳常申畫，訓典旁宣；刑部郎中王橋，平亭疑法，嘉樂章逢；右布政使王元敬、右叅政張明正、左叅議胡時化、副使鄭岳、僉事侯應爵、沈植、張友舜、薛夢雷、總兵官署都督僉事黃應甲、副總兵陳璘、于嵩、叅將成大儒、葉歡、濮朝宗、張應科、遊擊李棟、署都指揮僉事秦經國、胡九經，咸綜理防範，協襄盛典。而副使劉倬、右叅議陸萬鍾、署都指揮僉事陳居仁以入賀行，按察使今陞廣西右布政
translation_en: …Wang Ji 王緝 have set forth the constant norms and clearly demarcated our boundaries, while broadly proclaiming the instructive canons; Director in the Ministry of Justice Wang Qiao 王橋 has adjudicated doubtful cases with fairness and equity, delighting in and encouraging the scholars in their ceremonial dress; Administration Commissioner of the Right Wang Yuanjing 王元敬, Administration Vice Commissioner of the Right Zhang Mingzheng 張明正, Assistant Administration Commissioner of the Left Hu Shihua 胡時化, Surveillance Vice Commissioner Zheng Yue 鄭岳, Assistant Surveillance Commissioners Hou Yingjue 侯應爵, Shen Zhi 沈植, Zhang Youshun 張友舜, and Xue Menglei 薛夢雷, Regional Commander and Acting Assistant Commissioner-in-Chief Huang Yingjia 黃應甲, Vice Regional Commanders Chen Lin 陳璘 and Yu Song 于嵩, Assistant Regional Commanders Cheng Daru 成大儒, Ye Huan 葉歡, Pu Chaozong 濮朝宗, and Zhang Yingke 張應科, Mobile Corps Commander Li Dong 李棟, and Acting Assistant Regional Military Commissioners Qin Jingguo 秦經國 and Hu Jiujing 胡九經 all managed the overall administration and security precautions, jointly assisting in this grand ceremonial occasion. Furthermore, Surveillance Vice Commissioner Liu Zhuo 劉倬, Assistant Administration Commissioner of the Right Lu Wanzhong 陸萬鍾, and Acting Assistant Regional Military Commissioner Chen Juren 陳居仁, who departed to present congratulations at court, as well as Surveillance Commissioner, now promoted to Administration Commissioner of the Right of Guangxi…

punctuated:
使趙可懷以遷秩行，皆與有勞者，例得並書。

Respectfully prefaced by Chen Daochun 陳道淳, Instructor of the Confucian School of Wuchang County, Wuchang Prefecture, Huguang.

title: 萬曆十年廣東鄉試錄
text:
第壹場
四書
孔子曰益者三樂損者三樂樂節禮樂樂
道人之善樂多賢友益矣樂驕樂樂佚
遊樂宴樂損矣
或生而知之或學而知之或困而知之及
其知之一也或安而行之或利而行之
或勉强而行之及其成功一也子曰好
學近乎知力行近乎仁知恥近乎勇
===
稷思天下有饑者由巳饑之也
易
象曰天地交泰后以財成天地之道輔相
天地之宜以左右民初九拔茅茹以其
彙征吉象曰拔茅征吉志在外也九二
包荒用馮河不遐遺朋亡得尚于中行
象曰包荒得尚于中行以光大也
彖曰萃聚也順以說剛中而應故聚也
探賾索隱鉤深致遠以定天下之吉凶成
punctuated:
第壹場
四書
孔子曰：「益者三樂，損者三樂。樂節禮樂，樂道人之善，樂多賢友，益矣；樂驕樂，樂佚遊，樂宴樂，損矣。」
「或生而知之，或學而知之，或困而知之，及其知之，一也。或安而行之，或利而行之，或勉强而行之，及其成功，一也。」子曰：「好學近乎知，力行近乎仁，知恥近乎勇。」
「稷思天下有饑者，由巳饑之也。」
易
《象》曰：「天地交，泰。后以財成天地之道，輔相天地之宜，以左右民。」初九，拔茅茹，以其彙，征吉。《象》曰：「拔茅征吉，志在外也。」九二，包荒，用馮河，不遐遺，朋亡，得尚于中行。《象》曰：「包荒，得尚于中行，以光大也。」
《彖》曰：「萃，聚也。順以說，剛中而應，故聚也。」
「探賾索隱，鉤深致遠，以定天下之吉凶，成
translation_en:
First Session

The Four Books

Confucius said: "There are three kinds of delight that are beneficial, and three kinds of delight that are harmful. To delight in regulating oneself by ritual and music, to delight in speaking of the goodness of others, and to delight in having many worthy friends—these are beneficial. To delight in extravagant pleasures, to delight in idle wandering, and to delight in the pleasures of feasting—these are harmful."

"Some are born with knowledge of it, some learn it through study, and some learn it only after painful difficulty; yet once they know it, it comes to the same thing. Some practice it with natural ease, some practice it for the advantage it brings, and some practice it by forcing themselves to make the effort; yet once they achieve success, it comes to the same thing." The Master said: "To love learning is near to wisdom; to practice with vigor is near to benevolence; to know shame is near to courage."

"Hou Ji thought that if anyone in the world was starving, it was as if he himself had caused them to starve."

Book of Changes (Yi)

The Commentary on the Images (Xiang) says: "Heaven and earth are in communion: Peace (Tai). Thus the sovereign fashions and completes the way of heaven and earth, assists and regulates the adaptations of heaven and earth, in order to aid the people." Nine at the beginning: Pulling up thatch-grass with its roots tangled together, each according to its kind; going forward brings good fortune. The Commentary on the Images says: "Pulling up thatch-grass, going forward brings good fortune: his aspiration is directed outward." Nine in the second place: Embracing the uncultivated, crossing the river without a boat, not neglecting what is distant, and doing away with factionalism, one is able to match the central course. The Commentary on the Images says: "Embracing the uncultivated and being able to match the central course: because his light is great."

The Commentary on the Decision (Tuan) says: "Gathering Together (Cui) means assembling. Compliance coupled with joyousness, firmness in the center meeting with correspondence: therefore there is assembling."

"Exploring the complex and searching out the hidden, hooking up the deep and reaching to the distant, thereby determining good and bad fortune in the world and accomplishing…"

title: 萬曆十年廣東鄉試錄
text:
天下之亹亹者莫大乎蓍龜是故天生
神物聖人則之
神也者妙萬物而爲言者也動萬物者莫
疾乎雷橈萬物者莫疾乎風燥萬物者
莫熯乎火說萬物者莫說乎澤潤萬物
者莫潤乎水終萬物始萬物者莫盛乎
艮故水火相逮雷風不相悖山澤通氣
然後能變化旣成萬物也
書
===
帝曰俞允若兹嘉言罔攸伏野無遺賢萬
邦咸寧稽于衆舍己從人不虐無告不
廢困窮惟帝時克
后非民罔使民非后罔事無自廣以狹人
匹夫匹婦不獲自盡民主罔與成厥功
夙夜罔或不勤不矜細行終累大德爲山
九仞功虧一簣
太史司寇蘇公式敬爾由獄以長我王國
兹式有慎以列用中罰
punctuated:
天下之亹亹者，莫大乎蓍龜。是故天生神物，聖人則之。
神也者，妙萬物而爲言者也。動萬物者，莫疾乎雷；橈萬物者，莫疾乎風；燥萬物者，莫熯乎火；說萬物者，莫說乎澤；潤萬物者，莫潤乎水；終萬物始萬物者，莫盛乎艮。故水火相逮，雷風不相悖，山澤通氣，然後能變化，旣成萬物也。
書
帝曰：「俞！允若兹，嘉言罔攸伏，野無遺賢，萬邦咸寧。稽于衆，舍己從人，不虐無告，不廢困窮，惟帝時克。」
后非民罔使，民非后罔事。無自廣以狹人，匹夫匹婦不獲自盡，民主罔與成厥功。
夙夜罔或不勤。不矜細行，終累大德。爲山九仞，功虧一簣。
太史，司寇蘇公式敬爾由獄，以長我王國。兹式有慎，以列用中罰。
translation_en:
… the untiring endeavors of the world, nothing is greater than the yarrow stalks and the tortoise shell. Therefore, Heaven produced these spirit-like things, and the sages patterned themselves upon them.

"Spirit" is that which is spoken of as working wondrously in all things. In stirring all things, nothing is swifter than thunder; in bending all things, nothing is swifter than wind; in drying all things, nothing is more parching than fire; in gladdening all things, nothing is more gladdening than the marsh; in moistening all things, nothing is more moistening than water; in bringing all things to an end and giving all things a beginning, nothing is more flourishing than Gen [Mountain]. Therefore, water and fire overtake each other, thunder and wind do not conflict with each other, and mountain and marsh communicate theirvital breaths; only then can they transform and change, and bring all things to completion.

Book of Documents (Shu)

The Emperor said: "Yes! Truly if it is like this, admirable words will nowhere lie hidden, no worthy men will be left overlooked in the countryside, and the myriad states will all enjoy peace. To consult with the multitude, to set aside one's own views and follow others, not to oppress the helpless, and not to neglect the distressed and destitute—only the Sovereign Yao was equal to this."

Without the people, the sovereign has none to employ; without the sovereign, the people have none to serve. Do not aggrandize yourself so as to belittle others. If even a single common man or common woman does not obtain the full realization of their nature, the lord of the people will have none with whom to complete his work.

From early morning till late at night, never fail to be diligent. If you do not attend carefully to small actions, in the end it will compromise great virtue; in raising a mound nine fathoms high, the work may fall short by a single basket of earth.

Grand Scribe (taishi), Duke Su, the Minister of Crime (sikou), respectfully attended to the criminal cases he handled, thereby perpetuating our royal state. Here lay his standard of caution, whereby he graded and applied just punishments.

title: 萬曆十年廣東鄉試錄
text:
詩
七月食瓜八月斷壺
菁菁者莪在彼中沚旣見君子我心則喜
干祿百福子孫千億穆穆皇皇宜君宜王
不愆不忘率由舊章
天命降監下民有嚴
春秋
冬十有二月齊侯鄭伯盟于石門隱公三
年
===
春築臺于郎築臺于薛秋築臺于秦
俱莊公三十有一年六月雨僖公三年
八月公會齊侯宋公鄭伯曹伯邾人于檉
僖公元年秋齊侯宋公江人黃人會于
陽穀僖公三年遂伐楚次于陘楚屈
完來盟于師盟于召陵俱僖公四年
公會晉侯宋公陳侯衞侯鄭伯曹伯莒子
邾子滕子薛伯齊世子光吳人鄫人于
戚襄公五年
punctuated:
《詩》
七月食瓜，八月斷壺。
菁菁者莪，在彼中沚。旣見君子，我心則喜。
干祿百福，子孫千億。穆穆皇皇，宜君宜王。不愆不忘，率由舊章。
天命降監，下民有嚴。

《春秋》
冬十有二月，齊侯、鄭伯盟于石門。隱公三年。
春，築臺于郎，築臺于薛，秋，築臺于秦。俱莊公三十有一年。六月，雨。僖公三年。
八月，公會齊侯、宋公、鄭伯、曹伯、邾人于檉。僖公元年。秋，齊侯、宋公、江人、黃人會于陽穀。僖公三年。遂伐楚，次于陘。楚屈完來盟于師，盟于召陵。俱僖公四年。
公會晉侯、宋公、陳侯、衞侯、鄭伯、曹伯、莒子、邾子、滕子、薛伯、齊世子光、吳人、鄫人于戚。襄公五年。
translation_en:
Classic of Poetry (Shijing):
"In the seventh month we eat melons; in the eighth month we cut down the bottle-gourds."
"Lush grows the tarragon, there in the midst of the islet. Having seen the noble man, my heart is delighted."
"Seeking blessings and a hundred felicities, may his descendants be a thousand, a hundred million! Solemn and majestic, fit to be lord, fit to be king; neither erring nor forgetting, following the ancient statutes."
"The Mandate of Heaven looks down from on high, and the people below are held in awe."

Spring and Autumn Annals (Chunqiu):
"In winter, in the twelfth month, the Marquis of Qi and the Earl of Zheng made a covenant at Shimen." (3rd year of Duke Yin)
"In spring, a terrace was built at Lang; a terrace was built at Xue; in autumn, a terrace was built at Qin." (All in the 31st year of Duke Zhuang) "In the sixth month, it rained." (3rd year of Duke Xi)
"In the eighth month, the Duke met the Marquis of Qi, the Duke of Song, the Earl of Zheng, the Earl of Cao, and a representative of Zhu at Cheng." (1st year of Duke Xi) "In autumn, the Marquis of Qi, the Duke of Song, a representative of Jiang, and a representative of Huang met at Yanggu." (3rd year of Duke Xi) "Thereupon they invaded Chu and halted at Xing. Qu Wan of Chu came to make a covenant with the army; they made a covenant at Shaoling." (Both in the 4th year of Duke Xi)
"The Duke met the Marquis of Jin, the Duke of Song, the Marquis of Chen, the Marquis of Wei, the Earl of Zheng, the Earl of Cao, the Viscount of Ju, the Viscount of Zhu, the Viscount of Teng, the Earl of Xue, Heir Apparent Guang of Qi, a representative of Wu, and a representative of Zeng at Qi." (5th year of Duke Xiang)

title: 萬曆十年廣東鄉試錄
text:
禮記
將適公所宿齊戒居外寢沐浴史進象笏
書思對命旣服習容觀玉聲乃出揖私
朝煇如也登車則有光矣
大德不官大道不器
爲人君者謹其所好惡而已矣君好之則
臣爲之上行之則民從之詩云誘民孔
易此之謂也
敬愼者仁之地也
===
第貳場
論
王者如天
詔誥表〔內科一道〕
擬漢舉質樸敦厚遜讓有行者詔〔永光元年〕
擬唐以張說兼集賢院學士誥〔開元十三年〕
擬
punctuated:
《禮記》
「將適公所，宿齊戒，居外寢，沐浴，史進象笏，書思對命。旣服，習容，觀玉聲，乃出。揖私朝，煇如也；登車，則有光矣。」
「大德不官，大道不器。」
「爲人君者，謹其所好惡而已矣。君好之，則臣爲之；上行之，則民從之。《詩》云：『誘民孔易。』此之謂也。」
「敬愼者，仁之地也。」

第貳場
論
「王者如天」
詔誥表〔內科一道〕
擬漢《舉質樸敦厚遜讓有行者詔》〔永光元年〕
擬唐《以張說兼集賢院學士誥》〔開元十三年〕
擬
translation_en:
Record of Rites (Liji)
"When about to go to the duke's palace, he observed fasting and vigil the night before, residing in the outer apartment. Having washed his hair and bathed, the scribe presented the ivory tablet, on which he wrote his thoughts, what he had to reply, and the ruler's orders. Having put on his robes, he practiced his deportment and listened to the sound of his jade pendants, and then went out. When he bowed to those in his private court, his manner was bright and radiant; when he mounted his carriage, it seemed to shine with splendor."
"Great virtue does not confine itself to a single office; the great Way is not limited like a single vessel."
"He who is a ruler of men need only be careful about what he likes and dislikes. What the ruler likes, his ministers will do; what the superior practices, the common people will follow. The Book of Odes (Shi) says: 'To guide the people is very easy.' This is what is meant."
"Reverence and caution are the ground of benevolence."

Discourse
"The True King is Like Heaven"

title: 萬曆十年廣東鄉試錄
text:
上以
御製猗蘭操示輔臣謝表〔宣德七年〕
判語〔五條〕
加減罪例
功臣田土
行宮營門
聽訟迴避
帶造段疋
第叄場
===
策〔五道〕
問文武並用安寧長久之術譚君道者類
能言之夫文與武固相須與自古皇王
帝者之略所以經緯張弛率不外此其
道何若漢魏而降文章爲盛君臣上下
動以賦頌相雄而周官大閱之典季世
踵行以爲故事其於文武何居亦可得
而言其略與我
皇上
punctuated:
上以御製《猗蘭操》示輔臣謝表〔宣德七年〕

判語〔五條〕
加減罪例
功臣田土
行宮營門
聽訟迴避
帶造段疋

第叄場
策〔五道〕

問：文武並用，安寧長久之術，譚君道者類能言之。夫文與武固相須與？自古皇王帝者之略，所以經緯張弛，率不外此，其道何若？漢、魏而降，文章爲盛，君臣上下，動以賦頌相雄；而《周官》大閱之典，季世踵行以爲故事，其於文武何居？亦可得而言其略與？我皇上
translation_en:
… His Majesty Shows the Imperially Composed "Orchid Melody" (Yilan cao) to His Grand Secretaries (7th year of Xuande [1432]).

Legal Judgments [Five topics]
Rules for Increasing or Reducing Punishments
Lands of Meritorious Officials
Gates of Encampments at Travelling Palaces
Recusal in Hearing Litigation
Extra Fabrication of Silk Fabrics

Third Session
Policy Questions [Five questions]

Question: Employing both civil and military arts is the art of securing enduring peace and stability—those who discuss the Way of the ruler are generally able to speak of it. Do the civil and the military indeed depend on one another? Since antiquity, the grand strategies of sovereigns, kings, and emperors, by which they ordered the state and alternated tension with relaxation, have generally not gone beyond this. What was their Way like? From the Han and Wei dynasties onward, literary composition flourished, and rulers and ministers, superiors and inferiors, routinely vied for eminence through rhapsodies and eulogies; meanwhile, the Rites of Zhou (Zhouguan) canon of the Grand Military Review was followed by later ages merely as a routine observance. How did they stand with respect to civil and military affairs? Can an outline of this also be stated? Our August Emperor…

title: 萬曆十年廣東鄉試錄
text:
天縱
聖神乃文乃武邇來
萬幾之暇
特詔近臣披閱圖史抽對章句而暮春
教閱深惟先事之備天下欣然想見
太平之盛矣
聖學方新
聖治方勤抑有可爲
顯謨弘烈之助者否伏聞
===
皇上所口授儒臣洞然心性之語而
閱武之日諸所憫念憂勤
意至渥也將以何者可裨萬分一焉諸士夙抱
忠悃行且揚于
大廷必有所以先資自
獻者
問古稱才難天下事孰非須才而辦者五
三上世勿論兩漢以來亦各因俗爲治
不假於異代何謂無才蓋非才之難也
punctuated:
天縱聖神，乃文乃武。邇來萬幾之暇，特詔近臣披閱圖史，抽對章句；而暮春教閱，深惟先事之備。天下欣然，想見太平之盛矣。聖學方新，聖治方勤，抑有可爲顯謨弘烈之助者否？伏聞皇上所口授儒臣，洞然心性之語，而閱武之日，諸所憫念憂勤，意至渥也。將以何者可裨萬分一焉？諸士夙抱忠悃，行且揚于大廷，必有所以先資自獻者。
問：古稱才難。天下事孰非須才而辦者？五、三上世勿論，兩漢以來，亦各因俗爲治，不假於異代，何謂無才？蓋非才之難也，
translation_en:
…Heaven-endowed with sagehood and spirit, is accomplished in both civil and military affairs. Recently, in moments of leisure from his myriad affairs of state, he has specially decreed that his close courtiers open and peruse charts and histories, and draw out passages and sentences to match; and in the military reviews of late spring, he has deeply reflected on preparations made prior to events. All under Heaven rejoices, envisioning the flourishing of great peace! Now, as the sage learning is newly refreshed and the sage governance is diligent, might there be anything that can serve to assist his illustrious plans and grand achievements? We humbly hear that what the Emperor orally imparted to his Confucian courtiers were words penetrating into the mind and human nature, and that on the day of reviewing the troops, in all that he commiserated over and anxiously labored upon, his intentions were most generous. By what means might one contribute even a ten-thousandth part to this? You gentlemen have long cherished loyal sincerity and are soon to be presented at the great court; you must have that with which to make a preliminary offering to present yourselves.

Question: Antiquity said that talent is hard to find. Yet among the affairs of the world, which is not accomplished through the need for talent? Not to mention the high antiquity of the Five Emperors and Three Kings, since the Two Han dynasties, each era has also governed in accordance with its customs without borrowing talent from another age—so how can it be said that there was no talent? Indeed, it is not that talent in itself is hard to find;…

title: 萬曆十年廣東鄉試錄
text:
才而如九德三俊之徒者難也士固各
以才效用今之爲士者大略有四品脩
詞之家稍能操翰輒自許不朽盛事是
謂文章之士其不能者則自託於圓覺
定慧超悟本心是謂談禪之士及其高
者慷慨負俗蟬蛻當世浮游塵表是謂
清言之士又其通者俯仰儕俗敏捷便
給以赴事功是謂術霍之士斯四者可
以言才乎其亦有適於用否乎談轉移
===
於今日則遵何術或以爲宜登質直崇
正學責實功察似求眞何施而可諸士
其臚列而縷數之吾以觀才品焉
問史自尚書春秋左氏而下世稱太史遷
遷之書學者戶誦之訓故則若篤若廣
若駰若誕生若伯莊若貞若守節諸家
評隲則若固若勰若知幾若轍若周若
元量諸家可指言之與有議其記煩而
志寡者有恨其博不足者有知其有激
punctuated:
才而如九德、三俊之徒者，難也。士固各以才效用，今之爲士者，大略有四品：脩詞之家，稍能操翰，輒自許不朽盛事，是謂文章之士；其不能者，則自託於圓覺、定慧，超悟本心，是謂談禪之士；及其高者，慷慨負俗，蟬蛻當世，浮游塵表，是謂清言之士；又其通者，俯仰儕俗，敏捷便給，以赴事功，是謂術霍之士。斯四者可以言才乎？其亦有適於用否乎？談轉移於今日，則遵何術？或以爲宜登質直、崇正學、責實功、察似求眞，何施而可？諸士其臚列而縷數之，吾以觀才品焉。
問：史自《尚書》、《春秋》、《左氏》而下，世稱太史遷。遷之書，學者戶誦之。訓故則若篤、若廣、若駰、若誕生、若伯莊、若貞、若守節諸家；評隲則若固、若勰、若知幾、若轍、若周、若元量諸家，可指言之與？有議其記煩而志寡者，有恨其博不足者，有知其有激…
translation_en:
…Rather, it is talent on a par with the followers of the Nine Virtues and the Three Eminences that is rare. Scholars indeed each offer their service through their talent, and among those who act as scholars today, there are roughly four categories: Specialists in rhetoric, as soon as they are slightly able to wield the brush, promptly flatter themselves as accomplishing an immortal, grand enterprise—these are called scholars of literary composition. Those unable to do so entrust themselves to perfect enlightenment, meditative concentration, and wisdom, claiming to transcend and awaken to the original mind—these are called scholars who discourse on Chan. Coming to the lofty ones, they passionately turn their backs on convention, shed the world like a cicada's slough, and roam beyond the dusty realm—these are called scholars of pure conversation. And as for the adaptable ones, they adjust themselves to the common crowd, nimble and glib in pursuing practical achievements—these are called scholars of stratagems and expedients [? 術霍, likely for 術數 or 縱橫]. Can these four types be spoken of as possessing true talent? Are they, or are they not, suited for practical use? If we speak of transforming this situation today, what method should be followed? Some hold that we ought to advance the plain and upright, revere orthodox learning, demand substantive achievements, and scrutinize the specious to seek the genuine—what measures will suffice? Gentlemen, set them forth in order and enumerate them in detail, so that I may observe the quality of your talent.

Question: In historiography, coming down from the Book of Documents (Shangshu), the Spring and Autumn Annals (Chunqiu), and the Zuo Commentary (Zuoshi), the world acclaims the Grand Scribe Sima Qian (Taishi Qian). Sima Qian's book is recited in every scholar's household. As for exegesis and glosses, there are masters such as Yan Du 延篤, Xu Guang 徐廣, Pei Yin 裴駰,鄒誕生 Zou Dansheng, Liu Bozhuang 劉伯莊, Sima Zhen 司馬貞, and Zhang Shoujie 張守節; as for critical appraisal, there are masters such as Ban Gu 班固, Liu Xie 劉勰, Liu Zhiji 劉知幾, Su Zhe 蘇轍, Qiao Zhou 譙周, and Ge Yuanliang 葛元量 [? or Leu Yuanliang]—can you point them out and discuss them? Some criticize his work for being prolix in recording events yet scant in treatises; some regret that his erudition was insufficient; some recognize that he was provoked…

title: 萬曆十年廣東鄉試錄
text:
而言之者有稱其隱而彰直而寛簡而
明者稱多愛愛奇者博學善敘事者然
與非與後世治遷史各以其意以意尊
信不掩其瑕以意詆訶不掩其瑜以款
啓爲月旦不覩其全至其體裁綜覈品
騭甄錄間是非當否可指摘其一二與
舎遷史而外亦可刪削昭雪訂正成一
家言否與誠倂舉二十一史次第潤色
一準於遷史豈非千古快事而世或難
===
其人也諸士中蓋有博洽爾雅如遷者
幸相與折衷之毋讓
問孔子有言國家不患寡不患貧貧與寡
不足患則所患者可知已
明興二百餘年生養休息閭閻日庶稱夥矣
帑藏日積稱富矣顧衆之所聚螳食土田今
土非能加益也將歲竭
國計給之與彼衆靡窮而藏有限何以待之
與說者謂歷稽往牒金用三品通錢法
punctuated:
而言之者，有稱其隱而彰、直而寛、簡而明者，稱多愛、愛奇者，博學善敘事者，然與？非與？後世治遷史，各以其意：以意尊信，不掩其瑕；以意詆訶，不掩其瑜；以款啓爲月旦，不覩其全。至其體裁綜覈、品騭甄錄間，是非當否，可指摘其一二與？舎遷史而外，亦可刪削昭雪、訂正成一家言否與？誠倂舉二十一史，次第潤色，一準於遷史，豈非千古快事，而世或難其人也。諸士中蓋有博洽爾雅如遷者，幸相與折衷之，毋讓。
問：孔子有言，國家不患寡，不患貧。貧與寡不足患，則所患者可知已。明興二百餘年，生養休息，閭閻日庶，稱夥矣；帑藏日積，稱富矣。顧衆之所聚，螳食土田，今土非能加益也。將歲竭國計給之與？彼衆靡窮，而藏有限，何以待之與？說者謂歷稽往牒，金用三品，通錢法
translation_en:
… and spoke out of frustration; some praise him for being subtle yet manifest, forthright yet magnanimous, and concise yet clear; some call him fond of much and fond of the strange, or broadly learned and skilled at narrating events—are these judgments right or wrong? In later ages, those who studied Sima Qian's history each followed their own preconceptions: when revering and trusting him out of their own preconceptions, they could not conceal his flaws; when denouncing and scolding him out of their own preconceptions, they could not conceal his merits; and when making evaluations from narrow-minded views, they failed to see the whole picture. As for the comprehensiveness of his structure and style, and his appraisals and selections, can one point out one or two instances of what is right or wrong, appropriate or inappropriate among them? Setting aside Sima Qian's history, could one also abridge, vindicate, and revise other works to form an independent school of thought of one's own? If one were truly to take up all of the Twenty-One Histories together, polish them in sequence, and model them entirely upon Sima Qian's history, would that not be a most gratifying achievement for all eternity—even though the world might find it difficult to produce such a person? Among you gentlemen there are surely those as broadly learned and refined as Sima Qian; please weigh and judge these matters together, and do not hold back.

Question: Confucius had a saying that a state does not worry about scarcity of population and does not worry about poverty. If poverty and scarcity are not worth worrying about, then what is to be worried about can be known. Since the rise of the Ming more than two hundred years ago, the people have been nurtured and given rest; the common folk in the villages grow more numerous by the day and may be called abundant, while the state treasuries accumulate more day by day and may be called rich. Yet where the multitude gathers, they feed upon the farmland like locusts [?], and today the land cannot be increased. Shall we exhaust the state's finances every year to supply them? Those multitudes are endless while the treasuries are finite—how then shall we deal with this? Commentators say that, examining past records through the ages, metal currency was used in three grades, and circulating coinage…

title: 萬曆十年廣東鄉試錄
text:
以增民貲亦捄敝之一策與上自三代
下及漢唐宋籍爲國用
國家自洪永迄今阻格不甚行其故何在鼓
鑄不得其方流通不盡其術其弊何在
夫銅錢資也今銅散於委巷滯於商賈
而僅僅開滇池一隅尚有遺寶若乃錢
制病不精塗病未廣官病不耑譚錢法
者亦間及之甲是乙非未獲本策而以
曰法難通矣今諸士足掛市里周悉民
===
利願詳言之俟司計者裁焉
問東粵昔稱奧區自弄兵以來莫寧其所
則四戰之國巳比者賴
主上威靈
廟堂勝筭文武臣工朋心比力夷險除穢漸號
完土顧粵地內多重岡複嶺山寇尚間
有椎剽外連巨海水寇叵測其能即寢
武事以文令乎則戰非所諱言矣戰之
說有二曰大征曰鵰勦大征則糜財甚
punctuated:
以增民貲，亦捄敝之一策與？上自三代，下及漢、唐、宋，籍爲國用。國家自洪、永迄今，阻格不甚行，其故何在？鼓鑄不得其方，流通不盡其術，其弊何在？夫銅，錢資也。今銅散於委巷，滯於商賈，而僅僅開滇池一隅，尚有遺寶。若乃錢制病不精，塗病未廣，官病不耑，譚錢法者亦間及之。甲是乙非，未獲本策，而以曰「法難通」矣。今諸士足掛市里，周悉民利，願詳言之，俟司計者裁焉。

問：東粵昔稱奧區，自弄兵以來，莫寧其所，則四戰之國巳。比者賴主上威靈，廟堂勝筭，文武臣工朋心比力，夷險除穢，漸號完土。顧粵地內多重岡複嶺，山寇尚間有椎剽；外連巨海，水寇叵測。其能即寢武事以文令乎？則戰非所諱言矣。戰之說有二：曰大征，曰鵰勦。大征則糜財甚，
translation_en:
… in order to increase the people's wealth—is this not also one policy for remedying the present ills? From the Three Dynasties above down to the Han, Tang, and Song, [coinage] was relied upon for state expenditure. In our Dynasty, from the Hongwu and Yongle eras down to the present, it has met with obstruction and has not circulated very widely; what is the reason for this? Smelting and casting have not found the proper method, and circulation has not exhausted the proper arts; where do the abuses lie? Now copper is the raw material of coin. Today copper is scattered in back alleys and stagnates among merchants and traders, while mining is opened solely in the single corner of Dianchi (Yunnan), leaving unexploited treasures elsewhere. As for the defects that the standard of coinage is not refined, that the channels of circulation are not wide, and that the officials in charge are not specialized—those who discuss monetary policy also touch upon these from time to time. One party affirms what another denies; they have not grasped the fundamental policy, and consequently declare, "The system is difficult to make work!" Today you gentlemen set foot in the markets and neighborhoods and are thoroughly acquainted with what benefits the people. We wish you to speak of this in detail, awaiting the decision of those in charge of fiscal planning.

Question: Eastern Yue (Guangdong) was formerly called a richly sheltered region, but since the outbreaks of armed conflict, nowhere has enjoyed peace, so that it has become a land of warfare on all sides. Recently, relying on the august numinous power of His Majesty the Sovereign, the victorious calculations of the imperial court, and the united hearts and combined strength of civil and military officials, the perilous strongholds have been leveled and the filth cleared away, so that it is gradually called an intact territory once more. Yet within the land of Guangdong there are many layered ridges and doubled mountain ranges, where mountain bandits still occasionally commit robbery and pillage; outside, it joins the vast sea, where pirates are unpredictable. Can we then immediately lay aside military affairs and govern through civil ordinances alone? Thus warfare is not something we can shy away from speaking of. In discussions of warfare there are two approaches: one is called the grand campaign (dazheng), and the other is called the hawk-strike suppression (diaojiao, targeted raids). A grand campaign wastes immense financial resources, …

title: 萬曆十年廣東鄉試錄
text:
罄郡縣之貲無足以佐軍興鵰勦則漏
姦賊以遺禍二者孰宜戰守之兵在水
陸二寨或謂民甫息肩當撤兵以寬民
力或謂嶺外非馴民有角者觸有齒者
齧其天性固然解甲束馬脫有警能驅
市人與鬪乎即水陸二兵議留議撤緩
急輕重必有能辨之者諸士為粉榆籌
石畫當陳於未戰毋徒曰俟鼓之日也
punctuated: 罄郡縣之貲，無足以佐軍興；鵰勦則漏姦賊以遺禍。二者孰宜？戰守之兵，在水陸二寨。或謂民甫息肩，當撤兵以寬民力；或謂嶺外非馴民，有角者觸，有齒者齧，其天性固然，解甲束馬，脫有警，能驅市人與鬪乎？即水陸二兵，議留議撤，緩急輕重，必有能辨之者。諸士為粉榆籌石畫，當陳於未戰，毋徒曰俟鼓之日也。
translation_en:
… exhausting the resources of the prefectures and counties without sufficing to support military mobilization; whereas targeted raids let treacherous bandits slip through, leaving behind future trouble. Which of these two is more appropriate?

The troops for offense and defense are stationed in the naval and land stockades. Some say that the people have only just rested their shoulders from their burdens, so we should withdraw the troops to ease the strain on the people's strength. Others say that the people beyond the southern mountain passes are not docile: those with horns gore and those with teeth bite, for such is inherently their natural disposition; if we unstrap our armor and tether our horses, should an alarm suddenly arise, could we drive untrained townspeople to fight against them? Even regarding these naval and land forces—whether to deliberate on retaining them or withdrawing them—there must be someone able to discern their relative urgency and importance. You scholars, in devising rock-solid plans for your native homeland [reading 枌榆 for 粉榆], ought to set them forth before hostilities begin; do not merely say that you will wait until the day the war-drums sound!

title: 萬曆十年廣東鄉試錄
text:
第壹場
四書
孔子曰益者三樂損者三樂樂節禮樂樂
道人之善樂多賢友益矣樂驕樂樂佚
遊樂宴樂損矣
梁維屏
同考試官教諭姚批題多頭緒作者類煩冗
可厭此卷刋落言筌直見本色宜式多士
同考試官教諭高批渾厚古雅不事綺麗是
===
文之復古者
考試官教諭胡批醇雅可誦結意尤精
考試官教諭陳批發損益意精透
樂有損益于心之敬肆辨之也夫樂生于心者
也心敬則益心肆則損是以君子慎所樂與夫
子意謂吾人一心曷嘗無所用哉其有所向也
而樂生矣其有所入也而樂成矣顧均之爲樂
也樂得其道而益者有三樂得其欲而損者有
三何言乎益也心存于中感物而動其所深嗜
punctuated:
第壹場
四書
「孔子曰：『益者三樂，損者三樂。樂節禮樂，樂道人之善，樂多賢友，益矣。樂驕樂，樂佚遊，樂宴樂，損矣。』」
梁維屏
同考試官教諭姚批：題多頭緒，作者類煩冗可厭。此卷刋落言筌，直見本色，宜式多士。
同考試官教諭高批：渾厚古雅，不事綺麗，是文之復古者。
考試官教諭胡批：醇雅可誦，結意尤精。
考試官教諭陳批：發損益意精透。
樂有損益，于心之敬肆辨之也。夫樂，生于心者也。心敬則益，心肆則損，是以君子慎所樂與！夫子意謂：吾人一心，曷嘗無所用哉？其有所向也，而樂生矣；其有所入也，而樂成矣。顧均之爲樂也，樂得其道而益者有三，樂得其欲而損者有三。何言乎益也？心存于中，感物而動，其所深嗜
translation_en:
First Session
The Four Books
"Confucius said: 'There are three kinds of enjoyment that are beneficial, and three kinds of enjoyment that are harmful. To find enjoyment in the discriminating study of ceremonies and music, to find enjoyment in speaking of the goodness of others, and to find enjoyment in having many worthy friends—these are beneficial. To find enjoyment in extravagant pleasures, to find enjoyment in idle wandering, and to find enjoyment in the pleasures of feasting—these are harmful.'"
Liang Weiping 梁維屏
Comment by Associate Examiner and Instructor Yao 姚: The topic has many threads, and writers mostly fall into tiresome prolixity. This paper strips away the verbal traps to directly reveal the true essence; it is fit to serve as a model for the multitude of scholars.
Comment by Associate Examiner and Instructor Gao 高: Substantial, profound, and classically elegant, without striving for ornate embellishment—this is writing that restores antiquity.
Comment by Examiner and Instructor Hu 胡: Pure, elegant, and worthy of recitation; the concluding thought is especially refined.
Comment by Examiner and Instructor Chen 陳: It brings out the meaning of harm and benefit with refined thoroughness.
Whether enjoyment brings harm or benefit is distinguished by the reverence or laxity of the mind. Now, enjoyment is something born from the mind. When the mind is reverent, there is benefit; when the mind is lax, there is harm. Therefore, how cautious the gentleman is in what he enjoys! The Master's meaning is that this one mind of ours is never without something to which it applies itself. Where it has an inclination, enjoyment is born; where it enters deeply, enjoyment is completed. Yet while all are equally enjoyments, there are three that attain the Way and bring benefit, and three that indulge desires and bring harm. Why are they called beneficial? When the mind is preserved within and is moved in response to external things, that which it deeply relishes…

title: 萬曆十年廣東鄉試錄
text:
而篤好者節禮樂焉道人之善焉多賢友焉養
吾中和之德則本體益融廣吾觀摩之資則進
脩益懋蓋一念敬將上達無所不至始焉心樂
之既乃與之俱化而不自知也故曰益者三樂
何言乎損也心馳于外逐物而流其所深嗜而
篤好者驕樂焉佚遊焉宴樂焉矜夸之氣勝則
檢節之意微淫惰之習滋則賢善之交遠蓋一
念肆將下達無所不至始焉心樂之既亦與之
俱化而不自知也故曰損者三樂吁人之為學
===
求其益不求其損而一念易移入乎損即出乎
益盍早辨之而已是樂也豈惟學者宜慎之夫
快意當前恒情易溺而憸媚之徒日從臾其間
損之樂日益而益之樂日損非宣哲濬明疇能
鑒焉彼夫履綦鳴玉左規矩右準繩而又朝夕
箴圖先後師保以相為交儆斯能察於損益之
際而自得其心者與
或生而知之或學而知之或困而知之及
其知之一也或安而行之或利而行之
punctuated:
而篤好者，節禮樂焉，道人之善焉，多賢友焉。養吾中和之德，則本體益融；廣吾觀摩之資，則進脩益懋。蓋一念敬將，上達無所不至，始焉心樂之，既乃與之俱化而不自知也，故曰「益者三樂」。何言乎損也？心馳于外，逐物而流，其所深嗜而篤好者，驕樂焉，佚遊焉，宴樂焉。矜夸之氣勝，則檢節之意微；淫惰之習滋，則賢善之交遠。蓋一念肆將，下達無所不至，始焉心樂之，既亦與之俱化而不自知也，故曰「損者三樂」。吁！人之為學，求其益不求其損；而一念易移，入乎損即出乎益，盍早辨之而已？是樂也，豈惟學者宜慎之？夫快意當前，恒情易溺，而憸媚之徒日從臾其間，損之樂日益，而益之樂日損，非宣哲濬明，疇能鑒焉？彼夫履綦鳴玉，左規矩、右準繩，而又朝夕箴圖，先後師保，以相為交儆，斯能察於損益之際，而自得其心者與！
「或生而知之，或學而知之，或困而知之，及其知之，一也。或安而行之，或利而行之，
translation_en:
…and devotedly loves is finding enjoyment in the due regulation of ceremonies and music, finding enjoyment in speaking of the goodness of others, and finding enjoyment in having many worthy friends. When one nurtures one's virtue of equilibrium and harmony, the fundamental substance of the mind becomes ever more harmonious; when one broadens one's resources for observation and emulation, one's advancement and self-cultivation become ever more vigorous. Indeed, when a single thought is sustained by reverence, one progresses upward until there is nowhere one cannot reach; at first the mind takes pleasure in these things, and eventually it is completely transformed along with them without even realizing it. Therefore it is said, "There are three things men find enjoyment in which are advantageous." What is meant by being injurious? When the mind gallops outward, chasing after external things and drifting away, what it deeply craves and devotedly loves is finding enjoyment in extravagant pleasures, finding enjoyment in idleness and sauntering about, and finding enjoyment in the pleasures of feasting. When a boastful and arrogant spirit prevails, the intention of self-restraint and moderation grows faint; when dissolute and indolent habits proliferate, association with the worthy and good grows distant. Indeed, when a single thought is given over to unrestraint, one sinks downward until there is nowhere one will not stoop; at first the mind takes pleasure in these things, and eventually it too is completely transformed along with them without even realizing it. Therefore it is said, "There are three things men find enjoyment in which are injurious." Alas! In pursuing learning, a person seeks what is advantageous and does not seek what is injurious; yet a single thought easily shifts, and to enter into what is injurious is immediately to depart from what is advantageous—why not simply discern this early on? And as for such enjoyments, is it only scholars who ought to be cautious about them? When gratifying desires are right before one's eyes, ordinary human feelings easily drown in them, and when artful flatterers daily urge one on from within, injurious enjoyments increase day by day while advantageous enjoyments decrease day by day. Without comprehensive wisdom and profound clarity, who could perceive this? Only he who treads with shoe-ribbons and tinkling jade pendants, with compass and square to his left and plumb-line to his right, and who morning and evening consults admonitory diagrams, with Grand Preceptors and Grand Guardians before and behind him for mutual admonition, is able to discern the boundary between benefit and injury and truly possess his own mind!

"Some are born with the knowledge, some know it by study, and some acquire the knowledge after a painful feeling of their ignorance. But the knowledge being possessed, it comes to the same thing. Some practice them with a natural ease, some from a desire for their advantages,…

title: 萬曆十年廣東鄉試錄
text:
或勉强而行之及其成功一也子曰好
學近乎知力行近乎仁知恥近乎勇
莫維則
同考試官教諭鄒批題中一與近正相照應
此作最得肯綮而詞更冲雅錄之
考試官教諭胡批理精詞整
考試官教諭陳批大雅之文
論人於達德要之則一求之則近也夫終而一
者成德也始而近者入德也彼困勉者可自諉
===
耶且夫達德在人理本一而非二機本近而非
遠也人顧自力何如耳彼道著於人不必生知
而後可語知也或得之學或得之困雖若各一
其知及觀於既知之後無二知焉何也道要之
能知而止也道體於人不必安行而後可語行
也或由于利或由于勉雖若各一其行及觀於
成功之後無二行焉何也道要之能行而止也
夫于知可以觀知于行可以觀仁于知仁之一
而可以觀勇矣彼未能一者其何以近之哉天
punctuated:
或勉强而行之，及其成功，一也。子曰：「好學近乎知，力行近乎仁，知恥近乎勇。」

莫維則

同考試官教諭鄒批：題中「一」與「近」正相照應，此作最得肯綮，而詞更冲雅，錄之。
考試官教諭胡批：理精詞整。
考試官教諭陳批：大雅之文。

論人於達德，要之則一，求之則近也。夫終而一者，成德也；始而近者，入德也。彼困勉者可自諉耶？且夫達德在人，理本一而非二，機本近而非遠也，人顧自力何如耳。彼道著於人，不必生知而後可語知也。或得之學，或得之困，雖若各一其知，及觀於既知之後，無二知焉。何也？道要之能知而止也。道體於人，不必安行而後可語行也。或由于利，或由于勉，雖若各一其行，及觀於成功之後，無二行焉。何也？道要之能行而止也。夫于知可以觀知，于行可以觀仁，于知仁之一而可以觀勇矣。彼未能一者，其何以近之哉？天
translation_en:
… or some practice them only by strenuous effort; but when the achievement is made, it comes to one and the same thing. The Master said: "To be fond of learning is near to wisdom; to practice with vigor is near to humaneness; to know shame is near to courage."

Mo Weize 莫維則

Comment by Associate Examiner and County Director of Studies Zou 鄒: In the topic, "being one" and "being near" directly correspond to each other. This composition best grasps the crucial point, and its diction is even more composed and refined. Record it for printing.
Comment by Examiner and County Director of Studies Hu 胡: The reasoning is precise and the phrasing is well-ordered.
Comment by Examiner and County Director of Studies Chen 陳: Writing of great elegance.

In discussing people with respect to the universal virtues, in their ultimate summation they are one, and in seeking them they are near at hand. Now, to be one in the end is the completion of virtue; to be near at the beginning is the entry into virtue. How then could those who learn through difficulty and practice by strenuous effort make excuses for themselves? Moreover, as the universal virtues reside in humanity, their principle is fundamentally one and not twofold, and their vital mechanism is fundamentally near and not distant; it simply depends on how much effort a person exerts for himself. When the Way is manifested in people, one need not be born with knowledge before one can speak of knowing it. Whether one attains it through learning or attains it through difficulty, although each seems to have its own distinct way of knowing, when we observe them after they have come to know, there are not two kinds of knowledge. Why is this? Because the Way essentially requires only that one be able to know it, and stops there. When the Way is embodied by people, one need not practice it with natural ease before one can speak of practicing it. Whether it comes through pursuing advantage or comes through strenuous effort, although each seems to have its own distinct way of practicing, when we observe them after the achievement is made, there are not two kinds of practice. Why is this? Because the Way essentially requires only that one be able to practice it, and stops there. Now, in knowing, one may observe wisdom; in practicing, one may observe humaneness; and in the oneness of knowing and humaneness, one may observe courage. For those who have not yet been able to reach that oneness, by what means can they draw near to it? In the world …

title: 萬曆十年廣東鄉試錄
text:
下不皆生知知未易幾也惟學而好焉勵一求
通之心則何蔽不可袪而知近矣天下不皆安
行仁未易幾也惟行而力焉持一邁往之心則
何私不可克而仁近矣天下不皆知盡仁至之
人勇未易幾也惟知恥焉存一愧悟之心則何
懦不可起知與成功之一而勇近矣是蓋道隨
人而可行二之卽非道德隨人而可入遠之卽
非德知所求焉卽由近而一何難哉雖然近之
易一之難也故虞庭之傳心曰一夫子之貫道
===
曰一是一者聖學也帝治也此夫子本之行道
之一推之九經之一正欲舉其君於堯舜文武
耳若曰卑之無甚高論豈識聖人告君之心哉
稷思天下有饑者由己饑之也
吳正偉
同考試官訓導楊批聖人憂民饑處正在不
能人人敎稼穡上此作描寫精神入微矣
同考試官敎諭姜批格高詞偉鏗然乎希世
之音也可以式矣
punctuated:
下不皆生知，知未易幾也。惟學而好焉，勵一求通之心，則何蔽不可袪，而知近矣。天下不皆安行，仁未易幾也。惟行而力焉，持一邁往之心，則何私不可克，而仁近矣。天下不皆知盡仁至之人，勇未易幾也。惟知恥焉，存一愧悟之心，則何懦不可起，知與成功之一，而勇近矣。是蓋道隨人而可行，二之卽非道；德隨人而可入，遠之卽非德。知所求焉，卽由近而一，何難哉！雖然，近之易，一之難也。故虞庭之傳心曰「一」，夫子之貫道曰「一」。是「一」者，聖學也，帝治也。此夫子本之行道之一，推之九經之一，正欲舉其君於堯、舜、文、武耳。若曰卑之無甚高論，豈識聖人告君之心哉！

稷思天下有饑者，由己饑之也。
吳正偉
同考試官訓導楊批：聖人憂民饑處，正在不能人人敎稼穡上。此作描寫精神，入微矣。
同考試官敎諭姜批：格高詞偉，鏗然乎希世之音也，可以式矣。
translation_en:
… under heaven are not all born with knowledge, so wisdom is not easily attained. Only by learning and loving it, rousing a heart that seeks thorough comprehension, what obscurity cannot be dispelled? Then one is close to wisdom. People under heaven do not all practice with effortless ease, so humanity is not easily attained. Only by practicing and exerting oneself in it, maintaining a heart that presses boldly forward, what selfishness cannot be overcome? Then one is close to humanity. People under heaven are not all persons of exhaustive wisdom and utmost humanity, so courage is not easily attained. Only by knowing shame, preserving a heart of remorseful awakening, what cowardice cannot be roused to reach the oneness of knowledge and successful achievement? Then one is close to courage. This is because the Way can be practiced according to the person—to divide it in two is not the Way; virtue can be entered according to the person—to keep it at a distance is not virtue. If one knows what to seek, then proceeding from being close to reaching oneness, what difficulty is there? Even so, coming close to it is easy, whereas achieving oneness is difficult. Therefore, the transmission of the mind in the court of Yu [Shun] was called "oneness," and the Master's thread running through his Way was called "oneness." This "oneness" is the learning of the sages and the governance of the emperors. Here the Master rooted it in the oneness of practicing the Way and extended it to the oneness of the Nine Standard Rules, precisely wishing to elevate his ruler to the level of Yao, Shun, King Wen, and King Wu. If one were to say that he lowered his discourse to offer nothing very lofty, how would that be to understand the sage's heart in counseling his ruler?

"Ji thought that if anyone in the world was starving, it was as if he himself had caused them to starve."

Wu Zhengwei 吳正偉

Comment by Associate Examiner Assistant Instructor Yang 楊: The point where the sage worries about the people starving lies precisely in his inability to teach everyone sowing and reaping in person. This essay depicts the spirit with subtle penetration.

Comment by Associate Examiner Instructor Jiang 姜: Elevated in structure and grand in diction, it rings with the resonant sound of a rare treasure in the world; it can serve as a model.

title: 萬曆十年廣東鄉試錄
text:
考試官教諭胡批〔發意明盡詞更悠然〕
考試官教諭陳批〔思深語到〕
聖臣念當世之饑而任失養之責焉夫稷以養
民爲職者也失養而饑責將誰諉此稷之所以
深思與孟子發禹稷救民之意如此且夫任天
下之職者當先天下之憂禹職在治水固思溺
由巳矣而稷則何思哉蓋舜嘗憂民之饑而以
播時百穀屬之於稷稷巳承舜之命而以粒我
烝民引之於躬官以稷名固天下之所賴以爲
===
養者乃其心俯仰以思九州如此其廣吾之疆
理焉得在在而履之苟吾之疆理一有未至九
州之內得無有枵焉而待食者乎此枵焉而待
食者不可歸之於天也職我之故耳世有稷在
固天下之所恃以無饑者乃其心蚤夜以思百
姓如此其衆吾之稼穡焉得人人而教之苟吾
之稼穡一有未周百姓之中得無有闕焉而望
歲者乎此闕焉而望歲者不可咎之於人也時
予之辜耳不以帝命率育爲巳有相之功猶以
punctuated:
考試官教諭胡批：〔發意明盡，詞更悠然。〕
考試官教諭陳批：〔思深語到。〕
聖臣念當世之饑，而任失養之責焉。夫稷以養民爲職者也，失養而饑，責將誰諉？此稷之所以深思與！孟子發禹、稷救民之意如此。且夫任天下之職者，當先天下之憂。禹職在治水，固思溺由巳矣；而稷則何思哉？蓋舜嘗憂民之饑，而以播時百穀屬之於稷；稷巳承舜之命，而以粒我烝民引之於躬。官以「稷」名，固天下之所賴以爲養者。乃其心俯仰以思：「九州如此其廣，吾之疆理焉得在在而履之？苟吾之疆理一有未至，九州之內，得無有枵焉而待食者乎？此枵焉而待食者，不可歸之於天也，職我之故耳。」世有稷在，固天下之所恃以無饑者。乃其心蚤夜以思：「百姓如此其衆，吾之稼穡焉得人人而教之？苟吾之稼穡一有未周，百姓之中，得無有闕焉而望歲者乎？此闕焉而望歲者，不可咎之於人也，時予之辜耳。」不以「帝命率育」爲巳有相之功，猶以
translation_en:
Examiner and Instructor Hu's comment: [The exposition of the meaning is clear and exhaustive, and the phrasing is even more unhurried and graceful.]
Examiner and Instructor Chen's comment: [The thought is profound and the language hits the mark.]
The sagely minister was mindful of the hunger of his age and took upon himself the responsibility for failing to nourish the people. Now, Hou Ji held the office of nourishing the people; if they lacked nourishment and went hungry, upon whom could the blame be shifted? Was this not why Hou Ji thought so deeply! Mencius thus brought forth the intention of Yu and Hou Ji in rescuing the people. Moreover, one who bears an office for the whole world ought to put the worries of the world first. Yu's office lay in controlling the waters, so he naturally thought of any drowning as being caused by himself; what, then, did Hou Ji think? Indeed, Shun had once worried about the people's hunger and entrusted to Hou Ji the seasonal sowing of the hundred grains; Hou Ji, having received Shun's command, took upon his own person the task of providing grain food for the multitude of the people. Since his office was named "Millet" (Ji), he was truly the one upon whom the whole world relied for nourishment. Yet in his heart, looking up and down, he reflected: "The Nine Provinces are so vast—how can my surveying and dividing of the land reach every single place in person? If my surveying and dividing of the land fails to reach even a single spot, within the Nine Provinces might there not be those who are hollow-bellied, waiting to be fed? That there are those hollow-bellied and waiting to be fed cannot be blamed on Heaven; it is simply on account of my office." With Hou Ji present in the world, he was truly the one upon whom the world depended so as not to go hungry. Yet in his heart, morning and night, he reflected: "The common people are so numerous—how can I teach agriculture to every single person? If my teaching of agriculture is anything less than comprehensive, among the common people might there not be those who are destitute, longing for a good harvest? That there are those destitute and longing for a good harvest cannot be blamed on other men; this is simply my own transgression." Not taking the "receiving of the Sovereign's mandate to nourish all" as a mérito of assistance already achieved, he still regarded…

title: 萬曆十年廣東鄉試錄
text:
庶奏艱食爲已未盡之責惟其思之也深故其
救之也急此稷之所以勤其官而爲天下烈與
大抵三代而上君爲民立命三代而下民莫能
自必其命爲民立命者視民饑由已民莫必其
命者以爲饑於我何與焉安有玉食萬方而恕
然若是者即能加意窮民又或不罪已而罪歲
嗟乎任人如舜任事如稷則阻饑之民可轉而
爲厚生之民夫歲固君人者自爲之也
易
===
彖曰萃聚也順以說剛中而應故聚也
嚴旗先
同考試官教諭鄒批發明上下萃道詞不費
而義自盡
考試官教諭胡批典確可誦
考試官教諭陳批精當
彖傳釋萃之名義以上下之一心也夫情以一
而聚也卦之德體上下通爲一矣此其所以萃
與彖傳曰人君以一人之身能使天下翕然從
punctuated:
庶奏艱食爲已未盡之責。惟其思之也深，故其救之也急，此稷之所以勤其官而爲天下烈與！大抵三代而上，君爲民立命；三代而下，民莫能自必其命。爲民立命者，視民饑由已；民莫必其命者，以爲饑於我何與焉？安有玉食萬方而恕然若是者？即能加意窮民，又或不罪已而罪歲。嗟乎！任人如舜，任事如稷，則阻饑之民可轉而爲厚生之民。夫歲固君人者自爲之也。

易

彖曰：「萃，聚也。順以說，剛中而應，故聚也。」
嚴旗先
同考試官教諭鄒批：發明上下萃道，詞不費而義自盡。
考試官教諭胡批：典確可誦。
考試官教諭陳批：精當。

《彖傳》釋《萃》之名義，以上下之一心也。夫情以一而聚也，卦之德體上下通爲一矣，此其所以萃與！《彖傳》曰，人君以一人之身，能使天下翕然從
translation_en:
… feeding the multitude with hard-won food as his own unfulfilled responsibility. Only because he pondered it deeply did he rescue them urgently; is this not why Hou Ji was diligent in his office and achieved illustrious merit throughout the realm! Generally speaking, during the Three Dynasties and earlier, rulers established the livelihood of the people; after the Three Dynasties, the people could no longer be certain of their own livelihood. Those who established the livelihood of the people regarded the people's hunger as their own doing; whereas under those where the people cannot be certain of their livelihood, rulers think, "What does their hunger have to do with me?" How can one enjoy the fine delicacies of the myriad regions and yet be so callously indifferent [reading 恕 as 恝]? Even if they manage to pay some attention to the destitute, they still may blame the harvest rather than themselves. Alas! If one employs men as Shun did and takes on tasks as Hou Ji did, then people suffering from hunger can be transformed into people with abundant livelihoods. Indeed, a good harvest is something that the ruler of men brings about himself.

The Book of Changes (Yi)

The Commentary on the Judgments (Tuan) says: "'Cui' (Gathering Together) means gathering. Compliant and joyous, firm in the center and responding, therefore they gather together."
By Yan Qixian.
Associate Examiner Instructor Zou comments: It elucidates the way of gathering together between superior and inferior; the words are not wasteful, yet the meaning is fully expressed.
Examiner Instructor Hu comments: Classical, precise, and worthy of recitation.
Examiner Instructor Chen comments: Essential and fitting.

The Commentary on the Judgments explains the name and meaning of the hexagram Cui (Gathering Together) in terms of the unity of mind between superior and inferior. Now, sentiments gather together through unity; in the virtues and structure of this hexagram, superior and inferior are thoroughly united as one—is this not why they gather together! When the Commentary on the Judgments speaks of this, it means that the ruler of men, in his single person, is able to cause the whole realm to harmoniously follow…

title: 萬曆十年廣東鄉試錄
text:
之而不忍離者無他焉有以一其心故也茲卦
之名曰萃則是天下有分土而無分民人心可
使聚而不可使散乃四海一家之時也於卦何
取哉蓋卦之德坤順兌說是順以從君者民也
而說道之使君實有以先之斯時也父母赤子
何其休戚之相關也卦之體剛中而應是誠實
下交者君也而虛中之誼臣又有以結之斯時
也元首股肱何其喜起之交協也上焉者聯屬
乎下則由朝廷而邦國而四方黎獻熙熙然其
===
若一人下焉者聯屬於上則由公卿而有司而
羣黎百姓藹藹然其若一心蓋方其未合也遠
而疎疎而渙即一堂之上已不相屬而況于民
及其既合也羣而聚聚而親即萬里之遠可以
相通而況于近吾於是而知萃在天下而所以
使之萃者君也通于此而可以識萃之名義矣
雖然萃固難而保萃尤難夫人之一身四肢百
骸融而為一苟精神元氣一日不貫即索然離
矣是故為人君者運其精神以馭羣工培其元
punctuated: 之而不忍離者，無他焉，有以一其心故也。茲卦之名曰「萃」，則是天下有分土而無分民，人心可使聚而不可使散，乃四海一家之時也，於卦何取哉？蓋卦之德，坤順兌說，是順以從君者民也，而說道之使，君實有以先之。斯時也，父母赤子，何其休戚之相關也！卦之體，剛中而應，是誠實下交者君也，而虛中之誼，臣又有以結之。斯時也，元首股肱，何其喜起之交協也！上焉者聯屬乎下，則由朝廷而邦國、而四方黎獻，熙熙然其若一人；下焉者聯屬於上，則由公卿而有司、而羣黎百姓，藹藹然其若一心。蓋方其未合也，遠而疎，疎而渙，即一堂之上已不相屬，而況于民？及其既合也，羣而聚，聚而親，即萬里之遠可以相通，而況于近？吾於是而知萃在天下，而所以使之萃者，君也。通于此，而可以識萃之名義矣。雖然，萃固難，而保萃尤難。夫人之一身，四肢百骸融而為一，苟精神元氣一日不貫，即索然離矣。是故為人君者，運其精神以馭羣工，培其元…
translation_en: …him and cannot bear to part is for no other reason than that he has the means to unite their hearts. Now, that this hexagram is named Cui [Gathering Together] means that while all under Heaven has divided territories, it has no divided people; human hearts can be made to gather and cannot be made to scatter—it is truly a time when the four seas are one family. What is drawn from the hexagram to show this? In the virtues of the hexagram, Kun is compliant and Dui is joyous: those who compliantly follow the ruler are the people, while in employing the way of joy, the ruler truly initiates it first. At such a time, like parents and newborn babes, how closely bound are their joys and sorrows! In the structure of the hexagram, the firm is central and finds response: the one who sincerely associates with those below is the ruler, while with open-hearted rectitude, the ministers in turn bind themselves to him. At such a time, like the head and the limbs, how harmonious is their joyful and vigorous cooperation! When those above are joined to those below, then from the royal court to the feudal states and the worthy commoners of the four quarters, all are harmoniously like a single person; when those below are joined to those above, then from the grandees and ministers to the officials in charge and the multitude of the common people, all are amicably of a single heart. For when they are not yet united, distance leads to estrangement, and estrangement leads to dispersion—even within a single hall they are already unconnected to one another, how much more so with the people? Yet once they are united, coming together in groups leads to gathering, and gathering leads to intimacy—even across a distance of ten thousand li they can communicate with one another, how much more so with those nearby? From this I know that while gathering together takes place throughout the realm, the one who causes them to gather together is the ruler. By comprehending this, one can understand the meaning of the name Cui. Even so, gathering together is certainly difficult, and preserving that gathering is harder still. In a person's body, the four limbs and hundred bones are fused into one; yet if the spirit and vital energy fail to course through them for a single day, they immediately fall apart in exhaustion. Therefore, for one who is a ruler of men, exercising his spirit to direct the body of officials, and cultivating his vital…

title: 萬曆十年廣東鄉試錄
text:
氣以厚黎民者保萃之道也
神也者妙萬物而爲言者也動萬物者莫
