莫熯乎火說萬物者莫說乎澤潤萬物
者莫潤乎水終萬物始萬物者莫盛乎
艮故水火相逮雷風不相悖山澤通氣
然後能變化旣成萬物也
鄺行可
同考試官敎諭鄒批格高意渾而變化轉換處絶無痕迹佳作也
===
考試官敎諭胡批是大家機軸錄之
考試官敎諭陳批思致筆力不凡
造物之妙神化相須者也夫一故神兩故化也
兩不可見而一神之用不幾於息哉大傳合先
後天而發之也若曰至矣造化之功其極天下
之至神者乎以爲倚於物也而未始滯於有以
爲離於物也而未始淪於無蓋妙萬物而爲言
者也何也天下之物成於造化而造物之功成
punctuated:
氣以厚黎民者，保萃之道也。
神也者，妙萬物而爲言者也。動萬物者莫疾乎雷，撓萬物者莫疾乎風，燥萬物者莫熯乎火，說萬物者莫說乎澤，潤萬物者莫潤乎水，終萬物始萬物者莫盛乎艮。故水火相逮，雷風不相悖，山澤通氣，然後能變化，旣成萬物也。
鄺行可
同考試官敎諭鄒批：格高意渾，而變化轉換處絶無痕迹，佳作也。
考試官敎諭胡批：是大家機軸，錄之。
考試官敎諭陳批：思致筆力不凡。
造物之妙，神化相須者也。夫一故神，兩故化也。兩不可見，而一神之用不幾於息哉？《大傳》合先後天而發之也，若曰：至矣造化之功，其極天下之至神者乎！以爲倚於物也，而未始滯於有；以爲離於物也，而未始淪於無。蓋妙萬物而爲言者也。何也？天下之物成於造化，而造物之功成
translation_en:
… vital energy to enrich the common people—this is the way to preserve gathering together (Cui).

"Spirit (shen) is a term for the wondrous working within the myriad things. For stirring the myriad things, nothing is swifter than thunder; for bending the myriad things, nothing is swifter than wind; for parching the myriad things, nothing is more scorching than fire; for gladdening the myriad things, nothing is more gladdening than the marsh; for moistening the myriad things, nothing is more moistening than water; for bringing the myriad things to an end and giving the myriad things a new beginning, nothing is more flourishing than Gen (Mountain). Thus water and fire complement each other, thunder and wind do not conflict with each other, and mountain and marsh interchange their vital breaths; only then can there be transformation and change, bringing all the myriad things to completion."

Kuang Xingke 鄺行可

Associate Examiner, Instructor (jiaoyu) Zou comments: The structure is lofty and the conception profound, while the transitions and turns leave no trace of artifice—a fine piece.
Examiner, Instructor Hu comments: This has the framework of a great master; record it.
Examiner, Instructor Chen comments: Extraordinary in both thought and brushwork.

The wondrousness of the Creator lies in the mutual dependence of spirit (shen) and transformation (hua). Now, because it is One, it is spirit; because it is Two, it is transformation. If the Two could not be seen, would not the operation of the One spirit nearly cease? The Great Commentary (Dazhuan) combines the Earlier Heaven (xiantian) and Later Heaven (houtian) sequences to elucidate this, as if to say: Supreme indeed is the achievement of creation and transformation—does it not reach the utmost spirit in all under Heaven? If one takes it as relying upon things, yet it has never been mired in being; if one takes it as separate from things, yet it has never sunk into non-being. Indeed, it is a term for the wondrous working within the myriad things. Why is this so? The things of the world are brought to completion through creation and transformation, and the achievement of the Creator is brought to completion…

title: 萬曆十年廣東鄉試錄
text:
於六子雷吾知其動物風吾知其撓物顧其所
以動且撓者雷風不與也神也火吾知其燥物
澤吾知其說物顧其所以燥且說者火澤不與
也神也水吾知其潤物艮吾知其終始物顧其
所以潤所以終始者坎艮不與也神也生成各
專其一而存主莫測其用所謂神妙萬物者非
耶然是六子之變化也豈自爲之運哉而物之
成也豈自爲之成哉吾觀於先天之卦水火則
相逮矣雷風則不相悖矣山澤則通氣矣而分
===
陰分陽者藏其宅夫是以變化之餘物得其潤
且燥焉物得其動且撓焉物得其說且成焉而
根陰根陽者神其功是變非他也陰之合於陽
而後變也化非他也陽之合於陰而後化也成
非他也陰陽之相須而成也故觀先天後天之
卦而神化合體用備矣大抵神統乎形神主其
逸而形任其勞者動靜之分也後天聖人退二
老于不用而生剋嗣續各因其時無非所以尊
神道耳噫造化之神常得於靜人心之神常失
punctuated: 於六子。雷，吾知其動物；風，吾知其撓物；顧其所以動且撓者，雷風不與也，神也。火，吾知其燥物；澤，吾知其說物；顧其所以燥且說者，火澤不與也，神也。水，吾知其潤物；艮，吾知其終始物；顧其所以潤、所以終始者，坎艮不與也，神也。生成各專其一，而存主莫測其用，所謂「神妙萬物」者非耶？然是六子之變化也，豈自爲之運哉？而物之成也，豈自爲之成哉？吾觀於先天之卦，水火則相逮矣，雷風則不相悖矣，山澤則通氣矣，而分陰分陽者藏其宅。夫是以變化之餘，物得其潤且燥焉，物得其動且撓焉，物得其說且成焉，而根陰根陽者神其功。是變非他也，陰之合於陽而後變也；化非他也，陽之合於陰而後化也；成非他也，陰陽之相須而成也。故觀先天、後天之卦，而神化合、體用備矣。大抵神統乎形，神主其逸而形任其勞者，動靜之分也。後天聖人退二老于不用，而生剋嗣續，各因其時，無非所以尊神道耳。噫！造化之神常得於靜，人心之神常失
translation_en:
…through the six offspring [trigrams]. As for thunder, I know that it stirs things; as for wind, I know that it bends things; yet as for that whereby they stir and bend them, thunder and wind have no part in it—it is Spirit. As for fire, I know that it dries things; as for the marsh, I know that it gladdens things; yet as for that whereby they dry and gladden them, fire and marsh have no part in it—it is Spirit. As for water, I know that it moistens things; as for Gen [Mountain], I know that it brings things to an end and a beginning; yet as for that whereby they moisten and bring about ending and beginning, Kan [Water] and Gen have no part in it—it is Spirit. In generating and completing, each is dedicated to a single function, while the abiding master is unfathomable in its operation—is this not what is meant by "Spirit wondrously working through the myriad things"?

Yet as for the changes and transformations of these six offspring, how could they revolve of their own accord? And as for the completion of things, how could they reach completion of their own accord? When I observe the trigrams of the Prior-to-Heaven [Fuxi] arrangement: water and fire complement each other, thunder and wind do not clash with each other, mountain and marsh communicate their vital breaths, while those that divide yin and divide yang [Qian and Kun] conceal themselves in their abodes. Therefore, in the wake of change and transformation, things obtain their moistening and drying, things obtain their stirring and bending, things obtain their gladdening and completion, while that which is rooted in yin and rooted in yang makes wondrous its achievement. Thus, change is nothing other than yin uniting with yang and thereafter changing; transformation is nothing other than yang uniting with yin and thereafter transforming; completion is nothing other than yin and yang depending on each other to reach completion. Therefore, when one observes the trigrams of the Prior-to-Heaven and Posterior-to-Heaven [King Wen] arrangements, Spirit and transformation are united, and substance and function are complete.

In general, Spirit governs form; that Spirit presides over ease while form bears the toil is the distinction between movement and stillness. In the Posterior-to-Heaven arrangement, the Sage retired the two parents [Qian and Kun] from active use, while generation, overcoming, succession, and continuation each followed its season—all of which was simply the means to honor the Way of Spirit. Alas! The Spirit of creation and transformation is always attained in stillness, whereas the spirit of the human mind is always lost…

title: 萬曆十年廣東鄉試錄
text:
於動柰之何其不思
書
后非民罔使民非后罔事無自廣以狹人
匹夫匹婦不獲自盡民主罔與成厥功
余鏜
同考試官訓導楊批詞理俱精而說無自廣
狹人處更有關係可錄
同考試官教諭姜批就題發揮無一字不精
到
===
考試官教諭胡批構詞命意迥異衆作
考試官教諭陳批得伊尹告君之意
大臣論君民相須而欲取善廣其量焉夫人君
合天下以成其善也知君民之相須而取善可
有遺乎且人君非一人之身也聖德非一善之
積也盍觀君民之際乎彼君使人者也非民則
孰與奉一人之役是君不可無民也民事人者
也非君則孰與統萬姓之心是民不可無君也
故庶民之論議雖微而有可採一己之聰明雖
punctuated:
於動，柰之何其不思？

《書》

「后非民罔使，民非后罔事。無自廣以狹人，匹夫匹婦不獲自盡，民主罔與成厥功。」

余鏜

同考試官訓導楊批：詞理俱精，而說「無自廣狹人」處更有關係，可錄。
同考試官教諭姜批：就題發揮，無一字不精到。
考試官教諭胡批：構詞命意，迥異衆作。
考試官教諭陳批：得伊尹告君之意。

大臣論君民相須，而欲取善廣其量焉。夫人君合天下以成其善也，知君民之相須，而取善可有遺乎？且人君非一人之身也，聖德非一善之積也，盍觀君民之際乎？彼君，使人者也，非民則孰與奉一人之役？是君不可無民也。民，事人者也，非君則孰與統萬姓之心？是民不可無君也。故庶民之論議雖微而有可採，一己之聰明雖
translation_en:
… in movement; how can one fail to reflect on this?

Classic of Documents (Shu)

"The sovereign without the people has none whom he can employ; the people without the sovereign have none whom they can serve. Do not think yourself so large as to deem others small. If ordinary men and women do not find the opportunity to give full development to their ability, the people's lord will be without those to help him complete his merit."

Yu Tang 余鏜

Associate Examiner and Assistant Instructor Yang 楊 comments: Both the diction and the reasoning are refined, and the exposition of the passage "do not think yourself so large as to deem others small" is especially significant; worthy of selection for the record.
Associate Examiner and Instructor Jiang 姜 comments: Expounding closely upon the theme, there is not a single word that fails to hit the mark with precision.
Examiner and Instructor Hu 胡 comments: In phrasing and conception, it stands far apart from the crowd of essays.
Examiner and Instructor Chen 陳 comments: It grasps the true intent of Yi Yin's 伊尹 counsel to his sovereign.

The great minister discusses the mutual dependence of sovereign and people, desiring that in adopting what is good the ruler should broaden his capacity. Now, the ruler of men brings together the whole realm in order to perfect his goodness; once he understands the mutual dependence of sovereign and people, how can anything be overlooked in adopting the good? Moreover, the ruler of men does not exist as a single isolated individual, nor is sage virtue the accumulation of a single good deed; why not observe the relationship between sovereign and people? The sovereign is one who employs others: without the people, who would perform service for the One Man? Thus the sovereign cannot do without the people. The people are those who serve others: without the sovereign, who would unite the hearts of the myriad surnames? Thus the people cannot do without the sovereign. Therefore, although the discussions of the common people are humble, there is much in them worth adopting; and although the intelligence of one's own person is…

title: 萬曆十年廣東鄉試錄
text:
高而不可恃寧以聖人而擇芻蕘之言也毋自
廣其能而狹人之能也寧以天子而納閭閻之
慮也毋自廣其善而狹人之善也何也生一自
廣之心則何德非巳存一狹人之念則何人有
德忠智之謨且阻于千里之外矣夫婦之愚安
能自效乎師保之訓且塞于九陛之下矣夫婦
之賤安能自達乎雖匹夫匹婦之善未必裨于
天子之聖明而一言一善之遺終有虧於聖人
之光大何自而成厥功耶信乎聖德無可滿之
===
量而庶官左右之外尤有不盡之師也人君可
不合天下以成其善哉嗟乎人君之最患莫大
乎有巳彼天之所大奉左右所從臾巍然自視
不勝其廣舉天下莫與比智而較能夫惟心虛
則萬善皆入而可以併包天下故堯稱大哉以
其能舍巳也此一德之本也
太史司寇蘇公式敬爾由獄以長我王國
茲式有慎以列用中罰
黃仕鳳
punctuated:
高而不可恃。寧以聖人而擇芻蕘之言也，毋自廣其能而狹人之能也；寧以天子而納閭閻之慮也，毋自廣其善而狹人之善也。何也？生一自廣之心，則何德非巳？存一狹人之念，則何人有德？忠智之謨，且阻于千里之外矣，夫婦之愚，安能自效乎？師保之訓，且塞于九陛之下矣，夫婦之賤，安能自達乎？雖匹夫匹婦之善，未必裨于天子之聖明，而一言一善之遺，終有虧於聖人之光大，何自而成厥功耶？信乎聖德無可滿之量，而庶官左右之外，尤有不盡之師也。人君可不合天下以成其善哉？嗟乎！人君之最患，莫大乎有巳。彼天之所大奉，左右所從臾，巍然自視，不勝其廣，舉天下莫與比智而較能。夫惟心虛則萬善皆入，而可以併包天下。故堯稱「大哉」，以其能舍巳也。此一德之本也。
太史、司寇蘇公式敬爾由獄，以長我王國。茲式有慎，以列用中罰。
黃仕鳳
translation_en:
… lofty, it cannot be relied upon. Better that as a sage he select from the words of grass-cutters and firewood-gatherers, rather than magnify his own abilities and belittle the abilities of others; better that as the Son of Heaven he accept the deliberations of the common alleys, rather than magnify his own goodness and belittle the goodness of others. Why is this? If he gives rise to a single thought of magnifying himself, then what virtue will he not claim as his own? If he harbors a single thought of belittling others, then whom will he regard as possessing virtue? The counsels of the loyal and wise will then be blocked a thousand li away—how then could ignorant men and women offer their service? The instructions of Grand Tutors and Grand Guardians will then be obstructed beneath the nine steps of the throne—how then could lowly men and women make themselves heard? Although the goodness of ordinary men and women may not necessarily add to the sagely intelligence of the Son of Heaven, the omission of a single word or a single good deed ultimately detracts from the glorious greatness of a sage. How then could he bring his achievements to completion? Truly, sagely virtue has a capacity that can never be filled to brimming, and beyond the various officials and close attendants, there are still inexhaustible teachers! How could a ruler not unite the entire realm to bring his goodness to perfection? Alas! The greatest affliction of a ruler is none greater than self-absorption. Greatly exalted by Heaven and urged on by his attendants, he regards himself as toweringly lofty and boundlessly broad, such that in the entire realm none can compare with his wisdom or contend with his ability. Yet only when the mind is humble and open can myriad virtues enter in, enabling him to encompass the entire realm. Thus Yao 堯 was praised as "great indeed!" because he was able to set aside his own ego. This is the foundation of pure and unitary virtue.

"The Grand Scribe! The Minister of Crime, Duke Su 蘇公, respectfully handled the criminal cases that passed through him, thereby perpetuating our royal state. Taking him as a model of caution, arrange and apply the just punishments."

By Huang Shifeng 黃仕鳳.

title: 萬曆十年廣東鄉試錄
text:
同考試官訓導楊批詞旨精透發周公倦倦
慎獄之意盎然當是作者
同考試官敎諭姜批發意明悉措語鏗鏘是
邃於經學者
考試官敎諭胡批朗然可誦
考試官敎諭陳批有藻思
大臣告太史欲以祥刑而垂憲焉蓋祥刑垂憲
萬世也蘇公以之太史可無書乎周公若曰刑
之所係大矣用之得人則以刑壽國用之匪人
===
則以刑病國爾太史其知哲人之刑乎彼司寇
蘇公之掌邦禁也一輕一重悉裁之於敬惕乎
天命之嚴一取一舍悉歸之於敬凜乎民情之
畏式敬爾由獄焉敬至則刑不濫而四海之大
命以立社稷有道之長若或延之也刑清則世
自泰而一代之元氣以培國家不拔之基若或
固之也用罰至是無乎不慎無乎不中而可爲
後世式矣爾其書之史焉俾嗣公而興者心公
之心典公之獄者法公之法輕之不可重之不
banxin: 山東鄕試錄 三十三
punctuated:
同考試官訓導楊批：詞旨精透，發周公倦倦慎獄之意盎然，當是作者。
同考試官敎諭姜批：發意明悉，措語鏗鏘，是邃於經學者。
考試官敎諭胡批：朗然可誦。
考試官敎諭陳批：有藻思。
大臣告太史，欲以祥刑而垂憲焉。蓋祥刑，垂憲萬世也。蘇公以之，太史可無書乎？周公若曰：刑之所係大矣！用之得人，則以刑壽國；用之匪人，則以刑病國。爾太史其知哲人之刑乎？彼司寇蘇公之掌邦禁也，一輕一重，悉裁之於敬，惕乎天命之嚴；一取一舍，悉歸之於敬，凜乎民情之畏，「式敬爾由獄」焉。敬至則刑不濫，而四海之大命以立，社稷有道之長，若或延之也；刑清則世自泰，而一代之元氣以培，國家不拔之基，若或固之也。用罰至是，無乎不慎，無乎不中，而可爲後世式矣。爾其書之史焉，俾嗣公而興者，心公之心；典公之獄者，法公之法。輕之不可，重之不
translation_en:
Associate Examiner and Assistant Instructor Yang comments: The diction and purport are refined and penetrating. It brings forth the Duke of Zhou's earnest intent to be cautious in judicial cases with rich abundance; this is truly the work of an accomplished writer.
Associate Examiner and Instructor Jiang comments: The expression of ideas is clear and thorough, and the phrasing is sonorous and forceful; this is someone well-versed in classical learning.
Examiner and Instructor Hu comments: Clear and bright, worthy of recitation.
Examiner and Instructor Chen comments: Possesses refined literary thought.
The great minister addresses the Grand Scribe, wishing to hand down a model through auspicious punishments. Indeed, auspicious punishments hand down a model for ten thousand generations. Duke Su practiced this—how could the Grand Scribe not record it? It is as if the Duke of Zhou said: What depends upon punishments is great indeed! When their application is entrusted to the right person, punishments prolong the life of the state; when entrusted to the wrong person, punishments harm the state. Do you, Grand Scribe, understand the punishments of a wise man? When the Minister of Justice, Duke Su, was in charge of the state's prohibitions, every lenient or severe measure was decided entirely out of reverence, standing in awe of the strictness of the Mandate of Heaven; every acceptance or rejection was grounded entirely in reverence, trembling before the dreadfulness of the people's sentiments—thus "reverently attending to the judicial cases you handle." When reverence reaches its utmost, punishments are not excessive, whereby the great mandate of the Four Seas is established, and the enduring longevity of the altars of soil and grain, governed by the Way, seems as though prolonged by it; when punishments are pure, the world is naturally at peace, whereby the vital energy of the age is nourished, and the unshakable foundation of the state seems as though consolidated by it. When the application of penalties reaches this point, there is nothing in which it is not cautious, nothing in which it does not hit the mean, and it can serve as a model for later generations. You should record this in the histories, so that those who rise up to succeed the Duke will take the Duke's mind as their own mind, and those who take charge of the Duke's judicial cases will take the Duke's laws as their own model. To make them too light is not…

title: 萬曆十年廣東鄉試錄
text:
可而輕重之間有中在也昭乎成憲之如新式
而用之爲天下持平而已矣取之不得舍之不
得而取舍之間有中在也秩然令章之咸具式
而用之爲朝廷執法而已矣敬獄之風異人如
一心而王國之長亦萬年如一日也哉吁用獄
敬則刑罰中紀載公則垂示遠周公旣以誤獄
戒成王而復以敬獄告太史其爲周家之慮深
哉蓋聞虞廷恤刑欽哉是敕夫敬所以制中也
爲民司命敢不敬與穆王荒耄猶曰何敬非刑
===
具嚴天威豈太史之書司寇之式有以啓之然
訓祥刑而列罰鍰何屑屑焉故下式敬而上罔
知體也
詩
菁菁者莪在彼中沚旣見君子我心則喜
黃維貴
同考試官教諭姚批發我心喜處透徹而精采燁如
同考試官教諭高批詞俊調高理明意婉詩
punctuated:
可，而輕重之間有中在也。昭乎成憲之如新，式而用之，爲天下持平而已矣。取之不得，舍之不得，而取舍之間有中在也。秩然令章之咸具，式而用之，爲朝廷執法而已矣。敬獄之風，異人如一心，而王國之長，亦萬年如一日也哉！吁，用獄敬則刑罰中，紀載公則垂示遠。周公旣以誤獄戒成王，而復以敬獄告太史，其爲周家之慮深哉！蓋聞虞廷恤刑，欽哉是敕。夫敬，所以制中也。爲民司命，敢不敬與？穆王荒耄，猶曰：「何敬非刑，具嚴天威。」豈太史之書、司寇之式有以啓之？然訓祥刑而列罰鍰，何屑屑焉！故下式敬而上罔知體也。
詩
菁菁者莪，在彼中沚。旣見君子，我心則喜。
黃維貴

translation_en:
…nor to make them heavy, for between light and heavy there lies the mean. Brightly do the established statutes remain as if new; taking them as their model and applying them, they simply maintain fairness for all under Heaven. One cannot arbitrarily convict, nor can one arbitrarily acquit, for between conviction and acquittal there lies the mean. In orderly fashion the good regulations are all complete; taking them as their model and applying them, they simply uphold the law for the royal court. With this custom of reverent care in judicial cases, different men will be as of one mind, and the longevity of the royal state will endure for ten thousand years as if a single day!

Alas! When judicial cases are handled with reverence, punishments hit the mark; when the historical records are impartial, the lessons handed down reach far. After the Duke of Zhou had admonished King Cheng against miscarriages of justice, he further instructed the Grand Scribe on reverent care in judicial cases—how deep was his concern for the House of Zhou! Indeed, one hears that at the court of Yu, in showing compassion in punishments, the charge was "Be reverent!" For reverence is that by which the mean is determined. As those who hold charge of the people's lives, how could one dare not be reverent? Even when King Mu was in his senile dotage, he still said: "What should you reverence if not punishments? Fully stand in awe of Heaven's majesty." Could it be that the writings of the Grand Scribe and the model of the Minister of Crime had inspired him? Yet in giving instruction on auspicious punishments while enumerating redemption fines in metal, how petty and trifling that was! Thus those below took reverence as their model, while those above knew not the fundamental principle.

Classic of Poetry (Shi)

義上乗也
考試官敎諭胡批以有儀來形心喜最妙

詩人興已之見賢而誠於喜焉夫喜出于心其
喜也誠矣詩人以之眞能悅賢者哉歌菁莪者
意謂見賢而喜者情也顧儀弗備則簡心弗至
則虛今之樂且有儀豈飾喜哉彼莪之菁菁而
盛也中沚在焉是物且因地而適矣況見君子
而喜也有不由于心乎吾知方其未見也仰而
===
思思而憂吾之精神先與君子相爲流通及今
旣見也遇斯喜喜斯陶吾之意氣自與君子相
爲浹洽喜起形于一堂匪迹也本吾中心好之
者爲社稷慶也慶歸社稷喜出吾心殆舉其素
所蘊結于衷者而盡宣之矣笑語形於九陛匪
文也本吾心乎愛之者爲生民幸也幸在生民
喜自吾心殆舉其素所抑鬱于衷者而盡暢之
矣是蓋鐘鼓載陳喜之聲也玉帛交錯喜之容
也於聲容而樂之其心猶有未慊式燕未舉心

義上乗也。
考試官敎諭胡批：以「有儀」來形「心喜」，最妙。
考試官敎諭陳批：題淡而文有味。
詩人興已之見賢，而誠於喜焉。夫喜出于心，其喜也誠矣。詩人以之，眞能悅賢者哉！歌《菁莪》者意謂：見賢而喜者，情也。顧儀弗備則簡，心弗至則虛。今之樂且有儀，豈飾喜哉？彼莪之菁菁而盛也，中沚在焉，是物且因地而適矣，況見君子而喜也，有不由于心乎？吾知方其未見也，仰而思，思而憂，吾之精神先與君子相爲流通；及今旣見也，遇斯喜，喜斯陶，吾之意氣自與君子相爲浹洽。喜起形于一堂，匪迹也，本吾中心好之者，爲社稷慶也；慶歸社稷，喜出吾心，殆舉其素所蘊結于衷者，而盡宣之矣。笑語形於九陛，匪文也，本吾心乎愛之者，爲生民幸也；幸在生民，喜自吾心，殆舉其素所抑鬱于衷者，而盡暢之矣。是蓋鐘鼓載陳，喜之聲也；玉帛交錯，喜之容也，於聲容而樂之，其心猶有未慊。式燕未舉，心
translation_en:
…essay of the highest caliber.

Examiner and County Director of Studies Hu comments: Using "with deportment" [from the next stanza of the poem] to bring out "my heart is glad" is most ingenious.

Examiner and County Director of Studies Chen comments: The topic is plain, yet the essay has savor.

The poet uses an evocative image to express his own meeting with the worthy and the sincerity of his joy therein. Now, when joy issues from the heart, that joy is sincere indeed. Taking this as his basis, how truly able the poet was to delight in the worthy! The meaning of the one who sang "Lush Tarragon" (*Jing'e*) is this: To feel joy upon seeing a worthy man is a natural sentiment. Yet if ceremonial deportment is not complete, it is negligent; if the heart is not fully present, it is hollow. Today's delight, accompanied as it is by proper deportment—how could it be a mere feigned display of joy?

That tarragon, so lush and flourishing, is there in the midst of the islet; thus even things find contentment according to their place. How much more, then, when seeing the noble man and feeling joy—could that fail to spring from the heart? I know that when I had not yet seen him, I looked up and longed for him, and longing for him I was anxious; my spirit was already in communion with the noble man beforehand. And now that I have seen him, meeting him brings joy, and joy brings elation; my spirit and disposition naturally blend in harmony with the noble man.

Joyous exhilaration takes form in the single hall—this is no mere outward trace; rooted in the fondness of my innermost heart, it is a celebration for the altars of soil and grain. The celebration belongs to the altars of soil and grain, while the joy issues from my own heart, well-nigh taking all that had long been pent up within my breast and giving it complete expression. Laughter and speech take form upon the nine-tiered steps of the throne—this is no mere outward embellishment; rooted in the love within my heart, it is a blessing for the common people. The blessing lies with the common people, while the joy comes from my own heart, well-nigh taking all that had long been stifled within my breast and giving it full vent.

Indeed, the bells and drums set out in array are the sounds of joy; the jades and silks exchanged in ceremony are the demeanor of joy. Yet if one delighted in him only through sounds and demeanor, one's heart would still not be fully satisfied. Before the feast is even held, the heart…

text:

儀始爲不虛吁菁莪詩人眞篤于好賢矣嘗觀
明良感召如宮應而角動由心先之故不介而
親也若儀不及物賢者豈虛拘哉然隰桑亦好
賢也惟欲其心之不謂不忘而是詩播之詠歌
彰之儀物若亟于自見其心何哉蓋隰桑喜見
欲心之藏于已菁莪燕賓欲心之達于人豈好
之有淺深耶
干祿百福子孫千億穆穆皇皇宜君宜王
===
不愆不忘率由舊章
王家相

先和也，幣帛未將，心先獻也。於根心而喜之，其儀始爲不虛。吁！《菁莪》詩人眞篤于好賢矣。嘗觀明良感召，如宮應而角動，由心先之，故不介而親也。若儀不及物，賢者豈虛拘哉？然《隰桑》亦好賢也，惟欲其心之不謂不忘，而是詩播之詠歌，彰之儀物，若亟于自見其心，何哉？蓋《隰桑》喜見，欲心之藏于已；《菁莪》燕賓，欲心之達于人。豈好之有淺深耶？

translation_en:
… is already in harmony; before the silk gifts are presented, the heart has already offered itself. Only when joy is rooted in the heart do the ceremonies become genuine and not empty. Ah! The poet of "Luxuriant Tarragon" (Jing'e) was truly sincere in his love for the worthy! I have observed that the mutual responsiveness between an enlightened ruler and worthy ministers is like the gong note resonating and the jue note vibrating in turn; because the heart takes the lead, they become close without needing an intermediary. If the ceremony does not match the material gifts, how could worthy men be detained by empty forms? Yet the ode "Lowland Mulberry" (Xisang) also expresses love for the worthy, desiring only not to speak of it and never to forget it in the heart; whereas this ode broadcasts it in song and displays it in ceremonial gifts, as if eager to make one's heart seen. Why is this? It is because "Lowland Mulberry" rejoices in seeing the worthy and wishes the feeling to be treasured within oneself, while "Luxuriant Tarragon" feasts the guests and wishes the feeling to be communicated to others. How could there be any difference in depth in their love for the worthy?

"Seeking blessings and a hundredfold good fortune, his sons and grandsons are in the thousands and hundreds of millions. Reverent and august, he is fit to be lord, fit to be king. Neither erring nor forgetting, he follows the old statutes."
Wang Jiaxiang

Comment by Examiner, Instructor Hu: It captures the spirit of offering praise without forgetting admonition.
Comment by Examiner, Instructor Chen: The language is dignified and resplendent.

text:
胤爲福也多而且賢百福孰大于是想其答君
貺若曰天下惟有道之君爲能集昌後之福故
帝王之享有全福每於後嗣徵之也王之福何
如哉吾知顯德在王其干祿也有道百福在天
其申錫也無窮福王之子而子以千億天若爲
宗社而發其祥福王之孫而孫以千億天若爲
邦家而衍其慶然非徒多而已也貞元會合則
賢聖繼出莫不穆穆焉皇皇焉王有世德而子

===

punctuated:

translation_en:
… descendants to be his blessing. When they are both numerous and worthy, which of the hundred blessings could be greater than this? Imagining how they responded to their lord's favors, it is as if they said: In all under Heaven, only a ruler who possesses the Way is able to gather the blessing of flourishing posterity; therefore, an emperor's or king's enjoyment of complete blessings is always verified in his heirs. What are the King's blessings like? We know that illustrious virtue resides in the King, and his pursuit of favor follows the Way; the hundred blessings reside in Heaven, and its repeated bestowals are无穷 (endless). It blesses the King's sons, so that his sons number in the thousands and сотни тысяч (hundreds of millions), as though Heaven were manifesting its auspicious signs for the ancestral temple and the altars of soil and grain; it blesses the King's grandsons, so that his grandsons number in the thousands and hundreds of millions, as though Heaven were extending its felicity for the state and the royal house. Yet it is not merely that they are numerous. When the cosmic cycles of貞 (constancy) and 元 (origin) converge, worthies and sages emerge in succession; none fails to be reverent and august, for the King possesses hereditary virtue and his sons and grandsons all emulate the worthy. When great virtue attains the throne, the sovereigns and kings are sage and enlightened; none fails to befit a ruler…

Comment by Examiner Instructor Chen: Well-ordered and fitting in form.

Moreover, that those who begin well do not necessarily end well has been recorded since antiquity. Yet when there are cases where a ruler of clear insight and a minister of superior talent are nevertheless unable to sustain things to the end, it was not so at the beginning. Just when Chu had not yet been subdued…

translation_en:
…and Duke Huan and Guan Zhong worried about it. They considered that Chu's watching for an opening to make a move was in reality testing our military prestige; and since Jiang and Huang had newly submitted, if we made use of them they would side with Qi, whereas if we did not, they would side with Chu—so good faith with them could not be lost. Therefore, at the meeting at Cheng, Zheng was diligently won over; at the meeting at Yanggu, the campaign against Chu was planned. Triumphing through diplomacy over ritual vessels, his influence spread across the central states and borderlands, and when reinforced by the support of allied states, his prestige was roused within and his good faith was trusted without. Before even a single punitive strike needed to be launched, the lands south of the Zhen and Wei rivers and east of Hanyang had all fallen within Qi's strategic design. Furthermore, they recognized that Chu's sending an envoy to meet the army and ask the reason for the expedition was in reality to observe our rhetoric; and when Qu Wan came to seek terms, they could be won over by virtue, whereas relying on superior numbers would prove difficult—so proper ritual propriety could not be lost. Therefore, when the army halted at Xing, the question of the wrapped three-ribbed rush was posed; when it withdrew to Shaoling, the ceremony of the covenant was completed. Through diplomatic pronouncements and dignified reproof, the spirit of a formidable enemy was broken, and when reinforced by the appeal to the former amity of their ancestors, his words were reasonable…

Examiner Chen, Instructor, comments: Majesitc and well-proportioned.

驕志驕而行肆陳之討遂紛紛矣攷桓仲之初
決策也固曰速得志於天下諸侯夫桓之得志
孰逾召陵者故桓仲之驕溢召陵以前爲之也
punctuated: 而桓、仲憂之，以爲楚之伺釁而動，寔甞我威；而江、黃新服，用則爲齊，不用則楚，其信不可失也。故檉會而鄭勤矣，陽穀會而伐楚謀矣。樽俎折衝，方行華裔，而加之與國之援，其威內振，其信外孚，將無俟撻伐一加，而溱、洧以南，漢陽以東，悉就齊之畫中矣。又以楚之逆師問故，寔觀我詞；而屈完來款，以德則服，以衆則難，其禮不可失也。故陘次而包茅問矣，召陵退而盟禮成矣。文告威讓，氣奪強敵，而加之先好之徵，其訓順，其禮恭，將無俟攻戰爲威，而方城之城，漢水之池，悉安齊之宇下矣。夫以桓、仲之憂楚，而思屈其力也如是，思屈其心也如是，慮其勝而持其勝也又如是，其爲念一何深，而爲禮一何謹也！此無異故焉，方憂之君，不必王德而可與慮危；方憂之臣，不必王佐而可與圖艱也。楚帖而志驕，志驕而行肆，陳之討遂紛紛矣。攷桓、仲之初決策也，固曰速得志於天下諸侯。夫桓之得志，孰逾召陵者？故桓、仲之驕溢，召陵以前爲之也。
translation_en:
… Duke Huan 桓公 and Guan Zhong 管仲 were anxious about it. They considered that Chu's 楚 watching for an opening to make a move was actually testing our military prestige; and since Jiang 江 and Huang 黃 had newly submitted, if we made use of them they would side with Qi 齊, whereas if we did not, they would side with Chu—so good faith with them could not be lost. Therefore, at the meeting at Cheng 檉, Zheng 鄭 was diligently attended to; at the meeting at Yanggu 陽穀, the campaign against Chu was planned. Repelling the enemy over ritual vessels at the diplomatic table was just taking effect among the central states and borderlands, and when backed by the support of allied states, Qi's prestige resonated internally and its good faith inspired confidence externally. Thus, without even waiting to launch a single punitive strike, the regions south of the Zhen 溱 and Wei 洧 rivers and east of Hanyang 漢陽 all fell within Qi's strategic design.

Furthermore, they considered that when Chu met our army to ask the reason for our advance, it was actually observing our rhetoric; and when Qu Wan 屈完 came to seek terms, Chu would submit if treated with virtue, whereas it would be difficult to subdue by sheer numbers—so proper ritual propriety could not be lost. Therefore, while halting at Xing 陘, the question of the wrapped three-ribbed rush (baomao 包茅) was raised; upon withdrawing to Shaoling 召陵, the rites of the covenant were completed. Through solemn declarations and stern reproaches, Qi's spirit overawed a formidable enemy, and when reinforced by appeals to former amity, its instructions were reasonable and its ritual propriety respectful. Thus, without even needing to rely on assault and battle for prestige, the ramparts of Fangcheng 方城 and the moat of the Han River 漢水 all rested peacefully beneath the shelter of Qi.

Indeed, considering how Duke Huan and Guan Zhong worried about Chu: they sought to subdue its strength like this, sought to subdue its heart like this, and planned for victory and maintained that victory like this—how deep was their forethought, and how cautious was their observance of ritual propriety! There is no other reason for this: a ruler who is currently anxious does not need the virtue of a True King to be someone with whom one can take precautions against danger; a minister who is currently anxious does not need to be a kingly counsellor to be someone with whom one can plan for hardships. Yet once Chu was pacified, their minds grew arrogant; once their minds grew arrogant, their actions became unrestrained, and the punitive expeditions against Chen 陳 subsequently fell into disorder. Examining when Duke Huan and Guan Zhong first decided upon their grand strategy, they had indeed said their aim was to quickly fulfill their ambitions among the feudal lords of the realm. Now, among Duke Huan's achievements in fulfilling his ambitions, which of them surpassed Shaoling? Therefore, the arrogance and excess of Duke Huan and Guan Zhong were already in the making even before Shaoling.

title: 萬曆十年廣東鄉試錄
text:
公會晉侯宋公陳侯衛侯鄭伯曹伯莒子
邾子滕子薛伯齊世子光吳人鄫人于
戚〔襄公五年〕
張萃
同考試官訓導鄭批傳中來會就是不爲主
此作發揮有思
考試官敎諭胡批融會二傳成文可誦
考試官敎諭陳批得進吳意
春秋于遠人與好而特進其慕義焉此吳之慕
===
義而聽會於戚異乎夷矣欲無進之得乎□于
戚之會吳以人稱我無所貶而彼爲可會何也
夫自伐郯以還而諸侯俛首於北吳人雄視於
東者逾十餘年而悼也賢伯也通吳以制楚義
舉也彼雖僭號之夷乃其慕我華風也甚堅而
欲從事於會也甚切是故悔淮上之不至而遣
壽越以求通也則曰寡君願徼福于唐叔二文
奉贄幣以見于君惟不虞之不戒以至失時寡
君敢伏其辜感善道之爲期而煩魯衞以告虞
punctuated:
公會晉侯、宋公、陳侯、衛侯、鄭伯、曹伯、莒子、邾子、滕子、薛伯、齊世子光、吳人、鄫人于戚。〔襄公五年〕
張萃
同考試官訓導鄭批：傳中「來會」就是不爲主，此作發揮有思。
考試官敎諭胡批：融會二傳，成文可誦。
考試官敎諭陳批：得進吳意。
《春秋》于遠人與好，而特進其慕義焉。此吳之慕義而聽會於戚，異乎夷矣，欲無進之，得乎？□于戚之會，吳以「人」稱，我無所貶，而彼爲可會，何也？夫自伐郯以還，而諸侯俛首於北，吳人雄視於東者，逾十餘年。而悼也，賢伯也；通吳以制楚，義舉也。彼雖僭號之夷，乃其慕我華風也甚堅，而欲從事於會也甚切。是故悔淮上之不至，而遣壽越以求通也，則曰：「寡君願徼福于唐叔、二文，奉贄幣以見于君，惟不虞之不戒，以至失時，寡君敢伏其辜。」感善道之爲期，而煩魯、衞以告虞
translation_en:
"The Duke met the Marquis of Jin, the Duke of Song, the Marquis of Chen, the Marquis of Wei, the Earl of Zheng, the Earl of Cao, the Viscount of Ju, the Viscount of Zhu, the Viscount of Teng, the Earl of Xue, Heir Apparent Guang of Qi, a man of Wu, and a man of Zeng at Qi." [Fifth year of Duke Xiang]

Zhang Cui 張萃

Associate Examiner and Assistant Instructor Zheng comments: In the commentary, "coming to the meeting" means not acting as the host; this essay develops the point thoughtfully.
Examiner and Instructor Hu comments: It synthesizes the two commentaries into an essay worthy of recitation.
Examiner and Instructor Chen comments: It grasps the intention behind elevating Wu.

When people from afar join in amity, the Spring and Autumn Annals (Chunqiu) specially elevates them for admiring righteousness. Here, Wu's admiring righteousness and complying with the meeting at Qi set it apart from the barbarians; even if one wished not to elevate it, how could that be done? [?] In the meeting at Qi, Wu is referred to as "a man"; we attach no censure to ourselves, and they are treated as worthy of meeting—why is this? Ever since the campaign against Tan, for more than ten years the feudal lords had bowed their heads in the north while the men of Wu looked on ambitiously in the east. Now Duke Dao [of Jin] was a worthy hegemon, and establishing relations with Wu in order to hold Chu in check was a righteous undertaking. Although Wu was a barbarian state that had usurped a royal title, its admiration for the customs of our Central States was exceedingly firm, and its desire to participate in the covenant meetings was exceedingly earnest. Therefore, regretting that it had failed to arrive at the upper Huai, it dispatched Shou Yue 壽越 to seek relations, saying: "Our ruler wishes to seek blessings from Shu of Tang and the two Wens, and to present gifts of introduction and silk to appear before your lordship; only because we failed to guard against the unexpected and thus missed the appointed time does our ruler dare to submit to his guilt." Moved by the scheduling of the meeting at Shandao, and troubling Lu and Wei to announce the arrangements…

title: 萬曆十年廣東鄉試錄
text:
也則又曰君幸惠徼于泰伯仲雍哀寡君而賜
之會寡君願與二三兄弟相見以謀其不庭君
無所辱命戚之會蓋以與中國之壇坫是幸者
而敢為主哉維時雞澤之盟內則諸侯聽命君
子以吳之來也其心同于友邦矣嘉父之款外
則諸戎事晉君子以吳之來也其事異乎夷狄
矣此之不進而亦從于柤之例待之是使夷不
變夏而中國不伸於夷也故特稱人以進之蓋
聖人之情春秋之義如此云於乎晉之通吳猶
===
楚之通秦也楚抑吳興儒者或謂悼非策煮以
吳當秦悼亦籌之審矣惟晉無悼而後吳興故
夫儒者之論是責人於無已也
禮記
大德不官大道不器
蔡德璋
同考試官訓導楊批講不官不器有分别而
華藻蔚然
考試官教諭胡批典雅不浮
punctuated:
也，則又曰：「君幸惠徼于泰伯、仲雍，哀寡君而賜之會，寡君願與二三兄弟相見，以謀其不庭，君無所辱命。」戚之會，蓋以與中國之壇坫是幸者，而敢為主哉？維時雞澤之盟，內則諸侯聽命，君子以吳之來也，其心同于友邦矣；嘉父之款，外則諸戎事晉，君子以吳之來也，其事異乎夷狄矣。此之不進，而亦從于柤之例待之，是使夷不變夏，而中國不伸於夷也，故特稱「人」以進之。蓋聖人之情、《春秋》之義如此云。於乎！晉之通吳，猶楚之通秦也。楚抑吳興，儒者或謂悼非策；煮以吳當秦，悼亦籌之審矣。惟晉無悼，而後吳興，故夫儒者之論，是責人於無已也。

《禮記》
「大德不官，大道不器。」
蔡德璋
同考試官訓導楊批：講「不官」、「不器」有分别，而華藻蔚然。
考試官教諭胡批：典雅不浮。
translation_en:
… then he said further: "Your Lordship has graciously sought blessings from the spirits of Taibo 泰伯 and Zhongyong 仲雍, taking pity on my ruler and granting him a meeting. My ruler wishes to meet with a few brother states to take counsel against those who do not attend court; Your Lordship need not demean yourself by issuing further commands." At the meeting at Qi 戚, Wu considered itself fortunate merely to participate at the covenant platforms of the Central States—how would it dare to act as the presiding host? At that time, inwardly, through the covenant at Jize 雞澤, the feudal lords obeyed commands; thus the gentleman judged that in Wu's coming, its heart was the same as that of the friendly states. Outwardly, through the peace overtures presented by Jiafu 嘉父, the various Rong 戎 tribes served Jin 晉; thus the gentleman judged that in Wu's coming, its conduct differed from that of the barbarians. Had the Sage not promoted Wu here, and instead treated it according to the precedent of the meeting at Cha 柤, that would have prevented the barbarians from transforming into the ways of the Xia 夏, and prevented the Central States from extending their authority over the barbarians. Therefore, the text specially refers to Wu as "men" (ren 人) in order to promote them. Such, indeed, was the sentiment of the Sage and the righteous principle of the Spring and Autumn Annals (Chunqiu 春秋). Alas! Jin's establishing relations with Wu was just like Chu's 楚 establishing relations with Qin 秦. Because Chu was checked only for Wu to rise in power, some Confucian scholars argue that Duke Dao 悼 lacked sound strategy. Yet [?] in using Wu to counterbalance Qin, Duke Dao had in fact calculated the matter thoroughly. It was only after Jin no longer had a ruler like Duke Dao that Wu rose to dominance; therefore, the criticism of those scholars is a case of demanding endlessly of others.

Record of Rites (Liji 禮記)
"Great virtue does not confine itself to a single office; the great Way does not confine itself to a single vessel."
Cai Dezhang 蔡德璋
Comment by Associate Examiner, Assistant Instructor Yang 楊: The explanation of "not confining to a single office" and "not confining to a single vessel" maintains clear distinctions, while its literary flourish is luxuriant.
Comment by Examiner, Instructor Hu 胡: Classically elegant and free of superficiality.

title: 萬曆十年廣東鄉試錄
text:
考試官敎諭陳批〔俊逸〕
惟道德之大者其用不能限焉蓋凡用之可限
者必本之未盛也曾謂道德之大而限於用哉
嘗謂君子之學以蘊于心而非無用也以效于
用而非無體也觀于聖道而知體用之相須矣
彼德之小者度德而官之誰曰不可惟天下有
大德彼其涵養甚充而其所蘊藉甚深也吾知
理煩治劇何所用而不宜任大投艱何所效而
不稱其始若未嘗以一長名而天下有大責任
===
於斯人乎負荷之而其蘊卒不可窺也若曰德
之各一其任如官之不相攝豈所以論於大德
者哉道之小者隨材而器之誰曰不可惟天下
有大道彼其抱負甚宏而其所設施者甚裕也
紛然臨之而泛應有全能卒然投之而妙用無
應迹其始若未嘗以一藝見而天下有大事功
於斯人乎運量之而其用卒不可究也若曰道
之各一其用如器之不相通豈所以論于大道
者哉吁惟不官然後見聖人之德惟不器然後
punctuated:
考試官敎諭陳批：〔俊逸。〕
惟道德之大者，其用不能限焉。蓋凡用之可限者，必本之未盛也。曾謂道德之大而限於用哉？嘗謂君子之學，以蘊于心而非無用也，以效于用而非無體也。觀于聖道，而知體用之相須矣。彼德之小者，度德而官之，誰曰不可？惟天下有大德，彼其涵養甚充，而其所蘊藉甚深也。吾知理煩治劇，何所用而不宜？任大投艱，何所效而不稱？其始若未嘗以一長名，而天下有大責任，於斯人乎負荷之，而其蘊卒不可窺也。若曰德之各一其任，如官之不相攝，豈所以論於大德者哉？道之小者，隨材而器之，誰曰不可？惟天下有大道，彼其抱負甚宏，而其所設施者甚裕也。紛然臨之，而泛應有全能；卒然投之，而妙用無應迹。其始若未嘗以一藝見，而天下有大事功，於斯人乎運量之，而其用卒不可究也。若曰道之各一其用，如器之不相通，豈所以論于大道者哉？吁！惟不官然後見聖人之德，惟不器然後
translation_en:
Examiner Instructor Chen comments: [Refined and spirited.]
Only when Way and Virtue are great can their function not be restricted. For wherever function can be restricted, the root must not yet be flourishing. Could one ever say that when Way and Virtue are great, they are restricted in their function? It has been said that the learning of the gentleman, as stored in the mind, is not without function; and as manifested in function, is not without substance. Observing the Way of the Sages, one knows how substance and function depend upon each other. As for those of lesser virtue, to measure their virtue and assign them a specialized office—who would say this is not permissible? Only when there is great virtue in the world, one's cultivation is exceedingly full, and what one holds in reserve is exceedingly deep. I know that in managing complexity and governing pressing affairs, to what use could it be put and not be suitable? In bearing great burdens and taking on hardships, to what task could it be applied and not be equal to the demand? At first, such a person seems never to have been known for a single specialty, yet when there are great responsibilities in the world, it is upon this person that they are shouldered, while what he holds in reserve ultimately cannot be fathomed. If one were to say that each virtue is limited to a single responsibility, just as offices do not overlap in jurisdiction, how could that be the way to discuss great virtue? As for the lesser ways, to employ them as specialized utensils according to their talent—who would say this is not permissible? Only when there is the great Way in the world, one's aspirations are exceedingly vast, and what one puts into practice is exceedingly ample. When affairs press upon him in confusion, he responds broadly with complete capability; when tasks are cast upon him suddenly, his marvelous function leaves no trace of its response. At first, such a person seems never to have been distinguished for a single skill, yet when there are great achievements to be wrought in the world, it is by this person that they are measured and directed, while his function ultimately cannot be exhausted. If one were to say that each way is limited to a single function, just as utensils are not interchangeable, how could that be the way to discuss the great Way? Ah! Only by not being confined to a single office is the virtue of the Sage seen; only by not being confined to a single utensil…

title: 萬曆十年廣東鄉試錄
text:
見聖人之道君子察此可有志於本矣斯人也
惟夫子足以當之觀其學殫累世藝兼多能其
却萊兵反侵地墮名都視天下事皆緒使也若
以偏材而欲輒試于用則窒而不達卽欲以狡
獪儇詞託之于通方而曰我且不官我且不器
謬矣學者可不務本哉
爲人君者謹其所好惡而已矣君好之則
臣爲之上行之則民從之詩云誘民孔
易此之謂也
===
翟廷策
同考試官訓導楊批根極理趣一洗塵言是
大雅文字
考試官敎諭胡批說謹字見理
考試官敎諭陳批明暢
論君心之當慎以其感人之易也蓋好惡通於
臣民君之誘人易矣徵於詩而可不慎與且夫
人君託於音樂以明其敎非徒自娛於音也將
以通天下之感也是故德音溺音邪正辨矣而
punctuated:
見聖人之道。君子察此，可有志於本矣。斯人也，惟夫子足以當之。觀其學殫累世，藝兼多能，其却萊兵、反侵地、墮名都，視天下事皆緒使也。若以偏材而欲輒試于用，則窒而不達；卽欲以狡獪儇詞，託之于通方，而曰「我且不官，我且不器」，謬矣！學者可不務本哉？

「爲人君者，謹其所好惡而已矣。君好之，則臣爲之；上行之，則民從之。《詩》云：『誘民孔易。』此之謂也。」
翟廷策
同考試官訓導楊批：根極理趣，一洗塵言，是大雅文字。
考試官敎諭胡批：說「謹」字見理。
考試官敎諭陳批：明暢。

論君心之當慎，以其感人之易也。蓋好惡通於臣民，君之誘人易矣，徵於《詩》而可不慎與？且夫人君託於音樂以明其敎，非徒自娛於音也，將以通天下之感也。是故德音、溺音，邪正辨矣，而
translation_en:
…is the Way of the sage made manifest. When the gentleman examines this, he can set his mind upon the fundamental. As for such a person, only the Master is worthy of the description. Observe how his learning exhausted the heritage of successive generations and his arts encompassed manifold abilities; in repelling the troops of Lai, recovering the invaded lands, and dismantling the great strongholds, he regarded all the affairs of the world as mere secondary tasks to be directed with ease. If one possesses only a partial talent and yet wishes at once to test it in practical use, one will be blocked and fail to get through. And if one then wishes to use crafty, glib words to pass oneself off as possessing comprehensive mastery, saying, "I am not limited to a single office; I am not limited to a single vessel," how absurd that is! How could those who pursue learning fail to devote themselves to the fundamental?

"One who is a ruler of men simply takes care regarding what he likes and dislikes. What the ruler likes, his ministers will do; what the superior practices, the common people will follow. The Book of Odes (Shi) says, 'To guide the people is very easy.' This is what it means." [Record of Music, Book of Rites]
Zhai Tingce 翟廷策
Associate Examiner and Assistant Instructor Yang comments: Grounded in the deepest principle and interest, sweeping away commonplace words—this is a piece of writing of great elegance.
Examiner and Instructor Hu comments: The discussion of the word "take care" (jin 謹) shows grasp of principle.
Examiner and Instructor Chen comments: Clear and fluent.

This discusses why the ruler's mind ought to be cautious, because it moves others so easily. Indeed, since likes and dislikes communicate themselves to ministers and the people, it is easy for the ruler to guide others; verified by the Book of Odes, how could he not be cautious? Moreover, when a ruler of men entrusts his sentiments to music in order to clarify his teachings, it is not merely to amuse himself with sounds; he intends thereby to communicate sentiments throughout the world. Therefore, between virtuous music and decadent music, the distinction between the perverse and the upright is clear, and…

title: 萬曆十年廣東鄉試錄
text:
爲人君者可不謹其好惡哉當知以好感者其
心易以淫君無以其淫者爲好也以謹其好必
要諸德音即弗入於心必察矣以惡感者其心
易以私君無以其私者爲惡也以謹其惡必要
諸溺音即習移於心弗顧矣所以當謹者曷故
哉正以臣不自爲惟君是爲君誠好矣臣即相
率而爲焉不問其所好何如也民無定從惟上
是從上誠行矣民即相率而從焉不問其所行
何如也此其爲之本在君不在臣從之機在上
===
不在下誘民何易易耶觀詩以誘民語君德以
孔易道民心正此好即爲行即從之謂也然則
謹其好惡孰非謹其誘民者哉而子夏之言進
乎音矣嗟乎人主之好惡易溺豈直是哉端儒
莊士程容於柔曼則遠親巽亢言激論角聽於
頌媚則距內異始之中其所好者不一二人既
則諧臣肩比諛歌耳滿爲而從之成風矣人主
達於子夏之說者何論聲音即通於政治可也
第貳場
punctuated:
爲人君者，可不謹其好惡哉？當知以好感者，其心易以淫，君無以其淫者爲好也，以謹其好，必要諸德音，即弗入於心，必察矣；以惡感者，其心易以私，君無以其私者爲惡也，以謹其惡，必要諸溺音，即習移於心，弗顧矣。所以當謹者，曷故哉？正以臣不自爲，惟君是爲，君誠好矣，臣即相率而爲焉，不問其所好何如也；民無定從，惟上是從，上誠行矣，民即相率而從焉，不問其所行何如也。此其爲之本在君不在臣，從之機在上不在下，誘民何易易耶！觀《詩》以「誘民」語君德，以「孔易」道民心，正此好即爲、行即從之謂也。然則謹其好惡，孰非謹其誘民者哉？而子夏之言進乎音矣。嗟乎！人主之好惡易溺，豈直是哉？端儒莊士，程容於柔曼，則遠親巽；亢言激論，角聽於頌媚，則距內異。始之中其所好者不一二人，既則諧臣肩比、諛歌耳滿，爲而從之成風矣。人主達於子夏之說者，何論聲音，即通於政治可也。
第貳場
translation_en:
…can one who is a ruler of men fail to be cautious in his likes and dislikes? He ought to recognize that when moved by fondness, the mind easily falls into excess. Let the ruler not take what is excessive as his fondness; in exercising caution over his likes, he must measure them against virtuous music (deyin), and even if such music does not immediately delight his heart, he must examine it carefully. When moved by aversion, the mind easily falls into partiality. Let the ruler not take what stems from partiality as his aversion; in exercising caution over his dislikes, he must measure them against decadent music (niyin), and even if habit has shifted his heart toward it, he must pay it no heed.

Why is it that he must be so cautious? Precisely because ministers do not act on their own initiative, but act only upon the ruler's lead. Once the ruler genuinely likes something, his ministers will lead one another to do it, without asking what the nature of his fondness might be. The common people have no fixed allegiance, but follow only their superiors. Once their superiors genuinely practice something, the people will lead one another to follow it, without asking what the nature of that practice might be. Thus the root of action lies with the ruler and not the ministers, and the pivot of compliance lies with those above and not those below—how very easy it is to guide the people! When we observe that the Book of Odes (Shi) speaks of the ruler's virtue in terms of "guiding the people" and describes the minds of the people as "most easily" led, it refers precisely to this principle: that what he likes is immediately done, and what he practices is immediately followed. If so, then in being cautious about his likes and dislikes, how is he not being cautious about how he guides the people? Truly, Zixia's words go beyond mere music!

Alas! How could the ease with which a sovereign becomes indulgent in his likes and dislikes be limited to music alone? When upright Confucians and dignified gentlemen have their demeanor measured against the soft and seductive, the ruler distances the worthy and draws close the obsequious; when forthright words and impassioned arguments compete for a hearing against eulogies and flattery, he repels those who differ and admits those who conform [?]. At first, those who cater to his likes are no more than one or two men; before long, sycophantic ministers stand shoulder to shoulder and flattering songs fill his ears, until acting upon and following his whims becomes the prevailing custom. For a sovereign who thoroughly comprehends Zixia's teaching, what need is there to speak only of musical sounds? It may be applied directly to governance as well.

Second Session

title: 萬曆十年廣東鄉試錄
text:
爲人君者可不謹其好惡哉當知以好感者其
心易以淫君無以其淫者爲好也以謹其好必
要諸德音卽弗入於心必察矣以惡感者其心
易以私君無以其私者爲惡也以謹其惡必要
諸溺音卽習移於心弗顧矣所以當謹者曷故
哉正以臣不自爲惟君是爲君誠好矣臣卽相
率而爲焉不問其所好何如也民無定從惟上
是從上誠行矣民卽相率而從焉不問其所行
何如也此其爲之本在君不在臣從之機在上
===
不在下誘民何易易耶觀詩以誘民語君德以
孔易道民心正此好卽爲行卽從之謂也然則
謹其好惡孰非謹其誘民者哉而子夏之言進
乎音矣嗟乎人主之好惡易溺豈直是哉端儒
莊士程容於柔曼則遠親巽亢言激論角聽於
頌媚則距內異始之中其所好者不一二人既
則諧臣肩比諛歌耳滿爲而從之成風矣人主
達於子夏之說者何論聲音卽通於政治可也
第貳場
punctuated:
爲人君者，可不謹其好惡哉？當知以好感者，其心易以淫，君無以其淫者爲好也。以謹其好，必要諸德音，卽弗入於心，必察矣。以惡感者，其心易以私，君無以其私者爲惡也。以謹其惡，必要諸溺音，卽習移於心，弗顧矣。所以當謹者曷故哉？正以臣不自爲，惟君是爲；君誠好矣，臣卽相率而爲焉，不問其所好何如也。民無定從，惟上是從；上誠行矣，民卽相率而從焉，不問其所行何如也。此其爲之本在君不在臣，從之機在上不在下，誘民何易易耶？觀《詩》以「誘民」語君德，以「孔易」道民心，正此好卽爲、行卽從之謂也。然則謹其好惡，孰非謹其誘民者哉？而子夏之言進乎音矣。嗟乎！人主之好惡易溺，豈直是哉？端儒莊士，程容於柔曼，則遠親巽；亢言激論，角聽於頌媚，則距內異。始之中其所好者不一二人，既則諧臣肩比，諛歌耳滿，爲而從之，成風矣。人主達於子夏之說者，何論聲音，卽通於政治可也。
第貳場
translation_en:
…How could one who serves as a ruler of men not be cautious in his likes and dislikes? He ought to know that when moved by what he likes, his mind easily falls into excess, so the ruler must not take what is excessive as his liking. To be cautious in what he likes, he must measure it against virtuous music (deyin); even if it does not immediately appeal to his heart, he must examine it closely. When moved by what he dislikes, his mind easily falls into partiality, so the ruler must not take his personal bias as his dislike. To be cautious in what he dislikes, he must measure it against decadent music (niyin); even if habit has swayed his heart toward it, he must pay it no heed. Why is it that he must be so cautious? Precisely because ministers do not act of their own accord, but act only upon the ruler's lead: once the ruler truly likes something, the ministers will immediately lead one another in practicing it, without asking what sort of thing he likes. The common people have no fixed allegiance, but follow only their superiors: once those above truly practice something, the people will immediately lead one another in following it, without asking what sort of thing is being practiced. Thus, the root of practice lies with the ruler and not the ministers, and the pivot of compliance lies with those above and not those below—how very easy it is to guide the people! Observe how the Classic of Poetry (Shi) speaks of the ruler's virtue in terms of "guiding the people" (you min) and describes the minds of the people as "very easy" (kong yi)—this refers precisely to how what is liked is immediately practiced, and what is practiced is immediately followed. This being so, in being cautious about his likes and dislikes, how is he not being cautious about how he guides the people? Indeed, Zixia's words go far beyond mere music! Alas! A ruler's likes and dislikes are easily indulged—how is this true only of music? When upright scholars andgrave gentlemen have their demeanor measured against the soft and seductive, the ruler distances the upright and draws close the compliant [?]; when forthright words and impassioned arguments compete for a hearing against eulogies and flattery, the ruler rejects the candid and embraces the sycophantic [?]. In the beginning, those who cater to his likes are no more than one or two men, but before long, fawning ministers stand shoulder to shoulder, flattering songs fill his ears, and practicing and following these things becomes the prevailing custom. For a ruler who thoroughly comprehends Zixia's discourse, why speak only of tones and music? He may apply it directly to governance.

Second Session

title: 萬曆十年廣東鄉試錄
text:
鼓以二氣運以四時吸之噓之通之復之吸則
寒噓則暑通則元亨復則利貞一翕一闢互爲
其根其榮茂也物不以爲德其凋落也物不以
爲怨何則無心故也天無心以萬物爲心榮茂
凋落皆物所自取故曰栽者培之傾者覆之因
材而篤而天無與焉人則各一其心形骸挌于
外情識橫乎中同我者是異我者非是我而予
之者德非我而奪之者怨棼棼藉藉莫適爲主
有聖人者出是天建于天下而全畀以所覆乃
===
相率而聽命於聖人故聖人繼天而王王者覆
冒天下者也洪範有之惟辟作威惟辟作福王
者操威福之柄可以養人可以教人可以榮人
辱人可以生人殺人而以有心與之舉天下惟
吾所欲爲而莫之敢抗將恣意肆行何所不至
而天下之后我者讎我者各任其喜怒交起而
爭王者亦人耳何以覆冒天下蓋嘗讀史至陶
唐之世而神游其天彼其出而作入而息鑿飲
而耕食孰非受放勳之賜者乃擊壤而歌帝力
punctuated: 鼓以二氣，運以四時，吸之噓之，通之復之。吸則寒，噓則暑，通則元亨，復則利貞，一翕一闢，互爲其根。其榮茂也，物不以爲德；其凋落也，物不以爲怨。何則？無心故也。天無心，以萬物爲心，榮茂凋落，皆物所自取。故曰：「栽者培之，傾者覆之。」因材而篤，而天無與焉。人則各一其心，形骸挌于外，情識橫乎中，同我者是，異我者非，是我而予之者德，非我而奪之者怨，棼棼藉藉，莫適爲主。有聖人者出，是天建于天下，而全畀以所覆，乃相率而聽命於聖人。故聖人繼天而王，王者，覆冒天下者也。《洪範》有之：「惟辟作威，惟辟作福。」王者操威福之柄，可以養人，可以教人，可以榮人辱人，可以生人殺人。而以有心與之，舉天下惟吾所欲爲，而莫之敢抗，將恣意肆行，何所不至？而天下之后我者、讎我者，各任其喜怒，交起而爭。王者亦人耳，何以覆冒天下？蓋嘗讀史至陶唐之世，而神游其天。彼其出而作，入而息，鑿飲而耕食，孰非受放勳之賜者？乃擊壤而歌：「帝力…
translation_en: …animates things through the two vital forces (yin and yang) and revolves through the four seasons, inhaling and exhaling, expanding and returning. When it inhales, there is cold; when it exhales, there is heat; when it expands, there is origination and flourishing (yuanheng); when it returns, there is advantage and firmness (lizhen). One contraction and one expansion serve as each other's root. When things flourish luxuriantly, they do not regard it as a favor; when they wither and fall, they do not regard it with resentment. Why is this? Because Heaven has no deliberate mind (wuxin). Heaven has no mind of its own, taking the myriad things as its mind; flourishing and withering are both brought upon themselves by the things. Therefore it is said: "What is planted it nourishes; what is tilting it overthrows." It strengthens them according to their nature, and Heaven has no personal involvement therein. Humans, however, each have their own individual mind. Their physical forms separate them on the outside, while passions and calculations run rampant within. Those who agree with me are deemed right, and those who differ from me are deemed wrong; those who affirm me and give to me are met with gratitude, while those who oppose me and take from me are met with resentment. In tangled confusion and clamor, there is no one fit to be master. When a sage appears, it is Heaven establishing him over the world and entrusting him completely with all that it covers, and so everyone leads one another to obey the commands of the sage. Therefore, the sage succeeds Heaven and rules as a true king; a true king is one who covers and shelters the world. The "Great Plan" (Hongfan) has it: "Only the sovereign makes awesomeness; only the sovereign makes blessings." A true king wields the handle of awesomeness and blessings: he can nourish people, can instruct people, can honor or disgrace people, and can give life to or put to death people. Yet if he engages with them through a partial, deliberate mind—supposing that throughout the whole world he may do whatever he desires and no one dares resist him—he will indulge his whims and act without restraint, stopping at nothing. Then throughout the world those who treat me as their sovereign and those who treat me as their enemy will each give rein to their own joy and anger, rising up together to contend. The king too is merely a human being; how then could he cover and shelter the world? Indeed, I have read history down to the era of Taotang (Emperor Yao), and my spirit roamed in that heavenly realm. Those people went out to work and came in to rest, dug wells to drink and plowed fields to eat—who among them was not receiving the bounty of Fangxun (Yao)? Yet they tapped the ground and sang: "What does the Emperor's power…

title: 萬曆十年廣東鄉試錄
text:
何有於我哉立我烝民莫非爾極矣而康衢之
謠方且不識不知吾以是知天之爲大而堯之
爲天也故曰大哉堯之爲君巍巍乎則天蕩蕩
乎無能名夫王者不以我治天下而以天下治
天下以我治天下者民寒而曰我衣之也民饑
而曰我食之也民遠於善而曰我敎之也民陷
於罪而曰我刑之也上知有我下亦知有我上
有我故任威福下有我故任德怨威福德怨交
于上下而喜怒叢生淳化日漓善乎禹之言曰
===
堯舜之民皆以堯舜之心爲心至於予而百姓
各自以其心爲心蓋慮之矣欲通天下以爲心
則莫若以天之心爲心以天之心爲心故知有
天下不知有我不知有我故有心於天下治無
心於治天下以無心治天下故上不任威福下
亦不任德怨皇極之敷言有之無偏無陂遵王
之義無有作好遵王之道無有作惡遵王之路
故未嘗衣食天下而農人舉趾紅女在機民以
爲自給自足而王者不言澤未嘗提命天下而
punctuated: 何有於我哉！」立我烝民，莫非爾極矣，而康衢之謠方且「不識不知」。吾以是知天之爲大，而堯之爲天也。故曰：「大哉堯之爲君！巍巍乎則天，蕩蕩乎無能名。」夫王者不以我治天下，而以天下治天下。以我治天下者，民寒而曰：「我衣之也。」民饑而曰：「我食之也。」民遠於善而曰：「我敎之也。」民陷於罪而曰：「我刑之也。」上知有我，下亦知有我；上有我故任威福，下有我故任德怨。威福德怨交于上下，而喜怒叢生，淳化日漓。善乎禹之言曰：「堯舜之民，皆以堯舜之心爲心；至於予，而百姓各自以其心爲心。」蓋慮之矣。欲通天下以爲心，則莫若以天之心爲心。以天之心爲心，故知有天下，不知有我；不知有我，故有心於天下治，無心於治天下。以無心治天下，故上不任威福，下亦不任德怨。皇極之敷言有之：「無偏無陂，遵王之義；無有作好，遵王之道；無有作惡，遵王之路。」故未嘗衣食天下，而農人舉趾，紅女在機，民以爲自給自足，而王者不言澤；未嘗提命天下，而
translation_en:
… has for me!" He established the multitude of the people, and there was none who did not take him as their standard, yet the folk song of the main thoroughfare went so far as to say, "Without knowing, without being conscious." From this I know the greatness of Heaven, and that Yao was like Heaven. Therefore it is said: "Great indeed was Yao as a sovereign! How lofty—he modeled himself upon Heaven; how vast—the people could find no name for it!"

Now, a true king does not govern the world through the self, but governs the world through the world. One who governs the world through the self says when the people are cold, "I clothe them"; when the people are hungry, "I feed them"; when the people stray far from goodness, "I instruct them"; and when the people fall into crime, "I punish them." When the ruler above is conscious of a self, those below are also conscious of a self. Because the ruler above has a self, he indulges in awe-inspiring punishments and blessings; because those below have a self, they indulge in gratitude and resentment. When punishments, blessings, gratitude, and resentment intermingle between above and below, joy and anger spring up in profusion, and pure customs daily grow thin. Well said were the words of Yu: "The people of Yao and Shun all took the mind of Yao and Shun as their own mind; by the time it came to me, the hundred surnames each took their own mind as their mind." Indeed, he was concerned about this.

If one wishes to unite the whole world into a single mind, nothing is better than taking the mind of Heaven as one's mind. Taking the mind of Heaven as one's mind, one is conscious of the world and not conscious of a self; not being conscious of a self, one has a mind for the world's being well-governed, yet no deliberate mind to govern the world. Governing the world without a deliberate mind, the ruler above does not indulge in punishments and blessings, nor do those below indulge in gratitude and resentment. The amplification of the Royal Perfection has it: "Without deflection, without unevenness, pursue the royal righteousness; without any selfish likings, pursue the royal way; without any selfish dislikings, pursue the royal path." Thus, he never deliberately clothed or fed the world, yet the farmers lifted their feet to plow and the weaving women were at their looms; the people considered themselves self-supplied and self-sufficient, while the true king did not speak of his beneficence. He never personally exhorted and enjoined the world, yet…

title: 萬曆十年廣東鄉試錄
text:
司徒敬敷典樂克諧民以爲自親自遜而王者
不言化未嘗敲扑天下而五聲兼聽三居克允
民以爲自恥自格而王者不言威我惠民而視
以爲雨露之滋我明民而視以爲曜曦之照我
戮民而視以爲風霆之震霜雪之肅當其時協
氣横流懷生浸潤固無咨嗟怨嘆之聲亦無感
恩圖報之迹上之心常通於下不出廟堂而九
垓八埏之外若端委而化下之心常通於上無
事煦沫而踵武逖聽之夫若玄默而信故曰王
===
者如天不令人喜不令人怒也彼偏霸之徒爲
驩虞之治欲以力征經營天下筭計見效似捷
於王者而不知其囿於天覆之中直醯雞視之
耳會葵丘示義安知大義問包茅示禮安知大
禮伐原示信安知大信戰泓示仁安知大仁故
曰眇乎小哉所以屬於人警乎大哉獨成其天
此天人之辨也夫天之所生孰非肖天者而自
棄於天則有我之心累之故同天者忘已希天
者克已不令人喜不令人怒王道之大也無有
punctuated: 司徒敬敷，典樂克諧，民以爲自親自遜，而王者不言化；未嘗敲扑天下，而五聲兼聽，三居克允，民以爲自恥自格，而王者不言威。我惠民，而視以爲雨露之滋；我明民，而視以爲曜曦之照；我戮民，而視以爲風霆之震、霜雪之肅。當其時，協氣横流，懷生浸潤，固無咨嗟怨嘆之聲，亦無感恩圖報之迹。上之心常通於下，不出廟堂，而九垓八埏之外，若端委而化；下之心常通於上，無事煦沫，而踵武逖聽之夫，若玄默而信。故曰：「王者如天，不令人喜，不令人怒」也。彼偏霸之徒，爲驩虞之治，欲以力征經營天下，筭計見效，似捷於王者，而不知其囿於天覆之中，直醯雞視之耳。會葵丘示義，安知大義？問包茅示禮，安知大禮？伐原示信，安知大信？戰泓示仁，安知大仁？故曰：「眇乎小哉，所以屬於人；警乎大哉，獨成其天。」此天人之辨也。夫天之所生，孰非肖天者？而自棄於天，則有我之心累之。故同天者忘已，希天者克已。不令人喜，不令人怒，王道之大也；無有
translation_en:
…the Minister of Education respectfully spreads the teachings and the Director of Music achieves harmony, the people consider themselves naturally affectionate and yielding, while the true king does not speak of his transforming influence. He has never flogged the empire, yet when the five tones of pleas are heard together and the three locales of banishment are justly applied, the people consider that they themselves feel shame and reform, while the true king does not speak of his majesty. When I show kindness to the people, they regard it as the nourishing moisture of rain and dew; when I enlighten the people, they regard it as the shining brilliance of the sun; when I punish the people, they regard it as the shock of wind and thunder or the severity of frost and snow. At such a time, harmonious vital energy flows everywhere and all living things are steeped in it; surely there are no sounds of sighing or resentment, nor is there any trace of feeling gratitude and seeking to repay it. The mind of the ruler is always in communion with those below: without leaving the ancestral temple and court, beyond the nine horizons and eight borders it is as though he transforms them while simply wearing ceremonial robes and cap. The minds of those below are always in communion with the ruler: without need for petty coddling, those who follow in his footsteps and listen from afar trust him as if in profound silence. Therefore it is said: "The true king is like Heaven; he neither makes men rejoice nor makes men angry."

As for those partial hegemons who practice a governance of superficial jubilation, wishing to manage the empire through forceful conquest, their calculated results seem quicker than those of the true king; yet they do not realize that they are confined beneath the canopy of Heaven and are regarded merely like gnats in a vinegar jar. Assembling at Kuiqiu to display righteousness—what did that know of great righteousness? Inquiring after the bundled cogon grass to display ritual propriety—what did that know of great ritual propriety? Attacking Yuan to display trustworthiness—what did that know of great trustworthiness? Fighting at the Hong River to display benevolence—what did that know of great benevolence? Therefore it is said: "Tiny and small indeed is that which belongs to man; vast and great indeed is he who alone perfects his Heaven." This is the distinction between Heaven and man.

Now among all whom Heaven gives birth to, who does not resemble Heaven? Yet when one abandons oneself from Heaven, it is because a self-centered mind burdens one. Thus, he who is one with Heaven forgets himself, and he who aspires to Heaven overcomes himself. Neither making men rejoice nor making men angry is the greatness of the Kingly Way; having no…

title: 萬曆十年廣東鄉試錄
text:
作好無有作惡王心之純也慕王道者先其心
而已矣
表
擬
上以
御製猗蘭操示輔臣謝表宣德七年
黃如珪
同考試官敎諭姚批藻麗博雅於陳謝中寫
出臣子引類報
===
國之意當是作手
同考試官敎諭高批博而不窮于辭麗而不
傷於巧是擅長抽對者
考試官敎諭胡批典贍有則
考試官敎諭陳批學富而詞工可錄

作好，無有作惡，王心之純也。慕王道者，先其心而已矣。

表

擬上以《御製猗蘭操》示輔臣謝表（宣德七年）

translation_en:
… indulging in personal likes and without indulging in personal dislikes: such is the purity of the kingly mind. Those who admire the Kingly Way need only begin with their own minds.

Memorial

Draft of a Memorial Giving Thanks for His Majesty's Showing the "Imperial Composition: Melody of the Luxuriant Orchid" (Yuzhi Yilan cao) to the Grand Secretaries (Seventh Year of the Xuande Reign [1432])

Huang Rugui 黃如珪
Comment by Associate Examiner and Instructor Yao: Florid and broadly refined; amid expressions of gratitude it brings out the ministers' intention to draw analogies and repay the state—truly the work of a skilled hand.
Comment by Associate Examiner and Instructor Gao: Broad without running short of words, ornate without suffering from over-cleverness—this is someone adept at matching parallel couplets.

title: 萬曆十年廣東鄉試錄
text:
龍章之懿
明庭播雅琳琅分
鳳藻之輝語出
仙葩儼
蘭函而日麗
寵頒儒素奉
芝檢以春融韻協羽商聲諠
朝野臣某等誠惶誠恐稽首頓首竊惟賢才
應運以出祥開草木之蕃哲后論德而官
心切菲葑之采故禮嚴琴瑟思在良臣而
語載芝蘭比于君子曆開蓂莢闢四門以
延英化衍菁莪來多士以楨國商林抜傅
巖之秀梅鼎惟馨周室樂苹野之賓鹿鳴
載詠自中阿之好旣熄致空谷之音無聞
惟宣父之興思託幽蘭以紀操謂紫莖被
九畹當作明王之香而丹穎賽千秋豈宜
衆卉之伍世雖傳其遺響誼旣遠於前徽
迎申生以蒲輪那識蓬心可採屈嚴陵於
punctuated: 龍章之懿，明庭播雅，琳琅分鳳藻之輝。語出仙葩，儼蘭函而日麗；寵頒儒素，奉芝檢以春融。韻協羽商，聲諠朝野。臣某等誠惶誠恐，稽首頓首。竊惟賢才應運以出，祥開草木之蕃；哲后論德而官，心切菲葑之采。故禮嚴琴瑟，思在良臣；而語載芝蘭，比于君子。曆開蓂莢，闢四門以延英；化衍菁莪，來多士以楨國。商林抜傅巖之秀，梅鼎惟馨；周室樂苹野之賓，鹿鳴載詠。自中阿之好旣熄，致空谷之音無聞。惟宣父之興思，託幽蘭以紀操。謂紫莖被九畹，當作明王之香；而丹穎賽千秋，豈宜衆卉之伍？世雖傳其遺響，誼旣遠於前徽。迎申生以蒲輪，那識蓬心可採；屈嚴陵於
translation_en:
… the excellence of the dragon-patterned writings; the Enlightened Court broadcasts elegance, and fine jades share the radiance of phoenix-like literary grace. The words issue forth like immortal blossoms, majestic in their orchid-scented cases, resplendent as the sun; favor is bestowed upon plain-robed scholars, who receive the magic-fungus-sealed tablets in the genial warmth of spring. The rhymes harmonize with the yu and shang notes, and their acclaim resounds through court and countryside.

Your servants So-and-so and others, in utmost awe and trepidation, bow our heads to the ground. We humbly reflect that worthy talents emerge in response to the fortune of the age, an auspicious sign unfolding like the luxuriance of plants and trees; and wise sovereigns confer offices on the basis of virtue, their hearts earnestly set on gathering even humble turnips and radishes. Thus the ritual teachings revere the zither and lute, with thoughts abiding in good ministers; and the recorded sayings speak of irises and orchids, comparing them to noble men. When the calendar opened with the auspicious calendar-plant, the four gates were flung wide to welcome outstanding heroes; when transforming influence spread like the luxuriant tarragon, a multitude of scholars came to serve as pillars of the state. The Shang court plucked the finest talent from the cliffs of Fu Yan, and the plum-seasoned tripod was fragrant indeed; the House of Zhou rejoiced in guests from the wormwood-covered wilds, and the song of "The Deer Cry" (Luming) was chanted once more.

Yet once the fondness for those in the midst of the gentle hills died out, the footsteps in the empty valley were heard no more. Only Father Xuan [Confucius], stirred to reflection, entrusted his feelings to the secluded orchid by composing the melody (cao). He held that since its purple stems cover nine acres (wan), it ought to serve as the fragrance of an enlightened king; and since its crimson buds rival a thousand autumns, how could it fittingly be ranked among the common weeds? Although the world handed down its lingering strains, its spirit had already drifted far from the ancient models. Though Master Shen (Shen Gong) was welcomed with rush-wrapped wheels, how could they recognize that a tangled heart might still be gathered? Though Yan Ling (Yan Guang) was bent into…

title: 萬曆十年廣東鄉試錄
text:
諫草疇云蘭味不忘映庭凝露之詩詞似
工而不關遺佚臨池從風之賦句雖麗而
奚裨譽髦文不在玆事應有待恭遇
皇帝陛下
九乾含粹
三象儲精
育德
青宮漱藝圃禮園之潤
敷文
===
紫極
覃冰天桂海之聲光
奕葉而
祖德有詩重本根而憫農有
詔
廟堂席側無取峭蒨菁蔥巖穴弓招旁及絲麻
菅蒯蓋已弘槱薪之道亦兼蓄梓漆之材
然猶思服媚于
國華廑縶維於場藿
punctuated: 諫草，疇云蘭味不忘？映庭凝露之詩，詞似工而不關遺佚；臨池從風之賦，句雖麗而奚裨譽髦？文不在玆，事應有待。恭遇皇帝陛下：九乾含粹，三象儲精。育德青宮，漱藝圃禮園之潤；敷文紫極，覃冰天桂海之聲光。奕葉而祖德有詩，重本根而憫農有詔。廟堂席側，無取峭蒨菁蔥；巖穴弓招，旁及絲麻菅蒯。蓋已弘槱薪之道，亦兼蓄梓漆之材；然猶思服媚于國華，廑縶維於場藿，
translation_en:
… the rank of Grand Master of Remonstrance [or: amid the grasses of remonstrance], who could say the fragrance of the orchid was not forgotten? As for the poem on "shining in the courtyard and congealing with dew," its diction seems skillful, yet it has nothing to do with neglected worthies; as for the rhapsody on "overlooking the pond and following the wind," though its lines are ornate, of what benefit are they to renowned talents? True culture does not lie in such things; the matter had to await its proper time.

We reverently encounter Your Majesty the Emperor: embracing the pure essence of the Nine Heavens, storing the quintessential spirit of the Three Luminaries. Nurturing your virtue in the Eastern Palace, you rinsed your mouth with the moisture of the garden of arts and the park of rites; spreading literary culture from the Purple Pole, you extended your renown and radiance to the icy heavens of the north and the cassia seas of the south. Across successive generations, there have been poems celebrating Ancestral Virtue; valuing the fundamental root, there have been edicts expressing compassion for the farmers. Beside the mats of the imperial court, you take no pleasure in mere flashy luxuriance; summoning recluses from cliffside caves with the bow, your reach extends even to humble hemp, silk, and rush. Indeed, you have already broadened the way of gathering firewood for sacrifice, and have likewise stored up timber of catalpa and lacquer; yet you still long to win the devotion of the flower of the state, and remain earnestly concerned with tethering those who feed upon the bean leaves of the vegetable garden, …

title: 萬曆十年廣東鄉試錄
text:
親揮
睿藻
特製猗蘭聯璧貫珠名雖沿於孔氏振幽拔滯
義實創自
宸衷曰身隱曰道光遺賢是慮若幽谷若茂草
潛德孔昭曄曄其芳一語仰
王言之麗嗟嗟厥茂四韻覩
御墨之華副在
蘭臺儼矣
===
明堂六雅
恩施芸閣猗與宣聖徽音豈徒美媲夫五絃將
用形求于九野昔
高皇
頒耆儒之
勅不棄芻蕘迨
文祖
賜明經之詩兼收草莽
先朝
punctuated: 親揮睿藻，特製《猗蘭》。聯璧貫珠，名雖沿於孔氏；振幽拔滯，義實創自宸衷。曰「身隱」、曰「道光」，遺賢是慮；若「幽谷」、若「茂草」，潛德孔昭。「曄曄其芳」，一語仰王言之麗；「嗟嗟厥茂」，四韻覩御墨之華。副在蘭臺，儼矣明堂六雅；恩施芸閣，猗與宣聖徽音。豈徒美媲夫五絃，將用形求于九野。昔高皇頒耆儒之勅，不棄芻蕘；迨文祖賜明經之詩，兼收草莽。先朝
translation_en: …personally wielding the imperial brush to compose a special piece, "The Flourishing Orchid" (Yilan). Like joined jade disks and strung pearls, though the title follows that of Confucius, its meaning of rousing the obscure and promoting the neglected truly originates from the imperial heart. Speaking of "hidden in person" and "radiant in the Way," his concern is for overlooked worthies; whether in "secluded valleys" or amid "luxuriant grasses," hidden virtue is made abundantly manifest. "Brilliant is its fragrance"—in a single phrase we look up to the elegance of the royal words; "alas for its luxuriance"—in four rhymes we behold the splendor of the imperial ink. With a copy deposited in the Orchid Terrace, it is as majestic as the Six Odes of the Bright Hall; with grace bestowed upon the Rue Pavilion, how admirable is this virtuous echo of the Sage! How could it merely rival the beauty of the five-stringed zither? It shall be used to seek out men by their likeness across the nine regions. In the past, the Exalted Emperor issued edicts to aged Confucian scholars, not forsaking grass-cutters and firewood-gatherers; when the Cultured Ancestor bestowed poems upon masters of the classics, he likewise gathered in men from the rustic wilds. The former reigns'…

title: 萬曆十年廣東鄉試錄
text:
特典
今日重光遂使篠派瑣材依白雲而翹首茅
茨羣品候清角以彈冠某等識謝爨桐
恩銜饔藥御仲由之瑟終闕響於丘門學宋玉
之謡未均音於郢路芳騰
金陛戴
周露之滋培蔭結
玉池仰
堯雲之芘覆猥荷
===
奎章之燦爛幸探
天旨之淵純
寶奏初
頒矚慶雲之五色
朱絃一拊聆韶律之九成足徵
丹扆雄文更詫黃扉奇覯敢不益勤吐握用廣
登崇聽賢人
予輔之聲期斷金以共濟遵羣材偕來之
旨務連茹以同升伏願
punctuated: 特典，今日重光。遂使篠派瑣材，依白雲而翹首；茅茨羣品，候清角以彈冠。某等識謝爨桐，恩銜饔藥。御仲由之瑟，終闕響於丘門；學宋玉之謡，未均音於郢路。芳騰金陛，戴周露之滋培；蔭結玉池，仰堯雲之芘覆。猥荷奎章之燦爛，幸探天旨之淵純。寶奏初頒，矚慶雲之五色；朱絃一拊，聆韶律之九成。足徵丹扆雄文，更詫黃扉奇覯。敢不益勤吐握，用廣登崇？聽賢人予輔之聲，期斷金以共濟；遵羣材偕來之旨，務連茹以同升。伏願
translation_en: … special grace shines forth anew today. Thus, minor talents from bamboo-rimmed streams raise their heads as they lean toward the white clouds, and the varied ranks from thatched cottages dust off their caps in anticipation of the clear jiao note. We, Your servants, lack the discernment to recognize the charred paulownia wood on the hearth, yet we hold in our mouths the grace of the medicinal herbs from the imperial kitchen. Playing the zither of Zhong You, our music ultimately falls short at the gate of Confucius; imitating the songs of Song Yu, we have yet to harmonize our tune along the roads of Ying. Fragrance rises upon the Golden Steps as we receive the nourishing cultivation of the dew of Zhou; shade gathers over the Jade Pool as we look up to the sheltering canopy of the clouds of Yao. Unworthily receiving the brilliance of the Imperial Composition, we are fortunate to fathom the profound purity of the Heavenly Intent. When the Precious Melody is first promulgated, we gaze upon the five-colored auspicious clouds; at a single pluck of the vermilion strings, we listen to the nine movements of the Shao music. It suffices to attest to the magnificent literature from behind the Vermilion Screen, and makes us marvel all the more at this rare encounter within the Yellow Doors of the Grand Secretariat. How dare we not be ever more diligent in spitting out our food and binding up our hair to welcome the worthy, thereby broadening the elevation and advancement of talent? Listening to the call of "worthy men, be My helpers," we hope for the unity that cuts through metal so as to cross the stream together; obeying the decree that "all talents shall come forth together," we shall strive to draw them up like intertwined roots so that they ascend in unison. We humbly pray that…

title: 萬曆十年廣東鄉試錄
text:
善人與居
德音是茂毋
採華而忘實毋
棄瑟而好竽于彼高岡于彼朝陽
收孝德馮翼而四方則以阜民財以解民慍
歌
明良喜起而萬事康臣等無任瞻
天仰
聖激切屛營之至謹奉
===
表稱
謝以
聞
第參場
策
第一問
梁維屏
同考試官教諭姚批〔闡揚皇上敷文振武之盛詞藻蔚然且忠規懇切尤見芹曝之忱〕
punctuated:
善人與居，德音是茂。毋採華而忘實，毋棄瑟而好竽。于彼高岡，于彼朝陽，收孝德馮翼而四方則；以阜民財，以解民慍，歌明良喜起而萬事康。臣等無任瞻天仰聖，激切屛營之至，謹奉表稱謝以聞。

第參場
策
第一問
梁維屏
同考試官教諭姚批：〔闡揚皇上敷文振武之盛，詞藻蔚然；且忠規懇切，尤見芹曝之忱。〕
translation_en:
…that Your Majesty may dwell in the company of good men and make flourishing Your virtuous reputation; that You may not gather the blossoms only to forget the fruit, nor cast aside the large zither in favor of the mouth organ; that upon that lofty ridge and facing that morning sun, You may gather in those of filial virtue and supportive aid so that the four quarters take them as their model; and that in enriching the people's wealth and relieving the people's resentment, songs of an enlightened ruler and worthy ministers rejoicing and rising to action together may ring out while all affairs prosper. Your servants, unimaginably overwhelmed with earnest devotion and awe-struck trepidation as we gaze up at Heaven and look upon Your Sacred Person, respectfully present this memorial of gratitude for the imperial hearing.

Third Session
Policy Essays
First Question
Liang Weiping 梁維屏
Comment by Associate Examiner Instructor Yao: [He sets forth and extols the flourishing splendor of His Majesty's propagation of civil culture and invigoration of martial prowess in luxuriant literary style; moreover, his loyal admonitions are earnest and sincere, especially revealing a heartfelt devotion like offering wild celery or warm sunlight to the sovereign.]

title: 萬曆十年廣東鄉試錄
text:
同考試官敎諭高批
今天子德備文武草茆儒生知有恬熙之化耳矣莊誦揚榷得其大本
如子者應不多見宜錄以
獻
考試官敎諭胡批經生中能鋪張
文治武烈而直摅忠悃知志在自效者
考試官敎諭陳批意忠懇而詞典雅得
盛世敷文振武氣象宜錄
聖人之所以合神順命則地揆天鴻名白
===
于天下而常爲稱首者道莫大乎文武夫
交靈通虛應煥藻摛菁思馳三玄談殫五
際鳥奕廊廟暐曄寰區其道懿矣盛矣若
乃撥亂夷世睿筭雄圖七德有耀羣策是
奄委命環裘歸心風海煌煌乎非大武之
弘烈歟故文與武非二物也肄武敷文非
二事也薦紳之家委蛇而歌肆夏則云帝
王德化不在用兵而武是用詘介冑之夫
攘臂而議韜略謂迂步闊武牴牾却敵不
punctuated:
同考試官敎諭高批：今天子德備文武，草茆儒生知有恬熙之化耳矣。莊誦揚榷，得其大本，如子者應不多見，宜錄以獻。
考試官敎諭胡批：經生中能鋪張文治武烈，而直摅忠悃，知志在自效者。
考試官敎諭陳批：意忠懇而詞典雅，得盛世敷文振武氣象，宜錄。
聖人之所以合神順命，則地揆天，鴻名白于天下，而常爲稱首者，道莫大乎文武。夫交靈通，虛應煥，藻摛菁，思馳三玄，談殫五際，鳥奕廊廟，暐曄寰區，其道懿矣、盛矣！若乃撥亂夷世，睿筭雄圖，七德有耀，羣策是奄，委命環裘，歸心風海，煌煌乎非大武之弘烈歟？故文與武非二物也，肄武敷文非二事也。薦紳之家，委蛇而歌《肆夏》，則云帝王德化不在用兵，而武是用詘；介冑之夫，攘臂而議韜略，謂迂步闊武，牴牾却敵不
translation_en:
Associate Examiner and Instructor Gao's comment: Today the Son of Heaven possesses virtue complete in both the civil and the martial; rustic scholars of the thatched huts merely know the transformative influence of peace and prosperity. Yet one who solemnly recites and broadly discusses this, grasping its fundamental basis like you, is surely seldom seen; it is fitting to record this to present to the throne.
Examiner and Instructor Hu's comment: Among students of the Classics, here is one able to set forth in full the civil governance and martial exploits while directly expressing loyal sincerity, showing that his ambition lies in dedicating himself to service.
Examiner and Instructor Chen's comment: The intent is loyal and earnest, and the diction classic and refined; it captures the spirit of a flourishing age that spreads civil culture and rouses martial vigor. It should be recorded.
That whereby the sage unites with the numinous and complies with the Mandate, models himself on Earth and measures Heaven, makes his great name illustrious throughout the realm, and is ever praised as preeminent—there is no Way greater than the civil and the martial. Now, communing in spirit and responding from emptiness, shining forth in literary brilliance and unfolding the finest essence, sending thoughts racing through the Three Mysteries and exhausting discourse on the Five Junctures, resplendent [鳥奕, for 舄奕] in the court and radiant throughout the world—how admirable, how flourishing is this Way! And when it comes to quelling disorder and pacifying the age, with sagely calculations and grand designs, the seven martial virtues shine forth and all strategies are encompassed; those in felt and furs submit their lives, and across winds and seas hearts turn in allegiance—brilliant indeed, is this not the vast achievement of great martial prowess? Therefore, the civil and the martial are not two separate things; practicing the martial and spreading the civil are not two separate affairs. Yet gentlemen of the official sash move with stately ease and sing the Sixia, saying that the moral transformation of emperors and kings does not lie in the use of arms, and thus the martial is disparaged; meanwhile, men in armor bare their arms and debate military strategy, claiming that with slow paces and wide-striding steps one goes at cross-purposes with repelling the enemy and cannot…

title: 萬曆十年廣東鄉試錄
text:
能以寸而文事方之左矣不知象意方先
性情未啓希微奥窔之中而匪文則何以
恢廓其精神而新天下端委甚都莊辭容
與而陡然當衷甲折衝之會匪武又何以
震耀其聽睹而服天下夫惟上聖之主含
吐陰陽彈壓山川吹萬各適得一以寧蓋
甞隆之仁義禮樂騰茂蜚英以盪文章而
新風雅乃又于天下從容之際藏人情之
所甚畏而脩其國容以養奇傑之氣至以
===
天子之尊而馳騁于原野親金鼓干戈之
事而不爲過吁此其爲文豈徒飾理詭曼
緣設小物賓賓焉以灼于世而其爲武豈
匹夫一劍之學沾沾一映而見爲威哉美
哉洋洋乎期運之會昌
聖神之芳軌而我
皇上文章之盛與其所以
大閱武承平之際者可得而揄揚其萬一矣蓋
自混沌既判黃皇肇基垂衣不足而爲結
punctuated: 能以寸，而文事方之左矣。不知象意方先，性情未啓，希微奥窔之中，而匪文則何以恢廓其精神而新天下？端委甚都，莊辭容與，而陡然當衷甲折衝之會，匪武又何以震耀其聽睹而服天下？夫惟上聖之主，含吐陰陽，彈壓山川，吹萬各適，得一以寧。蓋甞隆之仁義禮樂，騰茂蜚英，以盪文章而新風雅；乃又于天下從容之際，藏人情之所甚畏，而脩其國容以養奇傑之氣，至以天子之尊而馳騁于原野，親金鼓干戈之事而不爲過。吁！此其爲文，豈徒飾理詭曼，緣設小物，賓賓焉以灼于世？而其爲武，豈匹夫一劍之學，沾沾一映而見爲威哉？美哉洋洋乎！期運之會昌，聖神之芳軌，而我皇上文章之盛，與其所以大閱武承平之際者，可得而揄揚其萬一矣。蓋自混沌既判，黃皇肇基，垂衣不足而爲結…
translation_en: …unable to advance by even an inch, so that civil affairs by comparison are relegated to second place. They do not realize that when symbolic images and ideas were just beginning and human nature and feelings had not yet been awakened, amid what was subtle, indistinct, and deeply recessed, without civil culture how could one broaden the spirit and renew the realm? And when one issplendidly attired in ceremonial robes and caps, delivering grave speeches with leisurely composure, yet suddenly confronts an occasion of hidden armor and repelling enemy assaults, without martial prowess how could one awe people's ears and eyes and bring the realm to submission? Only a supremely sage ruler inhales and exhales yin and yang, holds sway over mountains and rivers, breathes life into the myriad things so each finds its proper place, and attains the One to bring peace. Indeed, he exalts benevolence, righteousness, ritual, and music, causing flourishing renown and brilliant talent to soar so as to stir literary culture and renew elegant customs; yet in times when the realm is at ease, he also keeps in reserve what human nature most dreads, cultivating the martial array of state to nurture the spirit of extraordinary heroes—even to the point that, with all the尊 dignity of the Son of Heaven, he gallops across the open plains and personally engages in the affairs of gongs, drums, shields, and halberds without it being an excess. Ah! Is such civil culture merely a matter of adorning principles with specious elaborations and contriving trifles, fastidiously seeking to shine in the world? And is such martial prowess merely the art of an ordinary man with a single sword, smugly flashing a single glance to make a show of might? How splendid, how vast! In this flourishing convergence of the destined age and the fragrant footsteps of the sage and divine, the flourishing of our August Emperor's literary culture and the manner in which he conducts the Grand Military Review in an era of enduring peace may thereby be extolled in at least one part in ten thousand. Ever since primordial chaos was divided and the Yellow Emperor laid the foundations of rule, governing by simply letting robes hang down was not enough, and so they resorted to knotting…

title: 萬曆十年廣東鄉試錄
text:
繩結繩不足而爲書契書契不足而玉龜
石馬瀠河而沉於洛河洛不足而舜戚軒
弧貢相望於堂階干戚不足而青丘丹浦
鮪水鳳墟相與從鞭弭于中原而夏籥虞
箭堯章湯濩雍煕恬愉之歌乃以爲象成
告功之具夫然後而知世之不能不文也
文之不能不武也勢也聖人所不能違也
而文之不可無武也武之不可無文也理
也聖人所不可偏廢也其後冥契綦闡圖
牒愈增抽演闕文網羅遺韻則詩歌賦頌
電發于清都岐陽石鼓蒐狩類禡奇正行
師方圓布陣則鞞琫韎鞈動容于章冕要
之趣向不同質文亦異建安六代之季君
臣上下流連于寶瑟瑤臺沉湎于輕紅濃
黛相與置酒迎風賡酬迭和所創音什蕩
靡不經如巫山芳樹朱鷺烏栖樅陽白紵
銅鞮元會相羊誇誕鋪張一時而栢梁之
體華林之編至與臣下競短爭長無復雅
punctuated: 繩，結繩不足而爲書契，書契不足而玉龜、石馬瀠河而沉於洛，河、洛不足而舜戚、軒弧貢相望於堂階，干戚不足而青丘、丹浦、鮪水、鳳墟相與從鞭弭于中原，而《夏籥》、《虞箭》、《堯章》、《湯濩》，雍煕恬愉之歌，乃以爲象成告功之具。夫然後而知世之不能不文也，文之不能不武也，勢也，聖人所不能違也；而文之不可無武也，武之不可無文也，理也，聖人所不可偏廢也。其後冥契綦闡，圖牒愈增，抽演闕文，網羅遺韻，則詩歌賦頌電發于清都；岐陽石鼓，蒐狩類禡，奇正行師，方圓布陣，則鞞琫韎鞈動容于章冕。要之，趣向不同，質文亦異。建安、六代之季，君臣上下流連于寶瑟瑤臺，沉湎于輕紅濃黛，相與置酒迎風，賡酬迭和，所創音什，蕩靡不經，如《巫山》、《芳樹》、《朱鷺》、《烏栖》、《樅陽》、《白紵》、《銅鞮》、《元會》，相羊誇誕，鋪張一時；而栢梁之體、華林之編，至與臣下競短爭長，無復雅
translation_en:
… knotted cords; when knotted cords did not suffice, they made written documents; when written documents did not suffice, the jade tortoise and stone horse swirled in the Yellow River and sank in the Luo River; when the Yellow River Chart and Luo River Writing did not suffice, the battle-axes of Shun and the bows of Xuanyuan were presented in view of one another upon the steps of the hall; when shields and battle-axes did not suffice, at Qingqiu, the Dan River, the Wei River, and Fengxu, they contended with whips and bow-ends in the Central Plains; and only then did the Flute of Xia, the Shao of Yu [written 箭 for 箾], the Dazhang of Yao, and the Dahuo of Tang—those songs of harmonious prosperity and tranquil joy—serve as the means to symbolize completion and announce achievement. Only after this does one know that the world cannot avoid becoming civil, and the civil cannot avoid turning to the martial: this is the trend of circumstances, which the sages could not oppose. Moreover, that the civil cannot do without the martial, and the martial cannot do without the civil: this is principle, neither side of which the sages could neglect.

Thereafter, as abstruse tallies were increasingly elucidated and charts and records multiplied ever more, drawing out and elaborating defective texts and gathering up surviving rhymes, poetry, songs, rhapsodies, and eulogies flashed forth like lightning in the pure capital; while with the Stone Drums of Qiyang, the spring and winter hunts and the sacrifices to Heaven and at the camp, marching armies by unorthodox and orthodox tactics, and deploying formations in squares and circles, ornamented scabbards and madder-dyed knee-covers stirred admiration among ceremonial caps and robes. In sum, as inclinations differed, substance and refinement also diverged. By the late years of the Jian'an era and the Six Dynasties, rulers and ministers, superiors and inferiors alike lingered over jeweled zithers and jasper terraces, steeping themselves in light rouge and heavy eyebrow-paint; together they set out wine to greet the breeze, exchanging verses in turn. The musical pieces they composed were dissolute, extravagant, and irregular—such as "Mount Wu," "Fragrant Trees," "Vermilion Egret," "Crows Roosting," "Zongyang," "White Ramie," "Copper Ti," and "New Year's Assembly"—roaming at ease in boastful extravagance to make a grand display for the moment; while with the "Cypress Beam" style and the "Hualin Park" compilations, rulers even competed with their subjects over literary merits and flaws, no longer retaining the elegant …

title: 萬曆十年廣東鄉試錄
text:
道而三代禮樂蕩然於斯矣乃若閱武之
禮代相沿踵太始咸寧有宣武堂之閱武
德有同宮之閱貞觀有城西之閱顯慶有
潏水之閱開元有新豐之閱建隆有金明
