之閱他如甘泉上苑長楊五柞校獵射熊
凝笳疊鼓不過以供一時之逸興侈千古
之雄心而已且也矜文則軍容不耀强武
則觚翰爲塵偏雄之技叔霸之風烏足尚
哉
===
天啓
聖神乃文乃武
參神玄造
叶契太虛協氣蒸于八埏太和溢于六宇蓋甞
觀于
今之天下海波謐矣邊塵淨矣倭酋達虜之
寇昔日所
宵旰而憂者今俱解辮面內爲
國家貢賦之土而荆魏之勇士宛洛之俠少
punctuated:
道，而三代禮樂蕩然於斯矣。乃若閱武之禮，代相沿踵：太始、咸寧有宣武堂之閱，武德有同宮之閱，貞觀有城西之閱，顯慶有潏水之閱，開元有新豐之閱，建隆有金明之閱。他如甘泉、上苑、長楊、五柞，校獵射熊，凝笳疊鼓，不過以供一時之逸興、侈千古之雄心而已。且也矜文則軍容不耀，强武則觚翰爲塵，偏雄之技、叔霸之風，烏足尚哉！
天啓聖神，乃文乃武，參神玄造，叶契太虛，協氣蒸于八埏，太和溢于六宇。蓋甞觀于今之天下，海波謐矣，邊塵淨矣。倭酋達虜之寇，昔日所宵旰而憂者，今俱解辮面內，爲國家貢賦之土；而荆、魏之勇士，宛、洛之俠少，
translation_en:
… elegance, and the rites and music of the Three Dynasties were utterly swept away at that point. As for the ritual of military reviews, successive dynasties followed in one another's footsteps: in the Taishi (265–274) and Xianning (275–280) eras there were the reviews at Xuanwu Hall; in the Wude era (618–626) there was the review at Tong Palace [?]; in the Zhenguan era (627–649) there was the review west of the capital city; in the Xianqing era (656–661) there was the review at the Jue River; in the Kaiyuan era (713–741) there was the review at Xinfeng; and in the Jianlong era (960–963) there was the review at Jinming Pool. Other events—such as enclosed hunts and bear-shooting at Ganquan Palace, the Supreme Park (Shangyuan), Changyang Palace, and Wuzuo Palace, with resonant reed-pipes and rolling drums—served merely to indulge the idle pleasures of a moment and flaunt a grandiose ambition for the ages. Moreover, when they prided themselves on civil culture, their military array failed to shine; when they strove for martial might, writing tablets and brushes were left to gather dust. How could the skills of partial hegemons and the customs of late-age overlords be worthy of esteem!

Heaven has enlightened our Sacred and Divine Sovereign, accomplished in both the civil and the martial, who participates in the mysterious workings of the spirit and harmonizes with the Great Void, so that auspicious vital energy rises across the Eight Reaches and supreme harmony overflows the Six Directions. Indeed, if one observes the realm today, the ocean waves are calm and the frontier dust has settled. The Japanese chieftains and Tatar raiders, whose depredations formerly caused the sovereign to worry from before dawn until after dark, have now all untied their plaits and turned inward in allegiance, becoming lands that offer tribute and taxes to the state; meanwhile, the brave warriors of Jing and Wei and the gallant youths of Wan and Luo…

title: 萬曆十年廣東鄉試錄
text:
悉籍爲戍卒驍騎破的揚威于萬里之外
士大夫雍容緩帶相與脩先秦西京之業
道路風騷而闤闠左國蓋嘉隆之纂組弘
正之講明洪永之謨謀臻厥盛媺集其大
成而文恬武煕之象郁郁皇皇轢三軼五
於都哉亦可謂
綦隆泰際矣乃
皇上猶聖不自聖本仁祖義摶剛梡柔以弘安
攘之烈
===
躬震夷夏之觀頃來
萬幾之暇
揮灑
宸翰
徧賜羣工而
特勅儒臣分直
內閣校讎圖史敘述賦誦抽對章句當斯時
也臯陶不及賡
明良之歌召公難於矢鳳凰之雅薄海內外想
punctuated: 悉籍爲戍卒驍騎，破的揚威于萬里之外。士大夫雍容緩帶，相與脩先秦、西京之業，道路風騷而闤闠左國。蓋嘉、隆之纂組，弘、正之講明，洪、永之謨謀，臻厥盛媺，集其大成。而文恬武煕之象，郁郁皇皇，轢三軼五。於都哉！亦可謂綦隆泰際矣。乃皇上猶聖不自聖，本仁祖義，摶剛梡柔，以弘安攘之烈，躬震夷夏之觀。頃來萬幾之暇，揮灑宸翰，徧賜羣工，而特勅儒臣分直內閣，校讎圖史，敘述賦誦，抽對章句。當斯時也，臯陶不及賡明良之歌，召公難於矢鳳凰之雅。薄海內外，想…
translation_en: …are all enrolled as garrison soldiers and valiant cavalry, hitting the mark and displaying martial might ten thousand li away. Scholar-officials, poised and in loosely belted robes, join together in cultivating the literary enterprise of the pre-Qin and Western Han; along the roads one hears poetry in the style of the Airs and Elegies, and in the marketplaces, prose in the manner of the Zuo Commentary and Discourses of the States. Indeed, the ornate artistry of the Jiajing (1522–1566) and Longqing (1567–1572) eras, the clear expositions of the Hongzhi (1488–1505) and Zhengde (1506–1521) eras, and the grand counsels of the Hongwu (1368–1398) and Yongle (1403–1424) eras have reached their utmost perfection and been gathered into a great synthesis. The scene of civil tranquility and martial peace is resplendent and majestic, surpassing the Three Dynasties and excelling the Five Emperors. Oh, how magnificent! This may truly be called an era of supreme prosperity and peace. Yet His Majesty, though sage, does not regard himself as sage; rooting himself in benevolence and modeling himself on righteousness, tempering firmness and shaping gentleness, he expands the glorious achievements of pacifying the interior and repelling the exterior, and in his own person inspires awe in the eyes of both non-Chinese and Chinese. Recently, in his leisure from the myriad affairs of state, he has freely wielded the imperial brush, bestowing his calligraphy widely upon the assembled officials, and has specially commanded Confucian courtiers to take turns on duty in the Grand Secretariat to collate books and histories, compose rhapsodies and odes, and match lines and verses. At such a time as this, Gao Yao could not keep pace in continuing the song of the enlightened ruler and worthy ministers, and the Duke of Shao would find it difficult to set forth the ode of the phoenix. Within and beyond the four seas, people eagerly…

title: 萬曆十年廣東鄉試錄
text:
望風聲快覩
化成之文有八九十老人相與含哺而謳吟而
我
明一代之文章行將自
皇上而裁成之已然而
皇上方且睠然南北
特軫先憂不矜承平不娛冶康爰當暮春之吉
遂敕
大閲
===
召諸五陵三輔六郡良家之子材官蹶張弘農
越騎藹然雲集
敕兵部先期演習十千萬全營法
上以是日
親試之諸凡前茅者中權者後勁者陣魚麗者
搴朱旗者擊刁斗者步射者隊射者射而
騎者飛驦驌者驥騄蹀躞者為賢王塞者
為將軍細柳者
上按轡而
punctuated: 望風聲，快覩化成之文，有八九十老人相與含哺而謳吟，而我明一代之文章，行將自皇上而裁成之已。然而皇上方且睠然南北，特軫先憂，不矜承平，不娛冶康。爰當暮春之吉，遂敕大閲，召諸五陵、三輔、六郡良家之子，材官、蹶張、弘農、越騎，藹然雲集。敕兵部先期演習十千萬全營法，上以是日親試之。諸凡前茅者、中權者、後勁者、陣魚麗者、搴朱旗者、擊刁斗者、步射者、隊射者、射而騎者、飛驦驌者、驥騄蹀躞者、為賢王塞者、為將軍細柳者，上按轡而
translation_en: …admiringly look toward His moral influence and delight in beholding the literary splendor of His transformative rule. Elders of eighty and ninety years sing praises together with food in their mouths, and the literary culture of our entire Ming dynasty is about to be shaped and perfected by His Majesty himself. Yet His Majesty still gazes with concern toward the north and south, taking special forethought in advance of trouble, neither boasting of peace nor indulging in pleasurable ease. Thus, on an auspicious day in late spring, He ordered a Grand Review. He summoned the sons of respectable families from the Five Imperial Tombs, the Three Metropolitan Areas, and the Six Commandery Regions, along with skilled infantry, foot-drawn crossbowmen, soldiers from Hongnong, and Yue cavalry, who gathered thick as clouds. He ordered the Ministry of War to drill in advance in the ten-thousand-strong Perfect Safety Camp formations, and on that day the Emperor personally tested them. All those serving as the vanguard, the central command, and the rear guard; those arrayed in the Fish-Scale formation; those seizing crimson banners and striking the night-watch kettles; those shooting on foot, shooting in squads, and shooting from horseback; those galloping on Suhuang steeds and prancing on Jilu chargers; those acting as the frontier barriers of the Worthy Kings or as the general's camp at Xiliu—the Emperor held his reins and…

title: 萬曆十年廣東鄉試錄
text:
親校其高下定其勝負爲推轂受鉞歌之采薇
杕杜鐃吹奏凱而歸天下聞之以爲天策
神兵芒星揮電舒雲艶日而遼左諸軍遂
以是時斬首虜四百四十閲之次日露布
上
聞始
命太常祀告
太廟
宣示中外江漢黎民遠方遐裔畚鍤鉏耰于節
===
旄之下吁亦盛矣而執事猶欲詢所以爲
芹曝之效愚又將何說而處於此竊聞
帝王之文與經生二
帝王之武與武弁二故丹青追琢特以爲
清閒之助而校蒐閲武間一行之以壯神氣而
已伏覩
皇上所分授詞調有孝弟忠信仁義禮智之目
御製聯語有靜裏收心涵養德性之句
大閲之日
punctuated: 親校其高下，定其勝負，爲推轂受鉞，歌之《采薇》、《杕杜》，鐃吹奏凱而歸。天下聞之，以爲天策神兵，芒星揮電，舒雲艶日。而遼左諸軍遂以是時斬首虜四百四十。閲之次日，露布上聞，始命太常祀告太廟，宣示中外，江漢黎民、遠方遐裔，畚鍤鉏耰于節旄之下。吁！亦盛矣！而執事猶欲詢所以爲芹曝之效，愚又將何說而處於此？竊聞帝王之文與經生二，帝王之武與武弁二。故丹青追琢，特以爲清閒之助；而校蒐閲武，間一行之，以壯神氣而已。伏覩皇上所分授詞調，有「孝弟忠信、仁義禮智」之目；御製聯語，有「靜裏收心、涵養德性」之句。大閲之日，
translation_en: … personally inspected their relative merits and determined their victories and defeats. For them, the chariot hubs were pushed and the battle-axes conferred; the odes "Picking Thorn-Ferns" (Caiwei) and "Solitary Pear Tree" (Didu) were sung for them, and with martial cymbals and pipes playing songs of triumph, He returned. When the realm heard of this, they regarded them as heavenly strategies and divine troops, like flashing stars wielding lightning, or spreading clouds brightening the sun. And it was just at this time that the various armies in Liaodong beheaded four hundred and forty enemy captives. On the day following the grand review, the unsealed dispatch of victory was submitted to His Majesty's attention. Only then did He command the Court of Imperial Sacrifices to offer sacrifice and announce the news at the Imperial Ancestral Temple, and to proclaim it at court and in the provinces, so that the common people of the Yangzi and Han regions and the distant peoples of the far frontiers worked with baskets, spades, hoes, and rakes beneath the imperial banners and pennants. Ah, how magnificent indeed! Yet Your Excellency still wishes to inquire how to offer the humble devotion of wild celery and warming in the sun—what words, then, can this simpleton find to address this? I have privately heard that the literary culture of emperors and kings is distinct from that of classical scholars, and the martial prowess of emperors and kings is distinct from that of military officers. Therefore, painting and fine carving serve merely as aids to moments of leisure, while hunting inspections and martial reviews are carried out only occasionally in order to invigorate the vital spirit, and nothing more. I have humbly observed that the lyric tunes distributed by His Majesty include the headings of "Filial Piety, Fraternal Submission, Loyalty, Trustworthiness, Benevolence, Righteousness, Ritual Propriety, and Wisdom," and that the couplets composed by His Majesty include the lines "In quietude, gather in the mind; nurture and cultivate one's moral nature." On the day of the Grand Review, …

title: 萬曆十年廣東鄉試錄
text:
憫念軍士勞苦倍加
賞賚又察其介胄之制堅利與
御前不類
特發
內帑於工部俾一新之
顯謨弘烈固非區區之所能窺測者而因得以
輸一二之悃焉夫
深宮燕閒之中而較之正人君子則敬肆異
濡毫染翰之際而較之
===
儲精垂思則華實異
聽朝訪道之頃而較神履盈持滿則乆暫異其
亦臨亦保慎獨之要也惟時惟幾身體之
學也慎終如始防微之道也凡此皆
文德之精而
皇上之所謂收心養性者其意蓋不越此也天
下之勢安若覆盂而薊遼黠虜狠貪叵測
焱服焱叛則羈縻之難嶺南諸猺憑林嘯
峒新州方設措置未安則約束之難更卒
punctuated: 憫念軍士勞苦，倍加賞賚；又察其介胄之制，堅利與御前不類，特發內帑於工部，俾一新之。顯謨弘烈，固非區區之所能窺測者，而因得以輸一二之悃焉。夫深宮燕閒之中，而較之正人君子，則敬肆異；濡毫染翰之際，而較之儲精垂思，則華實異；聽朝訪道之頃，而較神履盈持滿，則乆暫異。其「亦臨亦保」，慎獨之要也；「惟時惟幾」，身體之學也；「慎終如始」，防微之道也。凡此皆文德之精，而皇上之所謂「收心養性」者，其意蓋不越此也。天下之勢，安若覆盂，而薊遼黠虜，狠貪叵測，焱服焱叛，則羈縻之難；嶺南諸猺，憑林嘯峒，新州方設，措置未安，則約束之難；更卒
translation_en:
…taking pity on the toil and hardship of the soldiers, bestowed upon them redoubled rewards and bounties. Furthermore, observing that the construction of their armor and helmets did not match the sturdiness and sharpness of those before the Imperial Presence, He specially issued funds from the Inner Treasury to the Ministry of Works to have them completely renewed. Such illustrious plans and grand achievements are certainly beyond what this humble candidate can fathom, yet through them I am able to offer a few words of sincere devotion.

Now, if one compares the leisure within the deep palace to being in the presence of upright and noble men, there is a difference between reverence and laxity; if one compares the moments of moistening the brush and wielding the pen to storing up one's vital essence and applying deep thought, there is a difference between outward floridity and inner substance; if one compares the brief intervals of holding court and inquiring into the Way to keeping the spirit focused on treading carefully in fullness and maintaining balance [? 較神履盈持滿], there is a difference between permanence and transience. "Awe-struck as if approached by spirits, watchful as if preserving one's state"—this is the essential of being watchful over oneself when alone; "being ever timely and attentive to the subtle"—this is the learning of personal embodiment; "being as careful at the end as at the beginning"—this is the way of guarding againstincipient ills. All of these are the essence of civil virtue, and the meaning of what His Majesty calls "gathering the mind and nourishing the moral nature" surely does not go beyond this.

The state of the realm is as stable as an overturned bowl, yet the狡黠 (cunning) caitiffs of Jizhou and Liaodong are fierce, greedy, and unpredictable, suddenly submitting and suddenly rebelling—thus lies the difficulty of keeping them under loose rein; the various Yao tribes of Lingnan rely on the forests and whistle in their mountain grottoes, and with the new department just established and arrangements not yet settled—thus lies the difficulty of restraining them; the rotational conscripts…

title: 萬曆十年廣東鄉試錄
text:
繇戍役羨召募朽甲鈍戈緩急不足爲用
則練習之難故旣濟衣袽未雨桑土見以
爲迂闊而其機豫南顧議撫北顧議勦見
以爲參商而其謀周將知兵兵擇將識地
形器用利見以爲無奇而其筴當凡此皆
兵家之萬全而我
皇上之所以長慮却顧者其慮盖周乎此也而
又有說焉呂東萊曰聖人之文與天地並
綜以元氣之機軸斷以陰陽之斧斤濯以
===
江漢之波瀾日月雷霆嵩衡岱華來往毫
端聲隅子曰以道德爲疆場以仁義爲將
帥以命令爲陣伍以忠信爲干戈智以師
之禮以戰之則何戰而不克此之謂文武
合一之道長久安寧之術而
今日之所可爲
廟廊獻者書生之言惟執事擇焉
第二問
莫維則
punctuated:
繇戍役羨召募，朽甲鈍戈，緩急不足爲用，則練習之難。故「旣濟衣袽」、「未雨桑土」，見以爲迂闊而其機豫；南顧議撫、北顧議勦，見以爲參商而其謀周；將知兵、兵擇將，識地形、器用利，見以爲無奇而其筴當。凡此皆兵家之萬全，而我皇上之所以長慮却顧者，其慮盖周乎此也。

而又有說焉。呂東萊曰：「聖人之文，與天地並：綜以元氣之機軸，斷以陰陽之斧斤，濯以江漢之波瀾；日月雷霆、嵩衡岱華，來往毫端。」聲隅子曰：「以道德爲疆場，以仁義爲將帥，以命令爲陣伍，以忠信爲干戈，智以師之，禮以戰之，則何戰而不克？」此之謂文武合一之道、長久安寧之術，而今日之所可爲廟廊獻者。書生之言，惟執事擇焉。

第二問
莫維則
translation_en:
…from garrison duty and surplus to recruited troops, with rotting armor and blunt halberds that are insufficient for use in an emergency—herein lies the difficulty of training and drilling. Therefore, preparing “old rags after crossing the river” [from the hexagram Jiji] and “gathering mulberry root-bark before it rains” [from the Book of Odes] may appear pedantic and impractical, yet their foresight is precautionary; deliberating on pacification when looking south and deliberating on extermination when looking north may appear at odds like the stars Shen and Shang, yet the strategy is comprehensive; generals knowing their troops and troops selecting their generals, understanding the terrain and keeping weapons and equipment sharp may appear unremarkable, yet the plan is sound. All of these are the foolproof strategies of military tacticians, and the reason our August Emperor takes long-term thought and looks back with care is that His deliberations encompass all of this.

And there is yet more to say. Lü Donglai [Lü Zuqian 呂祖謙] said: “The civil culture of the sage stands equal with Heaven and Earth: it is woven on the loom of primordial vitality, hewn with the axes of yin and yang, and washed in the surging waves of the Yangtze and Han rivers; the sun, moon, thunder, and lightning, and the sacred peaks of Song, Heng, Dai, and Hua come and go at the tip of his brush.” Shengyuzi [Huang晞 黃晞, mistakes ‘Gou’ 聱 for ‘Sheng’ 聲] said: “Take morality and virtue as your borderlands, benevolence and righteousness as your generals and commanders, decrees and orders as your battle ranks, loyalty and trustworthiness as your shields and halberds; lead them with wisdom and fight by means of ritual propriety—then what battle will not be won?” This is what is meant by the Way of unifying civil and military affairs and the art of enduring peace and stability, which today may be offered up to the imperial court. Such are the words of a mere scholar; may Your Excellency select from among them.

Question 2
Mo Weize 莫維則

title: 萬曆十年廣東鄉試錄
text:
同考試官教諭鄒批人本嚴闢曲道是作𧦬
騰士品而惓惓於名實邪正之辨有深思矣
考試官教諭胡批評古今才品語語極剴切
考試官教諭陳批讀之覘子自處矣可式
學者尚論古昔至唐虞成周之間淳懿郅
隆類非後世所敢望云卽綿邈至于兩漢
何翩翩乎多才也
今天下非乏士也
累朝
===
列聖之所培植菁莪棫樸之所養育非不畢具
也高賢大良濯心勵志蘄豪傑自命非遜
能往喆也乃士判于名實習分于淳漓豈
人才與世相升降有不可究詰抑風靡于
漸俗成于習所從來長遠矣請卽執事所
問而以臆對天下蓋有文章之士絺章繪
句呻吻而談先秦櫛韻比聲拮居而卑大
曆一槼染則謂千古盛事一語稍合則謂
靈均以來此祕未覩意味偶同則嘵嘵然
punctuated:
同考試官教諭鄒批：人本嚴闢曲道，是作𧦬騰士品，而惓惓於名實邪正之辨，有深思矣。
考試官教諭胡批：評古今才品，語語極剴切。
考試官教諭陳批：讀之覘子自處矣，可式。
學者尚論古昔，至唐、虞、成周之間，淳懿郅隆，類非後世所敢望云。卽綿邈至于兩漢，何翩翩乎多才也！今天下非乏士也，累朝列聖之所培植，菁莪、棫樸之所養育，非不畢具也。高賢大良，濯心勵志，蘄豪傑自命，非遜能往喆也。乃士判于名實，習分于淳漓，豈人才與世相升降有不可究詰？抑風靡于漸，俗成于習，所從來長遠矣？請卽執事所問而以臆對。天下蓋有文章之士，絺章繪句，呻吻而談先秦；櫛韻比聲，拮居而卑大曆。一槼染，則謂千古盛事；一語稍合，則謂靈均以來，此祕未覩；意味偶同，則嘵嘵然
translation_en:
Comment by Associate Examiner Instructor Zou: The candidate's character fundamentally and strictly rejects crooked ways; this essay evaluates and elevates the caliber of scholars, showing earnest devotion to distinguishing between name and reality, heterodoxy and orthodoxy. It shows deep thought indeed.
Comment by Examiner Instructor Hu: In appraising the talent and character of past and present, every word hits the mark with utmost incisiveness.
Comment by Examiner Instructor Chen: Reading this reveals how the gentleman conducts himself; it may serve as a model.

When scholars evaluate antiquity and reach the eras of Tang, Yu, and the flourishing Zhou, they say that such pure excellence and supreme prosperity are generally beyond what later ages dare hope for. Yet even extending far down to the Western and Eastern Han, how brilliantly abundant were their men of talent! Today the empire does not lack scholars. That which has been cultivated by the successive reigns of our line of sagely emperors, and nurtured in the manner of the "Jing'e" and "Yupu" odes, is by no means incomplete. Lofty worthies and great men of goodness cleanse their hearts and steel their resolve, aspiring to style themselves heroes and outstanding figures, not yielding in ability to the wise men of the past. Why then are scholars divided between name and reality, and customs split between purity and degeneracy? Could it be that human talent rises and falls with the age in ways that cannot be fathomed? Or is it that trends are swept along gradually and customs are formed through habit, having come down from a long way off? Allow me to address what you, sir, have asked and reply with my own humble views. In the empire there are indeed scholars of belles-lettres: weaving chapters and painting phrases, they chant and drone while discoursing on the pre-Qin era; combing rhymes and matching tones, they laboriously [?] look down upon the Dali reign period (766–779). Once they dabble their brushes in imitation, they call it a grand event of a thousand ages; when a single phrase slightly accords with the ancients, they claim that since Lingjun (Qu Yuan 屈原) this secret had never been glimpsed; when the flavor and tone happen to coincide, they clamorously…

title: 萬曆十年廣東鄉試錄
text:
而謂努力中原鞭弭當世始而倡之者一
二人旣而和者數十人又其後人人能矣
蓋又有談禪之士襲空寂之微談執生滅
之幻論深者湛錮其中而遂以遺世淺者
借其言語文字之奧而姑以釣奇始而倡
之者一二人旣乃倣傚成風矣蓋又有清
言之士目不覩當世之務而土苴天下身
不接利害之交而焦螟萬物迹其議論非
不慷慨自負而考中叩蘊則未有淵然不
===
可窮之量確然不可奪之守徒沾沾自喜
者矣蓋又有術霍之士譎詭姽娗不可方
測極其能于詷刺乾沒而用其奇于脂臾
希合其便給敏捷能使人人當其意而命
之曰枃之四人者愚試取而品隲之夫照
矚三才暉麗萬有莫近于文玄辭之宰獨
照之匠精者發揮道妙大者鼓吹休明斯
亦何可少矣顧士之能文譬農之服耜工
之貿易其本業耳若乃高自矜詡黨同伐
punctuated: 而謂努力中原、鞭弭當世。始而倡之者一二人，旣而和者數十人，又其後人人能矣。蓋又有談禪之士，襲空寂之微談，執生滅之幻論；深者湛錮其中而遂以遺世，淺者借其言語文字之奧而姑以釣奇。始而倡之者一二人，旣乃倣傚成風矣。蓋又有清言之士，目不覩當世之務而土苴天下，身不接利害之交而焦螟萬物；迹其議論，非不慷慨自負，而考中叩蘊，則未有淵然不可窮之量、確然不可奪之守，徒沾沾自喜者矣。蓋又有術霍之士，譎詭姽娗，不可方測；極其能于詷刺乾沒，而用其奇于脂臾希合。其便給敏捷，能使人人當其意，而命之曰「枃」。之四人者，愚試取而品隲之。夫照矚三才，暉麗萬有，莫近于文。玄辭之宰、獨照之匠，精者發揮道妙，大者鼓吹休明，斯亦何可少矣？顧士之能文，譬農之服耜、工之貿易，其本業耳。若乃高自矜詡，黨同伐
translation_en: … and declare that they are striving for mastery in the Central Plains and vying with whips and bows in the present age. At first those who initiate it are only one or two people; before long dozens echo them; and later still, everyone claims to be capable of it. There are also scholars who discourse on Chan Buddhism, borrowing subtle talk of emptiness and stillness and clinging to illusory doctrines of birth and extinction. Those who go deeply into it become immersed and locked within it, and consequently turn their backs on the world; those who remain superficial borrow the abstruseness of its speech and writings merely to fish for novelty. At first those who initiate it are only one or two people, and before long imitation becomes a general trend. There are also scholars of pure conversation (qingyan), whose eyes do not look upon the affairs of the current world while they treat all under heaven as mere dross, and whose persons never engage the juncture of advantage and harm while they regard the myriad things as tiny midges. Judging by their discussions, they are not without impassioned self-assurance; yet if one examines what is within them and probes their inner store, they lack any deep, inexhaustible capacity or firm, unyielding integrity, and are merely smugly pleased with themselves. There are also scholars of calculating statecraft [? 術霍, for 術數], deceitful, shifting, and impossible to fathom by any square standard; they exhaust their abilities in spying, prying, and speculative opportunism, and employ their stratagems in greased flattery [? 脂臾, for 脂韋] and currying favor. Their glibness and quick-wittedness enable them to suit everyone's wishes, so that people style them "pivots" [? 枃, or "models"]. As for these four types of men, let me humbly take them up and evaluate them. Now, for illuminating the Three Powers and casting splendor upon the myriad things, nothing comes closer than literature. As masters of abstruse diction and craftsmen of solitary insight, in their subtlest works they expound the mysteries of the Way, and in their grandest they celebrate a glorious and enlightened era—how could such things be dispensed with? Yet for a scholar to be skilled in writing is like a farmer working with his plowshare or an artisan or merchant plying his trade [?]: it is simply his basic occupation. If, however, they boastfully exalt themselves, form cliques with the like-minded and attack…

title: 萬曆十年廣東鄉試錄
text:
異相掎摭而不能相下謬也命詞不依爾
雅而餖飣古文奇字期駴目詞心而止悖
也會弗能自發一識而掇拾前人之遺揭
日月而行之謬之謬者也二氏之學其精
深奥妙能使人之憬然有悟而其騖空虛
而遁溟涬足以澄汰其世累貪鄙之心顧
吾儒之理廣大精微何所不備士誠精于
理道則玄言精義纚纚具也况繇其言不
可用于天下國家斯於世敎所關不眇小
===
矣清言之士其雄談快論似足以抗俗而
破愚則不可謂無裨於世其虛而無當言
及而行背之則不可謂有裨于世若夫衛
霍者流彼非能肩鉅剸繁爲縣官備緩急
又非能持重馳悠爲元元倚辦大命彼其
所謂才者不過巧于觀時而捷于應物用
之而善亦足小辦用之而不善適足殃民
小人之雄哉嗟夫以彼其材皆世所謂高
明之士也彼其論辯足以傾動時流故耳
punctuated: 異，相掎摭而不能相下，謬也；命詞不依爾雅，而餖飣古文奇字，期駴目詞心而止，悖也；會弗能自發一識，而掇拾前人之遺，揭日月而行之，謬之謬者也。二氏之學，其精深奥妙，能使人之憬然有悟，而其騖空虛而遁溟涬，足以澄汰其世累貪鄙之心。顧吾儒之理，廣大精微，何所不備？士誠精于理道，則玄言精義，纚纚具也。况繇其言，不可用于天下國家，斯於世敎所關不眇小矣。清言之士，其雄談快論，似足以抗俗而破愚，則不可謂無裨於世；其虛而無當，言及而行背之，則不可謂有裨于世。若夫衛霍者流，彼非能肩鉅剸繁，爲縣官備緩急；又非能持重馳悠，爲元元倚辦大命。彼其所謂才者，不過巧于觀時而捷于應物，用之而善，亦足小辦；用之而不善，適足殃民，小人之雄哉！嗟夫！以彼其材，皆世所謂高明之士也。彼其論辯足以傾動時流，故耳…
translation_en:
…those who differ, carping at one another and refusing to yield to each other—this is absurd. When they craft their diction without following elegant standards, instead piecing together archaic graphs and strange characters merely aiming to startle the eye and dazzle the mind [?], this is perverse. And when they cannot even generate a single insight of their own, yet plagiarize the leftovers of predecessors and parade them about as if holding aloft the sun and moon, this is the height of absurdity!

As for the teachings of the Two Sects [Buddhism and Daoism], their profundity and subtlety can indeed bring people to sudden enlightenment, and their pursuit of emptiness and retreat into primordial vagueness suffice to cleanse the mind of worldly entanglements and greedy, base desires. Yet the principles of us Confucians are vast and subtle—what do they lack? If a scholar is truly well-versed in principle and the Way, then abstruse words and subtle meanings are already present in abundance. Moreover, if one follows their doctrines, they cannot be applied to the empire and the state; what is at stake here for worldly moral instruction is no small matter.

As for scholars of "pure conversation" (qingyan), their bold talk and incisive arguments seem sufficient to defy vulgarity and shatter ignorance, so one cannot say they are of no benefit to the world; yet because they are hollow and impractical, and their actions contradict the words they speak, one cannot say they are of benefit to the world.

As for those of the ilk of Wei Qing and Huo Qubing [i.e., schemers and opportunists], they are neither able to shoulder great burdens and cut through complexities to prepare for emergencies on behalf of the sovereign, nor able to maintain gravity and far-reaching vision so that the common people may rely on them to fulfill the great mandate. What they call "talent" is nothing more than cleverness in observing the times and nimbleness in responding to things. If employed well, it suffices for minor tasks; if employed poorly, it serves only to bring calamity upon the people—champions among petty men indeed!

Alas! By virtue of their talents, all of them are what the world calls men of lofty brilliance. Because their arguments and debates suffice to sway the currents of the time, those who listen to…

title: 萬曆十年廣東鄉試錄
text:
觀巷說之徒入焉而喜其聲稱足以歆艷
後進故希光附景之士入焉而信其機神
足以駕馭羣哲故負材抱奇之輩入焉而
愚于是維世君子搤掔而談以為洪永之
間其士質如元氣之在渾濛成弘之間其
士英如太阿之發于硎蓋至于今而文質
離矣夫天下惟上智為能不與世而推移
惟上智為能觀世而易化談轉移于
今日則遵何術哉愚以為質直之士宜雋也
===
夫以椎魯少文與纍瓦結繩校則其數不
勝以戇直不阿與剽輕儇捷較則其數不
勝顧其淵中沈識恥言過行渾兮若樸訥
兮若愚豫兮若冬涉川猶兮若畏四鄰猶
足以軌世而範俗不然則飾其鞶帨而雕
其渾樸將何所底止也愚以為吾儒之學
當講也有日月則爝火自微有正學則異
端自息僞學繁興天下惑于僞而遂疑其
眞其眞者旣無以自見而後一切洸洋謬
punctuated: 觀巷說之徒，入焉而喜；其聲稱足以歆艷後進，故希光附景之士，入焉而信；其機神足以駕馭羣哲，故負材抱奇之輩，入焉而愚。于是維世君子，搤掔而談，以為洪、永之間，其士質，如元氣之在渾濛；成、弘之間，其士英，如太阿之發于硎。蓋至于今而文質離矣。夫天下惟上智為能不與世而推移，惟上智為能觀世而易化。談轉移于今日，則遵何術哉？愚以為質直之士宜雋也。夫以椎魯少文與纍瓦結繩校，則其數不勝；以戇直不阿與剽輕儇捷較，則其數不勝。顧其淵中沈識，恥言過行，渾兮若樸，訥兮若愚，豫兮若冬涉川，猶兮若畏四鄰，猶足以軌世而範俗。不然，則飾其鞶帨而雕其渾樸，將何所底止也？愚以為吾儒之學當講也。有日月則爝火自微，有正學則異端自息。僞學繁興，天下惑于僞而遂疑其眞；其眞者旣無以自見，而後一切洸洋謬
translation_en:
…those who rely on hearsay and street talk enter into their circle and rejoice; their reputation and renown are sufficient to dazzle and entice the younger generation, and so scholars who seek to bask in their reflected glory enter into their circle and believe in them; their mental agility and spirit are sufficient to command and outmaneuver the multitude of wise men, and so those who possess talent and harbor extraordinary abilities enter into their circle and are fooled. Thereupon, gentlemen who uphold the moral order of the world clutch their wrists in earnest discussion, holding that during the Hongwu (1368–1398) and Yongle (1403–1424) eras, the scholars were substantial and unadorned, like primordial vitality in the midst of undifferentiated chaos; and that during the Chenghua (1465–1487) and Hongzhi (1488–1505) eras, the scholars were brilliant and heroic, like the great Tai'e sword freshly Hone from the whetstone. Yet down to the present day, refinement and substance have become severed from one another. Now, in all under heaven, only those of the highest wisdom are able to avoid shifting and drifting along with the age, and only those of the highest wisdom are able to observe the age and transform its customs. When we speak of reversing the trend at the present day, what method should we follow?

In my humble opinion, upright andsubstantial scholars ought to be promoted and distinguished. Now, if one compares the blunt, simple, and unembellished with those who pile up tiles and knot cords [in elaborate rhetorical display], then in sheer techniques the former cannot prevail; if one compares the straightforward, upright, and unbending with the nimble, frivolous, and quick-witted, then in sheer techniques the former cannot prevail. Yet their deep inner discernment, their shame at letting their words exceed their deeds—unadorned like uncarved wood, slow of speech as though foolish, cautious as though wading a stream in winter, hesitant as though fearful of neighbors on all four sides—are still sufficient to serve as a standard for the age and a model for customs. Otherwise, if men merely embellish their decorative sashes and carve away their simple, uncarved nature, where will it ever end?

In my humble opinion, the learning of us Confucians must be expounded and clarified. When the sun and moon are present, torch-fires naturally grow dim; when orthodox learning is present, heterodox teachings naturally subside. When spurious learning flourishes in profusion, the world is deluded by the spurious and consequently comes to doubt what is genuine; once what is genuine has no means to manifest itself, all manner of extravagant, unbridled, and荒謬…

title: 萬曆十年廣東鄉試錄
text:
悠之說得以自露其奇譬如寶在玄室有
所求而不見白日照焉則羣物斯辨學者
心之白日也今即不宜户分而畛析以增
言詮然使吾道炳若日星則彼閒閒詹詹
者將不攻而自破是孟氏反經之說也愚
又以爲責實之政宜詳也士之赴名若水
之就下責之以名則競于飾名而其計工
責之以實則巧於偷實而其計益工言與
行違不啻倍蓰必虚心以鑑之多方以觀
===
之真能天下弗顧而始信之高尚之士真
能請劍折檻而始信之節義之士真能剸
繁理鉅而始信之經濟之士其以虚辭相
矜詡與夫捷給爲佞警敏爲能舉無以自
售則實行其可興乎嗟乎人主未甞不欲
用材而求之以似則卒無以得其真天下
亦未甞不蘄用於人主而浮慕其名則卒
無以見其實此名實之所爲眩也語曰鼓
宫宫應鼓角角應夫以四海之大兆民之
punctuated: 悠之說，得以自露其奇。譬如寶在玄室，有所求而不見，白日照焉，則羣物斯辨。學者，心之白日也。今即不宜户分而畛析，以增言詮，然使吾道炳若日星，則彼閒閒詹詹者，將不攻而自破，是孟氏反經之說也。愚又以爲責實之政宜詳也。士之赴名，若水之就下。責之以名，則競于飾名，而其計工；責之以實，則巧於偷實，而其計益工。言與行違，不啻倍蓰。必虚心以鑑之，多方以觀之。真能天下弗顧，而始信之高尚之士；真能請劍折檻，而始信之節義之士；真能剸繁理鉅，而始信之經濟之士。其以虚辭相矜詡，與夫捷給爲佞、警敏爲能，舉無以自售，則實行其可興乎！嗟乎！人主未甞不欲用材，而求之以似，則卒無以得其真；天下亦未甞不蘄用於人主，而浮慕其名，則卒無以見其實。此名實之所爲眩也。語曰：「鼓宫宫應，鼓角角應。」夫以四海之大、兆民之
translation_en: …and far-fetched doctrines are able to display their novelty. It is like a treasure inside a dark chamber: when one seeks it, one cannot see it; yet once the bright sun shines inside, all things are clearly distinguished. Learning is the bright sun of the mind. Today, even though we should not divide into competing households and draw boundary lines so as to multiply verbal explanations, if we cause our Way to shine as brightly as the sun and stars, then those grandiloquent and petty chatterers will collapse of their own accord without being attacked—this is Mencius's doctrine of returning to the standard. I also hold that governance which demands substance ought to be meticulous. Scholars pursue reputation just as water flows downward. If one demands reputation of them, they compete in adorning their reputation, and their schemes are skillful; if one demands substance of them, they grow clever at counterfeiting substance, and their schemes become more skillful still. The divergence between their words and deeds is not merely twofold or fivefold. One must examine them with an open mind and observe them in manifold ways. Only when someone is truly able to disregard the whole world should one trust him as a scholar of lofty character; only when someone is truly able to request the imperial sword or break the balustrade in remonstrance should one trust him as a scholar of integrity and righteousness; only when someone is truly able to cut through complexities and manage great affairs should one trust him as a scholar of statecraft. When those who boast to one another with empty words, along with those who takeglibness as eloquence and quick-wittedness as ability, have no way at all to peddle themselves, then may substantive conduct perhaps be revived! Alas! A ruler never fails to desire the employment of talent, yet if he seeks it through mere resemblance, in the end he will have no means to obtain what is genuine; the world, too, never fails to hope for employment by the ruler, yet if it superficially covets reputation, in the end it will have no means to manifest true substance. This is why name and reality become confused. The proverb says: "Strike the gong note and the gong responds; strike the jue note and the jue responds." Now, with the vastness of the Four Seas and the multitude of the millions of people…

title: 萬曆十年廣東鄉試錄
text:
衆上之鼓舞淬礪者如此而下之應之者
如彼未之有矣且夫天下之索竒騖異者
固斯人爲之乃其恢翊世運扶張人紀亦
未始非斯人爲之顧所倡何如耳不然天
下之沁沁泯泯居無一物託之乎中庸其流爲頑
鈍而無恥安所用之且執事所惡惡其似
耳假令有能揚扢古今錯繹經緯追典紹
謨歌風續雅可以其文學而槩少之乎假
===
令有能精通性命而不遺世故妙契名理
而不襲言詮可以其爲釋老家言擯之乎
假令有能感嘅負俗是非不回能使人聞
其風而爲之興起可以清言棄之乎假令
有能併包衆能兼總萬略指顧而疆寓寧
談笑而事功集可以其敏給而槩論之乎
蓋聞之天下惟純粹竤懿之士默成象語
成爻徙倚乎汗漫之宇而浮揚乎無畛崖
之際淵然有潛渾然無隅凝然弗移而充
punctuated: 衆，上之鼓舞淬礪者如此，而下之應之者如彼，未之有矣。且夫天下之索竒騖異者，固斯人爲之；乃其恢翊世運、扶張人紀，亦未始非斯人爲之，顧所倡何如耳。不然，天下之沁沁泯泯，居無一物，託之乎中庸，其流爲頑鈍而無恥，安所用之？且執事所惡，惡其似耳。假令有能揚扢古今，錯繹經緯，追典紹謨，歌風續雅，可以其文學而槩少之乎？假令有能精通性命而不遺世故，妙契名理而不襲言詮，可以其爲釋老家言擯之乎？假令有能感嘅負俗，是非不回，能使人聞其風而爲之興起，可以清言棄之乎？假令有能併包衆能，兼總萬略，指顧而疆寓寧，談笑而事功集，可以其敏給而槩論之乎？蓋聞之：天下惟純粹竤懿之士，默成象，語成爻，徙倚乎汗漫之宇，而浮揚乎無畛崖之際，淵然有潛，渾然無隅，凝然弗移，而充
translation_en: …multitude of the millions of people, it has never happened that those above inspire and temper them in one way while those below respond in another. Moreover, as for those in the empire who seek after the strange and chase the extraordinary, it is indeed such men who do so; yet when it comes to expanding and assisting the fortunes of the age and upholding and extending human moral order, it is not that it is not also such men who do so—it simply depends on how they are led. Otherwise, if people in the empire are muddled and indistinct, possessing nothing within themselves while hiding behind the pretext of the Mean, degenerating into obtuse dullness and shamelessness, of what use would they be? Furthermore, what Your Excellency dislikes is merely their specious resemblance. Suppose there is someone capable of expounding upon antiquity and the present, weaving together warp and woof, emulating the canons and continuing the counsels, singing the Airs and continuing the Odes—can one summarily belittle him on account of his literary learning? Suppose there is someone capable of thoroughly mastering human nature and destiny without neglecting worldly affairs, wondrously grasping philosophical principles without merely parroting verbal explanations—can one reject him as speaking the words of Buddhists and Daoists? Suppose there is someone capable of righteous indignation that braves vulgar convention, unwavering in right and wrong, able to make others rise up upon hearing of his moral character—can one cast him aside on account of pure conversation? Suppose there is someone capable of encompassing a multitude of abilities and synthesizing ten thousand strategies, bringing peace to the frontiers at a point of the finger and a glance, and accomplishing feats amidst talk and laughter—can one summarily dismiss him on account of his quick-wittedness? Indeed, I have heard that in the world only the pure, magnanimous, and virtuous scholar forms emblems in his silence and hexagram lines in his speech, wandering through boundless space and soaring across the borderless expanse—deep and hidden like an abyss, whole and seamless without sharp corners, steadfast and unmoving, and full…

title: 萬曆十年廣東鄉試錄
text:
然不可以形拘斯其人不可多得其次則
聰明俊異其思必有所寄而其神必有所
之彼必不錄錄而與庸衆人伍故曰智士
無思慮之變則不樂辨士無談說之序則
不樂察士無凌誶之事則不樂夫惟操人
才之權者潛移而默化之使其精神意氣
盡導之于中正篤實之歸而不用之于奇
異頗僻之域則向之栩栩有述者皆可進
而九德三俊之徒也陶者之治埴也員者
===
中規方者中矩夫陶冶人才者亦若是也
唐虞成周之才且旦暮遇之矣
第三問
吳正偉
同考試官訓導楊批勘扠馬遷得其梗槩而
詞直追蹤之至欲刪潤二十一史甚中肯綮有
志哉
同考試官敎諭姜批遷史獨尊後代評騭至
於成林誠靖子四議當爲倔屈矣末復指摘二
punctuated:
然不可以形拘，斯其人不可多得。其次則聰明俊異，其思必有所寄，而其神必有所之，彼必不錄錄而與庸衆人伍。故曰：智士無思慮之變則不樂，辨士無談說之序則不樂，察士無凌誶之事則不樂。夫惟操人才之權者，潛移而默化之，使其精神意氣，盡導之于中正篤實之歸，而不用之于奇異頗僻之域，則向之栩栩有述者，皆可進而九德、三俊之徒也。陶者之治埴也，員者中規，方者中矩，夫陶冶人才者亦若是也，唐、虞、成周之才，且旦暮遇之矣。

第三問
吳正偉
同考試官訓導楊批：勘扠馬遷得其梗槩，而詞直追蹤之；至欲刪潤二十一史，甚中肯綮，有志哉！
同考試官敎諭姜批：遷史獨尊，後代評騭至於成林，誠靖子四議，當爲倔屈矣；末復指摘二
translation_en:
…and full, unable to be confined by external form—such people cannot often be obtained. Next to them are the intelligent, outstanding, and extraordinary: their thoughts must have something upon which to lodge, and their spirit must have somewhere to go; they will certainly not be mediocre and rank alongside the common crowd. Thus it is said: "A man of wisdom is not happy without variations in thought and deliberation; a man of eloquence is not happy without an occasion to discourse; a man of keen discernment is not happy without matters of contention and reproach." Only when those who hold the authority of nurturing talent imperceptibly shift and silently transform them—causing their spirit, vigor, and aspiration to be guided entirely toward the destination of uprightness and genuine substance, rather than being expended in the realm of the strange, eccentric, and one-sided—can all those who previously took lively pride in their own expositions advance to become fellows of the Nine Virtues and the Three Categories of Outstanding Talent. When a potter works with clay, what is round matches the compass, and what is square matches the carpenter's square. He who molds and refines human talent acts just like this; then the talents of Tang, Yu, and Glorious Zhou will be encountered morning and evening!

The Third Policy Question
Wu Zhengwei 吳正偉

Comment by Associate Examiner Assistant Instructor Yang: He examines and weighs Sima Qian 司馬遷, grasping his main outlines, while his diction directly follows in his footsteps. As for his desire to abridge and polish the Twenty-One Histories, it hits the vital points admirably. What high ambition!

Comment by Associate Examiner Instructor Jiang: Sima Qian's *Historical Records* stands alone in esteem; appraisals and criticisms in later ages have grown into a veritable forest. With the four discourses of Master Chengjing [?], they should be made to yield [?]. At the end, he further points out flaws in the Twenty-…

title: 萬曆十年廣東鄉試錄
text:
十一史欲加筆削咸得其大何謂申之當也
考試官敎諭胡批有史識而才足以發之
考試官敎諭陳批有多識有定見
史才之難自古記之若乃品隲𬝖林揚扢
述作豈不尤難矣哉自史遷出而其書彪
炳當世熠燿千載諸浚心之士各以其意
揚榷之至今日而闚闖龍門道路太史人
人能言之矣夫甲可乙否漫無指歸是一
鬨之市也白首習書索之茫如是女史之
===
授也傳耳和聲不綜終始是郢書之誤也
錯簡斷篇詮次不類是續鳧之譏也執事
慮之而欲諸生折衷其說生也鄙何足以
知之蓋聞之自昔治太史者有二家焉一
曰訓故若延篤音義徐廣音義裴駰集解
鄒誕生音義劉伯莊音義司馬貞索隱張
守節正義之類是已指專音釋窔奥未窺
然而錯節衍語昭昭然揭日月而行不可
廢也一曰評隲若班固之互見瑜瑕劉勰
punctuated:
十一史，欲加筆削，咸得其大。何謂申之當也？
考試官敎諭胡批：有史識，而才足以發之。
考試官敎諭陳批：有多識，有定見。
史才之難，自古記之。若乃品隲𬝖林，揚扢述作，豈不尤難矣哉！自史遷出，而其書彪炳當世，熠燿千載。諸浚心之士，各以其意揚榷之。至今日，而闚闖龍門，道路太史，人人能言之矣。夫甲可乙否，漫無指歸，是一鬨之市也；白首習書，索之茫如，是女史之授也；傳耳和聲，不綜終始，是郢書之誤也；錯簡斷篇，詮次不類，是續鳧之譏也。執事慮之，而欲諸生折衷其說，生也鄙，何足以知之？蓋聞之，自昔治太史者有二家焉：一曰訓故，若延篤《音義》、徐廣《音義》、裴駰《集解》、鄒誕生《音義》、劉伯莊《音義》、司馬貞《索隱》、張守節《正義》之類是已。指專音釋，窔奥未窺；然而錯節衍語，昭昭然揭日月而行，不可廢也。一曰評隲，若班固之互見瑜瑕、劉勰
translation_en:
… the Twenty-one Histories, wanting to edit and refine them—in all this he grasps the essentials. How fitting it is to expound on them!

Examiner and Instructor Hu comments: He possesses historical insight, and his talent suffices to bring it forth.

Examiner and Instructor Chen comments: He has broad learning and settled convictions.

The difficulty of possessing historical talent has been noted since antiquity. When it comes to evaluating the forest of literature and appraising historical writings, is that not even more difficult? Since Sima Qian (Shiqian 史遷) appeared, his work has shone brilliantly in his own age and gleamed across a thousand years. Scholars who delve deeply into it have each weighed and discussed it according to their own views. Down to the present day, peering into the Dragon Gate (Longmen 龍門, Sima Qian's birthplace) and talking along the roads about the Grand Scribe—everyone is able to speak of him. Yet when one person approves what another rejects, rambling without any settled conclusion, it is like a clamorous marketplace; when one studies a book until one's head turns white and yet seeks its meaning in vain, it is like the rote instruction of a female scribe; when one merely repeats what reaches the ear and echoes others' voices without synthesizing beginning and end, it is like the error of the letter from Ying; and when one forces together misplaced strips and broken chapters into an incongruous order, it invites the ridicule of lengthening a duck's legs. Your Honor is concerned about this and wishes us students to weigh and reconcile these views; yet I am crude and ignorant—how could I be adequate to know them?

Still, I have heard that since antiquity those who study the Grand Scribe have fallen into two schools. The first is called philological exegesis (xungu 訓故), such as the Pronunciation and Meaning (Yinyi 音義) by Yan Du 延篤, the Pronunciation and Meaning by Xu Guang 徐廣, the Collected Explanations (Jijie 集解) by Pei Yin 裴駰, the Pronunciation and Meaning by Zou Dansheng 鄒誕生, the Pronunciation and Meaning by Liu Bozhuang 劉伯莊, the Seeking the Obscure (Suoyin 索隱) by Sima Zhen 司馬貞, and the Correct Meaning (Zhengyi 正義) by Zhang Shoujie 張守節, and the like. Their aim is devoted exclusively to pronunciation and glosses, without peering into the deeper subtleties; yet through them knotted passages and superfluous words are made as bright and clear as holding up the sun and moon as one walks, so they cannot be dispensed with. The second is called critical evaluation (pingzhi 評隲), such as Ban Gu's 班固 showing both his merits and flaws, Liu Xie's 劉勰…

title: 萬曆十年廣東鄉試錄
text:
之多所褒予劉知幾史通備極詆訶蘇子
由古史尤多彈射以至譙周古史考褚元
量史記至言之類是已家爲同異人各牴
牾然其得與失相兼而不能相掩不可廢
也至于片語見褒單詞致貶不一而足其
謂史之失自遷固始記煩而志寡者文中
子也其謂以三千年之史籍而跼踖于七
八種之書恨其博不足者鄭樵也其謂先
黃老序游俠述貨殖有感其所遇有所激
===
而言之者晁無咎也其謂與善隱而彰懲
惡直而寬賤夷狄簡而明者蘇洵也其謂
多愛愛奇者秦觀也其謂博學善敘事傳
之簡牘千餘年而不磨滅者范祖禹也諸
如此類蓋無慮數百家未可更僕數愚竊
以爲論史多端而大致有三其嚴事史記
者高史遷之名而不敢有所齮龼豈惟順
之又從而爲之辭辭有未通務曲而傳之
于意意有未安務曲而證之于事轉相讚
punctuated: 之多所褒予，劉知幾《史通》備極詆訶，蘇子由《古史》尤多彈射，以至譙周《古史考》、褚元量《史記至言》之類是已。家爲同異，人各牴牾，然其得與失相兼而不能相掩，不可廢也。至于片語見褒，單詞致貶，不一而足。其謂史之失自遷、固始，記煩而志寡者，文中子也；其謂以三千年之史籍而跼踖于七八種之書，恨其博不足者，鄭樵也；其謂先黃老、序游俠、述貨殖，有感其所遇，有所激而言之者，晁無咎也；其謂與善隱而彰，懲惡直而寬，賤夷狄簡而明者，蘇洵也；其謂多愛愛奇者，秦觀也；其謂博學善敘事，傳之簡牘千餘年而不磨滅者，范祖禹也。諸如此類，蓋無慮數百家，未可更僕數。愚竊以爲論史多端，而大致有三。其嚴事《史記》者，高史遷之名，而不敢有所齮龼。豈惟順之，又從而爲之辭；辭有未通，務曲而傳之于意；意有未安，務曲而證之于事。轉相讚
translation_en:
… lavishing much praise, Liu Zhiji 劉知幾 in his Shitong 史通 (Comprehensive Perspectives on Historiography) exhausting all manner of harsh criticism, Su Ziyou 蘇子由 [Su Zhe 蘇轍] in his Gushi 古史 (Ancient History) leveling especially numerous attacks, and so on down to works such as Qiao Zhou's 譙周 Gushi kao 古史考 (Investigations of Ancient History) and Chu Yuanliang's 褚元量 [Chu Wuliang 褚無量] Shiji zhiyan 史記至言 (Ultimate Words on the Records of the Grand Historian). Each school has its agreements and differences, and each person contradicts the others; yet their merits and flaws coexist without obscuring one another, and they cannot be discarded.

As for those who offer praise in a brief phrase or censure in a single word, there are too many to count. He who said that the failings of historiography began with Sima Qian 司馬遷 and Ban Gu 班固, their narratives being prolix while their treatises were scant, was Master Wenzhong 文中子 [Wang Tong 王通]. He who said that with three thousand years of historical records Sima Qian confined himself narrowly to seven or eight books, regretting that his erudition was insufficient, was Zheng Qiao 鄭樵. He who said that in placing the Huang-Lao 黃老 school first, giving accounts of wandering knights-errant, and narrating the moneymakers, Sima Qian was moved by his own lot in life and spoke out of indignation, was Chao Wujiu 晁無咎 [Chao Buzhi 晁補之]. He who said that his commendation of the good is subtle yet manifest, his chastisement of evil forthright yet lenient, and his disparagement of the Yi 夷 and Di 狄 barbarians concise yet clear, was Su Xun 蘇洵. He who said that he loved much and loved the extraordinary was Qin Guan 秦觀. And he who said that he was erudite and skilled at narrating events, so that his work has been handed down on bamboo and wood for more than a thousand years without being effaced, was Fan Zuyu 范祖禹. Critics of this sort roughly number in the hundreds of schools and could not all be enumerated even if one changed attendants.

In my humble opinion, discussions of history have many facets, yet they fall roughly into three general tendencies. Those who revere the Shiji 史記 (Records of the Grand Historian) hold Sima Qian's name in high esteem and dare not find any fault with him. Not only do they defer to him, they go further and make excuses for him: where his wording does not make sense, they strive to twist it so as to attach it to some meaning; where his meaning is unsettling, they strive to twist it so as to substantiate it with facts. Passing along one another's eulogies…

title: 萬曆十年廣東鄉試錄
text:
述弗知其非此以意爲尊信者也寶夏后
氏之璜忘其考矣其詆毀史記者以史遷
雄眡千古而窺其所未軌於正以其雄眡
千古則務操其說而求勝以其未軌於正
則得乘其間而有所詆訾此以意爲詆訶
者也洗垢索其瘢痕吹毛求其瑕類矣其
信與疑半者則又執其片語隻字如覬若
講若之分蛟龍交龍之辨謂滅之字有力
謂後期勝後會等語此以款啓爲月旦者
===
也據大鼎而竊寸臠旣非全味執微類而
揜夜光亦未得矣故曰運千刃而後可以
飛碉操千曲而後可以聽聲談何容易哉
愚甞櫽括諸家參考聞見其可議者有四
而諸委瑣之談不與焉夫史以徵往信來
正名定分至不可紊也遷總之表志分爲
紀傳是矣而項羽則紀呂后則紀正統之
義何居陳勝則作世家孔子則作世家外
戚則作世家世繼之意奚取兵法一代之
punctuated: 述，弗知其非，此以意爲尊信者也，寶夏后氏之璜，忘其考矣。其詆毀《史記》者，以史遷雄眡千古，而窺其所未軌於正。以其雄眡千古，則務操其說而求勝；以其未軌於正，則得乘其間而有所詆訾。此以意爲詆訶者也，洗垢索其瘢痕，吹毛求其瑕類矣。其信與疑半者，則又執其片語隻字，如「覬若」、「講若」之分，「蛟龍」、「交龍」之辨，謂「滅之」字有力，謂「後期」勝「後會」等語。此以款啓爲月旦者也，據大鼎而竊寸臠，旣非全味；執微類而揜夜光，亦未得矣。故曰：「運千刃而後可以飛碉，操千曲而後可以聽聲。」談何容易哉！愚甞櫽括諸家，參考聞見，其可議者有四，而諸委瑣之談不與焉。夫史以徵往信來，正名定分，至不可紊也。遷總之表、志，分爲紀、傳，是矣；而項羽則紀，呂后則紀，正統之義何居？陳勝則作世家，孔子則作世家，外戚則作世家，世繼之意奚取？兵法，一代之…
translation_en: … repeat them without realizing their errors. These are people who revere and trust it out of personal bias; they treasure the semi-circular jade of the Lord of Xia while forgetting to examine its flaws. As for those who disparage the Records of the Grand Historian (Shiji), they see that Sima Qian (Shi Qian 史遷) looked out heroically over a thousand ages, yet they spy out the places where he failed to conform to orthodoxy. Because he looked out heroically over a thousand ages, they strive to wield their own arguments to get the better of him; because he failed to conform to orthodoxy, they are able to seize upon his gaps and heap slander and criticism upon him. These are people who disparage and scold out of personal bias; they wash away the dirt to search for scars, and blow aside the hairs to look for blemishes. As for those who half believe and half doubt, they fixate on single phrases and isolated words—such as the distinction between "peering as one" (ji ruo 覬若) and "harmonizing as one" (jiang ruo 講若), or the differentiation between "flood dragon" (jiaolong 蛟龍) and "intertwined dragons" (jiaolong 交龍), or claiming that the words "destroyed it" (mie zhi 滅之) are forceful, or saying that "a later appointed time" (hou qi 後期) is superior to "a later meeting" (hou hui 後會), and the like. These are people who pass critical judgments from a narrow, parochially informed view. Leaning over a great tripod to steal a one-inch slice of meat, one does not get the full flavor; seizing upon a tiny flaw to obscure a night-shining pearl, one also misses the mark. Therefore it is said: "Only after wielding a thousand blades can one carve [?] with flying skill; only after playing a thousand tunes can one truly understand music." How could discussing this be easy! I have surveyed and synthesized the various schools of thought and cross-referenced them with what I have heard and seen; there are four points in the work that are open to criticism, and those trivial, petty discussions are not among them. Now, history serves to verify the past and command belief in the future; in rectifying names and fixing statuses, it is most imperative that nothing be thrown into disorder. That Sima Qian synthesized things in the chronological tables (biao 表) and treatises (zhi 志) and divided them into basic annals (ji 紀) and biographies (zhuan 傳) was right. Yet he placed Xiang Yu 項羽 in the Basic Annals and Empress Lü (Lü Hou 呂后) in the Basic Annals—where does the principle of legitimate succession reside in this? He placed Chen Sheng 陳勝 in the Hereditary Houses (shijia 世家), Confucius (Kongzi 孔子) in the Hereditary Houses, and the Imperial In-laws (waiqi 外戚) in the Hereditary Houses—what sense of hereditary succession did he find in them? Military methods are a single era's…

title: 萬曆十年廣東鄉試錄
text:
重典也何以附于律書列傳賢否之衡鑑
也何以傳夫龜策序司馬相如于四夷之
後則詮次失宜大宛與南越諸夷不相序
次則分析何以此其體裁之宜議者一也
史貴闕文夫子志之理無足徵寧存而不
論乃高辛四妃皆以神異而生子虞舜見
阸遂以匿空而獲出文王之聖也而獻賄
以免臯伐崇以報忿何其誣也周公之聖
也而叔處之封竟以成人君之戲何其謬
===
也載后稷至文王凡十五世桉后稷始封
至文王卽位凡一千九十餘年則周之世
皆百餘歲以宰我爲臨淄大夫與田常作
亂夷其族則誤於闞止爲聖門羞此其綜
覈之宜議者二也史之詞有褒貶其權與
賞罰等而彰癉失眞世將何觀叡聖之篇
詩人所以詠武公也而謂其襲殺共伯后
兄之爭降王之對亞夫所以爲名臣也而
謂其守節不遜子貢居言語之科夫子蓋
punctuated: 重典也，何以附于《律書》？《列傳》，賢否之衡鑑也，何以傳夫《龜策》？序司馬相如于四夷之後，則詮次失宜；大宛與南越諸夷不相序次，則分析何以？此其體裁之宜議者一也。史貴闕文，夫子志之；理無足徵，寧存而不論。乃高辛四妃，皆以神異而生子；虞舜見阸，遂以匿空而獲出。文王之聖也，而獻賄以免臯，伐崇以報忿，何其誣也！周公之聖也，而叔處之封，竟以成人君之戲，何其謬也！載后稷至文王凡十五世，桉后稷始封至文王卽位，凡一千九十餘年，則周之世皆百餘歲？以宰我爲臨淄大夫，與田常作亂，夷其族，則誤於闞止，爲聖門羞。此其綜覈之宜議者二也。史之詞有褒貶，其權與賞罰等；而彰癉失眞，世將何觀？「叡聖」之篇，詩人所以詠武公也，而謂其襲殺共伯。后兄之爭、降王之對，亞夫所以爲名臣也，而謂其守節不遜。子貢居言語之科，夫子蓋
translation_en:
… momentous institution of an era—why attach it to the "Treatise on Pitch-pipes" (Lüshu)? The "Arrayed Traditions" (Liezhuan) are the balance and mirror for judging worthiness and unworthiness—why include a biography for "Turtle-shell and Milfoil Divination" (Guice)? Placing Sima 相如 (Sima Xiangru) after the four barbarian peoples shows an improper arrangement of order; when Dayuan is not grouped sequentially with Nanyue and the other foreign tribes, on what basis are they separated? This is the first point open to criticism: his structural format.

History values leaving blanks where evidence is lacking, as the Master recorded; when a principle cannot be sufficiently verified, it is better to preserve the matter without passing judgment. Yet the four consorts of Gaoxin are all said to have given birth to sons through miraculous anomalies; when Yu Shun was put in peril, he is said to have escaped through a hidden tunnel. Sage that King Wen was, to claim that he offered bribes to escape punishment and attacked Chong to avenge a personal grudge—how slanderous that is! Sage that the Duke of Zhou was, to claim that the enfeoffment of Shu Chu [Tang Shu Yu] was actually carried out to fulfill a ruler's jest—how absurd that is! He records that from Hou Ji to King Wen there were fifteen generations in all; yet if we examine the period from Hou Ji's initial enfeoffment to King Wen's accession to the throne, it spans more than one thousand and ninety years—would not every generation of the Zhou have lived over a hundred years [if not nearly a hundred]? And taking Zai Wo to be a Grand Master of Linzi who joined Tian Chang in rebellion and had his clan exterminated confuses him with Kan Zhi, bringing shame upon the Sage's school. This is the second point open to criticism: his verification of facts.

The words of history carry praise and blame, their authority equal to rewards and punishments; if the distinction between good and evil loses its truth, what will the world have to look to as a standard? The ode on the "perspicacious and sage" (Ruisheng) was composed by the poet to praise Duke Wu [of Wei], yet he claims that Duke Wu ambushed and murdered Gongbo. The dispute over enfeoffing the Empress's brother and the reply concerning the surrendered kings were the very reasons why [Zhou] Yafu was a renowned minister, yet he says that Yafu held to his integrity without humility. Zigong ranked in the category of speech and eloquence, and the Master indeed…

title: 萬曆十年廣東鄉試錄
text:
屢稱之而史遂夸飾其事如所稱存魯亂
齊破吳强晉業已厚誣何乃傳于貨殖使
聖門賢者與錙銖齷齪逐時俯仰之徒并
列郅都之爲中郎將野彘之爭引宗廟太
后之重其爲濟南守中尉道不拾遺貴臣
斂手何乃傳于酷吏使忠公之吏與椎埋
沈命舞文詆法之儔次比此其品隲之可
議者一也史之所重關治道則書裨世教
則書若徒以綺篇繡句彫章縟彩故可略
===
也董仲舒傳不載天人三策賈誼與屈原
同傳不載治安等書若長楊羽獵大人子
虛即義非奏雅詞可刪煩又孔子世家多
採論語舊說至管晏列傳則不錄其本書
以爲世俗所有夫諸子雜家經史外傳棄
而不錄微杜博聞此其甄錄之可議者一
也大抵持論則易授簡則難史如馬遷千
載讓傑焉彼其去古未遠其磅礴淳龐之
氣猶蘊崇而未漓故其文沉凝蘊藉渾厚
punctuated: 屢稱之，而史遂夸飾其事，如所稱「存魯、亂齊、破吳、强晉」，業已厚誣，何乃傳于《貨殖》，使聖門賢者與錙銖齷齪、逐時俯仰之徒并列？郅都之爲中郎將，野彘之爭，引宗廟太后之重；其爲濟南守、中尉，道不拾遺，貴臣斂手，何乃傳于《酷吏》，使忠公之吏與椎埋、沈命、舞文詆法之儔次比？此其品隲之可議者一也。史之所重，關治道則書，裨世教則書；若徒以綺篇繡句、彫章縟彩，故可略也。《董仲舒傳》不載《天人三策》，賈誼與屈原同傳，不載《治安》等書；若《長楊》、《羽獵》、《大人》、《子虛》，即義非奏雅，詞可刪煩。又《孔子世家》多採《論語》舊說，至《管晏列傳》，則不錄其本書，以爲世俗所有；夫諸子雜家、經史外傳，棄而不錄，微杜博聞？此其甄錄之可議者一也。大抵持論則易，授簡則難。史如馬遷，千載讓傑焉。彼其去古未遠，其磅礴淳龐之氣，猶蘊崇而未漓，故其文沉凝蘊藉，渾厚
translation_en:
…praised him repeatedly; yet the History proceeds to exaggerate and embellish his affairs. What it describes as "preserving Lu, throwing Qi into disorder, destroying Wu, and strengthening Jin" is already a grave slander—why then include his biography among the "Moneymakers" (Huozhi), placing a worthy of the Sage's school alongside petty, sordid fellows who haggle over trifles and bend with the times? When Zhi Du 郅都 served as Leader of Court Gentlemen (zhonglang jiang), in the dispute over the wild boar he invoked the weighty authority of the ancestral temple and the Empress Dowager; when he served as Grand Administrator (shou) of Jinan and Commandant of the Capital (zhongwei), no one picked up articles lost on the roads and noble ministers stayed their hands—why then include his biography among the "Harsh Officials" (Kuli), ranking a loyal and public-spirited official alongside grave-robbers, harborers of fugitives, and pettifoggers who pervert the law? This is one aspect in which its moral evaluation and ranking may be criticized.

What history values should be recorded if it concerns the way of governance, and recorded if it benefits public morals; if a work consists merely of華麗 chapters and embroidered phrases, carved compositions and ornate colors, it may well be omitted. Yet the "Biography of Dong Zhongshu" (Dong Zhongshu zhuan) does not include his three policy responses on Heaven and Man (Tianren sance), and Jia Yi 賈誼, sharing a biography with Qu Yuan 屈原, does not have his memorials on "Peace and Order" (Zhi'an) and the like included; whereas works like the "Changyang Palace" (Changyang), "Plume Hunt" (Yulie), "The Great Man" (Daren), and "Sir Fantasy" (Zixu), even though their meaning does not attain true elegance and their verbiage could be pruned of excess, are included [note: the former two are actually in the Han shu, though grouped here in the essay's critique]. Moreover, the "Hereditary House of Confucius" (Kongzi shijia) largely adopts old accounts from the Analects (Lunyu), yet when it comes to the "Biographies of Guan and Yan" (Guan Yan liezhuan), it does not record their actual books, on the grounds that the world already possesses them; if the various philosophers, miscellaneous schools, and outer traditions of the classics and histories are cast aside and not recorded, does this not close off broad learning? This is one aspect in which its selection of materials may be criticized.

On the whole, it is easy to hold forth in criticism, but difficult to take up the writing tablets oneself. Among historians, one like Sima Qian 司馬遷 must be yielded to as a towering figure for a thousand years. He was not yet far removed from antiquity, and its vast, pure, and abundant vital breath (qi) was still accumulated in him and had not yet grown thin; therefore his prose is deep, poised, and reserved, substantial and…

title: 萬曆十年廣東鄉試錄
text:
大雅後世淺中之士日規月摩而不能及
其覽矚千古感慨當世書無所不窺而神
有獨至故其文悲歌莽宕激卬悲壯後世
涂觀之士刻心滅志而不能及其浮江淮
上會稽探禹穴講業鄒魯名山大川無所
不歷故其文窮致極神翱翔變化後世耳
觀之士句摘字攻而不能及斯亦千載之
閱裁不朽之盛事也
今天下號稱郅隆而學士大夫爭爲古文辭
===
之業其博洽爾雅未必無足當司馬者而
又當史學大明前史之醇疵昭然在人耳
記得得以肆其力于藻飾而增損其事辭且
夫從古以來其躊駁可指固不獨一史記
也二十一史繁複過半或一事而代有志
述名異而詞襲或一人而各爲是非此抑
而彼揚則刪削宜嚴也漢末之董承耿紀
晉初之諸葛毋丘齊興而有劉康袁粲周
滅而有王謙尉迥殉身謀國大義凜然而
punctuated:
大雅，後世淺中之士，日規月摩而不能及；其覽矚千古，感慨當世，書無所不窺而神有獨至，故其文悲歌莽宕，激卬悲壯，後世涂觀之士，刻心滅志而不能及；其浮江淮，上會稽，探禹穴，講業鄒魯，名山大川無所不歷，故其文窮致極神，翱翔變化，後世耳觀之士，句摘字攻而不能及。斯亦千載之閱裁，不朽之盛事也。

今天下號稱郅隆，而學士大夫爭爲古文辭之業，其博洽爾雅，未必無足當司馬者。而又當史學大明，前史之醇疵，昭然在人耳記，得以肆其力于藻飾，而增損其事辭。且夫從古以來，其躊駁可指，固不獨一《史記》也。《二十一史》繁複過半：或一事而代有志述，名異而詞襲；或一人而各爲是非，此抑而彼揚，則刪削宜嚴也。漢末之董承、耿紀，晉初之諸葛、毋丘，齊興而有劉康、袁粲，周滅而有王謙、尉迥，殉身謀國，大義凜然，而
translation_en:
…and grandly elegant, such that shallow scholars of later ages, though imitating and polishing day and month, cannot match him. Gazing across a thousand ages and deeply moved by his own time, there was no book he did not peer into, and his spirit reached singular heights; thus his writing sings with sorrow and vast unrestrained sweep, rousing and tragic in its grandeur, such that superficial observers of later ages, though carving their hearts and exhausting their wills, cannot match him. He floated upon the Yangtze and Huai rivers, ascended Kuaiji, explored the Cave of Yu, lectured on learning in Zou and Lu, and there were no famous mountains or great rivers he did not traverse; thus his writing exhausts subtlety and reaches the utmost spirit, soaring and transforming, such that scholars of later ages who merely "observe with their ears," though picking at phrases and laboring over words, cannot match him. This too is a grand judgment for a thousand years, an immortal and glorious achievement!

Today the empire is acclaimed as supremely prosperous, and scholarly gentlemen and grandees vie in the pursuit of ancient-style prose (guwenci). In their broad learning and refined elegance, it is not necessarily the case that none are worthy of matching Sima Qian. Moreover, at a time when historical scholarship is brilliantly illuminated, the virtues and flaws of previous histories are crystal clear in people's ears and memories [? 耳記], allowing them to devote their full strength to literary refinement and to add to or trim the accounts and wording. Furthermore, from antiquity onward, the contradictions and impurities that can be pointed out are certainly not limited to the Records of the Grand Historian (Shiji) alone. More than half of the Twenty-One Histories (Ershiyi shi) is overly prolix and repetitive: sometimes a single matter is recorded across successive dynasties under different names but with plagiarized wording; sometimes a single person is judged differently by each, disparaged here and praised there—thus pruning and excision ought to be strict. Dong Cheng 董承 and Geng Ji 耿紀 at the end of the Han, Zhuge Dan 諸葛誕 and Guanqiu Jian 毌丘儉 at the beginning of the Jin, Liu Bing 劉秉 [transcribed 劉康] and Yuan Can 袁粲 at the rise of the Qi, and Wang Qian 王謙 and Yuchi Jiong 尉遲迥 [尉迥] at the fall of the Northern Zhou all sacrificed their lives in planning for the state, their great righteousness awe-inspiring, yet…

title: 萬曆十年廣東鄉試錄
text:
諸史俱以逆書則昭雪宜急也班范荀袁
之并紀漢王于之并紀晉徐裴之并紀宋
而體裁互異范曄以董宣爲酷吏陳壽以
諸葛亮非將才舊唐書以李義甫長孫無
忌爲伍而褒貶失真王喬鳧履出于風俗
通左慈羊鳴傳于抱朴子而引據未雅則
訂證宜急也諸如此類宜盡薈蕞而商榷
之成一家言執事謂難其人何也愚以天
下未嘗無人顧夫卓犖奇偉之才或沉伏
===
下僚或限於職業而不得當載筆之任則
其人難或志在名山沉淪思奮而不得並
窺石渠天祿之藏則其人難或書足譾聞
材堪授簡而不能以其力羅四方奇傑之
士各以所長見則其人難誠及此時自石
渠虎觀而外不靳別開一局以待天下文
學之士俾博學宏詞卓然當世者裁其總
而諸稱能染翰績學冢悉分局校讎充于
任使毋限以職業毋拘于隱顯毋計以歲
punctuated: 諸史俱以逆書，則昭雪宜急也。班、范、荀、袁之并紀漢，王、于之并紀晉，徐、裴之并紀宋，而體裁互異；范曄以董宣爲酷吏，陳壽以諸葛亮非將才，《舊唐書》以李義甫、長孫無忌爲伍，而褒貶失真；王喬鳧履出于《風俗通》，左慈羊鳴傳于《抱朴子》，而引據未雅，則訂證宜急也。諸如此類，宜盡薈蕞而商榷之，成一家言。執事謂難其人，何也？愚以天下未嘗無人。顧夫卓犖奇偉之才，或沉伏下僚，或限於職業，而不得當載筆之任，則其人難；或志在名山，沉淪思奮，而不得並窺石渠、天祿之藏，則其人難；或書足譾聞，材堪授簡，而不能以其力羅四方奇傑之士，各以所長見，則其人難。誠及此時，自石渠、虎觀而外，不靳別開一局，以待天下文學之士，俾博學宏詞卓然當世者裁其總，而諸稱能染翰績學冢，悉分局校讎，充于任使，毋限以職業，毋拘于隱顯，毋計以歲
translation_en: … yet all the histories record them as rebels, so exonerating them is an urgent priority. Ban Gu 班固, Fan Ye 范曄, Xun Yue 荀悅, and Yuan Hong 袁宏 all recorded the Han dynasty, Wang Yin 王隱 and Yu寶 (Gan Bao 干寶) [?] both recorded the Jin dynasty, and Xu Yuan 徐爰 and Pei Ziye 裴子野 both recorded the Song dynasty, yet their formats and styles differ from one another. Fan Ye classed Dong Xuan 董宣 among the harsh officials, Chen Shou 陳壽 deemed Zhuge Liang 諸葛亮 lacking in generalship, and the Old History of the Tang (Jiu Tangshu 舊唐書) placed Li Yifu 李義甫 and Zhangsun Wuji 長孫無忌 in the same company, so their praise and blame lost sight of the truth. The tale of Wang Qiao's 王喬 duck-shaped shoes comes from the Comprehensive Meaning of Customs (Fengsu tong 風俗通), and that of Zuo Ci 左慈 bleating like a sheep is transmitted in the Master Who Embraces Simplicity (Baopuzi 抱朴子), so their citations lack elegance; thus, emendation and verification are urgent priorities. All matters of this sort ought to be thoroughly gathered together and critically deliberated upon to form the coherent work of a single school. Why does Your Reverence say it is difficult to find the right person? In my humble view, the realm is never without capable men. Yet men of preeminent and extraordinary talent may be languishing in lowly posts or restricted by their official duties so that they cannot assume the responsibility of historiography—and thus finding the person is difficult. Or their ambitions may lie in composing works for posterity in "famous mountains," living in obscurity while yearning to rouse themselves, yet unable to gaze together upon the imperial collections of the Stone Canal Pavilion (Shiqu 石渠) and Heavenly Lu Pavilion (Tianlu 天祿)—and thus finding the person is difficult. Or they may possess learning sufficient to remedy shallow knowledge [?] and talent worthy of being handed the historian's tablets, yet lack the means on their own strength to gather the extraordinary scholars of the four quarters so that each may display his strengths—and thus finding the person is difficult. If indeed we seize this moment, and outside of the Stone Canal and White Tiger (Huguan 虎觀) Pavilions do not begrudge opening a separate bureau to await the literary scholars of the realm—allowing those of broad learning and grand composition who stand out in the present age to direct the overall compilation, while all those renowned as accomplished scholars skilled with the brush are assigned to sub-bureaus to collate and edit, filling the needed posts without restriction as to official profession, without regard to whether they are in retirement or in office, and without counting the years…

title: 萬曆十年廣東鄉試錄
text:
月俾上自羲皇迄于
本朝博而雅約而該以續詩書之際亦古今
一快事也而執事以爲可否
第四問
張萱
同考試官訓導鄭批譚錢法末有處置詳盡
若此者是識時務之士
考試□教諭胡批議論詳核足覩該博
考試官教諭陳批指陳利弊最切時宜
===
蓋經國理人者有衆與富之患而亦有旣
衆旣富之患古今所患者曰生齒未繁積
藏未豐斯二者小之乎其爲患也古之人
十年生聚十年教訓何憂於不衆惟林林
種種而衆矣饑之則亂食之則費故衆之
患甚於未衆者在弭亂而經費也一年餘
三年之積三年餘九年之積何憂於不富
惟煕煕穰穰而富矣專之則怨分之則竭
故富之患甚於未富者在釋怨而捄竭也
punctuated:
月，俾上自羲皇、迄于本朝，博而雅、約而該，以續《詩》、《書》之際，亦古今一快事也。而執事以爲可否？

第四問
張萱
同考試官訓導鄭批：譚錢法末有處置詳盡若此者，是識時務之士。
考試□教諭胡批：議論詳核，足覩該博。
考試官教諭陳批：指陳利弊，最切時宜。

蓋經國理人者，有衆與富之患，而亦有旣衆旣富之患。古今所患者，曰生齒未繁、積藏未豐，斯二者小之乎其爲患也。古之人，十年生聚，十年教訓，何憂於不衆？惟林林種種而衆矣，饑之則亂，食之則費；故衆之患甚於未衆者，在弭亂而經費也。一年餘三年之積，三年餘九年之積，何憂於不富？惟煕煕穰穰而富矣，專之則怨，分之則竭；故富之患甚於未富者，在釋怨而捄竭也。
translation_en:
… months and years, so that from the august Fuxi in antiquity down to our reigning dynasty, the work may be broad yet refined, concise yet comprehensive, continuing the tradition of the Book of Odes (Shi) and the Book of Documents (Shu)—truly this would be one of the most gratifying achievements of past or present! Does Your Excellency consider this feasible or not?

Fourth Policy Essay
By Zhang Xuan 張萱

Comment by Associate Examiner and Assistant Instructor Zheng 鄭: In discussing monetary policy, none has set forth measures at the end as thoroughly as this [Note: 末 may be a misprint for 未, "there has never been one whose proposed measures are as thorough as this"]; he is a scholar who understands the affairs of the times.
Comment by Examiner [□] and Instructor Hu 胡: The argumentation is detailed and well-verified, amply demonstrating his broad learning.
Comment by Examiner and Instructor Chen 陳: He points out the advantages and abuses in a way most pertinent to the needs of the present day.

Those who govern the state and order the people face the worry of making the population numerous and wealthy, yet they also face the worry of what to do once the population is already numerous and already wealthy. What people past and present have worried about is that the population is not yet thriving and the state's reserves are not yet abundant—but how minor a worry these two things actually are! Among the ancients, with ten years of population growth and gathering of resources, and ten years of instruction and training, what worry was there of not having a numerous populace? It is only when the people have multiplied in dense, teeming multitudes that if they are left hungry they will rebel, whereas if they are fed it will drain resources; therefore, the reason the worry of a numerous populace is worse than that of a sparse one lies in quelling rebellion and managing expenditures. When three years of labor leave one year's surplus of provisions, and nine years leave three years' surplus, what worry is there of not having wealth? It is only when the realm bustles in prosperous abundance and has become wealthy that if wealth is monopolized it breeds resentment, whereas if it is distributed it becomes exhausted; therefore, the reason the worry of wealth is worse than that of poverty lies in dispelling resentment and preventing exhaustion.

title: 萬曆十年廣東鄉試錄
text:
故夫豪傑之士所爲愁心積慮而講者莫
如食而分之食而分之者非朝饔之夕飧
之家給而戶賜之也蓋有道焉其在
今日則錢法所宜亟講者古昔盛時庶人家
授田百畝食鹽自丈夫至嬰兒月有數年
七十至九十饋肉有差家三幼以上至五
幼復征予葆凡三等此四者古人所以安
眾與富之道今皆不然然則古之民寡今
之民眾寡者富在於民而眾者富在於官
===
加之田不益毛海不益鹺國中之老者幼
者遞死遞生蕃育滋庶此不食而分之以
振其乏絕匪亂則怨徒食而分之而短於
經計匪費則竭司計者之憂也
明興餘二百年
高皇帝仁厚儉勤垂麻甚盛廓培厎於
列聖九有熙洽
聖天子蠲其
大德以覆露之自
punctuated:
故夫豪傑之士，所爲愁心積慮而講者，莫如食而分之。食而分之者，非朝饔之、夕飧之，家給而戶賜之也，蓋有道焉。其在今日，則錢法所宜亟講者。古昔盛時，庶人家授田百畝；食鹽自丈夫至嬰兒，月有數；年七十至九十，饋肉有差；家三幼以上至五幼，復征予葆，凡三等。此四者，古人所以安眾與富之道，今皆不然。然則古之民寡，今之民眾；寡者富在於民，而眾者富在於官。加之田不益毛，海不益鹺，國中之老者、幼者，遞死遞生，蕃育滋庶。此不食而分之，以振其乏絕，匪亂則怨；徒食而分之，而短於經計，匪費則竭，司計者之憂也。
明興餘二百年，高皇帝仁厚儉勤，垂麻甚盛，廓培厎於列聖，九有熙洽，聖天子蠲其大德以覆露之，自
translation_en:
Therefore, what men of extraordinary talent ponder with anxious hearts and accumulated deliberation and discuss is nothing other than feeding the populace and distributing wealth to them. Feeding them and distributing wealth to them does not mean providing them with morning and evening meals, or supplying every family and bestowing gifts upon every household; rather, there is a proper way to do it. In the present day, it is the monetary system that ought to be urgently discussed. In the flourishing times of antiquity, each commoner family was granted a hundred mu of land; for edible salt, from adult men down to infants, there was a monthly quota; for those aged seventy to ninety, gifts of meat were given in graded amounts; and for families with three to five young children, there were exemptions from levies and provisions of wet nurses, in three grades in all. These four measures were the means by which the ancients pacified a numerous and wealthy populace, yet none of them are practiced today. Even so, the people of antiquity were few, whereas the people of today are numerous; when they were few, wealth resided among the people, whereas when they are numerous, wealth resides with the state. Added to this, the fields do not yield more grain, nor does the sea yield more salt, while the old and the young within the realm die and are born in turn, multiplying into an ever greater multitude. Under these circumstances, if we do not feed them and distribute wealth to them so as to relieve their destitution, if they do not rebel, they will harbor resentment; yet if we merely feed them and distribute wealth to them while falling short in long-term fiscal planning, if it is not wasteful, it will lead to exhaustion—this is the worry of those in charge of fiscal administration.
More than two hundred years since the rise of the Ming, the August Emperor Gao, benevolent, generous, frugal, and diligent, bequeathed most abundant blessings [? 垂麻, for 垂休], which were broadened and cultivated down through the successive sage emperors, bringing peace and harmony to the Nine Provinces. His Sacred Majesty the Son of Heaven manifests his great virtue to shelter and nourish them; from…

title: 萬曆十年廣東鄉試錄
text:
海鎮界於山谷晝登雲梯夜設雲火以伺
賊出入士卒不多恐詒內地憂耳嗟乎此
二說者東粵之守也其在嘉隆之際則然
今日之粵母敢攻我土者可以守可以無
守故其議守也異於昔日必守之時蓋甞
以秦漢事叅之秦併天下略定楊粵置南
海象郡以謫徙民粵漸以亂任囂首事趙
佗阻兵馴至嘉德函封漢節粵大亂矣元
鼎之初樓船戈船出師十萬定爲九郡粵
===
漸以治其後輯寧終漢不叛至建武間蠻
里張游來獻白雉封歸漢君粵大治矣夫
十萬之師可以攻元鼎之虜而不可徵於
建武之際樓船之將可以斬亂越之呂嘉
而不可加歸漢之張游繇斯以談而今日
粵中之戰守其槩可論已夫粵豈忘戰之
國哉而當久創之餘民始息肩則鵰勦不
可廢而大征不可屢何以明之四面合圍
獸窮之攫可虞也千里輓車脫巾之呼可
punctuated: 海鎮界於山谷，晝登雲梯，夜設雲火，以伺賊出入，士卒不多，恐詒內地憂耳。嗟乎！此二說者，東粵之守也，其在嘉、隆之際則然。今日之粵，毋敢攻我土者，可以守，可以無守，故其議守也，異於昔日必守之時。蓋甞以秦、漢事叅之：秦併天下，略定楊粵，置南海、象郡，以謫徙民，粵漸以亂。任囂首事，趙佗阻兵，馴至嘉、德函封漢節，粵大亂矣。元鼎之初，樓船、戈船出師十萬，定爲九郡，粵漸以治。其後輯寧，終漢不叛。至建武間，蠻里張游來獻白雉，封歸漢君，粵大治矣。夫十萬之師，可以攻元鼎之虜，而不可徵於建武之際；樓船之將，可以斬亂越之呂嘉，而不可加歸漢之張游。繇斯以談，而今日粵中之戰守，其槩可論已。夫粵豈忘戰之國哉？而當久創之餘，民始息肩，則鵰勦不可廢，而大征不可屢。何以明之？四面合圍，獸窮之攫可虞也；千里輓車，脫巾之呼可
translation_en:
…the coastal garrisons border on mountain valleys; by day they climb scaling ladders to keep watch, and by night they set up signal fires to spy on the bandits' comings and goings. Because the soldiers are not numerous, one fears leaving trouble for the interior. Alas! These two views concern the defense of Eastern Yue [Guangdong], and they held true during the Jiajing (1522–1566) and Longqing (1567–1572) eras. In Guangdong today, there is no one who dares to attack our territory; it may be defended, or it may go without defense [母 read as 毋]. Therefore, discussing defense today is different from former times when defense was imperative.

I have tried to examine this by comparing it with the affairs of the Qin and Han dynasties. When Qin unified the empire, it pacified Yangyue and established Nanhai and Xiang commanderies, populating them with exiled convicts; Yue gradually fell into disorder. Ren Xiao 任囂 initiated autonomy and Zhao Tuo 趙佗 relied on military force to hold the passes, which gradually led to Lü Jia 呂嘉 and King Jian De 建德 sealing up the Han envoy's credentials [? or enclosing heads/seals in a box], and Yue fell into great chaos. At the beginning of the Yuanding era (116–111 BCE), the Tower-Ship and Halberd-Ship Generals led an army of a hundred thousand, settling the region into nine commanderies, and Yue gradually became well-governed. Thereafter it was peaceful and tranquil, not rebelling for the remainder of the Western Han. By the Jianwu era (25–56 CE), Zhang You 張游 of the Manli 蠻里 tribes came to present a white pheasant and was enfeoffed as Lord Who Submits to Han (Guihan jun 歸漢君), and Yue achieved great order.

Now, an army of a hundred thousand could be used to attack the enemies of the Yuanding era, but should not be levied during the Jianwu period; the Tower-Ship General could be used to behead Lü Jia who threw Yue into rebellion, but should not be set upon Zhang You who submitted to the Han. Discussing it from this perspective, the general outline of offense and defense in Guangdong today can be assessed. How could Guangdong be a region that forgets warfare? Yet in the aftermath of prolonged trauma, when the people are just beginning to rest their shoulders, swift pinpoint raids (diaojiao 鵰勦) cannot be abandoned, whereas massive campaigns (dazheng 大征) must not be repeatedly launched. How can this be made clear? When surrounded on all four sides, the desperate clawing of a cornered beast is to be feared; when hauling supply carts for a thousand li, the mutinous cries of soldiers stripping off their headcloths are to be…

title: 萬曆十年廣東鄉試錄
text:
鑄無若西漢二賈誼之言曰銅畢歸於上
山之言曰民不應與主共柄今姦民私鑄
陰持主柄以厲公錢果如誼言上收銅勿
令布民安所得銅而私鑄之故收銅之說
持柄息姦之要術也
高皇帝始定天下
令軍民惟鑄鑑及軍器一切廢銅並收之官
毋私藏無何寢罷至於今浮屠瞿曇與夫
齊民之鏞鈃銷盇大氐亡慮皆銅矣今將
===
剏焉而奪民銅則民駭貿以金則時絀儻
於
京師及三輔諸路支郡各責一官與民市銅
售之錢視銅之直私藏者罪無赦大約可
一歲收盡民銅民以銅得錢而可無私藏
罪其誰不欣然而輸之官官以錢得銅而
可為續鑄貲又何憚而不收之民況藏銅
于民銅直銅也而姦鑄有訾銅一入官銅
盡錢也而經用益饒
punctuated: 鑄，無若西漢二賈：誼之言曰「銅畢歸於上」，山之言曰「民不應與主共柄」。今姦民私鑄，陰持主柄以厲公錢。果如誼言，上收銅勿令布，民安所得銅而私鑄之？故收銅之說，持柄息姦之要術也。高皇帝始定天下，令軍民惟鑄鑑及軍器，一切廢銅並收之官，毋私藏。無何寢罷，至於今，浮屠瞿曇與夫齊民之鏞、鈃、銷、盇，大氐亡慮皆銅矣。今將剏焉而奪民銅，則民駭；貿以金，則時絀。儻於京師及三輔、諸路支郡，各責一官與民市銅，售之錢視銅之直，私藏者罪無赦，大約可一歲收盡民銅。民以銅得錢，而可無私藏罪，其誰不欣然而輸之官？官以錢得銅，而可為續鑄貲，又何憚而不收之民？況藏銅于民，銅直銅也，而姦鑄有訾；銅一入官，銅盡錢也，而經用益饒。
translation_en: … minting, nothing compares to the two Jias of the Western Han: Jia Yi 賈誼 said, "All copper should return to the sovereign," and Jia Shan 賈山 said, "The common people should not share the handle of authority with the ruler." Today, unscrupulous people engage in illicit minting, secretly grasping the ruler's handle of authority to the detriment of official coinage. If indeed, as Jia Yi advised, the sovereign collects all copper and does not allow it to circulate, where would the people obtain copper to mint illicitly? Therefore, the policy of collecting copper is a vital art for holding the handle of authority and putting an end to villainy. When the Exalted Emperor (Gao Huangdi 高皇帝, i.e., Emperor Taizu) first pacified the realm, he decreed that soldiers and civilians could cast only mirrors and military weapons, while all scrap copper was to be collected by the government, with private hoarding forbidden. Before long this lapsed, and down to the present day, Buddhist statues and bells, together with the cauldrons, vessels, pans, and bowls of the common people, are generally speaking almost all made of copper. If we now abruptly seize the people's copper, the people will be alarmed; if we purchase it with silver, current finances are straitened. Suppose that in the Capital, its surrounding prefectures, and the branch commanderies of the various circuits, one official is charged in each place with buying copper from the people, paying for it in cash according to the value of the copper, while those who hoard it privately are punished without pardon; within roughly a year, all the people's copper could be completely collected. When the people obtain cash for their copper and can avoid the crime of private hoarding, who among them would not gladly deliver it to the authorities? And when the government obtains copper for its cash, which can then serve as capital for continued minting, why should it hesitate to collect it from the people? Moreover, when copper is stored among the people, copper is merely copper, and illicit minting causes harm; once copper enters the government, all copper becomes money, and regular state expenditures will be ever more abundantly supplied. …

title: 萬曆十年廣東鄉試錄
text:
聖主所爲持大枋澹公私無先此畫者故銅之
權不可不收也黄帝封銅山令十里外乗
者行行者趨齊桓公封銅山令犯者左足
入刖左足右足入刖右今滇中之銅估人得
擅回易而盗相者罪止戍姦鑄者何慮無
銅今欲禁姦鑄則亡如封銅山而嚴盗相
令俾回易者亡得擅卽有項梁蔡木之徒
無自逞今故銅之源不可不固也或曰天
地之利不導之而封之何也曰非也法錢
===
未布則閉之以塞姦法錢旣流則開之以
疏利顧今之銅止滇南一隅隘矣山海經
曰海內銅山四百六十七漢鄧通鑄於嚴
道吳王鑄於豫章唐鑄於陝宣衢信銅冶
九十六宋鑄於諸路銅冶百三十六
國初
令天下行省置寶泉局
文皇帝
遣官於江浙閩廣鑄錢宣德間始罷採信饒銅
punctuated: 聖主所爲持大枋、澹公私，無先此畫者。故銅之權，不可不收也。黄帝封銅山，令十里外乗者行，行者趨；齊桓公封銅山，令犯者左足入刖左足，右足入刖右。今滇中之銅，估人得擅回易，而盗相者罪止戍，姦鑄者何慮無銅？今欲禁姦鑄，則亡如封銅山而嚴盗相令，俾回易者亡得擅，卽有項梁、蔡木之徒，無自逞今。故銅之源，不可不固也。或曰：「天地之利，不導之而封之，何也？」曰：「非也。法錢未布，則閉之以塞姦；法錢旣流，則開之以疏利。顧今之銅，止滇南一隅，隘矣。《山海經》曰：『海內銅山四百六十七。』漢鄧通鑄於嚴道，吳王鑄於豫章；唐鑄於陝、宣、衢、信，銅冶九十六；宋鑄於諸路，銅冶百三十六。國初，令天下行省置寶泉局；文皇帝遣官於江、浙、閩、廣鑄錢，宣德間始罷採信、饒銅，
translation_en: Among all that the Sage Ruler does to hold the great handle of authority and provide sufficiently for both the state and the public, no plan takes precedence over this. Therefore, control over copper must be reclaimed by the state. The Yellow Emperor sealed off the copper mountains, ordering that within ten li outside them, those riding in carriages had to walk, and those walking had to hurry past; Duke Huan of Qi (Qi Huan gong 齊桓公) sealed off the copper mountains, ordering that offenders who entered with their left foot should have their left foot amputated, and those who entered with their right foot should have their right amputated. Today, merchants are allowed to freely trade in the copper of Yunnan (Dian 滇), and those who illicitly prospect for mines are punished no more severely than with military exile—why then would illicit minters ever worry about lacking copper? If we now wish to prohibit illicit minting, nothing is better than sealing off the copper mountains and making strict the laws against illicit prospecting, so that traders cannot act on their own authority; then even if there were men of the ilk of Xiang Liang 項梁 or Cai Mu 蔡木 [?], they would have no way to indulge their schemes today. Therefore, the source of copper must be secured. Someone may ask: "Why seal off the bounties of Heaven and Earth instead of channeling them?" The answer is: Not so. When statutory cash has not yet been distributed, one closes the mines in order to block illicit activity; once statutory cash is in circulation, one opens them in order to let the benefits flow. Yet today's copper comes only from the single corner of southern Yunnan, which is far too narrow. The Classic of Mountains and Seas (Shanhai jing 山海經) says: "Within the seas there are four hundred and sixty-seven copper mountains." In the Han, Deng Tong 鄧通 minted coins at Yandao 嚴道, and the Prince of Wu (Wu wang 吳王) minted at Yuzhang 豫章; the Tang minted in Shan 陝, Xuan 宣, Qu 衢, and Xin 信 prefectures, with ninety-six copper smelters; the Song minted across the various circuits (lu 路), with one hundred and thirty-six copper smelters. At the beginning of our dynasty, the branch provinces (xingsheng 行省) of the empire were ordered to establish Coinage Services (Baoquan ju 寶泉局); Emperor Wen (Wen Huangdi 文皇帝, the Yongle Emperor) dispatched officials to mint coins in Jiangxi, Zhejiang, Fujian, and Guangdong (Jiang, Zhe, Min, Guang 江浙閩廣), and it was only during the Xuande 宣德 reign (1426–1435) that the mining of copper in Xin 信 and Rao 饒 prefectures was halted—…

title: 萬曆十年廣東鄉試錄
text:
則銅非僅產於滇也儻盡籍天下銅山倣
漢唐宋故事卽山鑄錢則天地之銅盡爲
國計故銅之利不可不開也善乎孔顗之言
曰民之盜鑄嚴法不能禁者由上惜銅愛
工故也上之惜銅愛工者曰鑄錢利國錢
成之利不足償工非也王者以四海爲家
費百萬以鑄百萬則二百萬費千萬以鑄
千萬則二千萬何契契乎錙兩之較也第
顗之說則又有未盡者不惜銅似矣不擇
===
銅而定其衡則雜不愛工似矣不擇工而
峻其防則疎銅者錢之質也蒼則蒼黃則
黃而誰能違之輕重者錢之衡也四銖則
太輕六銖則太重而誰能準之工者錢之
範而弊之藪也模不模範不範而誰能覈
之故惟不雜錫镴以虧其肉好獨留五銖
以一其耳目擇二局之良者分遣諸路爲
工倕而高垣墉嚴干擥以稽其姦挾斯弊
袪範良矣故錢之制貴精也夫錢泉也流
punctuated: 則銅非僅產於滇也。儻盡籍天下銅山，倣漢、唐、宋故事，卽山鑄錢，則天地之銅盡爲國計，故銅之利不可不開也。善乎孔顗之言曰：「民之盜鑄嚴法不能禁者，由上惜銅愛工故也。」上之惜銅愛工者，曰鑄錢利國，錢成之利不足償工。非也。王者以四海爲家，費百萬以鑄百萬，則二百萬；費千萬以鑄千萬，則二千萬。何契契乎錙兩之較也？第顗之說則又有未盡者：不惜銅似矣，不擇銅而定其衡則雜；不愛工似矣，不擇工而峻其防則疎。銅者，錢之質也，蒼則蒼，黃則黃，而誰能違之？輕重者，錢之衡也，四銖則太輕，六銖則太重，而誰能準之？工者，錢之範而弊之藪也，模不模，範不範，而誰能覈之？故惟不雜錫镴以虧其肉好，獨留五銖以一其耳目，擇二局之良者分遣諸路爲工倕，而高垣墉、嚴干擥以稽其姦挾，斯弊袪範良矣。故錢之制貴精也。夫錢，泉也。流
translation_en: …thus copper is not produced solely in Yunnan. If we were to register all the copper mountains in the empire and, following the precedents of the Han, Tang, and Song dynasties, mint coins right at the mountains, then all the copper between heaven and earth would serve the state's finances; therefore, the profit of copper must be opened up. Excellent indeed are the words of Kong Yi 孔顗: "That the people's illicit minting cannot be stopped even by severe laws is because the ruler begrudges copper and spares labor." Those above who begrudge copper and spare labor say that minting coins is meant to profit the state, and if the profit from the finished coins is insufficient to compensate for the labor, it is wrong. Yet a true king takes all within the four seas as his household: if he spends a million to cast a million, there are two million; if he spends ten million to cast ten million, there are twenty million. Why fret so anxiously over comparingmere fractions of an ounce? However, Kong Yi's theory still leaves something unsaid: not begrudging copper seems right, yet if one does not select the copper and fix its weight standard, the coins will be adulterated; not sparing labor seems right, yet if one does not select the artisans and heighten precautions against them, oversight will be lax. Copper is the substance of the coin: if it is greenish, it stays greenish; if yellow, it stays yellow—who can go against it? Weight is the standard of the coin: four zhu is too light, and six zhu is too heavy—who can standardize it? The artisans are the molders of the coins and the very hotbed of abuses: if the matrices are not true matrices and the molds are not true molds, who can verify them? Therefore, only by not mixing in tin or pewter to mar the coin's body and center hole, retaining the five-zhu weight alone to unify what people see and hear, selecting skilled artisans from the two bureaus and dispatching them to the various circuits as master craftsmen, and building high walls and enforcing strict patrols to inspect for smuggling and fraud—only then will abuses be eliminated and the casting be of fine quality. Thus, the system of coinage values refinement. Now, coins (qian 錢) are like a flowing spring (quan 泉). If they flow…

title: 萬曆十年廣東鄉試錄
text:
於下而壅於上行於賤而閡於貴卽日肆
人於市無以為也志曰天用莫如龍地用
莫如馬人用莫如龜此言用錢之涂不可
狹也漢隆慮主以錢千萬為其子贖死今
鍰金獨不可入乎漢律人出一筭筭百二
十錢今民賦獨不可入乎漢募豪民入粟
縣官而內錢於都內今開納獨不可入乎
漢館陶主為其子求郎不許賞錢千萬今
賞賚貴戚閹尹獨不可予乎漢胡降者贍以少
===
府禁錢今諸邊夷市獨不可予乎漢時時
出內庫錢賜軍士今養軍獨不可予乎夫
錢下而不上則其權在市井上而下下而
上則其權在
朝廷誠用之如循環行之如流水上闢其出
之涂若
賜予若吏祿若雇直無不以下下闢其入之涂
若軍興若筭事若鍰贖無不以上何不行
足慮故錢之涂貴廣也周立九府則周公
punctuated: 於下而壅於上，行於賤而閡於貴，卽日肆人於市，無以為也。《志》曰：「天用莫如龍，地用莫如馬，人用莫如龜。」此言用錢之涂不可狹也。漢隆慮主以錢千萬為其子贖死，今鍰金獨不可入乎？漢律，人出一筭，筭百二十錢，今民賦獨不可入乎？漢募豪民入粟縣官，而內錢於都內，今開納獨不可入乎？漢館陶主為其子求郎，不許，賞錢千萬，今賞賚貴戚、閹尹，獨不可予乎？漢胡降者，贍以少府禁錢，今諸邊夷市，獨不可予乎？漢時時出內庫錢賜軍士，今養軍獨不可予乎？夫錢，下而不上，則其權在市井；上而下，下而上，則其權在朝廷。誠用之如循環，行之如流水，上闢其出之涂，若賜予、若吏祿、若雇直，無不以下；下闢其入之涂，若軍興、若筭事、若鍰贖，無不以上，何不行足慮？故錢之涂貴廣也。周立九府，則周公
translation_en: … among those below yet is blocked from reaching those above, or circulates among the humble yet is obstructed among the noble, then even if one were to execute people in the marketplace every day, nothing could be accomplished. The *Treatise* says: "For Heaven's use nothing compares to the dragon; for Earth's use nothing compares to the horse; for human use nothing compares to tortoise shell and coin." This means that the channels for using coin must not be narrow. In the Han, Princess Longlü paid ten million coins to redeem her son from death; today, can judicial redemption fines alone not be paid in coin? Under the Han statutes, each person paid one poll-tax unit (suan), and a unit was one hundred and twenty coins; today, can the people's taxes alone not be paid in coin? The Han recruited wealthy commoners to deliver grain to the state and deposit coins in the Capital Treasury; today, can contributions for office or title alone not be paid in coin? In the Han, when Princess Guantao requested an appointment as Court Gentleman for her son, the emperor refused her but rewarded her with ten million coins; today, in bestowing rewards upon imperial relatives and palace eunuchs, can coin alone not be given? In the Han, surrendered northern tribesmen were supported with Privy Purse funds from the Lesser Treasury; today, at the frontier markets with foreign tribes, can coin alone not be given? The Han from time to time disbursed coins from the Inner Treasuries to reward soldiers; today, in maintaining the army, can coin alone not be given? Now with coin, if it goes down from above but does not come back up, then control over it rests with the marketplace; if it goes down from above and comes up from below, then control over it rests with the Royal Court.
