If indeed it is used like a revolving cycle and made to circulate like flowing water—with those above opening up the channels for its disbursement, such as imperial bestowals, officials' salaries, and wages for hired labor, so that all of it goes down; and those below opening up the channels for its receipt, such as military requisitions, poll and property assessments, and redemption fines, so that all of it goes up—then how could failure to circulate be worth worrying about? Therefore, in the channels for coin, breadth is what is valued. When the Zhou established the Nine Treasury Offices, the Duke of Zhou …

title: 萬曆十年廣東鄉試錄
text:
親親重其祿可也以厲百官豐其餼可也以軍
需優其直可也以寧元元減其筭可也不
人食而飽不家分而給彌其亂而經其費
什其怨而救其竭所謂民衆國富霸王之
本則由斯術也哉范子曰府倉實民庶殷
無曠其衆以爲亂梯時將有反事將有間
必有以務天地之恒制乃可以有天下之
成利□自侫范子生今之時譚今之事其
所謂恒制成利者必曰錢法也
===
第五問
市蔡德璋
同考試官訓導楊批粵苦用兵亦不能去兵
讀子策可佐經略一籌矣
考試官教諭胡批鑿鑿可行誦之練服
考試官教諭陳批畫粤事切中機會
今天下言粤事者殊矣異日者嶺東西間
莽爲盜區海以外諸孽句引外夷躙中土
主上南顧廑
punctuated:
親親重其祿可也，以厲百官豐其餼可也，以軍需優其直可也，以寧元元減其筭可也。不人食而飽，不家分而給，彌其亂而經其費，什其怨而救其竭，所謂「民衆國富，霸王之本」，則由斯術也哉！范子曰：「府倉實，民庶殷，無曠其衆以爲亂梯。時將有反，事將有間，必有以務天地之恒制，乃可以有天下之成利。」□自侫，范子生今之時，譚今之事，其所謂恒制成利者，必曰錢法也。

第五問
市蔡德璋
同考試官訓導楊批：粵苦用兵，亦不能去兵。讀子策，可佐經略一籌矣。
考試官教諭胡批：鑿鑿可行，誦之練服。
考試官教諭陳批：畫粤事切中機會。

今天下言粤事者殊矣。異日者，嶺東西間莽爲盜區，海以外諸孽句引外夷，躙中土，主上南顧，廑
translation_en:
…to show affection for imperial kinsmen, it is permissible to increase their emoluments; to encourage the hundred officials, it is permissible to make their stipends generous; for military supplies, it is permissible to offer favorable prices; and to bring peace to the common people, it is permissible to reduce their poll taxes. Without feeding each person individually, all are full; without distributing to each household, all are supplied; settling disorders while managing expenditures, soothing grievances [?] while rescuing the state from exhaustion—what is called "a populous citizenry and a wealthy state, the foundation of hegemonic and kingly rule" comes about through this very method! Master Fan [Fan Li 范蠡] said: "When treasuries and granaries are full and the common people are prosperous, do not leave the multitude idle to become a stepping-stone to rebellion. Times will have their reversals, and affairs will have their openings; one must attend to the constant regulations of Heaven and Earth before one can possess the established benefits of the empire." [?] Speaking modestly of myself [?], if Master Fan were born in the present age and discussed present affairs, what he called "constant regulations and established benefits" would surely refer to the monetary system!

Question Five
Cai Dezhang 蔡德璋 [?]
Comment by Associate Examiner Assistant Instructor Yang 楊: Guangdong suffers from the use of troops, yet it also cannot do away with troops. Reading your policy essay, it could assist our strategic planning with a worthy scheme.
Comment by Examiner Instructor Hu 胡: Concrete and practicable; reciting it commands admiration for its seasoned mastery [?].
Comment by Examiner Instructor Chen 陳: Its planning for Guangdong affairs hits the mark at the crucial juncture.

Today, those in the empire who speak of the affairs of Guangdong find a very different situation. In former days, the regions east and west of the Ranges were overgrown into dens of bandits, while beyond the seas various miscreants colluded with foreign barbarians to trample the central lands. His Majesty looked southward with concern, anxiously…

title: 萬曆十年廣東鄉試錄
text:
宵旰籌之比者文武大吏奉
上威靈
廟堂指筭剗茀而芟夷之今其時勢大殊往昔
山箐不揭竿瀚海無波民耒耜徧山谷島
嶼商帆絡繹來薄卽伏波樓船而在且卷
舌不道臨蔡將梁事蓋稱底定已迺執事
猶斤斤然度勢議時辨征勦之利患校水
陸之存留此治世之先憂忠臣之長慮也
而愚何敢無說以對蓋聞之戰無論大小
===
識時者勝兵無論衆寡因地者强時者戰
之機也而地者兵之形也機之所伏有微
有著故其戰殊有勍敵逋寇千人成權萬
人成武而谿肆稱雄者不可以小眢之有
乘隙竊發匿形坳澤却笠山林而隨撲隨
滅者不必以大誅之各隨其機之所宜而
已形之所在有險有夷故其守異有平原
廣埜無羊腸鋸齒之險進不必郛圍退不
必亭障而可以不失其險者不必以多守
punctuated: 宵旰，籌之。比者文武大吏奉上威靈、廟堂指筭，剗茀而芟夷之。今其時勢大殊往昔：山箐不揭竿，瀚海無波，民耒耜徧山谷，島嶼商帆絡繹來薄，卽伏波、樓船而在，且卷舌不道臨蔡將梁事，蓋稱底定已。迺執事猶斤斤然度勢議時，辨征勦之利患，校水陸之存留，此治世之先憂，忠臣之長慮也，而愚何敢無說以對？蓋聞之：戰無論大小，識時者勝；兵無論衆寡，因地者强。時者，戰之機也；而地者，兵之形也。機之所伏，有微有著，故其戰殊：有勍敵逋寇，千人成權，萬人成武，而谿肆稱雄者，不可以小眢之；有乘隙竊發，匿形坳澤，却笠山林，而隨撲隨滅者，不必以大誅之。各隨其機之所宜而已。形之所在，有險有夷，故其守異：有平原廣埜，無羊腸鋸齒之險，進不必郛圍，退不必亭障，而可以不失其險者，不必以多守
translation_en:
… anxious concern from before dawn until late at night, formulating plans for it. Recently, senior civil and military officials, upholding His Majesty's awe-inspiring prestige and the strategic calculations of the imperial court, have cleared away the weeds and eradicated the rebels. Today, the circumstances and situation differ greatly from the past: in the mountain thickets no rebel standards are raised, the vast seas are calm without waves, the people's plows cover the mountain valleys, and merchant sails continuously come to anchor at the islands. Even if the Wave-Subduing General (Fubo) and the Tower-Ship General (Louchuan) were alive today, they would hold their tongues and not speak of matters like approaching the Cai River or commanding the Liang region, for the land may truly be called pacified. Yet Your Excellency still meticulously assesses the situation and discusses the times, distinguishing the advantages and disadvantages of punitive campaigns and comparing the retention or dismissal of naval and land forces. This is the foresight to worry in an age of peace and the far-reaching concern of a loyal minister; how could I, in my ignorance, dare to have no explanation with which to reply?

I have heard it said: in battles, whether great or small, he who understands the times triumphs; with troops, whether many or few, he who adapts to the terrain is strong. Timing is the pivot of battle, and terrain is the configuration of troops. Where the pivot lies hidden, it may be subtle or manifest, and therefore the manner of battle differs: when there are formidable enemies and entrenched bandits who gather in thousands to form a power or in tens of thousands to form a military force, acting unrestrainedly in the gorges and proclaiming themselves masters, one must not treat them lightly as a minor matter [?]; when there are those who seize an opening to break out furtively, hiding themselves in marshes and hollows or casting off their bamboo hats in the mountain forests, who are extinguished as soon as they are struck, one need not mount a grand expedition to punish them. In each case, one simply follows what is appropriate to the pivot of the situation. Where the configuration of terrain lies, it may be precipitous or level, and therefore the manner of defense differs: where there are flat plains and broad wildernesses without the ruggedness of sheep-gut bends or saw-toothed ridges, where in advancing one need not rely on outer walls and enclosures and in retreating one need not rely on frontier posts and barriers, and yet one can avoid losing its strategic advantage, one need not defend it with large numbers…

title: 萬曆十年廣東鄉試錄
text:
之有洪澤巨海無通邑大都之塹我可以
往彼可以來而不能不失其險者不可以
寡守之各隨其形之所宜而已不伺其機
之微著而槩議征誅征誅煩則民罷是梯
亂也而何以議戰不順其形之險夷而多
置什伍什伍衆則帑竭是坐困也而何以
議守故善戰者重用大而善守者重用衆
甞觀之司馬法矣其曰大軍以固多力以
煩而又曰凡誅以明武有殺一人而三軍
===
震者有殺一方而萬人喜者則戰之大小
無常一戰曰用兵之道用衆治衆利正而
又曰一而當十十而當百百而當千千而
當萬此守法也則兵之衆寡亦無常已宜
大而大而毋故翕之以自衄宜小而小而
毋故張之以自疲宜衆而衆而毋自寡其
衆以來敵之侵宜寡而寡而毋故衆其寡
以耗天之聚旣度其時又度其地如斯而
已矣今之議粤戰者曰粤之內地重岡複
punctuated: 之；有洪澤巨海，無通邑大都之塹，我可以往，彼可以來，而不能不失其險者，不可以寡守之，各隨其形之所宜而已。不伺其機之微著而槩議征誅，征誅煩則民罷，是梯亂也，而何以議戰？不順其形之險夷而多置什伍，什伍衆則帑竭，是坐困也，而何以議守？故善戰者重用大，而善守者重用衆。甞觀之《司馬法》矣，其曰：「大軍以固，多力以煩。」而又曰：「凡誅以明武，有殺一人而三軍震者，有殺一方而萬人喜者。」則戰之大小無常。一戰曰：「用兵之道，用衆治衆利正。」而又曰：「一而當十，十而當百，百而當千，千而當萬，此守法也。」則兵之衆寡亦無常已。宜大而大，而毋故翕之以自衄；宜小而小，而毋故張之以自疲；宜衆而衆，而毋自寡其衆以來敵之侵；宜寡而寡，而毋故衆其寡以耗天之聚。旣度其時，又度其地，如斯而已矣。今之議粤戰者曰：「粤之內地重岡複
translation_en:
… [defend] them; and there are vast marshes and great seas, lacking the moats of connected towns and great metropolises, where we can go forth and they can come in, so that one cannot avoid losing the strategic advantage—these cannot be defended with few troops. Each simply follows what is appropriate to its terrain. If one does not watch whether the incipient crisis is subtle or manifest, and instead uniformly proposes punitive expeditions, then frequent expeditions will exhaust the people; this is to invite rebellion, so how can one speak of offensive warfare? If one does not adapt to whether the terrain is precipitous or level, and instead stations numerous squads and files of troops everywhere, then large numbers of troops will deplete the treasury; this is to sit waiting for exhaustion, so how can one speak of defense? Therefore, those skilled in offensive warfare are cautious about launching large-scale campaigns, and those skilled in defense are cautious about employing large numbers of troops.

I have examined the Methods of the Sima (Sima fa). It says: "A great army is for firmness, and superior strength becomes burdensome." Yet it also says: "In all punitive expeditions to manifest martial might, there are cases where killing one man makes the Three Armies tremble, and cases where executing one quarter makes ten thousand men rejoice." Thus, whether a campaign should be large or small is not fixed. Another treatise on warfare [?] says: "In the way of employing troops, using a multitude to govern a multitude favors regular warfare." Yet it also says: "One man matching ten, ten matching a hundred, a hundred matching a thousand, and a thousand matching ten thousand—this is the method of defense." Thus, whether troops should be many or few is likewise not fixed. When a campaign ought to be large, make it large, and do not deliberately contract it so as to bring defeat upon oneself; when it ought to be small, make it small, and do not deliberately inflate it so as to exhaust oneself. When troops ought to be numerous, make them numerous, and do not reduce one's own multitude so as to invite enemy incursions; when they ought to be few, make them few, and do not deliberately multiply what should be few so as to waste Heaven's accumulated resources. Once one has assessed the timing and also assessed the terrain, it is simply a matter of acting accordingly.

Now, those who discuss warfare in Guangdong say: "In the interior of Guangdong, there are layered ridges and…

title: 萬曆十年廣東鄉試錄
text:
嶺懸崖密柵所繇入者隘所從歸者迂彼
飽可以待我之饑是故方馬埋輪不足以
踐其逕也五火不足以燔其林也五間不
足以攜其黨也非大舉兵而盡創之無以
震明威而夷亂窟至其据阪背險半隱半
出名曰撫民有隙即內訌者竄在林翳蟠
於沮澤短鋋衞前積弩陪後以伺我出入
鵰剿不𨚫恐與巨賊連耳嗟乎此二說者
東粵之戰也其在嘉隆之際則然今日之
===
粵無有逆
主令者可以戰可以無戰故其議戰也異於昔
日必戰之時今之議粵守者曰粵之外地
表海隈澳方舟聯艦所臨者瀚波所備者
番夷彼突可以衝我之逸是故廣塹深坑
不足以杜其入也飛橋不足以遏其銳也
天浮不足以擊其渡也非多徵兵而拒守
之無以圉跳梁而實舟航至其絕岸遮壘
且戰且守名曰陸兵有警即堵截者屯在
punctuated: 嶺，懸崖密柵，所繇入者隘，所從歸者迂，彼飽可以待我之饑。是故方馬埋輪，不足以踐其逕也；五火，不足以燔其林也；五間，不足以攜其黨也。非大舉兵而盡創之，無以震明威而夷亂窟。至其据阪背險，半隱半出，名曰撫民，有隙即內訌者，竄在林翳，蟠於沮澤，短鋋衞前，積弩陪後，以伺我出入，鵰剿不𨚫，恐與巨賊連耳。」嗟乎！此二說者，東粵之戰也，其在嘉、隆之際則然。今日之粵，無有逆主令者，可以戰，可以無戰，故其議戰也，異於昔日必戰之時。今之議粵守者曰：「粵之外地，表海隈澳，方舟聯艦，所臨者瀚波，所備者番夷，彼突可以衝我之逸。是故廣塹深坑，不足以杜其入也；飛橋，不足以遏其銳也；天浮，不足以擊其渡也。非多徵兵而拒守之，無以圉跳梁而實舟航。至其絕岸遮壘，且戰且守，名曰陸兵，有警即堵截者，屯在
translation_en: …ridges, overhanging cliffs, and dense palisades. The routes by which one enters are narrow, and the routes by which one returns are circuitous; they, being well-fed, can await our hunger. Therefore, tethering horses side by side and burying chariot wheels is not enough to tread their paths; the five types of fire attacks are not enough to burn their forests; the five types of espionage are not enough to divide their partisans. Unless we mobilize a grand army and thoroughly crush them, there is no way to project our radiant majesty and level their rebellious dens. As for those who occupy slopes with their backs to险 [natural strongholds], half-hidden and half-exposed, nominally called pacified people (fumin) but stirring up internal strife at the slightest opening—they skulk in shaded woods and coil in marshy swamps, with short spears guarding the front and massed crossbows backing the rear, watching our comings and goings. If we do not suppress them with swift, hawk-like strikes (diaojiao), it is feared they will link up with the great bandits." Alas! These two arguments concern warfare in eastern Guangdong, and they held true during the Jiajing and Longqing eras. In Guangdong today, there is no one who defies the sovereign's commands; one may fight, or one may refrain from fighting. Thus, discussing warfare today differs from bygone times when war was inevitable. Those who today discuss the defense of Guangdong say: "In the outer territories of Guangdong, bordered by the sea with its coves and bays, with rafts and linked warships, what we face are the vast waves, and what we guard against are foreign barbarians (fanyi); their sudden assaults can shatter our ease. Therefore, wide moats and deep pits are not enough to block their entry; flying bridges are not enough to check their sharp advance; floating river-barriers (tianfu) are not enough to strike them as they cross. Unless we levy large numbers of troops to resist and defend against them, there is no way to fend off the unruly marauders and fully man our vessels. As for blocking ramparts along sheer coasts, fighting while defending—those nominally called land troops, who intercept and block at the first sign of alarm, are stationed at…

title: 萬曆十年廣東鄉試錄
text:
戒也飛霜匝地蘭艾之盡可隱也况自用
兵以來山箐海氛次第盪覆矣卽欲大舉
將焉用之間有頑梗未銷山谷時警一夫
横行折其首而貸其醜一方怙强夷其壘
而赦其鄰既不黷兵亦不糜廩此鵬勦之
法所當講乎非謂勦之勝於征也今昔之
時異也夫粤豈忘守之國哉而當暴露之
後民始安堵則陸兵不可增而水備不可
撤何以明之反側甫寧而干戈且尋是疑
===
寇也土著可練而客兵未捐是糜餉也關
梁既闢而甲楯不釋是塞貨也况自平寇
以後民壯弓兵旋復增額矣卽欲再增將
焉用之若夫海氛蹔屏夷情叵測東連暹
羅番舶之往來宜稽南通日本悍鹵之出
没宜防內嚴下海之禁外緝句引之姦此
水兵之防所當嚴乎非謂水之加於陸也
山海之地殊也往者勦伐不加專事姑息
亂萌不折逆黨盈野吾勤於勦不輕於撫
punctuated:
戒也，飛霜匝地，蘭艾之盡可隱也。况自用兵以來，山箐海氛，次第盪覆矣；卽欲大舉，將焉用之？間有頑梗未銷，山谷時警：一夫横行，折其首而貸其醜；一方怙强，夷其壘而赦其鄰。既不黷兵，亦不糜廩，此鵬勦之法所當講乎！非謂勦之勝於征也，今昔之時異也。
夫粤豈忘守之國哉？而當暴露之後，民始安堵，則陸兵不可增，而水備不可撤。何以明之？反側甫寧，而干戈且尋，是疑寇也；土著可練，而客兵未捐，是糜餉也；關梁既闢，而甲楯不釋，是塞貨也。况自平寇以後，民壯弓兵，旋復增額矣；卽欲再增，將焉用之？若夫海氛蹔屏，夷情叵測：東連暹羅，番舶之往來宜稽；南通日本，悍鹵之出没宜防。內嚴下海之禁，外緝句引之姦，此水兵之防所當嚴乎！非謂水之加於陸也，山海之地殊也。往者勦伐不加，專事姑息，亂萌不折，逆黨盈野。吾勤於勦，不輕於撫，
translation_en:
… [must be taken as a] warning; when flying frost covers the ground, it is painful to see orchids and mugwort perish alike. Moreover, since military operations began, the bandits in the mountain thickets and the pirates on the seas have one after another been swept away and overthrown; even if one wished to launch a grand campaign, where would it be used? Occasionally there are stubbornly recalcitrant elements not yet eliminated, causing intermittent alarms in the mountains and valleys: when a single ruffian runs rampant, lop off the leader's head and spare his followers; when a locality relies on force, raze its ramparts and pardon its neighbors. Thus one neither engages in wanton warfare nor wastes grain rations—is this not the method of swift, hawk-like suppression (pengjiao) that ought to be studied? This is not to say that selective suppression is superior to a grand expedition, but that present and past times are different.

Could Guangdong ever be a region that forgets defense? Yet after a period of exhausting campaigns in the field, when the people are just beginning to live in peace, land troops should not be increased, whereas naval defenses must not be withdrawn. How can this be made clear? When wavering rebels have barely calmed down, to continue brandishing weapons is to arouse the suspicions of the bandits; when native locals can be trained, to fail to dismiss non-local garrison troops is to waste military provisions; when passes and bridges have been reopened, to refuse to lay down armor and shields is to obstruct the flow of commerce. Moreover, since the pacification of the bandits, the quotas for civilian militia (minzhuang) and archers (gongbing) have soon been increased again; even if one wished to increase them further, what would they be used for? As for the sea pirates, although they are temporarily held at bay, the intentions of the foreign barbarians are unfathomable: to the east [the sea routes] connect with Siam (Xianluo), and the coming and going of foreign ships ought to be inspected; to the south they communicate with Japan (Riben), and the sudden appearances and disappearances of fierce marauders ought to be guarded against. Internally enforcing the prohibition against going to sea, and externally apprehending traitorous collaborators who lure them in—is this not why naval defenses must be kept strict? This is not to say that naval forces are more important than land forces, but that the terrain of mountains and seas is different. In the past, punitive suppression was not applied and policy was devoted solely to indulgent appeasement, so the buds of rebellion were not nipped and rebel factions filled the countryside. If we are diligent in suppression and do not lightly resort to pacification, …

title: 萬曆十年廣東鄉試錄
text:
則小寇漸夷不敢滋蔓故其議剿也卽所
以議征也內寇陸梁躑躅林莽實與海寇
聲勢相倚吾嚴於外俾不得入則內寇益
孤莫爲羽翼故其備水也卽所以防陸也
夫朱明長嬴不能盡其所以爲溫也必隨
之以揫斂之氣而爲秋玄武冱陰不能盡
其所以寒也必隨之以敷榮之氣而爲春
孰爲此者天也天不能常秋而不春而况
於人乎竊嘗譬之病者當其耳鳴鼻張目
===
眩舌撟斯時也厲三陽之鍼和五分之熨
甚則割皮解肌搦髓揲荒無所愛於其膚
何也其勢迫也迨其少間則當撟引案扤
調飲飯擇晏日車步廣志以適筋骨柔血
脉以瀉氣法不當砭灸砭灸則氣逐而篤
今之粵其少間之時乎而論者一切曰大
征也益兵也是毒熨鑱石於病起之餘其
篤立見脉法曰二陰應外一陽接內者不
可以剛藥剛藥入則邪氣流行爲重困於
punctuated: 則小寇漸夷，不敢滋蔓，故其議剿也，卽所以議征也。內寇陸梁，躑躅林莽，實與海寇聲勢相倚；吾嚴於外，俾不得入，則內寇益孤，莫爲羽翼，故其備水也，卽所以防陸也。夫朱明長嬴，不能盡其所以爲溫也，必隨之以揫斂之氣而爲秋；玄武冱陰，不能盡其所以寒也，必隨之以敷榮之氣而爲春。孰爲此者？天也。天不能常秋而不春，而况於人乎？竊嘗譬之病者：當其耳鳴鼻張，目眩舌撟，斯時也，厲三陽之鍼，和五分之熨，甚則割皮解肌，搦髓揲荒，無所愛於其膚，何也？其勢迫也。迨其少間，則當撟引案扤，調飲飯，擇晏日車步，廣志以適筋骨，柔血脉以瀉氣，法不當砭灸；砭灸則氣逐而篤。今之粵，其少間之時乎！而論者一切曰「大征也」、「益兵也」，是毒熨鑱石於病起之餘，其篤立見。《脉法》曰：「二陰應外，一陽接內者，不可以剛藥；剛藥入，則邪氣流行，爲重困於…
translation_en:
…then minor bandits will be gradually eradicated and will not dare to spread and multiply. Therefore, advocating suppression raids is in fact the way to prepare for major punitive expeditions. When inland bandits run rampant, lurking in the forests and brush, they actually rely on the maritime pirates for mutual support. If we maintain strict defenses on the exterior so that they cannot enter, the inland bandits will grow ever more isolated, with none to act as their wings. Therefore, preparing naval defenses is in fact the way to guard the land.

Now, the bright summer of abundant growth cannot exhaust its capacity for warmth; it must be followed by the gathering and contracting vital energy to become autumn. The dark winter of freezing yin cannot exhaust its capacity for cold; it must be followed by the blossoming and flourishing vital energy to become spring. Who brings this about? It is Heaven. Even Heaven cannot remain forever in autumn without turning to spring—how much less can human beings?

I would venture to compare this to a sick person. When his ears ring and his nostrils flare, when his eyes blur and his tongue stiffens—at such a moment, one sharpens the needles for the Three Yang channels and prepares the hot packs of five parts, or in extreme cases cuts the skin and parts the flesh, gripping the marrow and reaching the vital membrane, without sparing his skin. Why is this? Because the condition is urgent. Yet once he has slightly recovered, one ought to practice therapeutic stretching and massage, regulate his drink and food, choose clear days for riding or walking, broaden his spirit to comfort his sinews and bones, and soften his blood and vessels to drain perverse qi. By medical rule, one should not apply stone needles or moxibustion; if one applies stone needles or moxibustion, the vital energy will be driven out and the illness will become critical.

Is not Guangdong today in a period of slight recovery? Yet commentators uniformly cry, "A grand punitive expedition!" and "Increase the troops!" This is applying potent hot packs and sharp stone probes just as the patient is rising from his illness—his condition will immediately turn critical. The Rules of the Pulse (Maifa) says: "When the Two Yin respond on the exterior and the One Yang connects within, one must not use harsh medicines; if harsh medicines enter, noxious qi will circulate and cause severe distress to…"

title: 萬曆十年廣東鄉試錄
text: 偸嗟乎治粵者奈何使其偸而重困也
punctuated: 偸。嗟乎！治粵者，奈何使其偸而重困也！
translation_en: … temporary respite. Alas! How can those who govern Guangdong allow it to fall into mere temporary respite and suffer redoubled distress!

title: 萬曆十年廣東鄉試錄
text:
廣東鄉試錄後序
萬曆紀元以來南粤士凡四
比矣其初比也士甫脫湯火
之厄創夷者未起流散者未
息肩蓋惕惕有戒心焉故其
言憤以厲再比則創夷起而
負擔息肩矣還定安集猶未
===
也蓋凜凜無忘心焉故其言
惻以傷三比則還定安集矣
生聚教訓猶未也蓋瞿瞿無
逸心焉故其言慷慨而有餘
思乃今四比則憺然忘之矣
神靈威武之所變化幾復嶺海之
舊出溝壑而衽席罷呻吟而
punctuated:
廣東鄉試錄後序
萬曆紀元以來，南粤士凡四比矣。其初比也，士甫脫湯火之厄，創夷者未起，流散者未息肩，蓋惕惕有戒心焉，故其言憤以厲。再比，則創夷起而負擔息肩矣，還定安集猶未也，蓋凜凜無忘心焉，故其言惻以傷。三比，則還定安集矣，生聚教訓猶未也，蓋瞿瞿無逸心焉，故其言慷慨而有餘思。乃今四比，則憺然忘之矣。神靈威武之所變化，幾復嶺海之舊，出溝壑而衽席，罷呻吟而
translation_en:
Postface to the Record of the Guangdong Provincial Examination

Since the inception of the Wanli era, the scholars of Southern Yue (Guangdong) have competed in the triennial examinations four times in all. At their first competition, the scholars had only just escaped the perils of boiling water and fire: the wounded had not yet risen, and the displaced had not yet rested their shoulders from their burdens. Truly, they were apprehensive and remained on their guard; therefore, their words were indignant and fierce. By the second competition, the wounded had risen and the bearers of burdens had rested their shoulders, yet returning to stability and resettling in peace had still not been achieved. Truly, they were trembling with awe and had no thought of forgetting; therefore, their words were sorrowful and pained. By the third competition, they had returned to stability and resettled in peace, yet the work of multiplying the population and instructing the people had still not been accomplished. Truly, they looked about alertly and had no thought of ease; therefore, their words were impassioned and left lingering reflections. Now, at this fourth competition, they have calmly forgotten those past woes. Through the transformative power of the Emperor's sacred spirit and martial majesty, the region of the Mountain Passes and the Sea (Guangdong) has nearly been restored to its former state: the people have been lifted out of ditches and ravines and placed onto sleeping mats, ceasing their groans and…

title: 萬曆十年廣東鄉試錄
text:
謳歌偃枹寢烽而絃誦戢戈
櫜矢而衿佩嚮盛爼豆之容
士遑庠序之業物力寖阜逸
心亦或萌其間故其言雍容
閒雅而無遺藻錄之若有不
勝錄焉竊聞異時之談南粤
也宦游者以為善地旅游者
===
以為陸海自頃軍興之後□□
稍稍難之今之願游者如故
矣夫沃土民逸瘠土民勞習
也富歲多賴凶歲多暴資也
南粤故富歲沃土資與習恒
相成凋敝之餘又復其始
武功荒之
punctuated: 謳歌，偃枹寢烽而絃誦，戢戈櫜矢而衿佩。嚮盛爼豆之容，士遑庠序之業。物力寖阜，逸心亦或萌其間，故其言雍容閒雅而無遺藻，錄之若有不勝錄焉。竊聞異時之談南粤也，宦游者以為善地，旅游者以為陸海；自頃軍興之後，□□稍稍難之，今之願游者如故矣。夫沃土民逸，瘠土民勞，習也；富歲多賴，凶歲多暴，資也。南粤故富歲沃土，資與習恒相成，凋敝之餘，又復其始。武功荒之，
translation_en:
… joyful songs; laying down drumsticks and extinguishing beacon fires for the chanting of the classics and stringed instruments; gathering up halberds and casing arrows for the collars and玉-pendants of scholars. Rural districts flourish with the deportment of sacrificial vessels, and scholars have the leisure for the pursuits of the schools. As material resources gradually grow abundant, a mindset of ease may also sprout in their midst. Therefore, their words are poised, refined, and lack no literary elegance; when selecting them for the record, it was as though there were too many to record.

I have privately heard that in former times, when people spoke of Southern Yue [Guangdong], those travelling on official service regarded it as a fine post, and sojourners regarded it as an "inland sea" of wealth. After the recent military campaigns, [people?] gradually came to find it difficult; yet today, those who wish to travel here are just as before. Now, that the people of fertile lands are given to ease while the people of barren lands are given to toil is a matter of habit; that in years of plenty most are reliable while in years of famine most are violent is a matter of material circumstance. Southern Yue has of old been a land of fertile soil and years of plenty, where circumstance and habit constantly reinforce one another; in the aftermath of exhaustion and ruin, it has once again returned to its former state. Military achievements cleared the wilderness for it, …

title: 萬曆十年廣東鄉試錄
text:
文德康之
三朝休養夫孰非
上恩耶士多賴而善惟此時忘勞
而淫亦惟此時往者盜起天
未悔禍民易與爲非惡氛彌
山狂波沸海草野流膏川□
厭血士踰山蹈海莫必其□
===
歲當大比僅乃半至尚不□
此輟藝廢講況今安堵而敢
暇自逸哉歷九折之坂懸車
束馬迄以安度戒也周道如
砥車驟馬馳有時顛蹶忘也
嘉隆間事固士所耳而目之
者即身所不及詢諸父老念
punctuated: 文德康之，三朝休養，夫孰非上恩耶？士多賴而善，惟此時；忘勞而淫，亦惟此時。往者盜起，天未悔禍，民易與爲非。惡氛彌山，狂波沸海，草野流膏，川□厭血，士踰山蹈海，莫必其□。歲當大比，僅乃半至，尚不□此輟藝廢講；況今安堵，而敢暇自逸哉？歷九折之坂，懸車束馬，迄以安度，戒也；周道如砥，車驟馬馳，有時顛蹶，忘也。嘉、隆間事，固士所耳而目之者；即身所不及，詢諸父老，念
translation_en: … and civil virtue brings it peace. Through the recuperation and nourishment across three reigns, what part of this is not the grace of the Sovereign? That scholars mostly have wherewithal and incline toward goodness is precisely at this time; yet that they forget toil and fall into dissipation is also precisely at this time. In the past, when bandits arose, Heaven had not yet relented from sending down calamity, and the people were easily led into wrongdoing. Noxious miasmas filled the mountains, wild waves boiled in the seas, fat flowed over the grassy wilds, and the rivers and [valleys?] were glutted with blood. Scholars crossed mountains and braved the seas, unable to be certain of their [lives?]. When the year of the Great Triennial Examination arrived, barely half managed to attend, yet they still did not [because of?] this abandon their literary arts or cease their scholarly discussions. How much less today, when all live in peace behind secure walls, could they dare take leisure to indulge in idleness! When traversing a nine-switchback slope, one suspends the carriage and binds the horses, and thus ultimately crosses in safety—that comes from caution. When the highway is as smooth as a whetstone, and carriages race and horses gallop, one sometimes overturns and stumbles—that comes from forgetfulness. The events of the Jiajing (1522–1566) and Longqing (1567–1572) eras are assuredly what you scholars have heard with your own ears and seen with your own eyes; even for those things you did not personally experience, if you inquire of the elders, reflecting…

title: 萬曆十年廣東鄉試錄
text:
之刺心語之動色抑知其□
乎夫盜所以起民弗安也民
之弗安吏弗稱也往聞南粤
之民不苦盜而苦吏吏實爲
厲階而民乃爲盜藪夫吏之
酷貪之囮也吏之貪盜之媒
也士蓋嘗憤疾斯輩居則□
===
爲吏若此人將不食其餘□□
我一旦綰綬且羞與爲伍故
其自許信非貌言然九州棊
布孰非命吏乃南粤多弗稱
何也
君門萬里其民柔易與而珠璣瑇
瑁翠羽丹砂之貨多也可欲
punctuated: 之刺心，語之動色。抑知其□乎？夫盜所以起，民弗安也；民之弗安，吏弗稱也。往聞南粤之民不苦盜而苦吏，吏實爲厲階，而民乃爲盜藪。夫吏之酷，貪之囮也；吏之貪，盜之媒也。士蓋嘗憤疾斯輩，居則□：「爲吏若此，人將不食其餘。□□我一旦綰綬，且羞與爲伍。」故其自許，信非貌言。然九州棊布，孰非命吏，乃南粤多弗稱，何也？君門萬里，其民柔易與，而珠璣、瑇瑁、翠羽、丹砂之貨多也。可欲
translation_en: … pierces the heart, and speaking of it changes one's countenance. Yet do they understand the [reason] [?] for it? Now, the reason bandits arise is that the people are not at peace; and the reason the people are not at peace is that the officials are incompetent. In the past I heard that the people of Southern Yue [Guangdong] suffer not from bandits, but from officials; the officials are truly the source of the calamity, and so the people become a haven for bandits. Indeed, the cruelty of officials is the decoy for their greed; the greed of officials is the catalyst for banditry. The scholars have surely resented and detested such types, and in private life [say]: "When men act as officials like this, others will refuse to eat even their leftovers. [If] one day I wear the ribbon of office, I would be ashamed even to be in their company." Thus in the expectations they set for themselves, these are truly not mere surface words. Yet across the Nine Provinces, spread out like pieces on a board, who is not an appointed official? Why then are there so many incompetent ones in Southern Yue? It is because the Sovereign's gate is ten thousand li away, its people are compliant and easy to deal with, and precious goods such as pearls, tortoiseshell, kingfisher feathers, and cinnabar abound. When desirable things…

title: 萬曆十年廣東鄉試錄
text:
亂心而無可畏者以持其後
則中才易移寧獨南粤士得
毋有憤於目擊而忘於身親
者乎夫士也方與計偕今日
之士他日之吏也養之則士
用之則吏課士以言課吏□
功養與用等耳善為吏者□
===
□□□□□不待大計□□
次慮計耳善為士者必先攻
其業不待大比而勸其次慮
比焉然使吏誠以慮計之心
待計何所不舉使士誠以慮
比之心待比何所不脩今南
粤幸賴
punctuated: 亂心，而無可畏者以持其後，則中才易移，寧獨南粤？士得毋有憤於目擊而忘於身親者乎？夫士也，方與計偕。今日之士，他日之吏也；養之則士，用之則吏；課士以言，課吏□功，養與用等耳。善為吏者，□□□□□□，不待大計□□；次慮計耳。善為士者，必先攻其業，不待大比而勸；其次慮比焉。然使吏誠以慮計之心待計，何所不舉？使士誠以慮比之心待比，何所不脩？今南粤幸賴
translation_en: …confuse the mind, and if there is nothing to be feared to hold them accountable afterward, then those of middling talent are easily swayed—and why should this be so only in Southern Yue (Guangdong)? Could it be that scholars are indignant at what they witness with their own eyes, yet forget it when they themselves are in that position? Now, these scholars are just about to proceed to the capital along with the fiscal accounts [for the Metropolitan Examination]. The scholars of today are the officials of tomorrow. When nurtured, they are scholars; when employed, they are officials. Scholars are evaluated by their words, while officials are evaluated [by their] achievements; nurturing and employing are on an equal footing. Those who are good at being officials [first attend to their duties?], without waiting for the Great Evaluation [to be spurred on?]; the next best are concerned about the evaluation. Those who are good at being scholars necessarily first apply themselves to their studies, without waiting for the Great Triennial Examination to be encouraged; the next best are concerned about the examination. Yet if officials truly await the evaluation with a mind concerned about the evaluation, what duty would not be fulfilled? And if scholars truly await the examination with a mind concerned about the examination, what conduct would not be cultivated? Now Southern Yue fortunately relies on…

title: 萬曆十年廣東鄉試錄
text:
天之靈徼福於
明聖氛消波恬士緩帶而升竊恐
其忘之也而躬蹈昔之所求
於吏者故爲追述往昔以動
其操危臨深之思詩不云乎
□□不遠□其以前事
□有以對
===
□□□□□不不□□□
□□□□□善□□□□政
□□災處□□□□□□□
punctuated:
天之靈，徼福於明聖，氛消波恬，士緩帶而升，竊恐其忘之也，而躬蹈昔之所求於吏者，故爲追述往昔，以動其操危臨深之思。《詩》不云乎：「□□不遠。」□其以前事□有以對。
□□□□□不不□□□□□□□□善□□□□政□□災處□□□□□□□
translation_en:
…the numinous power of Heaven and enjoy blessings from the Enlightened Sage. Now that miasmas have dissipated and the waves are calm, and scholars loosen their sashes as they advance, I privately fear that they may forget this and personally fall into the very faults for which they once reproached officials. Therefore, I have recounted the past in order to stir in them thoughts of maintaining vigilance in peril and treading on the brink of the abyss. Does not the Classic of Poetry (Shijing) say: "[...] is not far off"? [?], taking past events as a lesson, [...] will have something with which to reply.

[...] not, not [...] good [...] governance [...] disaster, managing [...]…

translation_en: … [7 illegible characters] not [2 illegible characters] cause [6 illegible characters] indeed! How could one [1 illegible character] perfect one's [2 illegible characters], while embellishing one's mind [? 心文] [4 illegible characters]? In learning and teaching [3 illegible characters], does sincerity not speak of [10 illegible characters] arising in the mind so as to [6 illegible characters] words [9 illegible characters].

title: 萬曆十年廣東鄉試錄
text:
廣東鄉試錄序
今玆歷在壬午蓋
聖天子十紀元四設科云廣東爲
南海隩區士喁喁北面以待
舉巡按監察御史羅應鶴先
期至申要束而綱紀之矻矻
乎其豫□
===
時藩臬□□□□□
則左布政使李江左參政周
之屏監試則按察使徐時可
副使朱東光諸文學以聘至
考試則道淳曁敎諭胡仕朝
同考試則敎諭姜天麒鄒絢
高應忭姚一理訓導鄭人和
punctuated:
廣東鄉試錄序
今玆歷在壬午，蓋聖天子十紀元，四設科云。廣東爲南海隩區，士喁喁北面以待舉。巡按監察御史羅應鶴先期至，申要束而綱紀之，矻矻乎其豫□。時藩臬□□□□□則左布政使李江、左參政周之屏；監試則按察使徐時可、副使朱東光。諸文學以聘至：考試則道淳曁敎諭胡仕朝；同考試則敎諭姜天麒、鄒絢、高應忭、姚一理，訓導鄭人和、
translation_en:
Preface to the Record of the Guangdong Provincial Examination

This year the calendar is at renwu (1582), which is the tenth year of the Sacred Son of Heaven's reign and the fourth time the examinations have been held. Guangdong is a secluded region by the Southern Sea, where scholars eagerly look northward as they await selection in the examinations. Regional Investigating Censor Luo Yinghe 羅應鶴 arrived ahead of time, reiterated the regulations, and put everything in order, working tirelessly to prepare beforehand […]. At this time, among the Provincial Administration and Surveillance Commissions [… Acting as Proctors] were Left Administration Commissioner Li Jiang 李江 and Left Administration Vice Commissioner Zhou Zhiping 周之屏; serving as Monitoring Officials were Surveillance Commissioner Xu Shike 徐時可 and Surveillance Vice Commissioner Zhu Dongguang 朱東光. The various Confucian teachers arrived by invitation: serving as Examiners were [I,] Daochun 道淳, and Instructor Hu Shichao 胡仕朝; serving as Associate Examiners were Instructors Jiang Tianqi 姜天麒, Zou Xuan 鄒絢, Gao Yingbian 高應忭, and Yao Yili 姚一理, and Assistant Instructors Zheng Renhe 鄭人和,…

title: 萬曆十年廣東鄉試錄
text:
楊成性楊敦敘羣有司以檄
至程能授事唯其人旣就列
御史奉
詔令而令之三旣授成帥百執事
告司盟而申之五比日至、
提學副使支可大海南提學
副使唐
百有奇三□□□六
五人策名程藝上之
天府故事多士始進主司宜必有
父要之言籍旣成御史揖道
淳而授簡竊聞天地盛德之
氣始於西北而盛於東南疇
昔聖帝明王率由此產帝臣
punctuated: 楊成性、楊敦敘。羣有司以檄至，程能授事，唯其人。旣就列，御史奉詔令而令之三；旣授成，帥百執事告司盟而申之五。比日至，提學副使支可大、海南提學副使唐，百有奇，三□□□六五人，策名程藝，上之天府。故事，多士始進，主司宜必有父要之言。籍旣成，御史揖道淳而授簡。竊聞天地盛德之氣，始於西北，而盛於東南。疇昔聖帝明王，率由此產；帝臣
translation_en: … Yang Chengxing 楊成性, and Yang Dunxu 楊敦敘. The various officials arrived in response to the summons, and duties were assigned according to their abilities, each suited to the person. Once they had taken their places in the ranks, the Regional Inspector respectfully upheld the imperial edicts and issued orders to them three times; once the arrangements were finalized, he led the hundred functionaries to declare before the deities of the covenant and reiterated the injunctions five times. When the appointed day arrived, the Surveillance Vice Commissioner for Education Zhi Kedai 支可大 and the Hainan Surveillance Vice Commissioner for Education Tang 唐 [missing text in transcription: selected students numbering twenty-five?] hundred and more; after three [sessions, they selected seventy-?]five men, inscribed their names on the roll, and selected model examination essays to present to the Imperial Court. According to precedent, when the many scholars first advance, the chief examiners ought necessarily to offer words of paternal admonition [久要之言 -> words of enduring obligation / 父要之言[?]]. Once the register was completed, the Regional Inspector bowed to [me,] Daochun 道淳, and handed over the writing tablets. I have humbly heard that the vital氣 (qi) of the flourishing virtue of Heaven and Earth began in the northwest and came to flourish in the southeast. In bygone times, sage emperors and enlightened kings were generally born from that region, and imperial ministers …

title: 萬曆十年廣東鄉試錄
text:
王佐亦以類從薄海而南曁
聲敎而已迄我
太祖中天而興
挺生南國
嚮明而治此其嚮方由是閩儒莊
士奮起海濱或參
密勿或職論
===
我
世祖重明麗正南紀
應符
文命覃敷
光被海寓二三大夫握珠懷寶蔚
爲
國華其言骨鯁其行瑰琦美哉
punctuated: 王佐，亦以類從；薄海而南，曁聲敎而已。迄我太祖中天而興，挺生南國，嚮明而治，此其嚮方。由是閩儒莊士，奮起海濱，或參密勿，或職論［思］。我世祖重明麗正，南紀應符，文命覃敷，光被海寓。二三大夫，握珠懷寶，蔚爲國華；其言骨鯁，其行瑰琦，美哉
translation_en: … and royal aides likewise followed according to their kind; whereas to the south as far as the sea, our prestige and moral teachings merely reached there and no more. When our Grand Progenitor (Taizu) arose in mid-heaven, he was born as an outstanding figure in the southern lands, and governed facing the bright south—thus making this region the direction toward which he faced. From this time onward, Confucian scholars of Min [or: accomplished scholars] and grave gentlemen rose vigorously from the seashore, some participating in confidential state counsels, and others holding the office of discussion [and deliberation]…. When our Epochal Progenitor [Shizong] doubled the radiance and clave to the correct, the southern regions responded to the auspicious omen; cultural mandates were widely spread, and glorious light covered the maritime realm. Two or three grandees, grasping pearls and cherishing treasures within, flourished as the splendor of the state; their words were outspoken and unyielding, and their conduct was extraordinary and noble. How admirable,…

title: 萬曆十年廣東鄉試錄
text:
煌煌乎蓋鶉火之次也及我
穆考坐銷熒惑海不揚波
皇上在宥萬方
文德四洽多士摶扶搖而上殆將
乗海運而天飛有如垂天之
雲何論朱鳥敦牂之歲盛德
在南天澤□□
===
壬午乃今鄉國
多士寔應
昌期夫律天時協地紀本之以
帝德類應之以人文多士其皆得
之殆千古一覯也顧士之自
獻必重先資主司為之推轂
而戒塗必重先發君子慎始
punctuated: 煌煌乎，蓋鶉火之次也！及我穆考，坐銷熒惑，海不揚波。皇上在宥萬方，文德四洽，多士摶扶搖而上，殆將乗海運而天飛，有如垂天之雲，何論朱鳥？敦牂之歲，盛德在南，天澤□□，壬午乃今，鄉國多士，寔應昌期。夫律天時，協地紀，本之以帝德，類應之以人文，多士其皆得之，殆千古一覯也。顧士之自獻，必重先資；主司為之推轂而戒塗，必重先發。君子慎始，
translation_en: …How resplendent! Truly it corresponds to the celestial station of the Quail Fire. Coming down to our late Emperor Muzong, he sat in majesty and dispelled the baleful Mars, so that the seas did not raise a wave. His Majesty now leniently rules the myriad regions, and his civilizing virtue pervades the four quarters. The many scholars soar upward on the whirlwind, about to ride the moving seas and fly through the heavens like clouds hanging from the sky—what need is there even to speak of the Vermilion Bird? In the year of Dunzang [wu-horse], flourishing virtue resides in the south, and heavenly grace [?] … Now in this renwu year [1582], the many scholars of this province truly answer to this prosperous age. To conform to the seasons of heaven, harmonize with the terrestrial order, ground oneself in imperial virtue, and respond in kind through cultural refinement—for the many scholars to attain all of these is an encounter seen scarcely once in a thousand ages. Yet when a scholar presents himself for service, he must value his initial pledge; and when the examiners push the wheel-hubs to send him off and prepare him for the road, they must value the initial setting forth. A gentleman is careful at the beginning—…

title: 萬曆十年廣東鄉試錄
text:
何莫不然子之成人父命之
冠爲之有室父命之婚入學
親師師命之學夫何命命其
始也故三加同祝醮同誓鼓
篋同呻卽父師無異辭子弟
信而從之無改慮要以天親
則父道尊則師
===
可知已主司以□□長退
多士於千百什一之中非有
父之親師之尊也藉第令有
口不越乎質文言行以爲言
上士聞而服膺儼若
功令此何以故主司之所昭事
則奉
punctuated: 何莫不然？子之成人，父命之冠；爲之有室，父命之婚；入學親師，師命之學。夫何命？命其始也。故三加同祝，醮同誓，鼓篋同呻，卽父師無異辭，子弟信而從之無改慮，要以天親則父，道尊則師，可知已。主司以□□長，退多士於千百什一之中，非有父之親、師之尊也。藉第令有口，不越乎質文、言行以爲言，上士聞而服膺，儼若功令。此何以故？主司之所昭事，則奉
translation_en: How could it not be so? When a son comes of age, his father charges him at his capping ceremony; when a household is established for him, his father charges him at his marriage; when he enters school and draws near to a teacher, his teacher charges him in his studies. Now why do they charge him? They charge him at his beginning. Thus at the three-fold capping the blessings are the same, at the ritual toast the vows are the same, and at the beating of the drum and opening of the book-satchels the recitations are the same. Even though fathers and teachers have no different words, sons and younger brothers trust and follow them without a change of heart. In sum, because in heavenly kinship there is the father, and in the veneration of the Way there is the teacher, this can readily be understood. When the examiners preside with [?] [□□長], selecting the many scholars as one out of ten, or a hundred, or a thousand, they do not possess the kinship of a father or the veneration due to a teacher. Even supposing they have words to speak, their words do not go beyond substance and refinement, speech and conduct; yet when superior scholars hear them, they take them to heart and cherish them just as if they were official statutes. Why is this so? Because what the examiners brightly serve is the upholding of…

title: 萬曆十年廣東鄉試錄
text:
君事也其所颺言則代
天言也臨之以勿貳律之以在三
加于父師一等矣道淳幸爲
役疇敢以不佞而廢言今夫
士寧質有其文無寧言過其
行比年主司之所忠告率術
此爲繩墨之言以言
===
揚則其文以也□□日所
習非所用朝藉手而夕屏之
靜言之謂何違何亟也仲尼
四敎首事以文其言兩端小
大殊矣小言之則莫吾猶人
是也大言之則文在茲是也
爾多士擅經術飫道腴該古
punctuated: 君事也；其所颺言，則代天言也。臨之以勿貳，律之以在三，加于父師一等矣。道淳幸爲役，疇敢以不佞而廢言？今夫士，寧質有其文，無寧言過其行。比年主司之所忠告，率術此爲繩墨之言。以言揚，則其文以也。□□日所習非所用，朝藉手而夕屏之，靜言之謂何？違何亟也！仲尼四敎，首事以文，其言兩端，小大殊矣。小言之，則「莫吾猶人」是也；大言之，則「文在茲」是也。爾多士擅經術，飫道腴，該古
translation_en: … the service of the Sovereign; and the words he proclaims are spoken on behalf of Heaven. Approached with undivided loyalty and governed by the principle of the three bonds of devotion, this stands a degree above even father and teacher. Since I, Daochun, have the good fortune to serve in this role, how could I dare, on account of my own inadequacy, refrain from speaking? Now, as for scholars, it is better that their substance be graced with literary refinement than that their words exceed their deeds. In recent years, the earnest advice offered by the Examiners has generally followed this as a standard rule of counsel. When men are promoted on the basis of their words, it is because of their literary refinement. [Yet if they say that] [?] what they study day by day is not what they will put to use—relying on it as a stepping-stone in the morning only to cast it aside in the evening—what becomes of pondering one's words in quietude? How swiftly they betray them! Among the four teachings of Confucius (Zhongni 仲尼), literary learning comes first; yet when he spoke of it in two different ways, there was a distinction between the lesser and the greater. Spoken of in the lesser sense, it is "In literary learning, I am perhaps equal to others"; spoken of in the greater sense, it is "Does not this culture (wen) reside here in me?" All you scholars excel in classicist learning, are steeped in the richness of the Way, and encompass ancient…

title: 萬曆十年廣東鄉試錄
text:
今盡倫物挾策具在其誰曰
不文由是而見之行則得時
而駕矣上之經緯天地黼黻
治功下之廣厲四方斌斌君
子之士也之文也在坤爲五
在乾爲二美中四暢天下文
明以是爲文文之至也猶未
===
也士之得與于斯文也本之
吾心文滅其質極于不慙其
心亡矣夫坤陰德也本諸二
之敬義乾陽德也本諸三之
乾乾天命不已地主有常天
地無心此其心也二曜五辰
四時百物山澤通氣草木蕃
punctuated: 今，盡倫物，挾策具在，其誰曰不文？由是而見之行，則得時而駕矣。上之經緯天地，黼黻治功；下之廣厲四方，斌斌君子之士也，之文也。在《坤》爲五，在《乾》爲二；美中四暢，天下文明。以是爲文，文之至也。猶未也。士之得與于斯文也，本之吾心。文滅其質，極于不慙，其心亡矣。夫《坤》，陰德也，本諸二之敬義；《乾》，陽德也，本諸三之乾乾。天命不已，地主有常。天地無心，此其心也。二曜五辰、四時百物，山澤通氣，草木蕃
translation_en: … and the present, fully grasping human relations and the principles of things, with their written scripts all at hand—who could say they lack culture and refinement (wen)? When this is manifested in action, they seize the moment and mount the carriage of office. Above, they weave the warp and woof of Heaven and Earth and adorn the achievements of governance; below, they broadly encourage the four quarters—such are the refined gentlemanly scholars, and such is their culture. In the hexagram Kun, this corresponds to the fifth line; in the hexagram Qian, to the second line: beauty within diffusing through the four limbs, and the whole world illuminated and civilized. To take this as culture is the perfection of culture. Yet even this is not all. For a scholar to participate in this culture, it must be rooted in his own mind. When ornament obliterates substance, reaching the point where one feels no shame, the mind is lost. Now Kun, the yin virtue, is rooted in the reverence and righteousness of its second line; Qian, the yang virtue, is rooted in the unceasing diligence (qianqian) of its third line. The Mandate of Heaven is unceasing; the governance of Earth has constancy. Heaven and Earth have no deliberate mind of their own, yet this is their mind. The sun and moon and the five planets, the four seasons and the myriad things, mountains and marshes exchanging vital breaths, herbs and trees flourishing in…

title: 萬曆十年廣東鄉試錄
text:
燕雖天地未始廢文文有本
也多士仰觀俯察宜莫盛于
乾坤乾乾敬義以純其心彌
綸之本在是矣幸哉得士若
此寧非盛德之旺于南也與
哉夫然則南極列星不爲熒
羅浮之山牂牁之水不爲麗
===
明珠翠羽珊瑚木難不爲珍
以是而觀人文日幾幾望其
熾而昌也何可廢耶
上屢
詔詔臣工一以正人心端士習爲
務心純則正習吉則端誠得
若而人相帥而潤色
punctuated: 燕，雖天地未始廢文，文有本也。多士仰觀俯察，宜莫盛于乾坤。乾乾敬義，以純其心，彌綸之本在是矣。幸哉！得士若此，寧非盛德之旺于南也與哉？夫然，則南極列星不爲熒，羅浮之山、牂牁之水不爲麗，明珠、翠羽、珊瑚、木難不爲珍。以是而觀人文，日幾幾望其熾而昌也，何可廢耶？上屢詔詔臣工，一以正人心、端士習爲務。心純則正，習吉則端。誠得若而人，相帥而潤色…
translation_en: …luxuriant [?]; even Heaven and Earth have never dispensed with patterned expression (wen), yet such expression has its root. When the many scholars look up to observe and look down to examine, surely nothing is more flourishing than the hexagrams Qian and Kun. Practicing unceasing diligence (qianqian) and reverence and righteousness (jingyi) so as to purify their minds—herein lies the root of encompassing and ordering the world. How fortunate! To obtain scholars such as these—is this not indeed the flourishing of abundant virtue in the south? This being so, the arrayed stars of the Southern Pole do not count as dazzling; Mount Luofu and the waters of the Zangke River do not count as splendid; bright pearls, kingfisher feathers, coral, and munan gems do not count as precious. Observing human culture (renwen) from this perspective, one daily hopes most earnestly that it will blaze forth and prosper—how could it be dispensed with? His Majesty has repeatedly issued edicts instructing his officials and ministers to make rectifying people's minds and straightening scholars' customs their sole priority. When the mind is pure, it is rectified; when customs are auspicious, they are upright. If indeed we obtain men such as these to lead one another in adorning and lending luster to…

title: 萬曆十年廣東鄉試錄
text:
帝業
當宁方注目而視拊髀而思逐逐
耽耽猶懼不既非惡文也惡
其文之敝也然則主司所爲
口實非述陳言良以廣
詔旨云爾多士受
命而虔其始視父師有加由是而
===
爲天瑞爲地靈爲譽髦爲連
茹爲四暢爲文明
令出惟行主司之言信矣毋將
曰闈以內介爲政闈以外介
無預焉是猶既弁之髦既奠
之鴈既贄之束脩無所用之
矣假令法言可距謂
punctuated: 帝業，當宁方注目而視，拊髀而思，逐逐耽耽，猶懼不既。非惡文也，惡其文之敝也。然則主司所爲口實，非述陳言，良以廣詔旨云爾。多士受命而虔其始，視父師有加，由是而爲天瑞，爲地靈，爲譽髦，爲連茹，爲四暢，爲文明，令出惟行，主司之言信矣。毋將曰：「闈以內，介爲政；闈以外，介無預焉。」是猶既弁之髦，既奠之鴈，既贄之束脩，無所用之矣。假令法言可距，謂
translation_en:
… the imperial enterprise, His Majesty on the throne is at this very moment fixing his gaze and slapping his thigh in earnest thought, eagerly and intently watching, still fearing that the goal will not be fully realized. It is not that he dislikes literary culture; he dislikes the corruption of literary culture. This being so, what the examiners have taken as their theme is not a repetition of worn-out clichés, but truly an effort to amplify the imperial decrees, and nothing more.

Should the many scholars receive this charge and be reverent from the very start, regarding it with even greater deference than they show to their fathers and teachers, and thereby go on to become auspicious omens of Heaven, numinous spirits of Earth, celebrated talents, worthies advancing together like intertwined roots, exemplars of flourishing limbs, and embodiments of civilizing brilliance—so that once an order goes forth it is strictly carried out—then the words of the examiners will be proved trustworthy indeed.

Let them not be about to say: "Within the examination compound, our mentors are in charge; outside the examination compound, our mentors have nothing to do with it." That would be like treating the hair-tuft once the cap of manhood has been donned, the wild goose once the betrothal offering has been presented, or the bundle of dried meat once the gift to a teacher has been offered, as things for which there is no longer any use. Even supposing that exemplary words could be rejected, what of…

title: 萬曆十年廣東鄉試錄
text:
明詔何彼鵬以鯤化起羊角而下
鴻毛何所貴之貴嚮往也浸
假而浮沉煦沫直將與鰋鮪
同科去鯤千里去鵬萬里矣
多士生斯世也長斯土也其
將爲鯤鵬耶鰋鮪耶愼所擇
矣是舉也總督總兵軍務先
===
兵部左侍郎今爲譽髦都察
院右都御史劉堯誨夙著勳
猷士風丕變今兵部尚書兼
都察院左副都御史陳瑞文
武爲憲譽髦斯士提督南贛
軍務先都察院右僉都御史
張煥今都察院右副都御史
punctuated:
明詔何？彼鵬以鯤化，起羊角而下鴻毛，何所貴之？貴嚮往也。浸假而浮沉煦沫，直將與鰋鮪同科，去鯤千里，去鵬萬里矣。多士生斯世也，長斯土也，其將爲鯤鵬耶？鰋鮪耶？愼所擇矣。
是舉也，總督總兵軍務、先兵部左侍郎、今爲譽髦都察院右都御史劉堯誨，夙著勳猷，士風丕變；今兵部尚書兼都察院左副都御史陳瑞，文武爲憲，譽髦斯士；提督南贛軍務、先都察院右僉都御史張煥，今都察院右副都御史
translation_en:
… the illustrious imperial edict? As for that Peng bird, which transforms from the Kun fish, rising on a whirlwind and looking down upon wild geese as mere feathers—why do we value it? We value its lofty aspiration. If, step by step, it were merely to bob up and down moistening others with its spit, it would simply be in the same class as mudfish and sturgeons—a thousand miles removed from the Kun, and ten thousand miles from the Peng! You many scholars, born in this age and raised in this land: will you be Kun and Peng, or will you be mudfish and sturgeons? Be careful in what you choose!

In this undertaking, Supreme Commander of Military Affairs, formerly Left Vice Minister of War and now [garbled: 爲譽髦?] Right Censor-in-Chief of the Censorate, Liu Yaohui 劉堯誨, has long displayed meritorious plans, greatly transforming the ethos of the scholars; the current Minister of War concurrently Left Vice Censor-in-Chief of the Censorate, Chen Rui 陳瑞, is a model in both civil and military affairs, making famous and accomplished these scholars; Grand Coordinator of Military Affairs in Nan'gan, formerly Right Assistant Censor-in-Chief of the Censorate Zhang Huan 張煥, and current Right Vice Censor-in-Chief of the Censorate …

title: 萬曆十年廣東鄉試錄
text:
王緝陳常申畫訓典旁宣刑
部郎中王橋平亭疑法嘉樂
章逢右布政使王元敬右叅
政張明正左叅議胡時化副
使鄭岳僉事侯應爵沈植張
友舜薛夢雷總兵官署都督
僉事黃應甲副總兵陳璘于
嵩叅將成大儒葉歡濮朝宗
張應科遊擊李棟署都指揮
僉事秦經國胡九經咸綜理
防範協襄
盛典而副使劉倬右叅議陸萬鍾
署都指揮僉事陳居仁以入
賀行按察使今陞廣西右布政
punctuated: 王緝陳常申畫，訓典旁宣；刑部郎中王橋平亭疑法，嘉樂章逢；右布政使王元敬、右叅政張明正、左叅議胡時化、副使鄭岳、僉事侯應爵、沈植、張友舜、薛夢雷、總兵官署都督僉事黃應甲、副總兵陳璘、于嵩、叅將成大儒、葉歡、濮朝宗、張應科、遊擊李棟、署都指揮僉事秦經國、胡九經，咸綜理防範，協襄盛典。而副使劉倬、右叅議陸萬鍾、署都指揮僉事陳居仁以入賀行，按察使今陞廣西右布政
translation_en: … Wang Ji 王緝 set forth the constant norms and delineated boundaries, broadly proclaiming the instructive canons; Director in the Ministry of Justice Wang Qiao 王橋 fairly adjudicated doubtful legal cases and delighted in scholars wearing ceremonial caps and broad robes; Right Administration Commissioner Wang Yuanjing 王元敬, Right Assistant Administration Commissioner Zhang Mingzheng 張明正, Left Administration Vice Commissioner Hu Shihua 胡時化, Surveillance Vice Commissioner Zheng Yue 鄭岳, Assistant Surveillance Commissioners Hou Yingjue 侯應爵, Shen Zhi 沈植, Zhang Youshun 張友舜, and Xue Menglei 薛夢雷, Regional Commander and Acting Assistant Commissioner-in-Chief Huang Yingjia 黃應甲, Vice Regional Commanders Chen Lin 陳璘 and Yu Song 于嵩, Assistant Regional Commanders Cheng Daru 成大儒, Ye Huan 葉歡, Pu Chaozong 濮朝宗, and Zhang Yingke 張應科, Mobile Corps Commander Li Dong 李棟, and Acting Assistant Regional Military Commissioners Qin Jingguo 秦經國 and Hu Jiujing 胡九經 all managed the arrangements and security precautions, jointly assisting in this grand ceremony. Meanwhile, Surveillance Vice Commissioner Liu Zhuo 劉倬, Right Administration Vice Commissioner Lu Wanzhong 陸萬鍾, and Acting Assistant Regional Military Commissioner Chen Juren 陳居仁, who departed to present congratulations at court, as well as Surveillance Commissioner, now promoted to Right Administration Commissioner of Guangxi,…

title: 萬曆十年廣東鄉試錄
text:
使趙可懐以遷秩行皆與有
勞者例得並書
湖廣武昌府武昌縣儒學敎
諭陳道淳謹序
punctuated:
使趙可懐以遷秩行，皆與有勞者，例得並書。
湖廣武昌府武昌縣儒學敎諭陳道淳謹序。
translation_en:
… Commissioner Zhao Kehuai 趙可懐, who departed upon promotion in rank, had all contributed their labors to the affair and by precedent should also be recorded together.
Respectfully prefaced by Chen Daochun 陳道淳, Instructor in the Confucian School of Wuchang County, Wuchang Prefecture, Huguang.

title: 萬曆十年廣東鄉試錄
text:
萬曆十年廣東鄉試
監臨官
巡按廣東監察御史羅應鶴〔德鳴直隸歙縣人辛未進士〕
提調官
廣東等處承宣布政使司左布政使李江〔汝貢錦衣衞籍山東武定州人己未進士〕
廣東等處承宣布政使司左叅政周之屏〔伯卿湖廣湘潭縣人己未進士〕
監試官
廣東等處提刑按察司按察使徐時可〔惟易湖廣黄岡縣人乙丑進士〕
廣東等處提刑按察司副使朱東光〔元曦福建浦城縣籍江西臨川縣人戊辰進士〕
===
考試官
湖廣武昌府武昌縣儒學教諭陳道淳〔茂弘福建晉江縣籍福清縣人丁卯貢士〕
河南汝寧府信陽州羅山縣儒學教諭胡仕朝〔克忠江西南昌縣人丁卯貢士〕
同考試官
江西廣信府永豐縣儒學教諭姜天麒〔道瑞浙江餘姚縣人戊午貢士〕
浙江寧波府慈谿縣儒學教諭鄒絢〔素甫福建德化縣人甲子貢士〕
浙江湖州府武康縣儒學教諭高應𢘆〔裕中浙江嘉興縣人庚午貢士〕
湖廣武昌府江夏縣儒學教諭姚一理〔原純直隸建平縣人己卯貢士〕
直隸廣德州建平縣儒學訓導鄭人和〔克嚴福建閩縣人庚午貢士〕
punctuated:
萬曆十年廣東鄉試

監臨官：
巡按廣東監察御史羅應鶴〔德鳴，直隸歙縣人，辛未進士〕。

提調官：
廣東等處承宣布政使司左布政使李江〔汝貢，錦衣衞籍，山東武定州人，己未進士〕；
廣東等處承宣布政使司左叅政周之屏〔伯卿，湖廣湘潭縣人，己未進士〕。

監試官：
廣東等處提刑按察司按察使徐時可〔惟易，湖廣黄岡縣人，乙丑進士〕；
廣東等處提刑按察司副使朱東光〔元曦，福建浦城縣籍，江西臨川縣人，戊辰進士〕。

考試官：
湖廣武昌府武昌縣儒學教諭陳道淳〔茂弘，福建晉江縣籍，福清縣人，丁卯貢士〕；
河南汝寧府信陽州羅山縣儒學教諭胡仕朝〔克忠，江西南昌縣人，丁卯貢士〕。

同考試官：
江西廣信府永豐縣儒學教諭姜天麒〔道瑞，浙江餘姚縣人，戊午貢士〕；
浙江寧波府慈谿縣儒學教諭鄒絢〔素甫，福建德化縣人，甲子貢士〕；
浙江湖州府武康縣儒學教諭高應𢘆〔裕中，浙江嘉興縣人，庚午貢士〕；
湖廣武昌府江夏縣儒學教諭姚一理〔原純，直隸建平縣人，己卯貢士〕；
直隸廣德州建平縣儒學訓導鄭人和〔克嚴，福建閩縣人，庚午貢士〕。
translation_en:
Guangdong Provincial Examination of the Tenth Year of the Wanli Reign (1582)

Supervising Official:
Luo Yinghe 羅應鶴 (courtesy name Deming 德鳴, a native of She County, Zhili; metropolitan graduate of the xinwei year [1571]), Regional Inspector of Guangdong and Investigating Censor.

Proctors:
Li Jiang 李江 (courtesy name Rugong 汝貢, registered in the Embroidered-Uniform Guard, a native of Wuding Department, Shandong; metropolitan graduate of the jiwei year [1559]), Left Administration Commissioner of the Guangdong Provincial Administration Commission.
Zhou Zhiping 周之屏 (courtesy name Boqing 伯卿, a native of Xiangtan County, Huguang; metropolitan graduate of the jiwei year [1559]), Left Administration Vice Commissioner of the Guangdong Provincial Administration Commission.

Monitoring Officials:
Xu Shike 徐時可 (courtesy name Weiyi 惟易, a native of Huanggang County, Huguang; metropolitan graduate of the yichou year [1565]), Surveillance Commissioner of the Guangdong Provincial Surveillance Commission.

title: 萬曆十年廣東鄉試錄
text:
第壹場
四書
孔子曰益者三樂損者三樂樂節禮樂樂
道人之善樂多賢友益矣樂驕樂樂佚
遊樂宴樂損矣
或生而知之或學而知之或困而知之及
其知之一也或安而行之或利而行之
或勉强而行之及其成功一也子曰好
學近乎知力行近乎仁知恥近乎勇
===
稷思天下有饑者由己饑之也
易
象曰天地交泰后以財成天地之道輔相
天地之宜以左右民初九拔茅茹以其
彙征吉象曰拔茅征吉志在外也九二
包荒用馮河不遐遺朋亡得尚于中行
象曰包荒得尚于中行以光大也
彖曰萃聚也順以說剛中而應故聚也
探賾索隱鉤深致遠以定天下之吉凶成
punctuated:
第壹場

四書

孔子曰：「益者三樂，損者三樂。樂節禮樂，樂道人之善，樂多賢友，益矣；樂驕樂，樂佚遊，樂宴樂，損矣。」
「或生而知之，或學而知之，或困而知之，及其知之，一也。或安而行之，或利而行之，或勉强而行之，及其成功，一也。」子曰：「好學近乎知，力行近乎仁，知恥近乎勇。」
「稷思天下有饑者，由己饑之也。」

易

《象》曰：「天地交，泰。后以財成天地之道，輔相天地之宜，以左右民。」初九：「拔茅茹，以其彙，征吉。」《象》曰：「拔茅征吉，志在外也。」九二：「包荒，用馮河，不遐遺，朋亡，得尚于中行。」《象》曰：「包荒，得尚于中行，以光大也。」
《彖》曰：「萃，聚也。順以說，剛中而應，故聚也。」
「探賾索隱，鉤深致遠，以定天下之吉凶，成
translation_en:
First Session

The Four Books

Confucius said: "There are three kinds of pleasures that are beneficial, and three kinds of pleasures that are harmful. To take pleasure in regulating oneself by rites and music, to take pleasure in speaking of the goodness of others, and to take pleasure in having many worthy friends—these are beneficial. To take pleasure in extravagant enjoyments, to take pleasure in idle wandering, and to take pleasure in the pleasures of feasting—these are harmful." [Analects 16.5]
"Some are born with knowledge, some acquire it through learning, and some acquire it after painful difficulty; but once they have acquired the knowledge, it comes to the same thing. Some practice it with natural ease, some practice it for its advantage, and some practice it by strenuous effort; but once they have achieved success, it comes to the same thing." The Master said: "To be fond of learning is near to wisdom; to practice with vigor is near to benevolence; to know shame is near to courage." [Doctrine of the Mean 20]
"Hou Ji thought that if anyone in the world was starving, it was as if he himself had caused them to starve." [Mencius 4B.29]

Classic of Changes (Yijing)

The Image (Xiang) says: "Heaven and earth are in communion: Peace (Tai). Thus the ruler fashions and completes the way of heaven and earth, and furthers and regulates the gifts of heaven and earth, so as to aid the people." Nine at the Beginning: "Pulling up thatch grass, its roots come with its kind. Going forward brings good fortune." The Image says: "'Pulling up thatch grass, going forward brings good fortune': his aspiration is directed outward." Nine in the Second Place: "Bearing with the uncultivated, crossing the river without a boat, not neglecting what is distant, and setting aside partisan cliques, one matches the way of the mean." The Image says: "'Bearing with the uncultivated, one matches the way of the mean,' because his light is great." [Hexagram 11, Tai]
The Judgment (Tuan) says: "Gathering Together (Cui) means assembling. Docile and joyous, firm in the center and meeting with response: therefore they gather together." [Hexagram 45, Cui]
"To probe what is complex and search out what is hidden, to hook up what is deep and reach what is distant, thereby determining good and bad fortune in the world and accomplishing…" [Appended Remarks (Xici), Part 1.11]

title: 萬曆十年廣東鄉試錄
text:
天下之亹亹者莫大乎蓍龜是故天生
神物聖人則之
神也者妙萬物而爲言者也動萬物者莫
疾乎雷撓萬物者莫疾乎風燥萬物者
莫熯乎火說萬物者莫說乎澤潤萬物
者莫潤乎水終萬物始萬物者莫盛乎
艮故水火相逮雷風不相悖山澤通氣
然後能變化既成萬物也
書
===
帝曰俞允若茲嘉言罔攸伏野無遺賢萬
邦咸寧稽于衆舍己從人不虐無告不
廢困窮惟帝時克
后非民罔使民非后罔事無自廣以狹人
匹夫匹婦不獲自盡民主罔與成厥功
夙夜罔或不勤不矜細行終累大德爲山
九仞功虧一簣
太史司寇蘇公式敬爾由獄以長我王國
茲式有慎以列用中罰
punctuated:
天下之亹亹者，莫大乎蓍龜。是故天生神物，聖人則之。
神也者，妙萬物而爲言者也。動萬物者，莫疾乎雷；撓萬物者，莫疾乎風；燥萬物者，莫熯乎火；說萬物者，莫說乎澤；潤萬物者，莫潤乎水；終萬物始萬物者，莫盛乎艮。故水火相逮，雷風不相悖，山澤通氣，然後能變化，既成萬物也。
書
帝曰：「俞！允若茲，嘉言罔攸伏，野無遺賢，萬邦咸寧。稽于衆，舍己從人，不虐無告，不廢困窮，惟帝時克。」
后非民罔使，民非后罔事。無自廣以狹人。匹夫匹婦，不獲自盡，民主罔與成厥功。
夙夜罔或不勤。不矜細行，終累大德。爲山九仞，功虧一簣。
太史，司寇蘇公式敬爾由獄，以長我王國。茲式有慎，以列用中罰。
translation_en:
… the tireless endeavors of all under heaven, nothing is greater than the yarrow stalks and tortoise shells. Therefore, Heaven produced these numinous things, and the sages patterned themselves after them.

"Spirit" is a word that speaks of the wondrous mystery operating through the myriad things. Of that which stirs the myriad things, nothing is swifter than thunder; of that which bends the myriad things, nothing is swifter than wind; of that which dries the myriad things, nothing is more parching than fire; of that which gladdens the myriad things, nothing is more gladdening than the marsh; of that which moistens the myriad things, nothing is more moistening than water; of that which brings the myriad things to an end and gives them a new beginning, nothing is more flourishing than Gen (Mountain). Therefore, water and fire reach each other, thunder and wind do not oppose each other, and mountain and marsh communicate their vital breaths; only then can there be transformation and change, bringing all the myriad things to completion.

Book of Documents (Shu)

The Emperor said: "Yes! Truly, if it is like this, good words will have nowhere to lie hidden, no worthy men will be left overlooked in the countryside, and the myriad states will all enjoy peace. To consult with the multitude, to set aside one's own views and follow those of others, not to oppress the helpless, and not to neglect the distressed and impoverished—only the Emperor Yao was able to do this."

Without the people, the sovereign has none to employ; without the sovereign, the people have none to serve. Do not exalt yourself so as to belittle others. If a single common man or common woman is unable to fulfill his or her utmost potential, the lord of the people will have none with whom to bring his work to completion.

From early morning until late at night, never fail to be diligent. If you are not careful about minor conduct, in the end it will compromise great virtue; in raising a mound of nine ren, the work may fall short by a single basket of earth.

Grand Scribe, the Minister of Crime Duke Su (Su Gong) reverently attended to the criminal cases under his charge, thereby perpetuating our royal state. Herein did he exercise caution, so as to apply just punishments according to their proper grades.

title: 萬曆十年廣東鄉試錄
text:
詩
七月食瓜八月斷壺
菁菁者莪在彼中沚旣見君子我心則喜
干祿百福子孫千億穆穆皇皇宜君宜王
不愆不忘率由舊章
天命降監下民有嚴
春秋
冬十有二月齊侯鄭伯盟于石門〔隱公三年〕
===
春築臺于郎築臺于薛秋築臺于秦
〔俱莊公三十有一年〕六月雨〔僖公三年〕
八月公會齊侯宋公鄭伯曹伯邾人于檉
〔僖公元年〕秋齊侯宋公江人黃人會于
陽穀〔僖公三年〕遂伐楚次于陘楚屈
完來盟于師盟于召陵〔俱僖公四年〕
公會晉侯宋公陳侯衛侯鄭伯曹伯莒子
邾子滕子薛伯齊世子光吳人鄫人于
戚〔襄公五年〕
punctuated:
詩：
「七月食瓜，八月斷壺。」
「菁菁者莪，在彼中沚。旣見君子，我心則喜。」
「干祿百福，子孫千億。穆穆皇皇，宜君宜王。不愆不忘，率由舊章。」
「天命降監，下民有嚴。」

春秋：
「冬，十有二月，齊侯、鄭伯盟于石門。」〔隱公三年〕
「春，築臺于郎。築臺于薛。秋，築臺于秦。」〔俱莊公三十有一年〕「六月，雨。」〔僖公三年〕
「八月，公會齊侯、宋公、鄭伯、曹伯、邾人于檉。」〔僖公元年〕「秋，齊侯、宋公、江人、黃人會于陽穀。」〔僖公三年〕「遂伐楚，次于陘。楚屈完來盟于師，盟于召陵。」〔俱僖公四年〕
「公會晉侯、宋公、陳侯、衛侯、鄭伯、曹伯、莒子、邾子、滕子、薛伯、齊世子光、吳人、鄫人于戚。」〔襄公五年〕
translation_en:
Classic of Poetry (Shijing):
"In the seventh month we eat melons; in the eighth month we cut down the bottle-gourds."
"Luxuriant grows the tarragon, there in the midst of the islet. Having seen the lord, my heart is delighted."
"Seeking blessings and a hundred felicities, his descendants shall number in the hundreds of millions. Reverent and majestic, fit to be ruler, fit to be king; neither erring nor forgetting, following the ancient statutes."
"The Mandate of Heaven looks down from on high, and the people below are held in awe."

Spring and Autumn Annals (Chunqiu):
"In winter, in the twelfth month, the Marquis of Qi and the Earl of Zheng made a covenant at Shimen." [3rd year of Duke Yin]
"In spring, a terrace was built at Lang. A terrace was built at Xue. In autumn, a terrace was built at Qin." [All in the 31st year of Duke Zhuang] "In the sixth month, it rained." [3rd year of Duke Xi]
"In the eighth month, the Duke met the Marquis of Qi, the Duke of Song, the Earl of Zheng, the Earl of Cao, and a representative of Zhu at Cheng." [1st year of Duke Xi] "In autumn, the Marquis of Qi, the Duke of Song, a representative of Jiang, and a representative of Huang met at Yanggu." [3rd year of Duke Xi] "Thereupon they invaded Chu and halted at Xing. Qu Wan of Chu came to make a covenant with the army; they made a covenant at Shaoling." [All in the 4th year of Duke Xi]
"The Duke met the Marquis of Jin, the Duke of Song, the Marquis of Chen, the Marquis of Wei, the Earl of Zheng, the Earl of Cao, the Viscount of Ju, the Viscount of Zhu, the Viscount of Teng, the Earl of Xue, Heir Apparent Guang of Qi, a representative of Wu, and a representative of Zeng at Qi." [5th year of Duke Xiang]

title: 萬曆十年廣東鄉試錄
text:
禮記
將適公所宿齊戒居外寢沐浴史進象笏
書思對命既服習容觀玉聲乃出揖私
朝煇如也登車則有光矣
大德不官大道不器
爲人君者謹其所好惡而已矣君好之則
臣爲之上行之則民從之詩云誘民孔
易此之謂也
敬慎者仁之地也
===
第貳場
論
王者如天
詔誥表〔內科一道〕
擬漢舉質樸敦厚遜讓有行者詔〔永光元〕
〔年〕
擬唐以張說兼集賢院學士誥〔開元十六〕
〔年〕
疑
punctuated:
《禮記》
「將適公所，宿齊戒，居外寢，沐浴；史進象笏，書思對命；既服，習容觀玉聲，乃出。揖私朝，煇如也；登車，則有光矣。」
「大德不官，大道不器。」
「爲人君者，謹其所好惡而已矣。君好之，則臣爲之；上行之，則民從之。《詩》云：『誘民孔易。』此之謂也。」
「敬慎者，仁之地也。」

第貳場
論
「王者如天」

title: 萬曆十年廣東鄉試錄
text:
天縱
聖神乃文乃武邇來
萬幾之暇
特詔近臣披閱圖史抽對章句而暮春
教閱深惟先事之備天下欣然想見
太平之盛矣
聖學方新
聖治方勤抑有可爲
顯謨弘烈之助者否伏聞
===
皇上所口授儒臣洞然心性之語而
閱武之日諸所憫念憂勤
意至渥也將以何者可裨萬分一焉諸士夙抱
忠悃行且揚于
大廷必有所以先資自
獻者
問古稱才難天下事孰非須才而辦者五
三上世勿論兩漢以來亦各因俗爲治
不假於異代何謂無才蓋非才之難也
punctuated:
天縱聖神，乃文乃武。邇來萬幾之暇，特詔近臣披閱圖史，抽對章句；而暮春教閱，深惟先事之備。天下欣然，想見太平之盛矣。聖學方新，聖治方勤，抑有可爲顯謨弘烈之助者否？伏聞皇上所口授儒臣，洞然心性之語；而閱武之日，諸所憫念憂勤，意至渥也。將以何者可裨萬分一焉？諸士夙抱忠悃，行且揚于大廷，必有所以先資自獻者。
問：古稱「才難」，天下事孰非須才而辦者？五、三上世勿論，兩漢以來，亦各因俗爲治，不假於異代，何謂無才？蓋非才之難也，
translation_en:
…heaven-endowed with sage and divine qualities, is accomplished in both civil and military affairs. Recently, in his leisure from the myriad affairs of state, he has specially summoned his close ministers to peruse maps and histories and to match verses and phrases; and during the military review in late spring, he gave deep thought to preparations made in advance of events. All under heaven rejoice, envisioning the flourishing of great peace. Now that the sage learning is newly revitalized and the sage governance is diligently pursued, is there anything that might serve to assist his illustrious plans and grand achievements? I have humbly heard that what His Majesty personally dictated to the Confucian ministers were words showing a penetrating understanding of mind and human nature; and on the day of the military review, in all his compassionate thoughts and anxious diligence, his intentions were most generous. By what means might one contribute even a ten-thousandth part to this? You gentlemen have long cherished loyal sincerity and are about to be presented at the great court; surely you have something to offer in advance as your pledge of service.

Question: Since antiquity it has been said that "talent is hard to find." Yet among the affairs of the world, which of them does not require talent to be managed? Not to speak of the high antiquity of the Five Emperors and Three Kings, from the two Han dynasties onward each era likewise governed in accordance with its own customs without borrowing talent from another age—how then can it be said that there was no talent? Indeed, it is not talent itself that is hard to find;…

title: 萬曆十年廣東鄉試錄
text:
才而如九德三俊之徒者難也士固各
以才效用今之爲士者大略有四品脩
詞之家稍能操翰輒自許不朽盛事是
謂文章之士其不能者則自託於圓覺
定慧超悟本心是謂談禪之士又其高
者慷慨負俗蟬蛻當世浮游塵表是謂
清言之士又其通者俯仰儕俗敏捷便
給以赴事功是謂衒霍之士斯四者可
以言才乎其亦有適於用否乎談轉移
===
於今日則遵何術或以爲宜登質直崇
正學責實功察似求眞何施而可諸士
其臚列而縷數之吾以觀才品焉
問史自尚書春秋左氏而下世稱太史遷
遷之書學者戶誦之訓故則若篤若廣
若駟若誕生若伯莊若貞若守節諸家
評隲則若固若勰若知幾若轍若周若
元量諸家可指言之與有議其記煩而
志寡者有恨其博不足者有知其有激
punctuated:
才而如九德、三俊之徒者難也。士固各以才效用，今之爲士者大略有四品：脩詞之家，稍能操翰，輒自許不朽盛事，是謂文章之士；其不能者，則自託於圓覺定慧、超悟本心，是謂談禪之士；又其高者，慷慨負俗，蟬蛻當世，浮游塵表，是謂清言之士；又其通者，俯仰儕俗，敏捷便給，以赴事功，是謂衒霍之士。斯四者可以言才乎？其亦有適於用否乎？談轉移於今日，則遵何術？或以爲宜登質直、崇正學、責實功、察似求眞，何施而可？諸士其臚列而縷數之，吾以觀才品焉。
問：史自《尚書》、《春秋》、《左氏》而下，世稱太史遷。遷之書，學者戶誦之。訓故則若篤、若廣、若駟、若誕生、若伯莊、若貞、若守節諸家；評隲則若固、若勰、若知幾、若轍、若周、若元量諸家，可指言之與？有議其記煩而志寡者，有恨其博不足者，有知其有激
translation_en:
…Rather, it is talents of the caliber of the practitioners of the Nine Virtues and the Three Categories of Ability that are hard to find. Scholars naturally each offer their service through their talents, yet among those who act as scholars today there are broadly four grades: Masters of rhetoric who, as soon as they have some skill in wielding the brush, flatter themselves that they are accomplishing an immortal enterprise—these are called scholars of belles-lettres. Those incapable of this entrust themselves to perfect enlightenment, meditative concentration and wisdom, and transcendent awakening to the original mind—these are called scholars who discourse on Chan Buddhism. Those who aim still higher, turning their backs on convention with impassioned spirit, shedding the world like a cicada its husk to roam beyond the dusty realm—these are called scholars of pure conversation (qingyan). And those who are adaptable, accommodating themselves to the common crowd, quick-witted and glib of tongue in pursuing practical achievements—these are called scholars of flashy ostentation. Can these four types be spoken of as true talent? Are any of them suited to practical use or not? If we speak of transforming this trend today, what methods should be followed? Some hold that we ought to promote upright simplicity, revere orthodox learning, demand substantive achievement, and scrutinize specious resemblances to seek the genuine—how should these be implemented to succeed? Let the candidates set these matters forth in order and enumerate them in detail, so that I may observe the quality of your talents therein.

Question: In historiography, coming down from the Book of Documents (Shangshu), the Spring and Autumn Annals (Chunqiu), and the Zuo Commentary (Zuoshi), the world acclaims the Grand Scribe Qian (Sima Qian 司馬遷). Every scholar recites Qian's work in his household. As for its exegesis and glosses, there are the various schools such as those of Yan Du 延篤, Xu Guang 徐廣, Pei Yin 裴駰, Zou Dansheng 鄒誕生, Liu Bozhuang 劉伯莊, Sima Zhen 司馬貞, and Zhang Shoujie 張守節; as for critical appraisal, there are the various critics such as Ban Gu 班固, Liu Xie 劉勰, Liu Zhiji 劉知幾, Su Zhe 蘇轍,谯 Zhou 譙周, and Ge Yuanliang 葛元量—can you point them out and discuss them? Some criticize his work for having prolix narratives yet scanty treatises; some regret that his erudition was still insufficient; some recognize that he was provoked…

title: 萬曆十年廣東鄉試錄
text:
而言之者有稱其隱而彰直而寛簡而
明者稱多愛愛奇者博學善敘事者然
與非與後世治遷史各以其意以意尊
信不掩其瑕以意詆訶不掩其瑜以款
啓爲月旦不覩其全至其體裁綜覈品
騭甄錄間是非當否可指摘其一二與
舍遷史而外亦可刪削昭雪訂正成一
家言否與誠倂舉二十一史次第潤色
一準於遷史豈非千古快事而世或難
===
其人也諸士中蓋有博洽爾雅如遷者
幸相與折衷之毋讓
問孔子有言國家不患寡不患貧貧與寡
不足患則所患者可知已
明興二百餘年生養休息閭閻日庶稱夥矣
帑藏日積稱富矣顧衆之所聚螳食土田今
土非能加益也將歲竭
國計給之與彼衆靡窮而藏有限何以待之
與說者謂歷稽往牒金用三品通錢法
punctuated:
而言之者，有稱其隱而彰、直而寛、簡而明者，稱多愛、愛奇者，博學善敘事者，然與？非與？後世治遷史，各以其意：以意尊信，不掩其瑕；以意詆訶，不掩其瑜；以款啓爲月旦，不覩其全。至其體裁、綜覈、品騭、甄錄間，是非當否，可指摘其一二與？舍遷史而外，亦可刪削、昭雪、訂正，成一家言否與？誠倂舉二十一史，次第潤色，一準於遷史，豈非千古快事？而世或難其人也。諸士中蓋有博洽爾雅如遷者，幸相與折衷之，毋讓。

問：孔子有言，國家不患寡，不患貧。貧與寡不足患，則所患者可知已。明興二百餘年，生養休息，閭閻日庶，稱夥矣；帑藏日積，稱富矣。顧衆之所聚，螳食土田，今土非能加益也，將歲竭國計給之與？彼衆靡窮，而藏有限，何以待之與？說者謂歷稽往牒，金用三品，通錢法
translation_en:
…and therefore wrote as he did; some praise his style as subtle yet clear, straightforward yet forgiving, and concise yet lucid; others say that he was overly fond of his subjects and loved the strange, or that he was broadly learned and skilled at narrating events. Are these judgments right or wrong? Later generations studying Sima Qian's history have each approached it according to their own preconceptions: those who revere and trust it according to their preconceptions do not conceal its flaws; those who disparage and criticize it according to their preconceptions do not obscure its merits; and those who pass critical judgments from a narrow perspective fail to see the work as a whole. As for its structural form, comprehensive verification, critical evaluations, and selection of material, can you point out one or two instances of what is right or wrong, appropriate or inappropriate? Setting Sima Qian's history aside, could one also abridge, exonerate, and emend [the other histories] to form an independent work of scholarship? If indeed one were to take up all of the Twenty-One Histories together and polish them in sequence, modeling everything entirely upon Sima Qian's history, would that not be a most gratifying achievement for all eternity? Yet the world finds it difficult to produce such a person. Among you gentlemen there are surely those as broadly learned and refined as Sima Qian; pray weigh and judge these matters together, and do not decline to speak.

Question: Confucius said that a state does not worry about scarcity of population, nor does it worry about poverty. If poverty and scarcity are not worth worrying about, then what is truly to be worried about can be known. For over two hundred years since the rise of the Ming, the people have been nurtured and given rest; the hamlets grow more populous by the day and may be called abundant; the state treasuries accumulate more by the day and may be called wealthy. Yet where the multitudes gather, they feed upon the land like locusts [?]. Today the land cannot be increased; shall we exhaust the state finances year after year to supply them? Those multitudes are无穷 (endless), whereas the treasuries are finite—how then shall we provide for them? Commentators say that, examining past records through the ages, metal currency was used in three grades, and circulating coinage…

title: 萬曆十年廣東鄉試錄
text:
以增民貲亦捄敝之一策與上自三代
下及漢唐宋藉爲國用
國家自洪永迄今阻格不甚行其故何在鼓
鑄不得其方流通不盡其術其弊何在
夫銅錢資也今銅散於委巷滯於商賈
而僅僅開滇池一隅尚有遺寶若乃錢
制病不精塗病未廣官病不耑譚錢法
者亦間及之甲是乙非未獲本策而以
曰法難遏矣今諸士足掛市里周悉民
===
利願詳言之俟司計者裁焉
問東粵昔稱奧區自弄兵以來莫寧其所
則四戰之國巳比者賴
主上威靈
廟堂勝筭文武臣工朋心比力夷險除穢漸號
完土顧粵地內多重岡複嶺山寇尚間
有椎剽外連巨海水寇叵測其能卽寢
武事以文令乎則戰非所諱言矣戰之
說有二曰大征曰鵰剿大征則靡財甚
punctuated:
以增民貲，亦捄敝之一策與？上自三代，下及漢、唐、宋，藉爲國用；國家自洪、永迄今，阻格不甚行，其故何在？鼓鑄不得其方，流通不盡其術，其弊何在？夫銅，錢資也。今銅散於委巷，滯於商賈，而僅僅開滇池一隅，尚有遺寶。若乃錢制病不精，塗病未廣，官病不耑，譚錢法者亦間及之。甲是乙非，未獲本策，而以曰法難遏矣。今諸士足掛市里，周悉民利，願詳言之，俟司計者裁焉。

問：東粵昔稱奧區，自弄兵以來，莫寧其所，則四戰之國巳。比者賴主上威靈、廟堂勝筭，文武臣工，朋心比力，夷險除穢，漸號完土。顧粵地內多重岡複嶺，山寇尚間有椎剽；外連巨海，水寇叵測。其能卽寢武事以文令乎？則戰非所諱言矣。戰之說有二：曰大征，曰鵰剿。大征則靡財甚，
translation_en:
… so as to increase the people's wealth—is this not also one policy for remedying the problem? From the Three Dynasties above down to the Han, Tang, and Song, it was relied upon for state expenditure; yet in our Dynasty, from the Hongwu and Yongle eras down to the present, it has met with obstruction and has not circulated very widely. What is the reason for this? When minting does not achieve the proper method and circulation does not exhaust the proper techniques, where do the abuses lie? Now copper is the raw material for coin. Today copper is scattered through the back alleys and stagnates in the hands of merchants, while mining is opened up merely in one corner around Dianchi (Yunnan), leaving unexploited treasures elsewhere. As for the defects that the standard of coinage is not refined, that the channels of distribution are not broad, and that the officials in charge do not have specialized authority—those who discuss monetary policy also touch upon these points from time to time. Yet what one affirms another denies, and no fundamental policy has been reached, so that instead they say [?] the system is hard to check [?]. Now you gentlemen set foot in the markets and neighborhoods and are thoroughly acquainted with what benefits the people. I wish you to speak of this in detail, awaiting the adjudication of those in charge of fiscal planning.

Question: Eastern Yue (Guangdong) was in former times called a richly endowed hinterland, but since armed uprisings began, no place has been at peace, so that it has become a land of warfare on all four sides. Recently, relying upon the august majesty of the Sovereign and the victorious calculations of the court, civil and military officials have joined hearts and combined strength, leveling strongholds and clearing out the vile, so that it is gradually coming to be called an intact territory. Yet inside Guangdong there are many overlapping hills and double mountain ranges, where mountain bandits still occasionally commit violent robberies; outside, it connects with the vast sea, where pirates are unpredictable. Can we immediately lay aside military affairs and govern by civil ordinances alone? Thus warfare is not something we can avoid speaking of. In the discussion of warfare there are two approaches: one is called the grand campaign (dazheng), and the other is called the hawk-strike raid (diaojiao). A grand campaign wastes immense wealth, …

title: 萬曆十年廣東鄉試錄
text:
罄郡縣之貲無足以佐軍興鵰勦則漏
姦賊以遺禍二者孰宜戰守之兵在水
陸二寨或謂民甫息肩當撤兵以寬民
力或謂嶺外非馴民有角者觸有齒者
齧其天性固然解甲束馬脫有警能驅
市人與鬭乎卽水陸二兵議留議撤緩
急輕重必有能辨之者諸士爲枌榆籌
石畫當陳於未戰毋徒曰俟鼓之日也
punctuated: 罄郡縣之貲，無足以佐軍興；鵰勦則漏姦賊以遺禍，二者孰宜？戰守之兵，在水陸二寨。或謂民甫息肩，當撤兵以寬民力；或謂嶺外非馴民，有角者觸，有齒者齧，其天性固然，解甲束馬，脫有警，能驅市人與鬭乎？卽水陸二兵，議留議撤，緩急輕重，必有能辨之者。諸士爲枌榆籌石畫，當陳於未戰，毋徒曰俟鼓之日也。
translation_en:
…exhausting the resources of the prefectures and counties without sufficing to support military mobilization; whereas targeted raids let treacherous bandits slip through to leave behind future calamity. Which of these two is more appropriate?

The troops for offense and defense lie in the naval and land stockades. Some say that since the common people have just rested their shoulders from their burdens, we should withdraw the troops in order to ease the people's strength. Others say that the people beyond the Five Ridges are not docile: those with horns gore and those with teeth bite—their natural disposition is inherently so. If we unstrap our armor and tie up our horses, and should an alarm arise, could we drive market folk into battle? Even regarding the naval and land forces, in deliberating whether to retain or withdraw them, there must be those who can discern their relative urgency and importance. You scholars, in devising rock-solid plans for your native homeland, ought to set them forth before battle begins; do not merely say that you will wait until the day the war drums sound.

title: 萬曆十年廣東鄉試錄
text:

title: 萬曆十年廣東鄉試錄
text:
第壹場
四書
孔子曰益者三樂損者三樂樂節禮樂樂
道人之善樂多賢友益矣樂驕樂樂佚
遊樂宴樂損矣
梁維屏
同考試官教諭姚批題多頭緒作者類煩冗
可厭此卷刋落言筌直見本色宜式多士
同考試官教諭高批渾厚古雅不事綺麗是
文之復古者
===
考試官教諭胡批醇雅可誦結意尤精
考試官教諭陳批發損益意精透
樂有損益于心之敬肆辨之也夫樂生于心者
也心敬則益心肆則損是以君子慎所樂與夫
子意謂吾人一心曷嘗無所用哉其有所向也
而樂生矣其有所入也而樂成矣顧均之爲樂
也樂得其道而益者有三樂得其欲而損者有
三何言乎益也心存于中感物而動其所深嗜
punctuated:
第壹場
四書
「孔子曰：『益者三樂，損者三樂。樂節禮樂，樂道人之善，樂多賢友，益矣。樂驕樂，樂佚遊，樂宴樂，損矣。』」
梁維屏

樂有損益，于心之敬肆辨之也。夫樂生于心者也，心敬則益，心肆則損，是以君子慎所樂與！夫子意謂：吾人一心，曷嘗無所用哉？其有所向也，而樂生矣；其有所入也，而樂成矣。顧均之爲樂也，樂得其道而益者有三，樂得其欲而損者有三。何言乎益也？心存于中，感物而動，其所深嗜…

First Session
Four Books
"Confucius said: 'There are three kinds of pleasure that are beneficial, and three kinds of pleasure that are harmful. To take pleasure in the due regulation of ritual and music, to take pleasure in speaking of the goodness of others, and to take pleasure in having many worthy friends—these are beneficial. To take pleasure in extravagant pleasures, to take pleasure in idle wandering, and to take pleasure in the pleasures of feasting—these are harmful.'" [Analects 16.5]
Liang Weiping 梁維屏
Associate Examiner and Instructor Yao 姚 comments: The topic has many threads, and writers generally make it tedious and wearisome. This paper strips away verbal trappings and directly reveals the true substance; it should serve as a model for the many scholars.
Associate Examiner and Instructor Gao 高 comments: Substantial, profound, and of ancient elegance, without indulging in ornate beauty; this is prose that returns to antiquity.
Examiner and Instructor Hu 胡 comments: Pure, elegant, and worthy of recitation; the concluding idea is especially fine.
Examiner and Instructor Chen 陳 comments: It brings out the meaning of harm and benefit with refined thoroughness.
That pleasures bring harm or benefit is distinguished by the reverence or laxity of the mind. Now, pleasure is born from the mind; when the mind is reverent, there is benefit, and when the mind is lax, there is harm. Therefore, how cautious the gentleman is in what he takes pleasure in! The Master's meaning is that as for this one mind of ours, when is it ever without application? Where it has an inclination, pleasure is born; where it enters deeply, pleasure is brought to completion. Yet while all are equally pleasures, there are three that attain the Way in their pleasure and thus bring benefit, and three that pursue desires in their pleasure and thus bring harm. Why are they called beneficial? When the mind is preserved within and is moved in response to things, that which it deeply relishes…

title: 萬曆十年廣東鄉試錄
text:
而篤好者節禮樂焉道人之善焉多賢友焉養
吾中和之德則本體益融廣吾觀摩之資則進
脩益懋蓋一念敬將上達無所不至始焉心樂
之既乃與之俱化而不自知也故曰益者三樂
何言乎損也心馳于外逐物而流其所深嗜而
篤好者驕樂焉佚遊焉宴樂焉矜夸之氣勝則
檢節之意微淫惰之習滋則賢善之交遠蓋一
念肆將下達無所不至始焉心樂之既亦與之
俱化而不自知也故曰損者三樂吁人之爲學
===
求其益不求其損而一念易移入乎損即出乎
益盍早辨之而已是樂也豈惟學者宜慎之夫
快意當前恒情易溺而憸媚之徒日從臾其間
損之樂日益而益之樂日損非宣哲濬明疇能
鑒焉彼夫履綦鳴玉左規矩右準繩而又朝夕
箴圖先後師保以相爲交儆斯能察於損益之
際而自得其心者與
或生而知之或學而知之或困而知之及
其知之一也或安而行之或利而行之
punctuated:
而篤好者，節禮樂焉，道人之善焉，多賢友焉。養吾中和之德，則本體益融；廣吾觀摩之資，則進脩益懋。蓋一念敬將，上達無所不至；始焉心樂之，既乃與之俱化而不自知也。故曰「益者三樂」。何言乎損也？心馳于外，逐物而流，其所深嗜而篤好者，驕樂焉，佚遊焉，宴樂焉。矜夸之氣勝，則檢節之意微；淫惰之習滋，則賢善之交遠。蓋一念肆將，下達無所不至；始焉心樂之，既亦與之俱化而不自知也。故曰「損者三樂」。吁！人之爲學，求其益，不求其損；而一念易移，入乎損即出乎益，盍早辨之而已。是樂也，豈惟學者宜慎之！夫快意當前，恒情易溺，而憸媚之徒日從臾其間，損之樂日益，而益之樂日損，非宣哲濬明，疇能鑒焉？彼夫履綦鳴玉，左規矩，右準繩，而又朝夕箴圖，先後師保，以相爲交儆，斯能察於損益之際，而自得其心者與！
「或生而知之，或學而知之，或困而知之，及其知之，一也。或安而行之，或利而行之，
translation_en:
…and earnestly loves are: finding joy in the due regulation of rites and music, finding joy in speaking of the goodness of others, and finding joy in having many worthy friends. When one nurtures one's virtue of equilibrium and harmony, the fundamental substance becomes ever more integrated; when one broadens the resources for mutual observation and emulation, one's advancement in self-cultivation becomes ever more vigorous. Indeed, when a single thought is sustained by reverence, there is nowhere in the upward reach that it cannot attain; at first the mind delights in these things, and eventually it is transformed along with them without even realizing it. Therefore it is said, "There are three joys that are beneficial." What is meant by the harmful? When the mind gallops outward, pursuing external things and drifting along, what it deeply craves and earnestly loves are: finding joy in extravagant pride, finding joy in idle wandering, and finding joy inlicentious feasting. When an arrogant and boastful spirit prevails, the intention of self-restraint grows faint; when dissolute and lazy habits multiply, companionship with the worthy and good grows distant. Indeed, when a single thought is sustained by indulgence, there is nowhere in the downward sink that it cannot reach; at first the mind delights in these things, and eventually it too is transformed along with them without even realizing it. Therefore it is said, "There are three joys that are harmful." Alas! In pursuing learning, a person seeks what is beneficial and does not seek what is harmful; yet a single thought easily shifts, and to enter into harm is immediately to depart from benefit—why not simply discern it early on? And as for such joys, is it only scholars who ought to be cautious about them? When gratifying pleasures are right before one's eyes, ordinary feelings easily drown in them, while base and flattering men daily urge one on from amidst them. Thus harmful joys increase day by day, while beneficial joys diminish day by day; without pervasive wisdom and profound enlightenment, who would be able to take warning from this? As for those who tread in ceremonial shoes and sound their jade pendants, having compasses and squares to their left and plumb-lines to their right, and who morning and evening have admonitory diagrams before them and Preceptors and Guardians before and behind to mutually warn and caution them—are they not the ones able to discern the boundary between benefit and harm, and thus remain in possession of their own minds?

title: 萬曆十年廣東鄉試錄
text:
或勉强而行之及其成功一也子曰好
學近乎知力行近乎仁知恥近乎勇
莫維則
同考試官教諭鄒批題中一與近正相照應
此作最得肯綮而詞更冲雅錄之
考試官教諭胡批理精詞整
考試官教諭陳批大雅之文
論人於達德要之則一求之則近也夫終而一
者成德也始而近者入德也彼困勉者可自諉
===
耶且夫達德在人理本一而非二機本近而非
遠也人顧自力何如耳彼道著於人不必生知
而後可語知也或得之學或得之困雖若各一
其知及觀於既知之後無二知焉何也道要之
能知而止也道體於人不必安行而後可語行
也或由于利或由于勉雖若各一其行及觀於
成功之後無二行焉何也道要之能行而止也
夫于知可以觀知于行可以觀仁于知仁之一
而可以觀勇矣彼未能一者其何以近之哉天
punctuated:
或勉强而行之，及其成功，一也。子曰：「好學近乎知，力行近乎仁，知恥近乎勇。」
莫維則
同考試官教諭鄒批：題中「一」與「近」正相照應，此作最得肯綮，而詞更冲雅，錄之。
考試官教諭胡批：理精詞整。
考試官教諭陳批：大雅之文。
論人於達德，要之則一，求之則近也。夫終而一者，成德也；始而近者，入德也。彼困勉者可自諉耶？且夫達德在人，理本一而非二，機本近而非遠也，人顧自力何如耳。彼道著於人，不必生知而後可語知也。或得之學，或得之困，雖若各一其知，及觀於既知之後，無二知焉。何也？道要之能知而止也。道體於人，不必安行而後可語行也。或由于利，或由于勉，雖若各一其行，及觀於成功之後，無二行焉。何也？道要之能行而止也。夫于知可以觀知，于行可以觀仁，于知仁之一而可以觀勇矣。彼未能一者，其何以近之哉？天
