What people past and present have worried about is that the population is not yet numerous and the stored reserves are not yet abundant; yet these two are minor as worries go! When the ancients spent ten years gathering and multiplying the populace and ten years instructing them, what worry was there of not having a large population? It is only when the people have become teeming and multitude that, if they are left hungry, they rebel, whereas if they are fed, it drains resources; therefore, the reason the worry of an already large population is worse than that of a small population lies in quelling rebellion while managing expenditures. When three years of labor leave one year's surplus of reserves, and nine years leave three years' surplus, what worry is there of not having wealth? It is only when everyone is bustling and prosperous in wealth that, if it is monopolized, it breeds resentment, whereas if it is distributed, it becomes exhausted; therefore, the reason the worry of already achieved wealth is worse than that of insufficient wealth lies in dissolving resentment while rescuing reserves from exhaustion. …

title: 萬曆十年廣東鄉試錄
text:
故夫豪傑之士所爲愁心積慮而講者莫
如食而分之食而分之者非朝饔之夕飧
之家給而戶賜之也蓋有道焉其在
今日則錢法所宜亟講者古昔盛時庶人家
授田百畝食鹽自丈夫至嬰兒月有數年
七十至九十饋肉有差家三幼以上至五
幼復征予葆凡三等此四者古人所以安
衆與富之道今皆不然然則古之民寡今
之民衆寡者富在於民而衆者富在於官
===
加之田不益毛海不益鹺國中之老者幼
者遞死遞生蕃育滋庶此不食而分之以
振其乏絕匪亂則怨徒食而分之而短於
經計匪費則竭司計者之憂也
明興餘二百年
高皇帝仁厚儉勤垂庥甚盛廓培底於
列聖九有煕洽
聖天子蠲其
大德以覆露之自
punctuated:
故夫豪傑之士所爲愁心積慮而講者，莫如食而分之。食而分之者，非朝饔之、夕飧之，家給而戶賜之也。蓋有道焉，其在今日，則錢法所宜亟講者。古昔盛時，庶人家授田百畝；食鹽自丈夫至嬰兒，月有數；年七十至九十，饋肉有差；家三幼以上至五幼，復征、予葆凡三等。此四者，古人所以安衆與富之道，今皆不然。然則古之民寡，今之民衆；寡者富在於民，而衆者富在於官。加之田不益毛，海不益鹺，國中之老者、幼者，遞死遞生，蕃育滋庶。此不食而分之以振其乏絕，匪亂則怨；徒食而分之而短於經計，匪費則竭，司計者之憂也。
明興餘二百年，高皇帝仁厚儉勤，垂庥甚盛；廓培底於列聖，九有煕洽。聖天子蠲其大德以覆露之，自
translation_en:
Therefore, what men of extraordinary talent anxiously deliberate over and discuss is nothing other than how to feed the people and distribute wealth among them. Yet feeding them and distributing wealth does not mean providing them with morning and evening meals, or bestowing gifts upon every household and door. Rather, there is a proper method to it; at the present day, it is the coinage policy that ought to be urgently discussed. In the flourishing eras of antiquity, each commoner family was allotted a hundred mu of land; edible salt was rationed monthly in fixed amounts from adult men down to infants; those aged seventy to ninety were presented with meat according to graded ranks; and families with three to five young children were granted exemptions from levies or given wet-nurses across three tiers. These four measures were the means by which the ancients secured a populous and wealthy society, yet none of them are practiced today. Thus, in antiquity the people were few, whereas today the people are numerous; when they were few, wealth resided among the people, whereas when they are numerous, wealth resides with the state. Moreover, the fields do not yield additional crops, nor do the seas yield additional salt, while the elderly and the young within the realm pass away and are born in turn, multiplying into an ever greater multitude. Under these circumstances, if we do not feed them and distribute wealth to relieve their destitution, there will be resentment if not rebellion; yet if we merely feed them and distribute wealth while falling short in long-term fiscal planning, resources will be exhausted if not squandered—this is the worry of those in charge of state finances.

More than two hundred years since the rise of the Ming, the August Emperor Gao (Hongwu) was benevolent, generous, frugal, and diligent, bequeathing a most abundant blessing; this was broadened and nurtured down through the successive Emperors, bringing harmony and prosperity to the Nine Provinces. His Sacred Majesty the Son of Heaven manifests his great virtue to shelter and nourish the realm, from…

title: 萬曆十年廣東鄉試錄
text:
玉牒之蕃以及閭閻生齒日息不可謂不眾
太倉之積與夫三輔諸路斂藏日盈不可
謂不富眾在於下不得不仰於上富在於
上不得不給於下故錢法者不收之田不
計之海不出之府庫無損於
國而利於民
今日捄敝上務也考之列星圖曰天錢十星
在北落西豈天之所布不可變而治天下
者當因之與夏鑄歷山商鑄莊山成周立
===
圜法泉府制獨詳則先王所籍也漢自元
狩至元始成五銖錢二百八十億萬唐開
元中天下七十餘爐歲入錢百萬宋元豐
中天下五十三監歲入錢千萬則後王所
貲也
國家百典上稽三代下陋漢唐宋乃自洪永
迄今錢阻格不甚行而欲富埒古人乎此
愚所未解也鑄不得其方用不盡其法一
或齟齬輒曰錢法難行吁亦過矣古今議
punctuated: 玉牒之蕃，以及閭閻生齒日息，不可謂不眾；太倉之積，與夫三輔諸路斂藏日盈，不可謂不富。眾在於下，不得不仰於上；富在於上，不得不給於下。故錢法者，不收之田，不計之海，不出之府庫，無損於國而利於民，今日捄敝上務也。考之《列星圖》，曰：「天錢十星，在北落西。」豈天之所布不可變，而治天下者當因之與？夏鑄歷山，商鑄莊山，成周立圜法、泉府，制獨詳，則先王所籍也。漢自元狩至元始，成五銖錢二百八十億萬；唐開元中，天下七十餘爐，歲入錢百萬；宋元豐中，天下五十三監，歲入錢千萬，則後王所貲也。國家百典，上稽三代，下陋漢、唐、宋，乃自洪、永迄今，錢阻格不甚行，而欲富埒古人乎？此愚所未解也。鑄不得其方，用不盡其法，一或齟齬，輒曰：「錢法難行。」吁！亦過矣。古今議
translation_en: … the proliferation of the imperial clan register (Yudie), down to the daily increase of the population in the towns and villages, it cannot be said that the people are not numerous. As for the reserves of the Metropolitan Granaries (Taicang), along with the daily filling of the tax stores in the Three Metropolitan Areas and the various circuits, it cannot be said that the state is not wealthy. Since the multitudes are below, they cannot but look for support from above; since the wealth is above, it cannot but be distributed to those below. Therefore, the system of coinage—which is not levied from the fields, not taxed from the seas, and not drawn out of the treasuries, causing no loss to the state while benefiting the people—is the paramount task for remedying our present ills. Examining the Chart of the Constellations (Liexing tu), it says: "The ten stars of Celestial Coin (Tianqian) lie west of Fomalhaut (Beiluo)." Is it not that what Heaven has arranged cannot be altered, and that those who govern the Empire ought to follow it? The Xia cast coins from Mount Li, the Shang cast coins from Mount Zhuang, and the accomplished Zhou established the Round-Coin System (huanfa) and the Treasury of Currency (Quanfu), whose regulations were uniquely detailed; these were what the former kings relied upon. In the Han, from the Yuanshou (122–117 BCE) to the Yuanshi (1–5 CE) eras, twenty-eight billion wuzhu coins were minted; in the Tang, during the Kaiyuan era (713–741), over seventy furnaces across the realm produced an annual revenue of a million strings of cash; in the Song, during the Yuanfeng era (1078–1085), fifty-three directorates across the realm produced an annual revenue of ten million strings of cash; these were the resources upon which later rulers depended. In all its hundred institutions, our Dynasty models itself above on the Three Dynasties and looks down below upon the Han, Tang, and Song; yet from the Hongwu (1368–1398) and Yongle (1403–1424) eras down to the present, coinage has been obstructed and does not circulate widely—and yet we wish our wealth to equal that of the ancients? This is what I, in my ignorance, cannot understand. When casting does not attain the proper method and usage does not exhaust its full regulations, at the slightest friction people immediately say, "The coinage system is difficult to carry out!" Alas, how excessive that is! Past and present discussions of …

title: 萬曆十年廣東鄉試錄
text:
鑄無若西漢二賈誼之言曰銅畢歸於上
山之言曰民不應與主共柄今姦民私鑄
陰持主柄以厲公錢果如誼言上收銅勿
令布民安所得銅而私鑄之故收銅之說
持柄息姦之要術也
高皇帝始定天下
令軍民惟鑄鑑及軍器一切廢銅並收之官
毋私藏無何寢罷至於今浮屠瞿曇與夫
齊民之鋪釺銷盋大氐亡慮皆銅矣今將
===
剏焉而奪民銅則民駭貿以金則時絀儻
於
京師及三輔諸路支郡各責一官與民市銅
售之錢視銅之直私藏者罪無赦大約可
一歲收盡民銅民以銅得錢而可無私藏
罪其誰不欣然而輸之官官以錢得銅而
可為續鑄貲又何憚而不收之民況藏銅
于民銅直銅也而姦鑄有訾銅一入官銅
盡錢也而經用益饒
punctuated: 鑄，無若西漢二賈：誼之言曰：「銅畢歸於上。」山之言曰：「民不應與主共柄。」今姦民私鑄，陰持主柄以厲公錢。果如誼言，上收銅勿令布，民安所得銅而私鑄之？故收銅之說，持柄息姦之要術也。高皇帝始定天下，令軍民惟鑄鑑及軍器，一切廢銅並收之官，毋私藏。無何寢罷，至於今，浮屠瞿曇與夫齊民之鋪釺銷盋，大氐亡慮皆銅矣。今將剏焉而奪民銅，則民駭；貿以金，則時絀。儻於京師及三輔、諸路支郡，各責一官與民市銅，售之錢視銅之直，私藏者罪無赦，大約可一歲收盡民銅。民以銅得錢而可無私藏罪，其誰不欣然而輸之官？官以錢得銅而可為續鑄貲，又何憚而不收之民？況藏銅于民，銅直銅也，而姦鑄有訾；銅一入官，銅盡錢也，而經用益饒。
translation_en: … coinage, none surpass the two Jias of the Western Han: Jia Yi 賈誼 said, "Let all copper return to the sovereign above," and Jia Shan 賈山 said, "The common people ought not share authority with the ruler." Today, villainous people engage in illicit minting, secretly usurping the ruler's authority to the detriment of official coins. If indeed, as Jia Yi suggested, the ruler were to collect all copper and not allow it to circulate widely, from where would the people obtain copper to mint illicitly? Therefore, the policy of collecting copper is the essential technique for holding fast to authority and putting an end to villainy. When the Exalted Emperor (Gao Huangdi 高皇帝, i.e., Emperor Taizu) first pacified the realm, he decreed that military and civilian households could cast only mirrors and military weapons, while all scrap copper was to be collected by the government, with private hoarding forbidden. Before long, this fell into abeyance, so that down to the present day, images of the Buddha Gautama, as well as the door knockers, inlays, cauldrons, and bowls [?] of the common people, are by and large almost all made of copper. If we were now suddenly to initiate a policy of seizing copper from the people, the people would be alarmed; yet if we were to purchase it with silver, current finances are strained. Suppose that in the Capital, the Three Metropolitan Areas, and the prefectures of the various circuits, an official were assigned in each place to buy copper from the people, paying them in coin according to the value of the copper, while punishing private hoarders without pardon—then in roughly a year all the people's copper could be completely collected. Since the people would obtain coins for their copper and avoid the crime of private hoarding, who among them would not gladly deliver it to the government? And since the government would obtain copper with coins and gain the capital for continued minting, why should it hesitate to collect it from the people? Moreover, when copper is stored among the people, copper is merely copper, and there is the defect of illicit minting; once copper enters the government, all copper becomes coin, and regular state expenditures are increasingly enriched. …

title: 萬曆十年廣東鄉試錄
text:
聖主所爲持大柄澹公私無先此畫者故銅之
權不可不收也黄帝封銅山令十里外乘
者行行者趨齊桓公封銅山令犯者左足
入刖左右足入刖右今滇中之銅估人得
擅回易而盗相者罪止戍姦鑄者何慮無
銅今欲禁姦鑄則亡如封銅山而嚴盗相
令俾回易者亡得擅即有項梁桼木之徒
無自逞矣故銅之源不可不固也或曰天
地之利不導之而封之何也曰非也法錢
未布則閉之以塞姦法錢旣流則開之以
疏利似今之銅止滇南一隅隘矣山海經
曰海内銅山四百六十七漢鄧通鑄於嚴
道吳王鑄於豫章唐鑄於陜宣衢信銅冶
九十六宋鑄於諸路銅冶百三十六
國初
令天下行省置寶泉局
文皇帝
遣官於江浙閩廣鑄錢宣德間始罷採信饒
punctuated: 聖主所爲持大柄、澹公私，無先此畫者。故銅之權不可不收也。黄帝封銅山，令十里外乘者行、行者趨；齊桓公封銅山，令犯者左足入刖左、右足入刖右。今滇中之銅，估人得擅回易，而盗相者罪止戍，姦鑄者何慮無銅？今欲禁姦鑄，則亡如封銅山而嚴盗相令，俾回易者亡得擅，即有項梁桼木之徒，無自逞矣。故銅之源不可不固也。或曰：「天地之利，不導之而封之，何也？」曰：「非也。法錢未布，則閉之以塞姦；法錢旣流，則開之以疏利。似今之銅，止滇南一隅，隘矣。《山海經》曰：『海内銅山四百六十七。』漢鄧通鑄於嚴道，吳王鑄於豫章；唐鑄於陜、宣、衢、信，銅冶九十六；宋鑄於諸路，銅冶百三十六。國初，令天下行省置寶泉局；文皇帝遣官於江、浙、閩、廣鑄錢；宣德間，始罷採信、饒…
translation_en: …As for how the Sagely Ruler holds the great handle of authority and provides for both public and private needs, no plan takes precedence over this. Therefore, the control over copper must be reclaimed by the state. The Yellow Emperor sealed off the copper mountains, ordering that from ten li away, riders must dismount to walk and walkers must hasten past; Duke Huan of Qi sealed off the copper mountains, ordering that trespassers who stepped in with their left foot have the left foot amputated, and those who stepped in with their right foot have the right foot amputated. Today, merchants are able to trade at will in the copper of Yunnan, and those who illicitly prospect [?] are punished with no more than military exile; why should illicit minters worry about lacking copper? If we now wish to prohibit illicit minting, nothing is better than sealing off the copper mountains and making strict the laws against illicit prospecting [?], so that traders cannot act on their own authority; then even if there are fellows like Xiang Liang and Qimu [?], they will have no way to work their will. Therefore, the sources of copper must be secured. Someone may ask: "Why seal off the benefits of Heaven and Earth instead of channeling them?" I reply: "Not so. When statutory coins have not yet been widely distributed, one closes the mines to block illicit profiteering; once statutory coins are in circulation, one opens them to channel the benefit. As things stand today, relying on copper from the single corner of southern Yunnan alone is far too narrow. The Classic of Mountains and Seas (Shanhai jing) says: 'Within the seas there are four hundred and sixty-seven copper mountains.' In the Han, Deng Tong minted coins at Yandao, and the Prince of Wu minted at Yuzhang; the Tang minted in Shan, Xuan, Qu, and Xin prefectures, with ninety-six copper smelteries; the Song minted across the various circuits, with one hundred and thirty-six copper smelteries. At the beginning of our dynasty, the branch secretariats throughout the empire were ordered to establish Coinage Services (Baoquan ju); the Wen Emperor [Emperor Chengzu] dispatched officials to mint coins in Jiangxi, Zhejiang, Fujian, and Guangdong; and only during the Xuande reign (1426–1435) did the court cease mining in Xin and Rao prefectures…"…

title: 萬曆十年廣東鄉試錄
text:
則銅非獨產於滇也儻盡籍天下銅山倣
漢唐宋故事即山鑄錢則天地之銅盡為
國計故銅之利不可不開也善乎孔顗之言
曰民之盜鑄嚴法不能禁者由上惜銅愛
工故也上之惜銅愛工者曰鑄錢利微錢
成之利不足償工非也王者以四海為家
費百萬以得百萬則二百萬費千萬以鑄
千萬則二千萬何契契乎錙兩之較也第
顗之說則又有未盡者不惜銅似矣不擇
===
銅而定其衡則雜不愛工似矣不擇工而
峻其防則疎銅者錢之質也蒼則蒼黃則
黃而誰能違之輕重者錢之衡也四銖則
太輕六銖則太重而誰能準之工者錢之
範而弊之藪也模不模範不範而誰能覈
之故惟不雜錫镴以虧其肉好獨留五銖
以一其耳目擇二局之良者分遣諸路為
工師而高垣闈嚴干掫以稽其姦挾斯弊
袪範良矣故錢之制貴精也夫錢泉也流
punctuated: 則銅非獨產於滇也。儻盡籍天下銅山，倣漢、唐、宋故事，即山鑄錢，則天地之銅盡為國計，故銅之利不可不開也。善乎孔顗之言曰：「民之盜鑄，嚴法不能禁者，由上惜銅愛工故也。」上之惜銅愛工者，曰鑄錢利微，錢成之利不足償工，非也。王者以四海為家，費百萬以得百萬，則二百萬；費千萬以鑄千萬，則二千萬，何契契乎錙兩之較也？第顗之說，則又有未盡者。不惜銅似矣，不擇銅而定其衡則雜；不愛工似矣，不擇工而峻其防則疎。銅者，錢之質也，蒼則蒼，黃則黃，而誰能違之？輕重者，錢之衡也，四銖則太輕，六銖則太重，而誰能準之？工者，錢之範而弊之藪也，模不模，範不範，而誰能覈之？故惟不雜錫鑞以虧其肉好，獨留五銖以一其耳目，擇二局之良者分遣諸路為工師，而高垣闈、嚴干掫，以稽其姦挾，斯弊袪範良矣。故錢之制貴精也。夫錢，泉也，流
translation_en:
… Thus, copper is not produced solely in Yunnan. If we were to register all the copper mountains in the empire and, following the precedents of the Han, Tang, and Song dynasties, mint coins right at the mountains, then all the copper between heaven and earth would serve the state's finances; therefore, the profit from copper must be opened up.

Well said were the words of Kong Yi 孔顗: "The reason private illicit minting by the people cannot be stopped even by severe laws is that the court above begrudges copper and spares labor." Those above who begrudge copper and spare labor claim that the profit from minting coins is slight and that the gain from the finished coins is insufficient to compensate for the labor—this is wrong. A true king takes all within the four seas as his household: if he spends a million to obtain a million, there are two million; if he spends ten million to mint ten million, there are twenty million. Why fret so anxiously over comparing pennies and ounces?

Yet Kong Yi's argument still leaves something unsaid. Not begrudging copper sounds right, but if one does not select the copper and fix its weight standard, the coins will be adulterated. Not sparing labor sounds right, but if one does not select the artisans and tighten precautions against them, oversight will be lax. Copper is the substance of the coin: if it is greenish, it stays greenish; if it is yellow, it stays yellow—who can alter that? Weight is the standard of the coin: four zhu is too light, and six zhu is too heavy—who can standardize that? Artisans are the molders of the coin and also the hotbed of abuses: if the patterns are not true patterns and the molds are not true molds, who can verify them? Therefore, only by not mixing in tin or pewter to impair the coin's body and hole, retaining the five-zhu weight alone to unify what people see and hear, selecting skilled artisans from the two mint bureaus to be dispatched to the various circuits as master craftsmen, and building high walls and gates while enforcing strict night patrols to inspect for smuggling and fraud—only then will abuses be eliminated and the casting be of fine quality. Thus, in the system of coinage, precision is what is valued.

Now, coins (qian) are like a flowing spring (quan): if they circulate…

title: 萬曆十年廣東鄉試錄
text:
於下而壅於上行於賤而閡於貴即曰肆
人於市無以為也志曰天用莫如龍地用
莫如馬人用莫如龜此言用錢之涂不可
狹也漢隆慮主以錢千萬為其子贖死今
鍰金獨不可入乎漢律人出一筭筭百二
十錢今民賦獨不可入乎漢募豪民入粟
縣官而內錢於都內今開納獨不可入乎
漢館陶主為其子求郎不許賞錢千萬今
賞賚貴戚閹尹獨不可予乎漢胡降者贍以少
===
府禁錢今諸邊夷市獨不可予乎漢時時
出內庫錢賜軍士今養軍獨不可予乎夫
錢下而不上則其權在市井上而下下而
上則其權在
朝廷誠用之如循環行之如流水上闢其出
之涂若
賜予若吏祿若雇直無不以下下闢其入之涂
若軍興若筭事若鍰贖無不以上何不行
足慮故錢之涂貴廣也周立九府則周公
punctuated: 於下而壅於上，行於賤而閡於貴，即曰肆人於市，無以為也。《志》曰：「天用莫如龍，地用莫如馬，人用莫如龜。」此言用錢之涂不可狹也。漢隆慮主以錢千萬為其子贖死，今鍰金獨不可入乎？漢律人出一筭，筭百二十錢，今民賦獨不可入乎？漢募豪民入粟縣官，而內錢於都內，今開納獨不可入乎？漢館陶主為其子求郎，不許，賞錢千萬，今賞賚貴戚、閹尹，獨不可予乎？漢胡降者贍以少府禁錢，今諸邊夷市，獨不可予乎？漢時時出內庫錢賜軍士，今養軍獨不可予乎？夫錢下而不上，則其權在市井；上而下、下而上，則其權在朝廷。誠用之如循環，行之如流水，上闢其出之涂，若賜予、若吏祿、若雇直，無不以下；下闢其入之涂，若軍興、若筭事、若鍰贖，無不以上，何不行足慮？故錢之涂貴廣也。周立九府，則周公、
translation_en: …below while remaining blocked above, and circulates among the lowly while being obstructed among the noble, then even if one were to execute people in the marketplace, nothing could be done about it. The Treatise says: "For the use of Heaven, nothing is like the dragon; for the use of Earth, nothing is like the horse; for the use of Man, nothing is like the tortoise-shell currency." This means that the channels for using coin must not be narrow. In the Han dynasty, the Princess of Longlü (隆慮主) paid ten million coins to redeem her son from the death penalty; today, can redemption fines alone not be paid in coin? Under Han law, each person paid one unit of poll tax (suan 筭), with a unit being one hundred and twenty coins; today, can the people's taxes alone not be paid in coin? The Han recruited wealthy commoners to deliver grain to the state and deposit coin in the Capital Treasury (Dunei 都內); today, can contributions for rank and office alone not be received in coin? In the Han, the Princess of Guantao (館陶主) requested an appointment as Court Gentleman (Lang 郎) for her son; the emperor refused, but bestowed upon her ten million coins; today, when bestowing rewards on imperial relatives and Palace Eunuchs, can coin alone not be given to them? The Han supported surrendered northern tribesmen with privy funds from the Lesser Treasury (Shaofu 少府); today, at the border markets for foreign tribes, can coin alone not be given to them? The Han frequently disbursed coin from the palace storehouses to reward soldiers; today, in maintaining the army, can coin alone not be given to them? Now, if coin goes downward from above without returning upward, then control over it rests with the marketplace; if it flows down from above and returns up from below, then control over it rests with the Royal Court. If indeed it is used like an endless circle and circulates like flowing water—with those above opening up channels for its disbursement, such that imperial bestowals, officials' salaries, and wages for hired labor are all paid downward in coin, and those below opening up channels for its receipt, such that military levies, poll and property taxes, and redemption fines are all paid upward in coin—then what need would there be to worry about it failing to circulate? Therefore, the channels for coin must be wide. When the Zhou established the Nine Treasuries (Jiufu 九府), the Duke of Zhou (Zhougong 周公)…

title: 萬曆十年廣東鄉試錄
text:
太公齊有管敬仲楚有孫叔敖咸宰相主
之唐賜爐止世民元吉則親王領之晏琦
以侍郎領鑄錢使於江淮杜鎬等以祕閣
校理討鑄錢故事於禁苑彼其利溥而用
鉅豈直法勝人亦與焉誠宜略倣古制如
愚所云專責一官者無惜稍假以權聽其
心計而終嚴以法正其黜陟贗而窳者黜
壅者□□汀者黜聽民開山藏器者黜從
姦鑄者黜又何不行為慮乎故錢之官貴
===
顓也夫收銅之權則利不散之委巷固銅
之源□□人無所牟於山澤開銅之利則
地不愛□精錢之制則姦鑄不得亂其形
廣錢之涂則下不賤錢顓錢之官則法必
行而民重犯六者雖管賈餘談而
國家完計亡以代此矣嗟乎海內
宗室歔食者半百官奉薄或至箕會瀕海閭
左動噪脫巾水旱夭行民室縣罄當此之
時使公錢之貫山積帑藏則以
punctuated: 太公；齊有管敬仲，楚有孫叔敖，咸宰相主之。唐賜爐止世民、元吉，則親王領之；晏、琦以侍郎領鑄錢使於江淮；杜鎬等以祕閣校理討鑄錢故事於禁苑。彼其利溥而用鉅，豈直法勝？人亦與焉。誠宜略倣古制，如愚所云專責一官者，無惜稍假以權，聽其心計，而終嚴以法，正其黜陟。贗而窳者黜，壅者□□汀者黜，聽民開山藏器者黜，從姦鑄者黜，又何不行為慮乎？故錢之官貴顓也。夫收銅之權，則利不散之委巷；固銅之源，□□人無所牟於山澤；開銅之利，則地不愛□；精錢之制，則姦鑄不得亂其形；廣錢之涂，則下不賤錢；顓錢之官，則法必行而民重犯。六者雖管、賈餘談，而國家完計亡以代此矣。嗟乎！海內宗室，歔食者半；百官奉薄，或至箕會；瀕海閭左，動噪脫巾；水旱夭行，民室縣罄。當此之時，使公錢之貫山積帑藏，則以
translation_en: … and the Grand Duke (Taigong); Qi had Guan Jingzhong (Guan Zhong) and Chu had Sun Shu'ao—all of these were overseen by grand councilors. In the Tang, when furnaces for minting were granted only to Li Shimin and Li Yuanji, imperial princes were in charge of them; Liu Yan and Diwu Qi served as Vice Ministers (shilang) while concurrently holding the post of Coinage Commissioner in the Jiang-Huai region; Du Hao and others, as Editors in the Imperial Archives (bige jiaoli), investigated historical precedents for minting coins within the Forbidden Park. That their benefits were so widespread and their utility so vast—was this merely due to the superiority of their laws? The men involved also played a part in it. We truly ought to roughly follow the ancient institutions, and—as I have suggested—place exclusive responsibility in a single official. Do not begrudge lending him a measure of authority to allow him to exercise his own fiscal calculations, while ultimately enforcing strict laws to rectify promotions and demotions. Those whose coins are counterfeit and shoddy should be dismissed; those who obstruct circulation [?] or [?] should be dismissed; those who allow the people to open mines or hoard bronze vessels should be dismissed; and those who abet illicit minting should be dismissed. Why then would there be any worry about the coins not circulating? Therefore, in the offices responsible for coinage, what is valued is exclusive authority. Now, by centralizing the authority to collect copper, profits will not dissipate into the back alleys; by securing the sources of copper, [?] people will have no way to profiteer from the mountains and marshes; by opening up the benefits of copper mining, the earth will not withhold its [treasures?]; by refining the standards of coinage, illicit minters will not be able to confuse the form of the coins; by broadening the channels for coins, those below will not undervalue them; and by granting exclusive authority to coinage officials, the laws will surely be enforced and the people will be reluctant to violate them. Although these six points are the leftover discourses of Guan Zhong and Jia Yi, as a complete plan for the state, nothing can replace them. Alas! Within the seas, half of the imperial clansmen sigh for lack of food; the stipends of the hundred officials are so meager that they sometimes resort to scraping together petty exactions; the conscripted commoners along the coast stir and clamor, ready to cast off their headscarves in mutiny; floods, droughts, and epidemics prevail, and the households of the people are left utterly empty, like hanging vessels. At a time like this, if strings of government cash were piled like mountains in the state treasuries, then to…

title: 萬曆十年廣東鄉試錄
text:
親親重其祿可也以厲百官豐其餼可也以軍
需優其直可也以寧元元減其筭可也不
人食而飽不家分而給彌其亂而經其費
什其怨而救其竭所謂民衆國富霸王之
本則由斯術也哉范子曰府倉實民庶殷
無曠其衆以爲亂梯時將有反事將有閒
必有以務笑地之恒制乃可以有天下之
成利聽自任范子生今之時譚今之事其
所謂恒制成利者必曰錢法也
===
第五問
蔡德璋
同考試官訓導楊 批 粵苦用兵亦不能去兵
讀子策可佐經略一籌矣
考試官教諭胡 批 鑿鑿可行誦之竦服
考試官教諭陳 批 畫粵事切中機會
今天下言粵事者殊矣異日者嶺東西間
莽爲盜區海以外諸孽句引外夷躙中土
主上南顧廑
punctuated:
親親重其祿，可也；以厲百官豐其餼，可也；以軍需優其直，可也；以寧元元減其筭，可也。不人食而飽，不家分而給，彌其亂而經其費，什其怨而救其竭，所謂「民衆國富，霸王之本」，則由斯術也哉！范子曰：「府倉實，民庶殷，無曠其衆以爲亂梯。時將有反，事將有閒，必有以務笑地之恒制，乃可以有天下之成利。」聽自任范子生今之時，譚今之事，其所謂「恒制成利」者，必曰錢法也。
第五問
蔡德璋
同考試官訓導楊批：粵苦用兵，亦不能去兵。讀子策，可佐經略一籌矣。
考試官教諭胡批：鑿鑿可行，誦之竦服。
考試官教諭陳批：畫粵事切中機會。
今天下言粵事者殊矣。異日者，嶺東西間莽爲盜區，海以外諸孽句引外夷，躙中土，主上南顧，廑
translation_en:
…show affection to imperial kinsmen by increasing their stipends; it would be possible to encourage the hundred officials by making their provisions abundant; it would be possible to meet military needs by offering generous pay; and it would be possible to bring peace to the common people by reducing their poll taxes. Without feeding each person individually, all are full; without distributing to each household, all are supplied. Suppressing disorder while regulating expenditures, soothing [?] their resentments while rescuing them from exhaustion—what is called "a populous citizenry and a wealthy state, the foundation of hegemonic and kingly rule" surely comes from this art! Master Fan (Fan Li 范蠡) said: "When storehouses and granaries are full and the common people are prosperous, do not leave the multitude idle to become a ladder for rebellion. Times will have reversals, and affairs will have openings; one must attend to the constant system of Heaven and Earth [?] before one can possess the established profits of the world." If we allow that Master Fan were born in the present time and discussing present affairs, what he called the "constant system and established profits" would surely be termed the monetary system!

Question Five
Cai Dezhang 蔡德璋
Associate Examiner, Assistant Instructor Yang 楊, comments: Guangdong suffers from the use of troops, yet it cannot dispense with troops either. Reading your policy essay, it could assist the military planners with a strategy.
Examiner, Instructor Hu 胡, comments: Concrete and practicable; reciting it inspires respectful admiration.
Examiner, Instructor Chen 陳, comments: In planning Guangdong's affairs, it hits squarely upon the crucial opportunities.

title: 萬曆十年廣東鄉試錄
text:
宵旰籌之比者文武大吏奉
上威靈
廟堂指筭剗茀而芟夷之今其時勢大殊往昔
山箐不揭竿瀚海無波民耒耜徧山谷島
嶼商帆絡繹來薄即伏波樓船而在且卷
舌不道臨蔡將梁事蓋稱底定已迺執事
猶斤斤然度勢議時辨征勦之利患校水
陸之存留此治世之先憂忠臣之長慮也
而愚何敢無說以對蓋聞之戰無論大小
===
識時者勝兵無論衆寡因地者强時者戰
之機也地者兵之形也機之所伏有微
有著故其戰殊有勍敵逋寇千人成權萬
人成武而谿肆稱雄者不可以小智之有
乘隙竊發匿形坳澤却笠山林而隨撲隨
滅者不必以大誅之各隨其機之所宜而
已形之所在有險有夷故其守異有平原
廣埜無羊腸鋸齒之險進不必郭圍退不
必亭障而可以不失其險者不必以多守
punctuated:
宵旰籌之。比者文武大吏奉上威靈、廟堂指筭，剗茀而芟夷之。今其時勢大殊往昔，山箐不揭竿，瀚海無波，民耒耜徧山谷，島嶼商帆絡繹來薄，即伏波、樓船而在，且卷舌不道臨蔡、將梁事，蓋稱底定已。迺執事猶斤斤然度勢議時，辨征勦之利患，校水陸之存留，此治世之先憂，忠臣之長慮也，而愚何敢無說以對？

蓋聞之：戰無論大小，識時者勝；兵無論衆寡，因地者强。時者，戰之機也；地者，兵之形也。機之所伏有微有着，故其戰殊：有勍敵逋寇，千人成權，萬人成武，而谿肆稱雄者，不可以小智之；有乘隙竊發，匿形坳澤，却笠山林，而隨撲隨滅者，不必以大誅之。各隨其機之所宜而已。形之所在有險有夷，故其守異：有平原廣埜，無羊腸鋸齒之險，進不必郭圍，退不必亭障，而可以不失其險者，不必以多守…
translation_en:
…devised plans through sleepless nights and late meals. Recently, senior civil and military officials, relying on His Majesty's awe-inspiring prestige and the strategic calculations of the court, have cleared away the weeds and eradicated these bandits. Now the times and circumstances are vastly different from the past: no rebel poles are raised in the mountain thickets, the vast seas are calm without waves, the people's plows cover the mountain valleys, and merchant sails from the islands arrive in an unbroken stream to drop anchor. Even if the Wave-Calming General (Fubo) and the Towered-Ship General (Louchuan) of old were alive today, they would hold their tongues and not speak of marching on Cai [?] or commanding the troops of Liang, for the region may indeed be called thoroughly pacified. Yet you, Sir, still vigilantly assess the circumstances and deliberate on the times, distinguishing the advantages and disadvantages of punitive campaigns and weighing the retention or disbanding of naval and land forces. This is the foresight that anticipates sorrow in an age of order and the far-reaching concern of a loyal minister; how could I, in my ignorance, dare to have no explanation with which to reply?

I have heard it said: in warfare, whether on a large or small scale, he who recognizes the times wins; in deploying troops, whether many or few, he who adapts to the terrain is strong. The times are the pivotal opportunity of warfare; the terrain is the configuration of troops. Where opportunities lie hidden, some are subtle and some are manifest, and therefore the mode of combat differs: when there are formidable enemies and entrenched bandits who gather by the thousands to form a power and by the tens of thousands to form a military force, running rampant in the gorges and styling themselves overlords, one cannot overcome them with petty stratagems [?]; when there are those who seize a crack to break out furtively, hiding their tracks in low-lying marshes or casting off their bamboo hats in the mountain forests, who can be extinguished as soon as they are struck, one need not exterminate them with a grand expedition. In each case, one simply follows what is appropriate to the pivotal opportunity. Where terrain is situated, some places are precipitous and some are level, and therefore the mode of defense differs: when there are flat plains and broad wildernesses without the strategic hazards of sheep-gut trails or saw-toothed ridges, where in advancing one need not rely on outer walls and enclosures and in retreating one need not rely on frontier posts and barriers, and yet one can avoid losing one's strategic advantage, one need not defend them with large numbers…

title: 萬曆十年廣東鄉試錄
text:
之有洪澤巨海無通邑大都之塹我可以
往彼可以來而不能不失其險者不可以
寡守之各隨其形之所宜而已不伺其機
之微著而槩議征誅征誅煩則民罷是梯
亂也而何以議戰不順其形之險夷而多
置什伍什伍衆則帑竭是坐困也而何以
議守故善戰者重用大而善守者重用衆
嘗觀之司馬法矣其曰大軍以固多力以
煩而又曰凡誅以明武有殺一人而三軍
===
震者有殺一方而萬人喜者則戰之大小
無常矣戰曰用兵之道用衆治衆利正而
又曰一而當十十而當百百而當千千而
當萬此守法也則兵之衆寡亦無常巳宜
大而大而毋故翕之以自衄宜小而小而
毋故張之以自疲宜衆而衆而毋自寡其
衆以來敵之侵宜寡而寡而毋故衆其寡
以耗天之聚旣度其時又度其地如斯而
巳矣今之議粤戰者曰粤之內地重岡複
punctuated: 之；有洪澤巨海，無通邑大都之塹，我可以往，彼可以來，而不能不失其險者，不可以寡守之。各隨其形之所宜而已。不伺其機之微著而槩議征誅，征誅煩則民罷，是梯亂也，而何以議戰？不順其形之險夷而多置什伍，什伍衆則帑竭，是坐困也，而何以議守？故善戰者重用大，而善守者重用衆。嘗觀之《司馬法》矣：其曰「大軍以固，多力以煩」，而又曰「凡誅以明武，有殺一人而三軍震者，有殺一方而萬人喜者」，則戰之大小無常矣；戰曰「用兵之道，用衆治衆利正」，而又曰「一而當十，十而當百，百而當千，千而當萬，此守法也」，則兵之衆寡亦無常巳。宜大而大，而毋故翕之以自衄；宜小而小，而毋故張之以自疲；宜衆而衆，而毋自寡其衆以來敵之侵；宜寡而寡，而毋故衆其寡以耗天之聚。旣度其時，又度其地，如斯而巳矣。今之議粤戰者曰：「粤之內地，重岡複
translation_en: … them; and where there are vast marshes and great seas without the moats of major towns and great metropolises, where we can go forth and they can come in, so that one cannot avoid losing the strategic advantage of the terrain, one cannot defend them with few troops. In each case, one simply follows what is appropriate to the terrain. If one does not watch for whether the strategic moment is subtle or manifest and instead uniformly proposes campaigns of chastisement, then frequent campaigns will exhaust the people; this is to invite rebellion—so how can one discuss warfare? If one does not adapt to whether the terrain is precipitous or level and instead stations numerous military squads, then large numbers of troops will deplete the treasury; this is to sit waiting for exhaustion—so how can one discuss defense? Therefore, those skilled in warfare are cautious about employing large-scale campaigns, and those skilled in defense are cautious about employing large numbers of troops. I have examined the Methods of the Minister of War (Sima fa): it says, "A great army is for firmness, yet excessive force brings trouble," and it also says, "All chastisement is to manifest martial prowess; there are cases where killing one man makes the Three Armies tremble, and cases where executing one quarter makes ten thousand men rejoice." Thus, the scale of warfare has no constant rule. On battle it says, "In the way of employing troops, when using the many to govern the many, the advantage lies in regular arrays," yet it also says, "One matching ten, ten matching a hundred, a hundred matching a thousand, and a thousand matching ten thousand—this is the method of defense." Thus, the numerical strength of troops likewise has no constant rule. When it is appropriate to be on a large scale, make it large, and do not purposely contract it to bring defeat upon oneself; when it is appropriate to be on a small scale, make it small, and do not purposely inflate it to exhaust oneself; when it is appropriate to use many, use many, and do not reduce one's own numbers so as to invite enemy incursion; when it is appropriate to use few, use few, and do not purposely multiply what should be few so as to squander heaven's accumulated resources. Once one has measured the timing and also measured the terrain, it is simply a matter of acting thus and nothing more. Those who discuss warfare in Guangdong today say: "In the interior of Guangdong, with its layered ridges and…

title: 萬曆十年廣東鄉試錄
text:
嶺懸崖密柵所繇入者隘所從歸者迂彼
飽可以待我之饑是故方馬埋輪不足以
踐其逕也五火不足以燔其林也五間不
足以攜其黨也非大舉兵而盡創之無以
震明威而夷亂窟至其据阪背險半隱半
出名曰撫民有隙即內訌者竄在林藂蟠
於沮澤短錟衞前積弩陪後以伺我出入
鵰剿亦只恐與巨賊連耳嗟乎此二說者
東粵之戰也其在嘉隆之際則然今日之
===
粵無有逆
主令者可以戰可以無戰故其議戰也異於昔
日必戰之時今之議粵守者曰粵之外地
表海隈澳方舟聯艦所臨者瀚波所備者
番夷彼突可以衝我之逸是故廣塹深坑
不足以杜其入也飛橋不足以遏其銳也
天浮不足以擊其渡也非多徵兵而拒守
之無以圉跳梁而實舟航至其絕岸遮壘
且戰且守名曰陸兵有警即堵截者屯在
punctuated: 嶺、懸崖密柵，所繇入者隘，所從歸者迂，彼飽可以待我之饑。是故方馬埋輪，不足以踐其逕也；五火，不足以燔其林也；五間，不足以攜其黨也。非大舉兵而盡創之，無以震明威而夷亂窟。至其据阪背險，半隱半出，名曰撫民，有隙即內訌者，竄在林藂，蟠於沮澤，短錟衞前，積弩陪後，以伺我出入。鵰剿亦只恐與巨賊連耳。」嗟乎！此二說者，東粵之戰也，其在嘉隆之際則然。今日之粵，無有逆主令者，可以戰，可以無戰，故其議戰也，異於昔日必戰之時。今之議粵守者曰：「粵之外地，表海隈澳，方舟聯艦，所臨者瀚波，所備者番夷，彼突可以衝我之逸。是故廣塹深坑，不足以杜其入也；飛橋，不足以遏其銳也；天浮，不足以擊其渡也。非多徵兵而拒守之，無以圉跳梁而實舟航。至其絕岸遮壘，且戰且守，名曰陸兵，有警即堵截者，屯在
translation_en: … ridges, overhanging cliffs, and dense stockades; the routes of entry are narrow and the ways of return circuitous, so that well-fed, they can await our hunger. Therefore, tethering horses in square formations and burying chariot wheels are insufficient to tread their paths; the five kinds of fire attacks are insufficient to burn down their forests; and the five types of spies are insufficient to divide their partisans. Unless we mobilize troops on a grand scale and thoroughly crush them, there is no way to project our illustrious might and level their nests of rebellion. As for those who occupy slopes with their backs to险峻 terrain, half-hidden and half-exposed—nominally called pacified subjects, yet inciting internal strife the moment an opening appears—they skulk in forest thickets and coil in marshes, with short spears guarding the front and massed crossbows supporting the rear, lying in wait for our comings and goings. Even if we conduct lightning raids like a swooping hawk, we still fear only that they will link up with the major bandits." Alas! These two arguments concern offensive warfare in Eastern Yue (Guangdong), and during the Jiajing and Longqing reigns they were indeed true. In the Yue of today, there are none who defy the ruler's commands; one may fight, or one may not fight. Therefore, deliberating on offensive warfare today differs from the time in the past when fighting was imperative. Those today who deliberate on the defense of Yue say: "The outer territories of Yue front the sea with winding bays where lashed boats and linked warships gather; what we face are vast waves, and what we guard against are foreign barbarians, whose sudden charges can shatter our ease. Therefore, wide moats and deep pits are insufficient to bar their entry; flying bridges are insufficient to check their sharp advance; and floating river-barriers (tianfu) are insufficient to strike them as they cross. Unless we levy numerous troops to hold them off in defense, there is no way to fend off the insolent marauders and fill our vessels and ships. As for cutting off the shores and screening with ramparts, simultaneously fighting and defending—nominally called land troops, who block and intercept the moment an alarm is raised—they are garrisoned at…

title: 萬曆十年廣東鄉試錄
text:
海鎮界於山谷晝登雲梯夜設雲火以伺
賊出入士卒不多恐貽内地憂耳嗟乎此
二說者東粤之守也其在嘉隆之際則然
今日之粤毋敢攻我土者可以守可以無
守故其議守也異於昔日必守之時蓋嘗
以秦漢事參之秦併天下略定楊粤置南
海象郡以謫徙民粤漸以亂任囂首事趙
佗阻兵馴至嘉德函封漢節粤大亂矣元
鼎之初樓船戈船出師十萬定爲九郡粤
===
漸以治其後輯寧終漢不叛至建武間蠻
里張游來獻白雉封歸漢君粤大治矣夫
十萬之師可以攻元鼎之虜而不可徵於
建武之際樓船之將可以斬亂越之吕嘉
而不可加歸漢之張游繇斯以談而今日
粤中之戰守其槩可論已夫粤豈忘戰之
國哉而當久創之餘民始息肩則鵰勦不
可廢而大征不可屢何以明之四面合圍
獸窮之攫可虞也千里輓車脫巾之呼可
punctuated: 海鎮，界於山谷，晝登雲梯，夜設雲火，以伺賊出入；士卒不多，恐貽内地憂耳。」嗟乎！此二說者，東粤之守也，其在嘉、隆之際則然。今日之粤，毋敢攻我土者，可以守，可以無守；故其議守也，異於昔日必守之時。蓋嘗以秦、漢事參之：秦併天下，略定楊粤，置南海、象郡，以謫徙民，粤漸以亂；任囂首事，趙佗阻兵，馴至嘉、德函封漢節，粤大亂矣。元鼎之初，樓船、戈船出師十萬，定爲九郡，粤漸以治。其後輯寧，終漢不叛。至建武間，蠻里張游來獻白雉，封歸漢君，粤大治矣。夫十萬之師，可以攻元鼎之虜，而不可徵於建武之際；樓船之將，可以斬亂越之吕嘉，而不可加歸漢之張游。繇斯以談，而今日粤中之戰守，其槩可論已。夫粤豈忘戰之國哉？而當久創之餘，民始息肩，則鵰勦不可廢，而大征不可屢。何以明之？四面合圍，獸窮之攫可虞也；千里輓車，脫巾之呼可…
translation_en: … coastal garrisons, bordering the mountain valleys, where by day they climb scaling ladders to keep watch and by night they set out signal fires to spy on the bandits' comings and goings; if the soldiers are not numerous, it is feared this will leave cause for worry in the interior." Alas! These two arguments concern the defense of Eastern Yue [Guangdong], and during the transition between the Jiajing (1522–1566) and Longqing (1567–1572) reigns, this was indeed the case. In the Yue of today, there is no one who dares to attack our territory; we may defend it, or we may go without defending it. Therefore, discussing defense today is different from the past, when defense was imperative. Let us examine this by comparing the affairs of the Qin and Han dynasties. When Qin unified the empire, it pacified Yang-Yue and established the commanderies of Nanhai and Xiang, populating them with exiled convicts, and Yue gradually fell into disorder. Ren Xiao initiated autonomous measures and Zhao Tuo relied on military force to seal off the borders, which eventually led to Lü Jia and Zhao Jiande sealing up the Han envoy's tallies in a box—and Yue fell into great chaos. At the beginning of the Yuanding era (116–111 BCE), the Tower-Ship and Halberd-Ship generals led an army of a hundred thousand forth and pacified the region into nine commanderies, whereupon Yue gradually became orderly. Thereafter it remained peaceful and did not rebel for the rest of the Han dynasty. By the Jianwu era (25–56 CE), Zhang You of the Man villages came to present a white pheasant and was enfeoffed as the Lord Who Submits to Han (Guihan jun), and Yue achieved great order. Now, an army of a hundred thousand could be used to attack the caitiffs of the Yuanding era, yet could not be levied during the Jianwu era; the Tower-Ship generals could be used to behead Lü Jia who threw Yue into rebellion, yet could not be inflicted upon Zhang You who submitted to Han. Discussing the matter from this perspective, the general principles of warfare and defense in Yue today can be assessed. Could Yue be a land that forgets warfare? Yet in the aftermath of prolonged trauma, when the people have only just rested their shoulders from their burdens, raptor-like surgical strikes cannot be abandoned, whereas massive punitive campaigns cannot be repeatedly launched. How can this be made clear? When an encirclement is closed on all four sides, one must beware the desperate clawing of a cornered beast; when supply carts are hauled for a thousand li, the mutinous cries of soldiers casting off their headscarves must be…

title: 萬曆十年廣東鄉試錄
text:
戒也飛霜匝地蘭艾之盡可隱也况自用
兵以來山箐海氛次第盪覆矣卽欲大舉
將焉用之間有頑梗未銷山谷時警一夫
横行折其首而貸其醜一方怙强夷其壘
而赦其鄰旣不黷兵亦不糜廩此鵰勦之
法所當講乎非謂勦之勝於征也今昔之
時異也夫粤豈忘守之國哉而當暴露之
後民心安堵則陸兵不可增而水備不可
撤何以明之反側甫寧而干戈且尋是疑
===
寇也土著可練而客兵未捐是糜餉也關
梁旣闢而甲楯不釋是塞貨也况自平寇
以後民壯弓兵旋復增額矣卽欲再增將
焉用之若夫海氛蹔屏夷情叵測東連暹
羅番舶之往來宜稽南通日本悍鹵之出
没宜防內嚴下海之禁外緝句引之姦此
水兵之防所當嚴乎非謂水之加於陸也
山海之地殊也往者勦伐不加專事姑息
亂萌不折逆黨盈野吾勤於勦不輕於撫
punctuated: 戒也；飛霜匝地，蘭艾之盡可隱也。况自用兵以來，山箐海氛次第盪覆矣；卽欲大舉，將焉用之？間有頑梗未銷，山谷時警，一夫横行，折其首而貸其醜；一方怙强，夷其壘而赦其鄰，旣不黷兵，亦不糜廩，此鵰勦之法所當講乎？非謂勦之勝於征也，今昔之時異也。夫粤豈忘守之國哉？而當暴露之後，民心安堵，則陸兵不可增，而水備不可撤。何以明之？反側甫寧，而干戈且尋，是疑寇也；土著可練，而客兵未捐，是糜餉也；關梁旣闢，而甲楯不釋，是塞貨也。况自平寇以後，民壯弓兵旋復增額矣；卽欲再增，將焉用之？若夫海氛蹔屏，夷情叵測，東連暹羅，番舶之往來宜稽；南通日本，悍鹵之出没宜防。內嚴下海之禁，外緝句引之姦，此水兵之防所當嚴乎？非謂水之加於陸也，山海之地殊也。往者勦伐不加，專事姑息，亂萌不折，逆黨盈野。吾勤於勦，不輕於撫，
translation_en:
… guarded against; when flying frost covers the ground, the destruction of orchids along with mugwort is to be grieved over. Moreover, ever since military operations began, the mountain thickets and maritime threats have been swept away and overturned one after another; even if one wished to launch a massive campaign, to what use would it be put? Occasionally there are stubborn and recalcitrant elements not yet eliminated, causing periodic alarms in the mountain valleys. When a single ruffian runs rampant, break their ringleader and spare his followers; when a locality relies on force, level its fortifications and pardon its neighbors. Thus one neither engages in wanton warfare nor wastes grain rations—is this not why the method of surgical strikes (diao剿) ought to be studied? This is not to say that surgical strikes are superior to grand expeditions, but that present and past times are different.

Now, how could Guangdong be a region that forgets defense? Yet in the aftermath of exposure in the field, when the people's hearts have settled in peace, land troops should not be increased, whereas naval defenses cannot be withdrawn. How to make this clear? When the wavering and rebellious have barely been pacified, yet shields and spears are still being taken up, this is to arouse suspicion among the bandits; when native inhabitants can be trained, yet outside troops have not been dismissed, this is to waste military provisions; when passes and bridges have already been opened, yet armor and shields are not laid down, this is to block the flow of goods. Moreover, since the pacification of the bandits, the quotas of civilian militia (minzhuang) and archers (gongbing) have soon been increased again; even if one wished to increase them further, to what use would they be put? As for the maritime threats, though they are temporarily held at bay, the intentions of the foreign peoples are unfathomable. To the east, the sea links with Siam (Xianluo), and the coming and going of foreign ships ought to be inspected; to the south, it connects with Japan (Riben), and the appearances and disappearances of fierce marauders ought to be guarded against. Internally enforcing the prohibition against going to sea, and externally apprehending traitorous collaborators who lure them in—is this not why the defense of the naval forces ought to be made strict? This is not to say that the water is more important than the land, but that the terrains of mountain and sea are different.

In the past, punitive strikes were not applied and officials devoted themselves exclusively to leniency and appeasement; the buds of rebellion were not nipped, and rebel factions filled the countryside. If we are diligent in surgical strikes and do not lightly resort to pacification, …

title: 萬曆十年廣東鄉試錄
text:
則小寇漸夷不敢滋蔓故其議剿也即所
以議征也内寇陸梁躑躅林莽實與海寇
聲勢相倚吾嚴於外俾不得入則内寇益
孤莫爲羽翼故其備水也即所以防陸也
夫朱明長贏不能盡其所以爲溫也必隨
之以揫斂之氣而爲秋玄武沍陰不能盡
其所以寒也必隨之以敷榮之氣而爲春
孰爲此者天也天不能常秋而不春而况
於人乎竊嘗譬之病者當其耳鳴鼻張目
===
眩舌撟斯時也厲三陽之鍼和五分之熨
甚則割皮解肌搦髓揲荒無所愛於其膚
何也其勢迫也迨其少間則當撟引案扤
調飲飯擇晏日車步廣志以適筋骨柔血
脉以瀉氣法不當砭灸砭灸則氣逐而篤
今之粵其少間之時乎而論者一切曰大
征也益兵也是毒熨鑱石於病起之餘其
篤立見脉法曰二陰應外一陽接内者不
可以剛藥剛藥入則邪氣流行爲重困於
punctuated: 則小寇漸夷，不敢滋蔓，故其議剿也，即所以議征也。内寇陸梁，躑躅林莽，實與海寇聲勢相倚。吾嚴於外，俾不得入，則内寇益孤，莫爲羽翼，故其備水也，即所以防陸也。夫朱明長贏，不能盡其所以爲溫也，必隨之以揫斂之氣而爲秋；玄武沍陰，不能盡其所以寒也，必隨之以敷榮之氣而爲春。孰爲此者？天也。天不能常秋而不春，而况於人乎？竊嘗譬之病者：當其耳鳴鼻張、目眩舌撟，斯時也，厲三陽之鍼，和五分之熨，甚則割皮解肌、搦髓揲荒，無所愛於其膚。何也？其勢迫也。迨其少間，則當撟引案扤，調飲飯，擇晏日車步，廣志以適筋骨，柔血脉以瀉氣，法不當砭灸；砭灸則氣逐而篤。今之粵，其少間之時乎！而論者一切曰大征也、益兵也，是毒熨鑱石於病起之餘，其篤立見。《脉法》曰：「二陰應外，一陽接内者，不可以剛藥；剛藥入則邪氣流行，爲重困於
translation_en:
… then minor bandits will gradually be leveled and will not dare to spread. Therefore, discussing localized suppression is precisely the means of discussing a grand campaign. When inland bandits rampage and skulk through the forests and brush, they actually rely on sea pirates for mutual support and momentum. If we maintain strict defenses on the outside so that they cannot enter, then the inland bandits will become increasingly isolated with no one to serve as their wings. Therefore, preparing naval defenses is precisely the means of defending the land.

Now, the flourishing growth of bright summer cannot exhaust its capacity for warmth; it must be followed by the gathering and contracting qi to become autumn. The congealed yin of dark winter cannot exhaust its capacity for cold; it must be followed by the blossoming and flourishing qi to become spring. Who brings this about? It is Heaven. Heaven cannot remain perpetually in autumn without turning to spring, and how much less can human beings?

I have ventured to compare this to a sick person. When his ears ring, his nostrils flare, his eyes grow dizzy, and his tongue stiffens—at such a time, one sharpens the needles for the Three Yang channels, prepares the hot compresses of five-tenths strength, and in extreme cases even cuts the skin, separates the flesh, grasps the marrow, and probes the vital membranes, showing no hesitation to spare his skin. Why is this? Because the condition is urgent. Yet once he experiences a slight remission, one should apply therapeutic stretching and massage, regulate his drink and food, choose clear days for riding or walking, broaden his mind to comfort his sinews and bones, and soften his blood and vessels to drain excess qi. By medical rule, one should not apply stone needles or moxibustion; if one applies stone needles or moxibustion, the vital qi is driven away and the illness becomes critical. Is not Guangdong today in a period of slight remission? Yet commentators uniformly cry out for grand campaigns and increasing troops! This is to apply potent hot compresses and sharp stone probes just as the patient is recovering from illness—his condition will immediately turn critical. The Rules of the Pulse (Maifa) says: "When the two yin respond on the outside and the one yang connects on the inside, one must not use harsh medicines; if harsh medicines enter, noxious qi will circulate freely, causing severe distress in…"

title: 萬曆十年廣東鄉試錄
text: 偷嗟乎治粤者奈何使其偷而重困也
punctuated: 偷。嗟乎！治粤者奈何使其偷而重困也！
translation_en: … lingering weakness. Alas! How can those who govern Guangdong allow it to fall into lingering weakness and suffer doubly grave distress!

title: 萬曆十年廣東鄉試錄
text:
廣東鄉試錄後序
萬曆紀元以來南粤士凡四
比矣其初比也士甫脫湯火
之厄創夷者未起流散者未
息肩蓋惕惕有戒心焉故其
言憤以厲再比則創夷起而
負擔息肩矣還定安集猶未
===
也蓋凜凜無忘心焉故其言
惻以傷三比則還定安集矣
生聚教訓猶未也蓋瞿瞿無
逸心焉故其言慷慨而有餘
思乃今四比則澹然忘之矣
神靈威武之所變化幾復嶺海之
舊出溝壑而衽席罷呻吟而
punctuated:
廣東鄉試錄後序

萬曆紀元以來，南粤士凡四比矣。其初比也，士甫脫湯火之厄，創夷者未起，流散者未息肩，蓋惕惕有戒心焉，故其言憤以厲。再比，則創夷起而負擔息肩矣，還定安集猶未也，蓋凜凜無忘心焉，故其言惻以傷。三比，則還定安集矣，生聚教訓猶未也，蓋瞿瞿無逸心焉，故其言慷慨而有餘思。乃今四比，則澹然忘之矣。神靈威武之所變化，幾復嶺海之舊，出溝壑而衽席，罷呻吟而
translation_en:
Postface to the Record of the Guangdong Provincial Examination

Since the inception of the Wanli reign (1573), the scholars of Southern Yue [Guangdong] have competed in the triennial examinations four times in all. At the first competition, the scholars had only just escaped the calamities of boiling water and fire; the wounded had not yet risen, and the displaced refugees had not yet rested their shoulders from their burdens. Truly, they were fearful and on their guard, and therefore their words were indignant and fierce. By the second competition, the wounded had risen and those bearing burdens had rested their shoulders, yet returning to stability and resettling in peace had still not been achieved. Truly, they were apprehensive and did not let their minds forget, and therefore their words were sorrowful and pained. By the third competition, they had returned to stability and resettled in peace, yet multiplying the population and instructing the people had still not been achieved. Truly, they were watchful and allowed their minds no ease, and therefore their words were impassioned and left lingering thoughts. Now, by this fourth competition, they have calmly forgotten those past woes. Through the transformations wrought by sacred spirit and martial awe, the region of the Ranges and the Sea has nearly been restored to its former state: emerging from ditches and ravines onto sleeping mats, ceasing their groaning and…

title: 萬曆十年廣東鄉試錄
text:
謳歌偃枹寢烽而絃誦戢戈
櫜矢而衿佩鄉盛爼豆之容
士遑庠序之業物力寖阜逸
心亦或萌其間故其言雍容
閒雅而無遺藻錄之若有不
勝錄焉竊聞異時之談南粤
也宦游者以為善地旅游者
===
以為陸海自頃軍興之後□
稍稍難之今之願游者如故
矣夫沃土民逸瘠土民勞習
也富歲多賴凶歲多暴資也
南粤故富歲沃土資與習恒
相成凋敝之餘又復其始
武功荒之
punctuated: 謳歌，偃枹寢烽而絃誦，戢戈櫜矢而衿佩，鄉盛爼豆之容，士遑庠序之業。物力寖阜，逸心亦或萌其間，故其言雍容閒雅而無遺藻，錄之若有不勝錄焉。竊聞異時之談南粤也，宦游者以為善地，旅游者以為陸海。自頃軍興之後，□稍稍難之，今之願游者如故矣。夫沃土民逸，瘠土民勞，習也；富歲多賴，凶歲多暴，資也。南粤故富歲沃土，資與習恒相成。凋敝之餘，又復其始。武功荒之，
translation_en: … songs of praise; laying down drumsticks and extinguishing beacon fires for the sound of stringed instruments and recitation; putting away halberds and casing arrows for the collars and pendants of scholars. The districts flourish with the deportment of ritual vessels, and scholars have leisure for their studies in the local schools. As material resources gradually become abundant, a desire for ease may also sprout among them. Thus their words are poised, refined, and lack no literary grace; when recording them for the examination record, it seems there are almost too many to record. I have heard that in former times, when people spoke of Southern Yue [Guangdong], those travelling on official service regarded it as a fine place, and travellers regarded it as a 'sea on land' [a land of rich abundance]. After the recent military campaigns, [people?] gradually came to view it as difficult; yet now those who wish to travel here are just as before. Now, that the people of fertile lands are given to ease while the people of barren lands are given to toil is a matter of habit; that in years of plenty people are mostly virtuous [or: reliant on goodness] while in years of famine they are mostly violent is a matter of material conditions. Southern Yue has ever been a land of abundant years and fertile soil, where material conditions and habits constantly reinforce one another. In the aftermath of exhaustion and ruin, it has once again returned to its former state. Military achievements cleared and pacified it, …

title: 萬曆十年廣東鄉試錄
text:
文德康之
三朝休養夫孰非
上恩耶士多賴而善惟此時忘勞
而淫亦惟此時往者盜起天
未悔禍民易與爲非惡氛彌
山狂波沸海草野流膏川原
厭血士踰山蹈海莫必其命
===
歲當大比僅乃半至尚不以
此輟藝廢講况今安堵而有
暇自逸哉歷九折之坂懸車
束馬迄以安度戒也周道如
砥車驟馬馳有時顛蹶忘也
嘉隆間事固士所耳而目之
者卽身所不及詢諸父老念
punctuated: 文德康之，三朝休養，夫孰非上恩耶？士多賴而善，惟此時；忘勞而淫，亦惟此時。往者盜起，天未悔禍，民易與爲非。惡氛彌山，狂波沸海，草野流膏，川原厭血，士踰山蹈海，莫必其命。歲當大比，僅乃半至，尚不以此輟藝廢講；况今安堵，而有暇自逸哉？歷九折之坂，懸車束馬，迄以安度，戒也；周道如砥，車驟馬馳，有時顛蹶，忘也。嘉、隆間事，固士所耳而目之者；卽身所不及，詢諸父老，念
translation_en: … and civil virtue brings it peace. Through the recuperation and nurturing of three reigns, how is any of this not due to His Majesty's grace? That scholars have much to rely upon and incline toward goodness is precisely at this time; yet that they forget toil and fall into dissipation is also precisely at this time. In the past, when bandits arose, Heaven had not yet relented from sending calamity, and the people were easily drawn into wrongdoing. Foul miasmas filled the mountains and raging waves boiled in the seas; the countryside ran with fat and the rivers and plains were glutted with blood. Scholars crossed mountains and braved the seas, unable to be sure of their very lives. When the year of the Triennial Examination arrived, barely half were able to attend, yet even so they did not on that account abandon their literary arts or cease their scholarly discussions. How much less today, when all live in peace and security, do they have leisure to indulge in ease! When traversing a slope of nine switchbacks, if one suspends the carriage and binds the horses, one ultimately crosses in safety—because of caution. When the royal highway is as smooth as a whetstone, if carriages race and horses gallop, at times they overturn and stumble—because of forgetfulness. The events of the Jiajing (1522–1566) and Longqing (1567–1572) eras are assuredly what scholars have heard with their own ears and seen with their own eyes; even for what they did not personally experience, if they inquire of the elders, reflecting…

title: 萬曆十年廣東鄉試錄
text:
之刺心語之動色抑知其□
乎夫盜所以起民弗安也民
之弗安吏弗稱也往聞南粤
之民不苦盜而苦吏吏實爲
厲階而民乃爲盜藪夫吏之
酷貪之囮也吏之貪盜之媒
也士蓋嘗憤疾斯輩居則
===
===
爲吏若此人將不食其餘
我一旦綰綬且羞與爲伍
其自許信非貌言然九州碁
布孰非命吏乃南粤多弗稱
何也
君門萬里其民柔易與而珠璣瑇
瑁翠羽丹砂之貨多也可欲
punctuated: 之刺心，語之動色，抑知其□乎？夫盜所以起，民弗安也；民之弗安，吏弗稱也。往聞南粤之民，不苦盜而苦吏。吏實爲厲階，而民乃爲盜藪。夫吏之酷，貪之囮也；吏之貪，盜之媒也。士蓋嘗憤疾斯輩，居則爲：「吏若此，人將不食其餘。我一旦綰綬，且羞與爲伍。」其自許信非貌言。然九州碁布，孰非命吏，乃南粤多弗稱，何也？君門萬里，其民柔易與，而珠璣、瑇瑁、翠羽、丹砂之貨多也。可欲
translation_en: … of them pierces the heart, and speaking of them changes one's countenance—yet do they know the [reason?] for this? Now, the reason bandits arise is that the people are not at peace; the reason the people are not at peace is that the officials are unequal to their duties. In the past, I heard that the people of Southern Yue [Guangdong] suffer not from bandits, but from officials. It is the officials who truly form the steps to ruin, and so the people become a refuge for bandits. Now, the cruelty of officials is the decoy of their greed, and the greed of officials is the matchmaker of banditry. Scholars have doubtless resented and detested such types, saying in private life [?]: "When officials are like this, people would not even eat their leftovers. Once I myself tie on an official ribbon, I would be ashamed even to be in their company." Such self-expectations are surely not mere empty words. Yet across the Nine Provinces, spread out like pieces on a chessboard, who among the officials is not appointed by imperial command? Why, then, are so many in Southern Yue unequal to their duties? It is because the palace gates of the sovereign are ten thousand li away, the people here are pliant and easy to deal with, and there is an abundance of precious goods—pearls, tortoiseshell, kingfisher feathers, and cinnabar. title: 萬曆十年廣東鄉試錄
text:
亂心而無可畏者以持其後
則中才易移寧獨南粤士得
毋有憤於目擊而忘於身親
者乎夫士也方與計偕今日
之士他日之吏也養之則士
用之則吏課士以言課吏以
功養與用等耳善爲吏者
===
□□不待大計
以慮計焉善爲士者以□□
其業不待大比而勸其次慮
比焉然使吏誠以慮計之心
待計何所不舉使士誠以慮
比之心待比何所不脩今南
粤幸賴
punctuated: 亂心，而無可畏者以持其後，則中才易移，寧獨南粤？士得毋有憤於目擊而忘於身親者乎？夫士也，方與計偕。今日之士，他日之吏也；養之則士，用之則吏。課士以言，課吏以功，養與用等耳。善爲吏者，□□不待大計；以慮計焉。善爲士者，以□□其業，不待大比而勸；其次慮比焉。然使吏誠以慮計之心待計，何所不舉？使士誠以慮比之心待比，何所不脩？今南粤幸賴
translation_en: …confound the mind, and when there is nothing to be feared to hold them in check afterward, those of average talent are easily swayed—and how could this be true of Southern Yue alone? Could it be that scholars feel indignation at what they witness with their own eyes, yet forget it when they experience office themselves? Now, these scholars are just about to go up to the capital along with the fiscal accounts. The scholars of today are the officials of tomorrow; when nurtured they are scholars, and when employed they are officials. Scholars are evaluated by their words, and officials are evaluated by their achievements—nurturing and employing are of equal principle. Those who excel at being officials […][?] without waiting for the Great Evaluation; [next are those who] anxiously anticipate the Evaluation [?]. Those who excel at being scholars […][?] their studies, and are encouraged without waiting for the Great Triennial Examination; next are those who anxiously anticipate the Examination. Yet if officials truly awaited the Evaluation with the mindset of anxiously anticipating it, what duty would not be fulfilled? If scholars truly awaited the Examination with the mindset of anxiously anticipating it, what conduct would not be cultivated? Today, Southern Yue fortunately relies upon…

title: 萬曆十年廣東鄉試錄
text:
天之靈徼福於
明聖氛消波恬士緩帶而升竊恐
其忘之也而躬蹈昔之所求
於吏者故為追述往昔以動
其操危臨深之思詩不云乎
鑑□遠士其以前事□
□有以對
punctuated: 天之靈，徼福於明聖，氛消波恬，士緩帶而升。竊恐其忘之也，而躬蹈昔之所求於吏者。故為追述往昔，以動其操危臨深之思。《詩》不云乎：「□鑑□遠。」士其以前事□□有以對。
translation_en: … the numinous grace of Heaven, and enjoying the blessings of our enlightened Sage Emperor, the miasmas of disorder have dissipated and the waves are calm, so that scholars may loosen their sashes and advance at ease. Yet I privately fear that they may forget the past, and themselves fall into the very faults for which they formerly reproached the officials. Therefore I have recounted past events in order to stir in them thoughts of maintaining vigilance in peril and treading as if on the brink of an abyss. Does not the Book of Odes (Shi) say: "The [Yin] mirror is [not] far off" [?]? May the scholars take past affairs [as their mirror and] have wherewithal to respond.
